my husband and i got married and i decided it was time to change coverage from a ppo to an hmo. ive stuck to ppo all these years because i was following my favorite dr around. well, he finally was promoted once again and left patient care. i bounced around from memorial care to hoag and just couldn't find the same care.

i remember going to kaiser as a child, but never have gone as an adult. it's been a little over a year since our transition to kaiser hmo and i have to say i love it. 

kaiser harbor-macarthur medical center is amazing. the staff is amazing. everything you need is found here as a one-stop shop which is ultra convenient. i've got nothing but the best care from the security guard to the front desk staff, the labs, pharmacy techs, urgent care, the nurses and drs. i'm especially happy to find dr pantig. 

dr pantig is so thorough with the best bedside manners. i feel she truly listens to my concerns, has so much wisdom and care to tend to my health. i couldn't be happier to find her and her awesome nurse, sandy! i really did miss the dr i followed around, but dr pantig and nurse sandy are "home" to me. it's great to feel so cared for again.

many people frown upon hmos, but i've got to say my experience here at kaiser habor-macarthur has been nothing, but great. to be honest, you get what you put out. with every visit, i sincerely appreciate the staff for their tireless and thankless work. they're so appreciative in return. i always leave with a smile on my face. kaiser harbor-macarthur is highly recommended.

i recently gave birth to my first baby at the abrazo location, and i just have to say i was very impressed with the staff and service i received while there, despite the rumors i've heard about labor and delivery. i gave birth during the coronavirus pandemic and the nurses were professional and made sure my husband and i were taken care of. i want to give a shout out specifically to a traveling nurse lindsey who helped me so much through delivery and made sure i was comfortable the whole time. i also want to give a shout out to another nurse denise who helped my husband and i during the recovery period and was so personable and professional. despite the circumstance, my husband and i were overall pleased with our stay. especially because of the service we received from lindsey and denise. the food however i will give 2 stars. that's my only complaint.

this hospital was a god sent. i was very nervous to be sent here to be on hospital bed rest with my twin babies after reading the reviews. but let me tell you, this was the most amazing hospital experience i've ever had. (and i am very picky)  i had my twin babies at 32 weeks and they were in nicu for 19 days after birth. the labor and delivery and triage nurses are just such wonderful loving people. erin in triage helped to calm my nerves and truly cared about my comfort, she took every concern i had and took me seriously and truly cared. all of the nurses i had in labor and delivery were absolutely amazing. they made sure i was comfortable and kept me updated with everything going on. ( i had preeclampsia ) no matter how many questions i had or how many times i called them in to help me use the restroom or get me water they always had the biggest smile and were eager to help. you could tell they just loved their job. now what i loved the most about this hospital was the nicu. those nurses truly love their jobs and it shows. they were nurses to my babies and therapists for me. having nicu babies is scary for any mom, but these nurses made my nicu stay very enjoyable. every nurse always took a little time out of their shift to sit and talk with me. they would ask me about my situation, how i'm doing, ask about my life, my interests, etc. i created some very strong bonds with these nurse and it made it so much easier when i was discharged and had to leave my babies with these amazing people. i would like to thank elizabeth, cyndi, jill, linda, amanda, heidi, sharon, and aja for everything you did to help me and my babies. this is one great hospital!!!

had surgery a month ago. it was scheduled prior to the pandemic and was worried it would have to be postponed. was able to have the surgery as planned.  very grateful to the staff that cared for me prior to and post operation. they were attentive to my needs and answered my questions regarding my recovery. even received a letter a week later signed by all the staff.  sincere thank you to all the dedicated professionals that are working to take care of everyone during this stressful time in our history.

had two of my children born here. both times my experience was fantastic. the nurses were some of the nicest,  kind and patient people i've ever met that parked in the medical field. the room where our baby was born was large, unlike with my first child at another hospital where the room was tiny. 

they also let the dads get involved in the birthing experience. and actually give dads respect, another experience i did not have when my first kid was born elsewhere.

the only thing i could say is a negative, something that's not really an issue, is how tiny their cafeteria is and few selection. this however would be more nitpicking on my part, so i don't hold that against them.

do not choose this hospital if you want compassion and people who really care. the nurses are unprofessional and uncaring, impersonal and rude. my mother's iv was unplugged for who knows how long, more than once, there was blood on the sheets and her gown, the nurse lied and said it was just a little bit of blood. in addition, she had hip surgery, was placed in a chair, with no one to assist but my sister who is not strong enough to hold my mother from falling. the nurse said my sister would
be the responsible person in the room to help my mother. we will never go back to this hospital.

i visited the er for chest pain tonight. i drove myself as i didn't want to waste time waiting for an ambulance. once inside, their focus was on the fake flu, not a possible heart attack! then i was told to "have a seat". note that i didn't see any other patients... just employees, casually talking amongst themselves.
after about 20 minutes i returned to the window and requested they give me my id back because i was leaving! they refused! then someone finally came out and took me into the screening room. again, i asked for my id... "nope". about ten minutes later they did an ekg.
about 30 minutes later another nurse came in to take me to x-ray. i asked her for my id and she said "we will be back in about two minutes, i'll get it for you then." which she did. by then i was feeling much better (on my own) so i continued to wait.
then i sat for another 10-15 minutes in the waiting room inside.
a nurse came up and wanted to start an iv, by this time i was feeling much better and thought i could make it to a better hospital. i asked to talk to a doctor first... because i was considering walking out. 
she took me to a room in the er, where i waited alone for almost 2 hours! i never saw a doctor!
during my long wait, i was able to observe about 6-10 staff members in the nurses station. none doing much other than chatting amongst themselves and snacking. they were wearing masks... but not on their faces!
since i was alone, and personally believe this current flu ordeal is 100% political, i too removed my mask.
shorty after someone came in to update my payment info. as they entered i put my mask on. for their comfort, not mine!
shortly after a very rude woman, staff member, came in and ordered that i was to wear a mask the entire time i was there!
i told her that if it's really that important, she should tell the 6-10 employees to put theirs on! she ignored me!
after finishing up with my personal info, i asked who that rude woman was... apparently just a secretary of some sort!
i told them i was leaving, & walked out! 
on my way to another hospital, i instructed my son to hire a lawyer if i had medical issues on my way to a safer hospital. he promised he would.
fortunately for the rude secretary, the incompetent staff and the hospital, nothing bad happened. i won't be returning!
if they are foolish enough to send me a bill... we will be going to court!

coca cola for someone getting out of surgery?????? after being discharged he started complaining about his right arm going numb. so i called the paramedics to rule out a possible stroke, they weren't sure and told me to go back to this hospital. once arrived at the er he was taken in fairly quickly. the nurse that came in to the room (brigitte?!) didn't introduce herself for one, took an ekg and dropped the heavy cables onto his crotch, when i told her to be careful she didn't even flinch (he had a vasectomy reversal so pain in groin) she then clipped the ekg on him. when she was done she just ripped them all off and left the stickers hangin on his body. she then came back a bit latter to take his blood samples. she didnt wear gloves, as she was opening the sterile packages needles and shots were in. she touched her hair and then touched the shots again. before she drew blood she put on her gloves last minute. again left the room without a word. later i called the nurse to help me get him to a rest room (he had a hard time walking and ways 170pounds) she came in and said "the restroom is right there". no wheelchair and not a care in the world. so i (130 pounds) helped him up and carried him to the restroom. this is at 2am. they then admitted him over night to keep an eye and run some test. told me to leave, i couldn't stay with him. the cafeteria is serving fast food, coca cola products, chips and ice cream. they have nothing healthy. what in the actual fuck is going on here???? my husband was taken by ambulance to abrazo arrowhead just before the outbreak thank goodness because he had pneumonia. he's also diabetic. do they not have a nutritionist on staff. for lunch he was served spaghetti. if you know anything about a diabetics diet they can only have a few carbs per day. spaghetti is loaded with carbs. when he was at home his blood tests were around 104 which is excellent and doesn't require him to take additional insulin. his dr had told him in october because his numbers were so good he only needed to test his blood once per week. at abrazo they had to check his blood four times per day and give him insulin everyday because his numbers were well over 150. they didn't have a menu with diabetic food to choose from. it took me three attempts to get his nurse to come to his room so i could get an update. that was a waste of time. not one medical personnel had written anything in his chart. it was blank!!! one cna was very nice. she would let himself hold onto the iv and use a cane during the day to use the bathroom. the next day a new cna would not take the alarm off but when he would call for assistance no one would come. so he started to get up but the cane fell. he was still sitting on the side of the bed. when the cna came because of the alarm she was yelling at him so loud and she grabbed his cane and wouldn't let him use it. she was screaming so loud at him that immediately there were five additional staff in his room. there was a student dr who wanted to let him walk the short distance to the bathroom but he apparently didn't have the authority but he obviously saw how ridiculous the situation was. he was perfectly capable to take the five steps to the bathroom. then  this same cna who didn't respond to his request in the first place responded by yelling at him. she would not close the bathroom door until he was sitting down on the toilet. he was capable of standing. they didn't give him a shower each day and because he couldn't get out of bed to use the bathroom they ended up spending whole lot more time changing his sheets and gown. i know the staff get busy but i have been hospitalized at a different hospital and i couldn't get out of bed ever by myself but when i called for help someone was there within five minutes. when he was being released i asked his nurse if the pneumonia was in both lungs and where it was located. the location makes a huge difference to their recovery. again she looked at his and i received the exact same words every time i asked her a question which was i don't know. i'm sure their bill will be huge. that's what they cared about was how much they could charge but little about quality time with him and showing respect to him as a patient. i will do everything in my power to never have an ambulance go to any abrazo facility.

i don't like leaving a bad review during a time like this, when things are frustrating and stressful for all of us, let alone hospital staff at the front lines of a pandemic. but whatever your personal feelings about a patient are, nurses in the er at the nurses' station shouldn't make fun of and mock their patients for ten minutes where they can hear every single word while receiving no care whatsoever. one nurse, the one making most of the comments, put the tv remote on my lap (no tv in the room that i saw) instead of the call button as well when i was not yet in a position to find it myself. regardless of whether you believe i am experiencing an emergency (it obviously feels like one to me or i would never be in the er), to make fun of a condition i was born with and am waiting to hear if i need neurosurgery for is also disheartening. this was a crushing experience for me. thank you to the nurse who actually looked after me today, who is extremely nice and compassionate and wished me well with my neurosurgery appointment. i hope all of you stay healthy and safe, but that some learn kindness from others and that words matter.

overall, i do recommend this adventhealth hospitals  for your medical needs. now, to recover and change the way i eat!

review: i went to this er on 3/15/20 @ about 7pm with what i thought was a 5 day migraine that wouldn't go away. it was different from my normal migraine though and had me concerned and i told the doctor this. he did a cat scan without die and the doctor was convinced he seen something even though radiologist said it was normal. the dr insisted something showed and said it would not be safe to send me home. (he took the time to call and constult on call neurologist at other hospitals) i was transferred by ambulance to a main hospital where an mri and ct with contrast, and liver ultrasound was done (my liver enzymes were high also). turned out i had a dissection of the left vertebral artery, this doctor taking me and my symptoms seriously most likely saved me from a stroke and possibly saved my life. the nurse on the other hand was belittling the doctor, rolling his eyes, when the doctor took what i said seriously. i felt like he treated me like i was there seeking pain medication because i didn't fit into the normal response of pain meds (he was shocked what they gave me didn't just knock me out.) i have chronic migraines, i have a high tolerance, and i avoid going to er because of being treated this way. the nurse almost had me convinced to just go home, still in pain (he even tried to scare me and tell me the main hospital would immediately do a spinal tap, if i chose to be transferred, and told me it was a lot of phone calls for him to get me transportation, to make sure i wanted to go) but i chose to go with my gut and with the doctor who insisted it wouldn't be safe for me to go home. i was in main hospital for 2 nights and sent home on blood thinners to avoid a stroke. so to the doctor that took me seriously and possibly saved my life, thank you. i hope the nurse learns to not make judgments that can risk a patients life.

tl;dr:  mt sinai's er doctors refused to provide me with care for excruciating pain and as a result i nearly lost my life to sepsis. months after this experience, i finally have the presence of mind to post this review as a warning to others.

i visited this er at the urging of my doctor, who is affiliated with mt sinai. he feared that i might have an infection in my spine and wanted me to have some imaging and blood tests done because they didn't feel it could wait until the next week. my partner drove me to the er and we were seen very quickly - it was very quiet and we could only see 3 or 4 patients with relatively mild issues. we met with a resident, erik sherman, who did not listen to my situation at all, saying flatly that there wasn't much they could do for back pain. we asked again for an mri and the resident said "well, mris are very expensive and you might be waiting for hours," and my partner replied that our insurance would absolutely cover it and that we were fine with waiting as long as needed. 

my partner asked to speak with the attending, bess storch, and we again explained the entire situation and serious concerns our doctor had that led him to us to the er. dr. storch repeated that they were unable to do imaging and that i should follow up next week because this was "an in-office case."when she left the room, my husband called my doctor's answering service, yelled for the attending to come back, and he handed her his phone and begged her to speak with him. my doctor confirmed everything we had told them, and asked for the same tests we had asked for. begrudgingly, the attending allowed me to have an x-ray only.

we waited for a few hours for the x-ray and by the time they wheeled me back (i couldn't walk) a nurse came and said they had already discharged me. we waited for another 2 + hours and then we were handed the imaging report, which showed that i had a compression fracture on one of the vertebrae in my upper back. they said it was common and not a concern so we just left, completely demoralized and just happy to be out of there after more than 8 hours. a few days later, i was taken to another er by ambulance and was diagnosed with sepsis caused by a severe infection and an abscess that was pushing against my spine so hard that it caused a fracture. i needed emergency surgery and i spent months recovering inpatient. if mt sinai's er doctors had just listened to us and run tests, we might have known about the abscess sooner and my life would not have been put in extreme jeopardy. i nearly died. you should all be ashamed to call yourselves doctors.

i looked at her crazy and said no he doesn't need to know, that's my business. and she's like are you sure he's worried about everything else. now my dad is looking at me like what else. i said nothing bad stuff that no one need to know. and jane blurs out my positive substance!!!! now i'm am an adult! i'm not under 18! and i know that personal business is not allowed to be spoken about if the patient says no! so for jane to do that it was sooooooo wrong! i bit my tongue not to disrespect this elder lady and not have my dad be even more mad at me. so we left and i paid. with no insurance the same girl tells me there's a discount today if you pay in full $2000 i said okay and what is it if i do payments she said $9000. so i did the $2000. which i don't think i should've paid either because now it's the next day i woke up with my throat closing!!! they discharged me too early and now i have to go to a different er. so i should get my money $2000 back.

review: stay as far away from this place as possible. everyone here is rude. i dropped my grandma off earlier and immediately the receptionist alejandra was annoyed because i came in to ask what to do. my grandma needed help out of the car and the receptionist looked at me like i was stupid because i said i was there to check my grandma in. this is the second time i have been to this hospital and both times neither receptionist greeted me and they both looked like they don't want to work there. i took my grandma in because her entire left arm was in severe pain, she couldn't walk, or move her neck. while in the room they took her vitals and that was all. they sent her on her way with a little bit of pain meds. my grandma had to ask the nurse multiple times to look her in the face while talking because she is hard of hearing. the doctor didn't care to listen to anything she said and wanted to get to her other patients. when i went to pick my grandma up they wheeled her to the waiting room and she was in tears. she was crying because how horrible she was treated in there. it makes sense because when i spoke to the nurse who wheeled her out, i questioned why they chose not to give her a ct scan or mri (their website states they do both) they said she doesn't need it. i made sure to inform them my grandma has lost teeth recently and that her mouth has been in pain and that maybe she could have infections in her mouth and maybe it was spreading to her brain or her body according to the stuff that i have read online. she said my grandma never mentioned any problems with her mouth and then she said she doesn't have any abscesses in her mouth. took me by surprise because she said my grandma never mentioned her mouth. i asked her if the doctor actually looked into her mouth and she said yes. i asked her what happened if she has an infection in her brain from it, they need to do an mri. that nurse left and grabbed another nurse. this other nurse she had blonde hair, bright blue eyes, and her nose was red( she looked sick) maybe that's why she didn't want to talk to me, she comes out and asks what we needed. i explained that nothing was done for my grandma and we are concerned. the discharge paper she sent home states if she is in severe pain, has neck pain, can't move her body or parts of her body, has headaches to get help right away. all that fits my grandma. when i asked the nurse why they are sending her home without doing an mri or anything she said that description is only if you are having a stroke. i am not a medical professional but, your paperwork is telling me to get help right away and you are sending me away. as i was speaking, the blonde lady was looking at the floor with a smirk on her face. i looked at her and said "i can tell you find me annoying, but i am trying to get help for my grandma." who by the way was still in tears. she looked at me and said i can multitask. i didn't know when you are speaking with a patient about concerns that that requires multitasking capabilities. my grandma asked the nurse what happens if she has a clogged artery in her neck that is building up and we won't know because they are refusing to do any imaging. the nurse ignored her question and said the doctor has cleared her of any emergencies. i don't see how they cleared her of a possible clogged artery by taking her blood pressure. i asked who the hospital manager was and she said she is the only nurse there. i asked her again who the office manager was and she said she doesn't know and i asked who i can file a complaint with, she gave me a business card for the billing department. i am not sure what good that is going to do but it definitely shows how uneducated they are here. you don't know who you report to or how to get information. they lack compassion and respect at this hospital. they sent my grandma out without anyone's help in a wheel chair knowing i needed help getting her into the car. they are there to get a paycheck and that is all. your loved ones will not be cared for here.

on sunday the emergency room took a culture. most cultures are ready in 48 hours. it can take up to 72 hours. 96 hours later the results are not available. on sunday early afternoon an mri was performed. the technician could not tell me what he sees, there is protocols restricting that. later that evening i asked the nurse to follow up with getting the pictures read. nurse contacted the dr on duty but she could not read the results because, and i quote, the doctor is on her boat. on monday night, after the podiatrist had done some small surgery on my foot i could not sleep. i asked for something to help. i was given ambien. an hour later the nurse woke me up to ask if it was working. that was at 11:30 pm. at 4:00 am the lights all came on in the room and the garbage cans were emptied. at 5:00 am all the lights came on so they could take my "room mates" vitals. i was still waiting for the results of the culture. my questions led me to believe that i would not get the results any time soon. there is a current pandemic. a hospital at hospital rates was not a good place to wait. i told them i was going to go home. my foot had a new open wound, i asked them to please dress it so i could leave, the hospital staff refused. i found some bandages in the room and dressed it myself. i then hobbled my way to the entrance to leave. they refused to help me. it was like dealing with a group of spiteful children. i and my doctor have been working for two days to get the culture results so the correct antibiotic can be identified to cure my ailment. neither of us can get anything from the hospital. there is no provision for patient advocacy. the last thing i heard is, " we have 24 hours to respond to you" not likely but if i have cellulitis as suspected it could get into my blood stream, my bones, vital organs or brain.

review: my mom came by ambulance to the er and was admitted fairly quickly. she has received the best care from some great doctors and nurses. with the covid-19 virus causing havoc everywhere, i know these folks are being stretched to the limit but they are not showing it. everyone has been so kind and helpful. god bless you all.

i only come here because my surgeon is a real keeper.  things started off well enough.  i came in with a bowel perforation and was in horrific pain.  ironically, i had a shoulder injury during the procedure that perforated my bowels.  my shoulder injury has been ignored completely 9 hours into my er visit.  it took several hours to get my first dose of pain meds, despite my overtly obvious pain.  the second dose took 6 calls to the desk and 3 hours to get.  the nurse was mia about 4 consecutive hours.  i was crying out in pain for several hours and no one ever checked on me despite my update i made with each call to the desk (this is my 6th call over 3 hour period and no one has checked on me yet...... my pain is a 10/10." finally the nurse came to see me- without an apology or an explanation. i had been told earlier that they were ready to do my ct scan, but that was before the 4 hour hiatus.  the surgeon was on standby pending results of the ct, in the event i needed emergent surgery.  at 3-4am, i was so frustrated that i stepped outside my room to glare disapprovingly at a group of emt's and nurses hanging out in the back hall by my room cackling and cutting up very loudly.  when my glare yielded no response, i went back out there to tell them their loud behavior was incredibly rude and disrespectful to the sick patients.  that finally quietened them done.  i should not have to go scold the staff for their very obnoxious and unprofessional behavior.  these situations are not isolated events.  the nursing care has been very unprofessional and disrespectful since i started coming here over two years ago.  i spent 5 weeks in the icu here earlier this year.  i've spent almost 12 weeks in icu over the last two years.  i'm a nurse myself.  i expect to be treated respectfully with compassion every visit.  unfortunately, excellence is never the standard of care here.

i'm currently writing this in the recovery room, having just delivered my second baby (first one with el camino, first was with ucsf in the city). i just wanted to use this moment to rave about my experience this time around compared to ucsf.

from triage to l&d to recovery, all the doctors and nurses here are by far the most experienced, kind, knowledgeable and kind people i have ever met. due to covid i never got a chance to do a hospital tour, so i had no idea what to expect when i checked in 2 nights ago after laboring for 24h at home.

at triage i was greeted by nurse melissa, who checked me and i hadn't progressed enough to be admitted. instead of just sending me home, she asked me to walk the hallway for 1h to see if it'll speed things up. and it did, i went from 3cm to 5cm during that hour and was admitted right after.

the rest of the nursing team were all super pleasant, knowledgeable and explained every little thing to me without me having to ask. there's a really positive energy and rapport between the nurses so it carries through the whole bedside manner. my iv drip at ucsf last time was a traumatic experience, they couldn't find my vein and blood kept spurting everywhere. this time at el camino, they had a nurse who specialized in iv insertion and she did it painlessly and perfectly in one to without any blood. 

i knew i wanted an epidural this time, and instead of dictating to me when i should get it, they told me to tell them whenever i wanted it. i decided to walk for another hour before asking for the epidural. now let's talk a bit about the epidural. i had dr. k (forget the full name) and he was so good. no pain, super calm, and the meds took effect almost immediately. with ucsf i was in so much pain and the injection didn't even work the first time, i had to wait 2h for the anesthesiologist to come back to up my dosage. this time, the dosage was perfect because i had no pain but eventually i could feel the pressure as i was nearing 10cm. i could move my legs and could feel the pressure of contractions so my pushing was super effective. i'm told this is the perfect dosage and that the doctor is really good.

now onto the pushing phase. at ucsf (since it's a teaching hospital) there were 10+ people in the room while i was pushing. some were helping while others were just spectating. this time, i had one nurse stay with me the whole time helping me push, and once it got to a certain point she called my ob and she came and took it to the finish line. hardly tore, got 2 stitches and no hemorrhages. i tore second degree and hemorrhaged pretty badly with my first.

once baby was here, they moved us to the mother & baby section. since the epidural wore off rather quickly i was able to pee way faster than with my first, and the nurses in recovery were all super nice and accommodating. i also had a fabulous lactation consultant help me with breastfeeding, who really gave me the most helpful pointers that i never got with my first. when i was at ucsf with my first, i had a lot of pain in latching and the lc there told me that nothing was wrong and a "little" pain is normal. basically made me feel like a wuss. turned out my firstborn had a tongue tie and lip tie but i didn't get that diagnosed til she was already 3mo. of course by then my breastfeeding journey was already a hot mess and did not go well at all. the lc at el camino (stacey was her name) took her time to teach me how to latch and basically said that proper breastfeeding should never hurt. after 30min of training i was able to find a good latch and now my baby is breastfeeding really well. night and day.

anyways, i just wanted to take the time to give credit to an incredible group of staff. it's seriously night and day to my experience at ucsf and i wouldn't have known unless i had something to compare against.

beaware and demand to see all lab results and question everything as er doctors like dr. reyes are not trustworthy!!!   as a 3rd generation "redlander" that was born at redlands community hospital and who has defended it many times when i have heard people say. "if you need more than a band-aid don't go there,"  i am saddened to write this review but feel it is important so that others are not victim to having to pay double co-payments when they should have never been released but they trusted what the doctor told them.  the only reason i give it 2 stars is because the nurses and staff at the er were kind and helpful.  i learned the hard way to challenge what a doctor tells you and never leave until you physically see your lab reports, as dr. reyes convinced my family and i that i should be fine and even though i still had many of the symptoms and pain that i came in with. but dr. reyes told me "as long as i was not vomiting i would be ok."  i should have never been discharged with lab levels 8 times the normal range (the doctor never told me the number - not sure even if she had the complete report when she released me).  it should have been quite obvious to an er physician that the lab results grossly indicated a severe, aggressive, and active infection when in reality my parents and i were not told anything besides, "you have some form of stomach issue and your labs seem a little wonky," by dr. sonia-maria reyes.  great medical vocab don't you think?   eight times the normal level  is anything besides a "little wonky" especially after telling her that my symptoms had gotten progressively worse over the previous 48 hour period and i was worried as i was leaving for college in less than12 days.  not being a doctor, and never being told just how "wonky" my lab results really were, i unfortunately trusted the doctor and followed the doctor's directive to go home not knowing any other option and not realizing i could object and that she was just "practicing" medicine.  if i had not been discharged and would have been admitted and started on iv antibiotics that day, i am certain that i would not have had to suffer another two days at home hoping that what the er doctor prescribed was going to eventually help, when in fact it did not and i was back at the er on 2 days later, to then be admitted and be charged yet again!  it was my primary doctor's office that called my mom to check on me on monday and was appalled that i was sent home with the lab results that they saw.  my primary called and talked to the head of the er and i was told to immediately return to rch to be admitted and stayed for 2  1/2 days on multiple iv doses of antibiotics.   i had no problem having to pay my $575 co-pay from when i was admitted but then i received another bill for my first er co-pay another $250 which would not have had to be paid if i was admitted the first day as i should have been.  
 i sent my bill and concern to rch's appeals process and never heard back so i resubmitted it.  i actually received a letter this time but it stated that i still have to pay it because "both my parents and i were made aware of discharge plan."  it would have never happened if i or my parents were made aware of my actual lab results so again i urge everyone to challenge everything the doctor tells you, have them show you proof and do your research before you let them kick you out - i now understand why medicare now institutes the "hospital readmission reduction program" that does not pay the hospital for discharges that had a readmission within 30 days.  maybe all insurance companies should look into that for all age patients to protect them too!  i hope rch will reconsider and reimburse me for the additional $250 that i should not have had to pay, but regardless, i will never just believe an er doctor again - i will sit in that bed until i physically see all of the results and take time to look things up as they are many reports online about similar lab results that i had and even some that were less than mine where patients were not discharged!  you have been warned - be your own advocate for sure!!!

the bedside manner is nonexistent and the nurses don't care if you get your pain pills there was several times my father was two hours late and crying in pain and not a nurse in sight. every nurse that works on the floor should be absolutely ashamed of themselves and should be forced to go back to nursing school because clearly they didn't learn a goddamn thing. sorry excuse for a hospital, sorry excuse for nurses. i could go on but i think you get the gist.

baptist please read this and fix this problem. start with the staff in the call center who don't even know how to communicate properly when you call. they belittle you and could care less that you are being billed thousands of dollars incorrectly. this is a serious issue and needs to resolved.

if i could, i would put negative stars. i'd go to a vet before i'd go to baptist main on kendall drive! 
     saturday march 28th my boyfriend noticed (when he woke up) that i seemed confused, was slurring my words, talking strangely, and appeared off balance ( previous stroke in my history). also had radiating chest pain and a blood producing cough. i have tons of health issues so he was pretty concerned.
      we went to baptist urgent care at 137th and 152nd street. everyone at this facility was wonderful! i was triaged and sped into a treatment area very quickly, and saw the doctor within 10 minutes. ekg, blood work, iv in place, tested for flu/ covid19, and evaluated amazingly fast. the doctor decided i needed to go to baptist main on kendall drive. we chose the expediency of driving there. i was still a little out of it, so my boyfriend was providing most of the info. the caregivers at urgent care kept him away from everyone, but close enough to answer questions.
      when we got to the main hospital, things just went downhill. we pulled up to the door and a nurse told him to just drop me off and they would call him. we tried to convey the reasoning for him to remain but were ignored. an orderly came with a wheelchair and asked why i was there. i tried to explain, but he said " really? cause you look fine!". 
     registered at the desk and was put in a room. guy from registration came in to get my info and for me to sign consent. i was wearing a mask the whole day up to this time. not one person at this point had one on. the registration gentleman brought over my papers to sign, and began flipping the various forms for me by licking his finger! no wonder there's have been confirmed cases at this hospital! 
     then, doctor micheal mai came in, he was masked and gloved.  but as soon as he spoke, i knew nothing was going to get better. i called my boy friend as planned, so he could voice his observations. we were both talked over, the symptoms down played, and he too said "you don't look sick now, though." we were both adamant that this wasn't something to brush off with all of my health problems. in an exasperated tone, we were told " to make us happy he'd run every test under the sun" . when he left my room, he began talking in an extremely loud voice and said ( there were other patients in the rooms on that hall) '" we'll run everything, to rule out the nothing that's wrong with her". 
     at that point i called the nurse (yiska) and asked for ama papers. the nurse also said i looked and sounded fine. three doctors! how lucky was i? i signed the papers and left. 
     to add insult to injury, security and the nurses at the door refused to give me the patient advocate number without explaining to them why i felt i needed it. 
     i've never been treated like a  hypochondriac, especially since they knew nothing about my medical history. total disregard for me as a patient with those inherent rights you hear about totally ignored, as well as contempt when a snap decision on their part was contested. i will assure you, not only will i and my loved ones never patronize this hospital, but i will be posting on social media and  by word of mouth how horribly i was treated. never again.

the er, with breathtaking negligence, almost killed me. i'd wanted to write the administration at the time but was experiencing a major illness so could not. another recent reviewer stated the er's decline has been recent but no, this happened back in mid august 2014, so it's been going on a long time. so im writing yelp, at this point im sure the administration is well aware of their own problems, my letter i'm confident would have fallen on deaf ears anyway 

   i had a large tablet lodge in my throat at home when i tried to swallow it, and barely had an airway. it was like trying to breathe through a coffee swizzle stick.  i was losing oxygen, and seeing glimmering floaters in my vision and couldn't feel my fingertips. and was starting to pass out. luckily i am an rn myself and am very good at handling emergency situations, and through the grace of god, managed to keep a cool head. 

  i knew i didn't have time to wait for an ambulance, and after failed self heimlich attempts, signaled my friend with my hands to grab her car to drive me directly to the er. as i was reflexively trying to cough and breathe, the tablet shifted to a spot where it completely blocked my airway, and i fell to all fours and almost passed out in the driveway. luckily it shifted back to the "swizzle stick" position, but then just continued to alternate between swizzle stick and complete obstruction. 

  "fortunately " i made it to the er. my friend drove straight up to the front of the building and burst through the doors with me in tow, explaining that i was choking and didn't have an airway. 

   i was handed a clipboard, "please fill out this paperwork (asking for name, address, insurance info etc)."  i desperately wrote "cant breathe - pill" in jagged, panicked handwriting and pointed (as in "please let me go there") to the er patient area behind her.  "no, we can't help you until you fill out the paperwork."

  at this point an rn walked behind the desk, and i showed him my note, and pointed to the door that lead into the patient area with the most imploring look of my life, and he begrudgingly let me in. 

  he told me he was going to take me to a room and let me wait there.  afraid to be left alone and knowing i needed immediate attention or could die, i grabbed his upper arm. i didn't think it was too tight, just really really scared and urgent. he immediately spun on his heels and reprimanded me like a 4 yr old, "no no no! do not touch me like that, or i won't be able to help you. you are still breathing mam, you can wait until we're ready for you." 

  i tried one more note in the presence of an aide, who looked at me pie eyed because he got what was happening. but he was too low on the totem pole, and his own attempt to say anything to the additional nursing staff outside was ineffective, and i was left alone. 

  realizing that the only thing that was going to get them to respond was my impending cyanotic collapse, i decided to try and help my own self one last time (because even at that point, by the time they perked up and eventually intubated me - if they could even handle that - i would have sustained permanent anoxic brain damage, if i survived it at all). all by myself, i found an empty gurney. the guard rails were at a better height apparently than the chair i used at home, and after another round of heimlich attempts, the tablet flew out (along with blood - the tablet was a prescribed digestive enzyme, and after such an extended amount of time, had started to dissolve and "digest" my throat). 

  their response still blows my mind. day 1 of nursing school, we're taught our "abc's", where "a" stands for "airway", the number one thing in need of protection to keep someone alive. for pete's sake, 16 yr old lifeguards are taught this. 

   shaken, the anger now starting to kick in now that i wasn't wholly absorbed with saving my own life, i walked straight back out of the double doors.  "i'm leaving now, it's out - thanks for nothing!!!!" as the nurses' station, full of qualified staff standing behind the counters doing god knows what, looked back at me with slightly confused but mainly empty, "just another day" stares. 

   i shudder at the number of people that must have died at this er's hands. i think of all the poor family members who have been told, "i'm sorry, we did all we could."  so i'm writing this yelp review to let you know - they didn't.  avoid this er at all costs.

*** edit: in case this makes a difference, i did also write in my note to the multiple staff "airway obstructing". i couldn't have been any clearer. from one er rn to another, what was happening was virtually mapped out to them in written form, since they couldn't see, or refused to see, what was happening in front of their own eyes

review: the new chief nursing officer is the best!!! etiosa uwumarogie is the right guy to run this facility and he is doing an exceptional job!

it's hard to put an exact star rating. every medical facility has its good and bad. but my two stars are a reflection that if i had time on my side and another choice of a medical provider, would i choose dominican? no. why?

my mom was rushed here. while the er care got my mom forwarded to icu where she belonged, they didn't explain to my sister what a dnr was. my sister was hysterical and passed over the care to me. i lifted the dnr because we didn't know yet what was going on and she deserved to be revived (if she coded) and time to be diagnosed.they need to explain legal definitions to people when they are making these kind of decisions.

the icu was a dream team. every single one of her nurses, if we weren't in a pandemic where i can't go in the hospital, i'd give them all hugs for their a+ care and compassion. dr. singh soon became my favorite doctor ever. he got to know who my mom is. he listened. he respected us. he's the guy you'd trust with your life because he's trustworthy by going above and beyond with earning it.  even specialist that we interacted with in the icu was just top notch. 

so why the low rating? once we had her moved to telemetry, the hospitalist was abusive screaming at me instead of giving facts or letting me check with the experts that i needed to verify risk versus reward in what was being requested. i fired her. then i got the grim reaper dr. binesh. he spoke fatalistically and pushed hospice on us when we didn't have a terminal diagnosis. when we said we didn't want it, he also sped up discharge to less than 24 hours but notified us on a saturday evening when we couldn't get in home care set up because it was after business hours. i had expressed to them that my mom's wishes was after she was stable enough, her transition goal was to be cared for at home. when my mom was able to talk she told the doctor that she wanted to go home as her next step. so why weren't they helping us?

hospice would get preferential treatment with a magic extension to allow her to stay in the hospital if they took the case,  but we weren't allowed to have an extension to set her up at home with a home health care company outside of hospice. without a terminal diagnosis, isn't that medicare fraud if you engage hospice? we didn't go that route because it wasn't applicable or part of our goal to let our mom go when she was still recovering and we didn't know what was going happen next.  

what happened felt unehtical and like medical blackmail. our only other option was to contest it with medicare and be on the hook for the bill for that time in the hospital past the premature discharge. so now she's in rehab (against her wishes but our best option under these circumstances) until we can get home health care set up because any money that we do have should be reserved for making her better, not fighting the grim reaper and his games.

this review is for the birthing center at sequoia hospital. like several other yelpers here, i too, had a wonderful experience delivering my baby at the birthing center a few weeks ago.

leading up to the birth, sequoia gave us all the information we needed. we attended a helpful orientation one month before the birth, and pre-registered ourselves so the hospital knew our due date and when to generally expect us. 

i began labor two days past due, and gave sequoia a call at 2am to let them know that i thought i was in labor. they were clear, calm, and provided instructions on coming to the hospital, where to park, etc. 

as soon as we got to the hospital, we were greeted and they had very short paperwork for me ready. after a few quick forms, they got me into a room and checked out a few things. once it was confirmed that i needed to stay, they got me settled into the room and we finished up the paperwork.

i'll spare readers my long birth story, but the major takeaways were-- sequoia has amazing nurses. literally, the best. i was at the hospital for a total of 96 hours and had several different nurses (they work in shifts of 12 hours each). each nurse was extremely well trained and highly competent in their respective area. i felt very well taken care of and appreciate that each nurse that clocked in took the time to read my birth plan and get familiar with my wishes. a special shout out to nurse ute who was my nurse during delivery. after a long and frustrating time laboring slowly, ute started her shift by instilling the confidence in me to have a baby that day. sure enough, my baby was delivered just as ute's shift was ending... and she stayed with me the whole time i was in labor.

sequoia also has fantastic doctors. my regular obgyn was out of the office during my delivery, but the other on-call doctors, dr. kassis (who delivered my baby and was super encouraging) and dr. rao, were absolutely fantastic. the anesthesiologist, dr. bradley, was also extremely skilled and delivered my epidural quickly and efficiently.

lastly, sequoia gave me everything i needed to take care of myself and my baby when i got home. as a first time mother, i had no idea what i needed to take care of myself. in the blur of labor, i didn't realize that sequoia had packed several bags of "after care" materials for me. it wasn't until i got home, i realized sequoia had given me everything i needed to heal at home.

thank you to all the nurses, doctors, cleaning staff, culinary staff, and others at sequoia for making this a memorable experience.

i had a negative experience at the er. i had never been to sequoia or used dignity health before, and *only* came here because it was the closest hospital near where i was. i came in with some of the most frightening symptoms of my entire life, that i had never experienced before, and that were horrifying. could not breathe. body was going numb. lightheaded and dizzy. felt like i was going to pass out. 

as soon as i got there, the doctor labeled me as an "anxiety" patient right away, upon my arrival, even before any tests were done. he even said things to me like "you are agitated and argumentative just like my other anxiety patients" all while i was frantic about not being able to breathe and was begging for help. i couldn't believe he called me those words; i was going through such an awful experience, he could have been more empathetic. the doctor seemed irritated that i was there, and discriminated against me using this label, as if having "anxiety" was my fault, that i could control what was happening to me, or as if these physical symptoms were not 100% real. 

so during my er visit they ran several blood tests and the doctor gave me ativan eventually. the ativan did help a little bit to calm me down, but my symptoms were still there (i had been having them for about a week). the doctor came in and was adamant that i had to see a psychiatrist. his tone in telling me this was condescending and rude. he made all of symptoms out to be a mental illness, and i 100% know that they are not. perhaps having these ongoing symptoms for an extended period of time resulted in anxiety, but this is not all due to anxiety. i was trying to explain my core symptoms to him - but he kept interrupting me. he treated me like i was not worthy of his time, like i was some sort of drug addict looking for pills (in this case just a human being looking for a diagnosis). 

the er doctor made it sound like i just hop around from er to er wasting everyone's time, even asking me "how many times have you been going to er's for your anxiety" and "when was the last time you went to the er for your anxiety" and trying to reprimand me and shame me for going to the er. well guess what, i don't regularly go to the er. i went one time recently, in the prior week, when all of this started, for similar symptoms. but that's it. and nobody at that time said anything about it being anxiety. they actually encouraged me to go back to the er if i didn't feel better...which is what i was doing! 

so bottom line i left the er after about an hour with the same underlying symptoms that i had and have been having for over a week now. it has been several days and i have the same symptoms 24/7 but they have gotten worse. i'm fatigued and out of breath. i can't even fold my laundry without taking naps every 10 minutes. i am very athletic and in shape but can barely walk without wheezing and gasping for air. 

i feel traumatized now that i was shamed for going to the er, and labeled and treated as an "anxiety patient". i know something is wrong with my body right now. i have a serious chronic health condition already, and i went through years of symptoms where doctors like this one labeled me as an anxiety patient. i was told that everything was anxiety. well, it wasn't. the doctor was quick to judge and overconfident in his diagnosis (after seeing me for such a short period of time). if its not a heart attack or a blood clot then...it's...anxiety? no, not in all cases.

the doctor that initially encouraged me to go to the er said to go to stanford. she never mentioned this hospital, even though it is closer to where i live. now i know why.

edit: i spoke with a psychiatrist who urged me to get medical attention. he said he could only prescribe me medication to calm me down as a result of my stress in having to deal with this, but my core symptoms are not due to anxiety. i am working with my doctor to figure out what this is. it could be gi related, heart related, or lung related. so, nope, not anxiety. it causes anxiety, but my severe ongoing shortness of breath from the last couple of weeks is due to something else. the er doctor at sequoia hospital refused to listen to or believe any of my symptoms. my doctor was pretty shocked when i told her what happened there.

i was instructed there was an atm in the hospital lobby so i reversed my car and parked. keep in mind that it's about 5:45am, the patient lobby is closed until 7am. i can see the atm from outside the locked doors; it's blue lit lettering taunting me. i am sleepy and i just want to go home, but no say the parking goblins. i am now sitting in my car awaiting the lobby opening. 

on a brighter note, there is a charger for electric vehicles right as you enter the garage. it takes cards. $2 for 1 hour charging on top of your parking fees. 

also, the closest open coffee place is a 10-15 minute walk. normally that'd be no big deal, but as i said, i came here to sleep. i have electrode goop in my hair. i'm not wearing a real bra. i'm donning birkenstocks with socks ala my romanian father-in-law. i'm foggy and attempting not to sleep in my car so i'm not sure questing for coffee in an area of the city i've never been in is wise. i didn't bring my sword so i could go link on any chickens i find and if you can't destroy things with a sword what's the point of a quest???

update: lobby opened promptly at 7 am. atm fee is $3.95. so all in all it cost me $3 with validated parking, $2 to charge my car while waiting for the atm to be accessible, and then $3.95 to withdraw $20 to fulfill my debt to the parking goblins. total: $8.95 and an hour and a half of my life i can never reclaim.  finally pulled up to the parking kiosk and paid, got my change and said thank you. goblin just blinked while furrowing at me. i expect this sort of bedside manner from doctors, unfortunately, but man, the goblin could have been polite back. i weep in sleep deprived silence as i drive home after nearly being hit by an elderly lady while trying to go turn into the parking lot for starbucks. huzzah. 

tldr: a+ for ruth @ the sleep clinic. parking goblins are no joke and will only accept antiquated currencies- cash or check only to leave the parking garage. i do not have any rubies or kiddos so i'm not sure if the goblins will accept shiny gems or a first born child as alternate payment.

i am once again very disappointed! i have an extensive and complicated medical history. i was admitted for abdominal pain and since have had unstable vital signs. no test other than labs have been done and based on that alone and despite vital signs being unstable and new symptoms the admitting doctor refuses to listen telling me i will just have to manage the symptoms on my own at home! one of my specialist even advised i seek treatment outside of the hospital. i am filing a formal complaint with the state of texas for the lack of actions by the physician. if you live in the brazos valley area and have a health issue i highly suggest you heads towards houston and seek real medical care. when i moved to the brazos valley area, medical care is the one big thing that disappoints me.

the staff at palm west is amazing. i am a first time mom. i brought my little bundle of joy into the world 06/18 at 11:10 am. it was honestly the best birthing experience making the experience empowering and everything i never thought i would have.  the staff was encouraging and positive every step of the way from l/d to discharge. i  was given so much information as a new parent without being overwhelming. they were attentive without intruding on my family getting to know each other. a comforting presence there to do a job but still show they care.  i was hesitant because no tour due to covid but after this experience i will be having every child there.

surgery went well with dr robertson. we appreciate the staff & anesthesiologist was really good, paranoid about covid but really great at his job!!! we understand because he is an older gentleman. dr badikkian (sp) 
sports injuries are worth it to head to tahoe, where people know what they are doing. 

thanks everyone!

thank you to everyone at the barton memorial emergency room!  i arrived father's day afternoon with a gash in my arm from a fall on rocks while hiking.  at least 8 people helped me and everyone was awesome - from check in to the doctor, many nurses, emt's, the guy that brought me my phone charger, they were all so kind - really friendly and nice people!  a great facility, very professional, don't hesitate to go if you need emergency room services!

i can't believed this hospital the staff is very rude and very lack of communication specially er staff. my mom went to er and i call the er and the nurse says she can't give information, and told her that i'm the daughter and she can ask or tell my mom if ok to give the information to me. and the nurse is very rude he hung up the phone..and called them again and said they can't give information . she said that my mom is an adult, i told them that i'm 75 miles away and very worried and want to talk to the dr that seen her, she said they're very busy. when my mom went home she said nobody told her that i called. what kind of staff they hired, most of people that i spoke to that they don't even want to go to that hospital because they don't know how to treat their customers . i can't even give a one star

this institute does pride itself on social justice. lies, bullies, and manipulation all in the name of self benefit. anything you have to say to anyone of importance will automatically fall of deaf ears. i do not at all recommend, i do not at all trust this facility.
i have been going to the imaging center for many years now and the staff is always great, the place always clean and the wait is never long. this is where i always prefer to go for my x-rays!
best er experience in all of brooklyn north. kind, caring and professional doctors and staff. in and out, efficient service.

review: sinus infection and allergies in the middle of covid-19 pandemic. i want to give a shout out to all my ed physicians especially dr abdoush for not only taking great care of the sick patients but also for looking out for hospital staff safety and well-being. i am very proud to be part of such a great team of physicians and healthcare workers all around. great job everyone. keep up the great work you do and be safe.

dr. abdoush and his team of nurses nerilyn, chris, and jasmin did a amazing job of taking care of me today. i came in with a dislodged shoulder and there were so patient and understanding with me. i was in a lot of pain and they all took there time understanding my needs. i didn't feel rushed at all. i'm so thankful that they gave me great care in the mist of corona virus. i was so scared about coming to the hospital but is was so clean, everyone had mask and gloves and i truly appreciate them helping me in my time of need. dr. abdoush even tried to make me feel comfortable and make me laugh i wasn't constantly thinking about my pain. thank you again gardena memorial!

fuck this hospital !! when my dad was missing memorial hospital didn't bother to contact me when my father was alive in a coma!! they had my father listed as homeless. he had an id with him and emergency contact in his wallet. he died in a different hospital. two months later i get a letter in the mail saying that my dad passed away. so please i don't recommend this hospital at all. this was two years ago!!

i don't even know how this hospital is still open, they don't care for patients or for their love ones. they are rude and disrespectful from the the doctors to the in charge nurses and as well as the administration of the hospital. my mother died at this hospital for careless people and on top of that they stole her credit cards and chain erased her phone completely who knows why and who authorized them to do such thing. this hospital needs to be shutdown or every needs to be replace because is not fair that we are trusting this people with our lives and lives of our love ones and they can't even take care of patients belongings. please don't come to this hospital.....

gardena memorial hospital is the worst hospital in l.a county. the staff is rude, unethical, and unprofessional. i feel bad for the people that live under the poverty line that have to endure this wicked facility. it's unsanitary and absolutely the worst hosptal i have ever recieved care from.
went in for an emergency, they are not taking cdc regulations for covid19 seriously. staff walking into  hospital without ppe or sterilizing hands upon entering. stay away.

if i could give them no stars i would. the front desk lady was nice and so was the first doctor that my son saw. we went in because he got a popcorn kernel stuck in his ear. the first doctor he saw agreed that that's what it was. she said it would need to be vacuumed out so i assumed they were going to do it. then a male doctor came in and was very rude. he said that all he saw was wax and that i didn't know what i was talking about. as he was checking he kept pushing it down into my sons ear. my son was screaming at this point and he looked at him and told him to "act his age". he said since i believed it was a popcorn kernel (which it was) that i needed to see a ent. we are leaving state wednesday so i asked if he could get us in somewhere asap. he said highly doubtful and was just plain rude. after he left the lady doctor came back in and i told her what was going on and what he said and she checked him again and confirmed that it was indeed a popcorn kernel! i am so disgusted with how he treated me and my son. in my opinion he has horrible bedside manner and shouldn't be allowed to treat people. he misdiagnosed my son and was the worst doctor we have ever seen. i will never return and i would advise others to go elsewhere.

the doctors are highly-qualified, caring, tireless, professionals, as are the nurses.  the facility is spacious, clean, & well maintained.  all of the elements are in place to be a 5 hospital, except for one, food service.

if left to its own autonomous rating, i'd give it 2's.  the preparation of meals is generally tasteless, tough, & so unimaginative in presentation as to think it's a high school culinary school with no experienced instructors.

my husband got a hernia surgery from dr. raposo and i couldn't be happier . he is such an amazing surgeon and human being . also nurse marcia and all the other nurses and team were amazing. i am very grateful . thank you

lack of professionalism. their security guards are scanning ids and then using their position for personal gain. roland cartier is one of them, a gentleman well into his 50s messaging me. i am appalled. utterly disgusted. i dragged my mother through the er doors, she was very ill and could not walk on her own, and this man has the audacity to message me during his shift to claim he knew me and i looked familiar, even though we had no mutual friends. i tried to file a complaint with their head of security and now mr. jim bullinger is not answering my calls. how ironic. i left hr a voicemail. no one is doing anything about my personal information being breached. no one is taking disciplinary actions against their disgusting security guards using their jobs for personal gain. not okay. if this hospital condones this behavior, their ethics need to be revised and the people need to think twice of going here.

my husband took my 14yr old daughter in because she has had chronic back pain and woke up in tears this particular morning. they got her into the er and she saw pa james calcut(she did not see a doctor.) he ordered an x-ray which came back normal. my husband and i both being in the medical field requested that an mri be done because we know the x-ray does not show everything that needs to be seen and this is a child so lets cover all the basis. mr. calcuts response was she does not meet the criteria and we only have one mri machine so if we get a stroke patient we will need it (you cant make this stuff up.) he then proceeded to ask my daughter if she was one her period because there was some blood in her urine, she said yes she was and he attributed the pain to that. my daughter spoke up and said i know its not that! mr. calcut looked at my husband and shook his head as to say she dosn't know what shes talking about! my daughter was discharged with a paper for chronic back pain really! the next business day she was taken to her pediatrician who ordered an mri! she has a herniated disc!!!!!!!!! i am so upset i wonder if she meets your criteria now! missed diagnosis that easily could have been prevented. unfortunately mr calcut did not listen to his patient! wondering what else he has missed. wish she could have seen an actual doctor (there is a doctors name all over the discharge paperwork though which is kind of weird since she never saw one.)

dr. h is a great doctor. tom our first nurse was awesome, made my daughter feel totally relaxed. then it went all down hill from there. the other nurses (if you could call them that) had one excuse after another why they neglected there patient, never checked in on them after there initial cont

i was checked in and prepped with in an hour or so for my mcl repair. i had my last surgery here about 5 years ago and had no issues. i encountered nothing but great people who kept me informed and comfortable during my brief stay. i was a little concerned about the surgery during this time of covid 19 so the the limit of operations and people allowed into the facility gave me some ease. all went well and was home in about 4 hours when all was said and done. thank you to the personnel who made me feel welcomed and safe.

i'm so disappointed that my loved one didn't get the help so desperately needed.  no medication tweaking, and very limited drinking water.  please don't expect that your love one to come out any different than when they went in.  everyone who i encountered inside of the facility seemed to have a chip on their shoulder.  i felt like no one was happy with their work.  my love one said that the doctor said that they should have never been there.  if that is true, why would a doctor say that to a patient?  why would they continue to keep them in the hospital if that was his assessment?  could it be that the insurance money was a factor in the decision to retain a patient?  do they really care?  it didn't seem like it at all.  my loved one was discharged, without a place to go, and told that they were placed on a waiting list, which wasn't true.  how could they think this was ok, especially in the midst of covid-19.

i am very disappointed in the care at this hospital, specifically the er. i went on a wednesday night with the worst pains i have ever had. after a short time, a doctor came to see me and asked what was wrong. i told him and included that my pain was a 10. it was close to shift change when the nurse came in. he tapped and felt for veins, but you could tell it was too late in the shift for him to want to deal with it. i'm a hard poke. he sent me to give a urine sample.

when i got back, i waited 10 minutes, then rang my button. a tech showed up, put in the iv line and said she'd tell my nurse i needed medicine. maybe 45 minutes go by and i'm crying and throwing up from pain. i rang my button again. a nurse came in and said she'd notify my nurse. i waited at least another 45 minutes when my nurse finally came in and gave me some nausea medication and pain medication. 

the ultrasound tech came and got me. she was the nicest person there. when the results came back, the doctor went over results including that i had sludge and multiple stones. also my liver enzymes were up and that was likely due to gallstones. then he sent me home. i went home with nausea medication and nothing else. he told me to follow up with my pcp and a surgeon. that was a task in its own!

when i left the er, i was stopped to pay my $200 copay. gotta make sure they get their money.

this was my second time at this er and i will never go back.

less than a week later i returned to the er, but went to providence novi because i knew the care would be better. with my elevations in my liver and pancreas, as well as the amount of stones i had, they said i should have never been sent home. even late at night i should have stayed and they could have called in a surgeon the next day. 

such bad care. it really makes me sad...

oh and i am giving 2 stars because of the ultra sound tech, the nurse who did my intake, and the cleanliness of the hospital. if it weren't for them, it'd be a 1 star.

review:
let me first say my inpatient experience for knee replacement was great. now the reason for 1 star and would give zero if available. the physical therapy rehab is the worst ever!! they have billed me and sent to collections for services not rendered!!  the quality of care is terrible and their incompetence extended my rehab at another qualified facility by 3 weeks.  on my 1st appt they did an eval that lasted 15 mins. walk 20 feet. sit on table take 1 measurement then asked did they give you exercises at discharge? answer yes. them "keep doing them". billed 1 hr and $505.  said comeback friday. (remember total knee replacement ). i show up 1 week to the day post op and they put me on a bike zero warmup nothing. tells me to start peddling and go all the way around!  don't make 1 revolution extreme pain feel ripping internally and pass out. where's therapist? 12-15' away not paying attention.  if you go here do at your own risk. pt is horrible management is worse. i have reported to state for falsifying medical records, incompetence, lack of proper equipment and more importantly billing for services not rendered ( federal crime).  keep coming st joes you're not getting paid, ins co investigating, feds will be knocking on door soon. run dont walk from this rehab center! tucson deserves better.

update 6-11-20. was contacted by a rep from hospital a week ago and they were "concerned about my experience and review" and was assured that i would be contacted. week later and zero communication other than another letter from collection company.  have now reported to state of az and to the joint commission (company that certifies hospitals)

visited my father here last summer, as he stayed overnight one night for observation. went to pour myself a cup of awful hospital coffee. so far, so good. pretty standard stuff. i pick up a styrofoam cup sitting atop the coffeemaker and pour. hot coffee cascades onto my short pants and tee shirt. wtf, i wonder. i look down. the styrofoam cup has a gaping hole in the bottom. wait, what? i bring this to the attention of staff: a woman tells me that staff deliberately keep such a cup around for some rubbish reason i've since forgotten. she admonishes me that this was my fault because i failed to peer into the bottom of the cup prior to pouring (because people always do that?). she and others laugh aloud at me. when i tell them i don't find this behavior mature, respectful, or amusing, they refused to apologize. i wouldn't be caught dead in this hospital.

first of all i cannot say they have the best customer service... tired to ask about covid test and someone had no idea  what i was talking about. them i talked to carol on customer service and was super rude when i was just asking questions about making an appointment for covid testing. had no interest in helping, short bitter then simply just hung up on me.

i have to leave a review to give you feedback on the services i received at st. joeseph's hospital. i had major surgery in november 2019. since it was planned, i was hoping that everything would go perfectly. admitting process went smoothly and the surgery was successful because i had a great surgeon, dr jerome steck. however, the management of my pain was not that successful. the nurses were not all that attentive and at times i had to wait 15-20 min when i rang the bell to get my pain relief. they wanted  to assist me going to the bathroom but after waiting 10 min for someone to come, i ended up going to the bathroom by myself. the food was dismal. i was not expecting gourmet  but they didn't even have an option for non-dairy milk. billing is also very poor. now, three months later, they are just getting some bills out to me that should have been taken care of long ago. so although i feel my surgery was successful, the nurses were overworked and not attentive and the billing department is very poorly orgainized.

went to the emergency room yesterday--was a little worried as i did not want to get covid--they did a very nice job of separating you at the entrance--no one can go in with you--while i was being cared for in the
non covid section everyone was so nice--many workers & i was not there long--happy how i was treated--thank you......

my elderly father was in there for non covid issues starting april 29th for 30 days. no visitors allowed.  communication with family was terrible.  he was there 30 days and we had one face time meeting the whole time.  at times we went days with no updates.  i called patient relations and left a message.  they never called me back. they discharged him to a rehab facility with less than 2 hours notice.  i cannot comment on the care he received because we were not allowed to visit.  but their communication during this time was awful up until the discharge with less than 2 hours notice.  still waiting for that call back from patients relations.  a joke!

this was the worst hospital experience of my life. got admitted to ob at 30 weeks pregnant for suspected appendecitis. was left on a bed in ob triage in pain with no one checking on me for 5 hours. had my call light on for a very long time before anyone bothered checking on me. i had to literally beg the nurse to find someone to transport me to the imaging department. loved the techs there! but again, no doctor would review my imaging results in ob until and i was left on a bed for another 4 hours. i almost walked out ama and only then did a doctor deign to review my results and decide the next steps. i am not delivering my child here when the time comes. i have never seen such neglect.

stay away! run fast!! go to st vincent or hendricks but do not go to methodist! they are a bunch of unorganized, sleep deprived, bitter people who hate their employer and they take it out on their patients. iu health is a horrible organization who treat their employees like garbage and it shows.

i recently was a patient in the pcu and have no complaints at all. at all times i was treated with kindness and respect. the nurses and lnas were professional and competent. 

happy to recommend concord hospital!

anita novak saved my life.  after being in multiple hospitals for my illness, anita gad me rushed to surgery where i had gone septic due to a perforated colon.  she saved me and is also the only person who cared about my terrible need for pain control. thank you anita!!

worse hospital ever 1st off doctor cooper kept telling me i had covid 19 which i don't i came in with lower abdominal pain which after 6 hours in pain she decides to give me a ct scan which shows issues in my female area. i saw my obgyn the next day i had a ultrasound done which they find a small tear in my uterus wall. 2nd again tested negative for the covid 19 at obgyn . doctor cooper needs to be more aware that i had no signs of the virus but kept consisting i had it. what if i'd had a appendicitis or rupturerd dappendix i would have died want on dr. cooper to get her shit together.

i was just in emergency and was treated extremely well along with the doctors and nurses they were knowledgeable and considerate to my needs.  stayed 2 days and the 2nd floor staff was awesome nurses go beyond caring and making you feel comfortable.  highly recommend this hospital.  everyone very professional and kind.

if you can avoid coming to this location, then please do. not only is the communication between staff and patient horrible, but wait time is horrible as well. had to come here twice only to get turned away and i don't live close. i will for sure be telling my doctor to refer me to a different location.

went to er. dr eric schnitzer was great professional, but the whole staff was very very rude unprofessional, the place was so dirty. would not recommend anyone to go there. if you need to go to a pih hospital definitely go to pih whittier.

my visit happened a couple of years ago but might still be helpful when making the decision to come to this er.
i came in with a lot of abdominal pain very similar to constipation pain. they took a ct of my intestines and saw no significant blockage. after a while, one of their male nurses came over and basically told me i was being a baby, to stop whining, that the ct scan showed nothing that would be causing the amount of pain i was displaying. some of the pain subsided with the meds they gave me and i finally went home after hours of being there.
about a couple weeks later the extreme pain came back. this time i tried pih in whittier. nurses there were a lot more kind, i felt like they actually cared to find out what was going on.
they decided to do an ultrasound of my uterus and found pretty big ovarian cysts, which would explain the pain i was having. 
i understand that a diagnosis like this sometimes takes time to rule out other causes first.. but my point is, nobody deserves to be talked to and belittled by nurses in this er like i did.

this is by far the worse hospital that i have known.
every employee hates his or her job. they all hate each other. how can you get a good care if the nurses are there to constantly write each other up and have cat fights ?
i have spoken to many of their doctors too , they are all miserable. they keep changing their jobs. upper management is as nasty as it can get.
so good luck getting a good care there and if you can't pay, the hospital will sue you!
