my son had a 103.7 fever and the next day it dropped to 95.1. for both visits to the emergency room the staff was very helpful! doctor austin was very informative!!! for a first time mommy he was patient with all of my questions and concerns of my 11 month old son!! thankfully my baby is back to normal and healthy. thank you to the 1:00-5:00 am staff! you guys are amazing, thank you for taking in my son with everything going on.

this review is for a specific er nurse named daniel gutierrez. he treats all his patients with the care, concern, and patience i can only imagine he would treat those he loves the most. he is a hero, an angel and breath of hope and comfort in the scary place that is any er. i thank him for making a very difficult, anxious, uncertain, worrisome experience the best it could possibly be.

while visiting lake martin community hospital may 19th, 2020 a monday afternoon with a toothache i found the facility to be clean..with a staff that was kind..quick..and very professional...thanks for making ne feel better..i appreciate you and your entire staff for all you are doing.

told to arrive at the hospital at 8:30 am for an 11:30 am procedure, in writhing abdominal pain and not given anything for it. still waiting for this procedure an hour later. not kept updated, have to ask for updates. best patient satisfaction scores my butt. rex patient advocates if you're reading this please contact me. this is unacceptable.

terrible place i will never go again i was forced to go here because my physician was on staff a surgeon and i was forced to go here from another hospital across town. emergency room staff are incompetent they can't even start an iv because they blew my vein twice after i specifically told them i was dehydrated. the head of mri at this facility is incompetent  because he would not allow me to have an mri scan completed without having my spinal stimulator removed from my back so my physician came removed it from my back and then he proceeded to tell my physician it mean that he had too many cases and could not perform the mri scan anymore after i'd already completed my surgery. so now i am being forced to go to another facility to have an mri scan completed because he refused to complete the mri scan even though i was already admitted into the hospital they're at memorial hermann medical center. no who wouldn't be upset about that? i will be reporting this all the way to the hospital administrator i'm very upset about this that i'm being forced to go to another facility to accommodate his lack of consideration. it's not my physicians fault nor my fault that he won't allow me to have my mri scan it's his fault that he wouldn't work me in the schedule and that's unacceptable and unethical. i will never go to this facility again

this place is terrible. avoid it if you can. the employees are slow, habitually rude, and uncooperative. their sign in the front has bullet holes and graffiti on it - if that gives you any indication of how it is inside. if that's what you see on the outside, just think of what level of care they provide where no one can see.

thank you so much nurse riza and all the staff i encountered today. i'm sorry i didn't see all your names. i felt so bad coming to the er at 4am especially during this covid 19 crisis. i was in distress and in so much pain i didn't think i could wait for urgent care to open. they treated me with kindness and compassion and gave me treatment that made my pain stop. i've had 2 children and many gallbladder attacks so i would not go if i didn't think it was serious and the pain i went through had me on my hands and knees crying and scared. thank you so much kaiser hospital for not making feel dramatic or like i was wasting resources or your time because i had so much guilt checking in. i appreciate you guys so much for being on the frontlines. may god bless you all and keep you safe from harms way.

i am a nurse practitioner who has never been to an er before in my entire life (well,as a patient at least)!! so best believe i really had to be in some pain to even come in, especially during a covid outbreak! i had some right sided pelvic pain that kept getting worse and finally started getting a fever and bad cva tenderness. worried i was developing pyelonephritis i presented to urgent care. they sent me to er to rule out appendicitis as well. had blood tests, ua, and ct scan all within half an hour and everyone was great!! very fast! and i loved how the kaiser app updated my labs immediately so i was able to review them myself lol! yep bad uti, and ovarian cysts! thank you urgent care and er for being very fast, nice, and thorough!

at 12:30am, i was desperate to see an ent during this pandemic- i had gotten the worst sinus infection of my entire life that has lasted months and called cedars thinking i'd be disappointed and still in pain like my last visit to the er but i was in such serious pain, i decided to try anyway. a couple weeks ago i had the same issue and went to usc verdugo hills by my house and i saw a doctor on a tablet, they addressed my problems vaguely with no concern for my actual pain and wanted me out as fast as possible. they didn't help me at all, didn't take my sinus infection seriously and basically laughed at my pain and offered me no help. that was not my experience here at cedars. when i got there, the people at the front were empathetic but obviously cautious during this time and gave me the necessary tests to keep everyone safe and make sure i didn't have corona virus before they concluded my sinus infection was just that and brought me to a bed where the doctors and nurses worked hard to figure out the issue, the resolution and gave me a prescription that works! a nasal spray that works! checked in on me frequently and provided me with the ability to breathe after weeks of headaches, ear aches and pressure that wouldn't stop, along with helping me even though i was drained from working all day, probably a little rude and desperate for a solution late at night. 

thank you to everyone who was there on monday, from the guy who answered the phone when i called crying to the lady who helped me check out at the very end and everyone in-between. thank you so much

a doctor allowed my mom to leave early when she went in the icu to the regular floor she wasn't ready to go to a rehabilitation center .!now she's gone don't allow this to happen to your love one . also make sure they are taking the proper care these doctors don't care they just want money . i loved my mom and i would do anything to bring her back :(((

they are all about the money! 
had gastric bypass here that has ruined me for life, left me on a full time feeding tube and unable to keep down food for life.... lifelong blood clots 
over 18 blood transfusions, chronic anemia, pancreatic disease, liver disease due to long term use of pic lines, doctors lies, unbelievable denial of hmo doctor prescribed procedures that hmo director dr. greene refuses to allow, 
hundreds of sepsis and blood infections, which have caused me to hospitalized at cedars over the last few years while my two young children have watched their mother as they have grown up 
as they have now have their own issues.

i hope they ref this and change their ways and test patients with the dignity that they deserve. 
thank you to those nurses who always were there for me and especially the three docs that never let go of my hands!

because of alexandria hospital i am alive to post this review. this is a heartfelt thank you for the wonderful care i received from everyone there. i was in icu for 4 days and was treated like i was the queen of england instead of  someone who looked homeless (was just going to 7-11) no makeup, no purse, no phone just my keys. the staff from soup to nuts was unbelievable. please whoever is reading i tend to jump around alot with my thoughts. i dont know why people complain about hospital food  it was great and i was on a heart healthy diet. the pot roast and whipped garlic potatoes i could not have cooked better and i am an awesome chef! my biggest thank you goes to joanna in icu (give this woman a raise now). she is a diamond was crying because i was afraid of being on a bed pan and making a mess. she told me that is what i'm here for to help you and do not worry. thank you for your kindness gentleness and being pure of heart joanna! to all of you from the cleaning people, food preparation and all in between.
as i said i  am alive thanks to all of you!!! i wish i had written everyones name down but i did not. i love you all!

you can do better than this hospital. i delivered my baby here in jan 2020. he's my first child, so i don't have other experiences to compare this one to. while i generally had decent care, there were many things about inova alexandria that were not as advertised, and as a result, we struggled on a few fronts. 

first, they actively advertise that they provide nitrous oxide to laboring mothers. this was one of the reasons i chose this hospital. they do not. i was already well into labor by the time i was told that there was no nitrous available at the hospital. i had mentioned this several times prior, had discussed it with my physician/midwife practice (who exclusively delivers at inova alexandria), and it was in my birth plan-- no one thought to tell me that there was no nitrous until go time. 

second, once i decided to get an epidural (given that there was no nitrous and i'd been induced a long time prior), the anesthesiologist clearly messed up as he was setting it up. to the point where he apologized to my doula-- not to me or my husband mind you. thank god i didn't end up with something terrible happening on that front. 

third, since i was induced, i was in the hospital for longer than expected before delivery. they had the most uncomfortable bed known to man. i got no sleep, and both my husband and i went into the delivery completely exhausted as a result. birth plan basically went out the window. 

fourth, this hospital prides itself on breastfeeding support. it's everywhere on the walls, the literature, you name it. but guess what-- their support is lousy. i had to request help multiple times. it got to the point where i had to beg the head nurse to ask a lactation consultant to sit with me and make sure he was latching. breastfeeding is hard regardless- but at a "baby friendly" hospital where they tell you about their fabulous lactation support, and i did literally everything in my power to flag that there was a problem and i was struggling, they failed me. i saw at least four different lactation consultants. there was a lot of happy talk, but very little practical help. when it wasn't working, they couldn't help me, and i left the hospital basically hopeless. i had to hire a lactation consultant to come to my house the next day and by that point my baby was a big fan of formula. 

fifth- as it turns out, part of the reason breastfeeding didn't work for me was b/c i had severe postpartum preeclampsia that went undiagnosed while in recovery, even though we spent extra days at the hospital because my son had jaundice. my body was busy trying to keep me from stroking out rather than producing milk. thank god i was told by a midwife to make an appt within 48 hours of discharge to have my blood pressure checked. i might very well have died in my sleep otherwise. 

sixth, i had the worst experience with a nurse of my life there. one particular nurse insisted on drawing blood from my days old son in the most painful way possible while he screamed as i've never heard a baby scream before. she was ignorant, ill-trained, and thinking of her to this day makes me furious. other blood draws were a breeze compared to this because they were done properly and he never screamed again. she clearly had no idea what she was doing. 

seventh, my baby had jaundice and they did a terrible job of giving you any option but to have a giant, drafty, old school light machine wheeled into your room so that you- in a hospital with trained staff and having had no sleep in days- have to make sure that a tiny baby who cannot have a blanket doesn't take off the thin fabric that protects his eyesight, etc. it was awful. 

eighth, there is not really a nursery here. they make this clear on the tour, but you might want a hospital with a decent nursery. what they have is makeshift, drafty, and not appropriate for proper care. 

ninth, they literally never let you sleep. i'm not talking about the baby keeping you up. they come to check vitals constantly at all times of the day even when there's a do not disturb sign up. we went home having not slept in basically five nights, which led to a nightmare scenario for a brand new family of three. despite all of this checking, they still didn't catch that my body was shutting down. maybe that wasn't possible to do-- but it is notable that i kept alerting nurses to classic preeclampsia symptoms and i was repeatedly told that those were normal after having been pumped with fluids during labor.

tenth, i left never wanting to come back to this place ever again. it was a miserable experience despite the fact that there were some staff who were helpful and tried their best. unfortunately, i had to go back to their er two days later because they had all of my recent birth records and health history on file. here's where they actually saved my life, and i had a generally good experience with excellent staff- save for the lactation consultant who was horrible, insulting, and should be fired.
horrible. be prepared to wait 3-4 hours even while pregnant. ended up leaving and going to another facility that took me back right away.

i have some sort of mystery sickness and was advised by my doc to go to an emergency room and since qotv was the closest one, there i went.
i'll list the good/okay points first:
evening parking was good, we got there after 8pm on a wednesday.
check-in was quick and the social distancing was observed by seating everyone outside in tents.
the wait time was in the middle. it took a couple of hours to get everything done and i could get out of there. wasn't the fastest, considering there weren't that many patients around, but it wasn't the slowest.
the nurse conducting the usual tests was doing her job. 
the doc that gave me the "diagnosis" did a job.
the check out nurse was really nice and helped me get up from the bench, which was a plus.

on to the not-so-good points:
i was having trouble standing but there was no place to sit when i was filling out the entry paperwork.
the nurse performing the initial blood tests and temp checks had a oral thermometer. of course it had those little sanitary sleeves, but this place doesn't have any of those non-touch forehead temperature sensors? during an epidemic? 
the doc came out and made a very general diagnosis and gave me some prescriptions. other than the covid-19, there were no other tests mentioned to figure out what i had. when i asked for the hospital to fax the information to my primary care doc, he replied that "they didn't have that technology." ... what?!  i haven't heard of a fax being called technology in a loong while. no wonder they don't have those other types of thermometers. i wonder how they communicate information, via smoke signals?
when the final nurse came out to give me the check out paperwork & prescriptions he said i could check on my test results via an online portal, color me surprised by that news. how is a place that doesn't have fax technology have a website portal. not very consistent this place.
okay, here it is days later and i feel less like death. i want to check my test results, so i try going to the link. first off let me say the "link" they provided is ridiculously long: https://portal.emanatehealth.org/templates/selfsignup-quvweb.livef-en-us.html 
most people access the internet on their phones, so i can't even imaging how frustrating it must be to type this crap into the address bar and don't even think about making a typo because it won't work if you do.
i tried logging into their online portal multiple times on three separate browsers with zero success. so i guess qotv's "website portal" is more in line with the level of tech savvy one would expect from a place that doesn't have fax technology.
no worries, i'll just call in (and probably get put on perpetual hold or never reach a human which would be par for course) and see if i can get my information that way.

over all, i'm not impressed by this place, but it's not the worst i've seen... but we are talking about the american healthcare "system" so the bar is set pretty low.

i recently reported monterey park hospital to the joint commission, the agency that accredits hospitals. i had many reasons, but here's a snapshot: 

 my mother was released from monterey park hospital on 5/24/2020. i just received the discharge summary today, june 2, 2020.
 a typical discharge summary is written with 24-48 hours of a patient's release because the information contained in it will be vital to the patient's aftercare. time, therefore, is of the essence.
 to obtain the ds (and address other concerns) for my 87-year-old mother, i had to write many emails--all unanswered--and in the final one, threaten to get "legal representation" to force the hospital to release a ds.
 my mother's attending physician explained the delay by stating that he had been on vacation. he also complained that he hadn't had a vacation in ten years, and that he and his wife had planned one for march/april, but those plans had fallen through.
 he further explained that when a doctor takes a vacation, he is allowed additional time to write a ds, which sounded to me like a bad excuse for turning your homework in late. 
 no provisions or safeguards are made for patients at monterey park hospital whose doctors go on vacation. my mother's attending physician insisted that the task of writing a ds could not be assigned to another doctor.
 the day after her discharge, my mother went to the emergency room due to pain from a leaking catheter. we had no idea why she had been catheterized in the first place. discharge papers from monterey park hospital did not explain the catheter, so emergency room workers were reluctant to remove it. a ds would have been helpful in that moment. a ds was also the first thing my mother's primary care doctor asked for when we took her in for follow-up care four days after her release from monterey park hospital. however, we had none to offer.
if the ds debacle were the only issue with monterey park hospital, i wouldn't be writing this review. however, there's more, which is why i contacted ericka smith, the coo, to alert her to the many wrong things that occurred during my mother's 5-day stay. but ericka smith was completely unresponsive. completely. she didn't even acknowledge that she had received my emails. she is either indifferent, incompetent, or reflexively anticipates lawsuits and stays silent as a matter of protecting herself.
leadership is reflected in the good and bad practices of any institution, so i don't think my mother's situation was an outlier, or the problem with monterey park hospital is due to individual "bad apples." i think the problems are systemic, and leadership is mute. this is why i alerted the joint commission. when lives are at stake--as my mother's was, and still is--a hospital can't be allowed to operate in this way.

2 different experiences at this er. fyi, i have now changed my insurance due to these experiences.

first experience:
back in january i was sick and had a high fever. i usually do not go to the hospital unless it's an emergency, so i stayed home and tried to treat myself. however, my fever did not get better and i started to get bad headaches, chills and couldn't keep anything down. i finally decided to go to the er when my body started to feel numb. i couldn't feel my face, my fingers or feet. i was in so much pain, i had to have a neighbor drive me. i arrive at the er with a very high fever and my body hurt so much (it's hard to describe, i've never felt anything like it). the nurse tells me to calm down and tells me i'm having a panic attack. i wanted to tell her that i've never had a panic attack in my life and my body has been in pain for about 3 hours. what they did was give me an iv and some medicine. my temperature was still high, but they told me to go home and rest. which i understand, there's nothing you can do at this point. 

later that day i ended up coming back and getting treated again by someone else. that rn actually did listen to me and helped me. 

second experience:
came to the er because i passed out at home after work. i came into the er and they checked my vitals. my bp was lower than usual and my heart rate was high. i thought it was weird and i tried to ask them more questions about why this happened and they told me it was due to work fatigue (i had 12 hr shifts). i knew that wasn't the reason; however, the md and rns didn't want to listen to me. they sent me home with some meds and told me to rest. 

the next couple of days was brutal. i couldn't go to work bc i had no energy and i wasn't myself. the next week i pass out again and go back to them. i get checked by someone else and i have the same low bp and high heart rate. i then get an ultrasound of my abdomen and it turns out my stomach was bleeding. i was so mad that i was left untreated for a week bc they did not want to listen to me. 

1 star is for the rn and md who actually helped me and made sure i was taken care of. 

if you come to this er it's a game of luck if you get someone good.

review:
labor and delivery team 04/02/20 - 04/04/20

i gave birth to my daughter crystalli rose one week ago and had to share our stay while in kaiser. as a first time mom and having to give birth during covid 19 of course i had so many worries and fears. i was pleasantly surprised with how calm, clean and attentive everyone was. from hard working cleaners, maintenance workers administrators, food handlers, nurses and doctors. i felt completely safe and well taken care of. 

i wish i had a kept track of every single nurse and doctor by full name or id number but here are a few that really went above and beyond.

04/02/20: dr. nelson and rn debbie explained every treatment and made sure i was as comfortable and cleaned up as possible. 

04/03/20: aipang was very attentive checking in with me every strong contraction and when my daughters heart rate kept dropping she told me her recommendations and got the approval from the doctor immediately to keep my baby closely monitored. aipang made sure i ate, had juice and stayed active to help prep my body for the next stage of labor. when i finally reached my pain limit and asked her opinion on when to get the epidural she reassured me now was the time and called to have that prepared. 

within minutes the anesthesiologist kevin was there! he was very good at explaining the process to me and coached me to relax my body before placing the epidural. he gave me breaks in between the most intense contractions and checked on me in 20 minutes to make sure i was okay and feeling better! i was able to get sleep, drink fluids and still move around in bed but was numb in all the right places.

04/04/20: rn liz was very sweet and attentive. we had great conversations as see took care of me. when ever my daughters heart rate would dropped she would help me position myself another way and that happened many times. during my active labor she was extremely compassionate and helped me get through my contractions and pain management.  before i knew it it was time to start pushing! she was fantastic explaining and coaching me to push properly. which i greatly appreciated since i was pretty numb down there. 

dr. fernandez explained me options to help assist my delivery. i was scared, exhausted and feeling overwhelmed but she gave me her opinion and understood my wishes( no episiotomy) 

rn velvet was wonderful teaching my husband and i how to feed, hold, burp, clean and bathe our. velvet worked with us to get discharged and back home as quickly as possible. she gave us formula to help the baby urinate and we were finally headed home. our daughter was born completely safe and healthy thanks to the amazing team at kaiser santa clara's l&d department!!

there needs to be an investigation into kp since i cannot understand how this conflict of interest is being allowed to continue. how can the group that charges insurance from public be solely responsible for hospitalization and medical services too... which costs money. where is the incentive for kp to provide proper medical care when not doing so means they get to save the money that they have already charges via insurance?  
this is the 3rd case of mis-management in my family.

review: do not go to the er here!!!!!! i just spent an hour on the phone trying to figure out why i was charged close to 6000 dollars for a ten minute visit. the hospital billed my insurance, but they let their physicians charge patience independently from the er visit. they did this by charging through a different state. i have ohp and i was sent an 1800 dollar bill on top of the (already covered) er bill... i have since gotten it taken care of, but fuck that shit. this is criminal. plus it was quarantine and the doctor didn't wear a mask.

i have never been treated so badly by a doctor that at this er.  
my doctor's office and my nurse case manager had told me i needed to go to the er because of my excruciating pain.  i had already been taking a high dosage of diulaud and baclofen and my pain level was off the charts.  i couldn't bend, walk or stand the pain was so bad.  my right hip was on fire.  my blood pressure was 199/112.  every time i moved i screamed in pain.   
i called am ambulance and they could tell how much pain i was in and they told me the er at the hospital i normal went to was closed for a cleaning due to the covid-19 so ask me which hospital i wanted to be taken to.   the closest hospital was huntington beach hospital so that was where i ask them to take me.  huge mistake!!! 
when i first got there the nurse was really nice and told me the doctor would be right in to see me.  i gave them my medical history and they were aware i had ms and fibromyalgia and i was pretty sure i was having a flare. the doctor didn't come for over 30 minutes and no one checked on me.  i had to scream out in pain many times asking someone to please help me before anyone even came in.  
the nurses were very nice when they finally came in and took my blood, started an iv and took an x-ray.   they started an iv with morphine,tiraspol and zoran. my pain level dropped t an 8 but i still hadn't seen the doctor.   
when dr ashok k madahar came in he never even examined where my pain was.  he never touched my hip at all.  he hadn't even seen me when i was in excruciating pain.  he came back in and told me "all the tests came back normal, there is nothing wrong with you!  you came to the wrong hospital!!"
when i came home and looked at my bloodwork both my cmp and my cbc say they were abnormal there was nothing stated about the x-ray.  
how was i suppose to know what hospital to go to?   this certainly was the wrong hospital.   i have never been treated so horribly at a hospital!   
i will say that the nurse nicole was super nice to me but if it hadn't been for her i wouldn't have been able to hold it together!   
they gave me one shot of morphine in my thigh and sent me home.  i ended up doubling my dilaud and lying perfectly still for the next 48 hours until my pain became somewhat tolerable.  
this hospital does not listen to you!  they don't care how much pain you are in!  they could have checked with my primary, pain or neurologist to verify my ms and my major pain issues.  they didn't have to treat me like they did!  
do not go to this hospital if you are in pain!!!

it's a beautiful hospital in a nice location. 
but in 2012 i had my second daughter at mercy 
and my doctor was dr. joseph triana. 
everything was going fine while in labor. 
i remember shifting myself to get comfortable in the bed, the monitor moved so a nurse came in. i told her that everything is fine, i just moved and that is why she heard muffled sound from the monitor.
dr triana showed up a little while later. as soon as he stepped a foot in the door, he said that i have to have a c-section. ??? 
absolutely nothing was wrong, but as a mother in labor you can scare us into a c-section when it isn't needed. "of course" the c-section went well, if a healthy person has surgery there is normally no problems.
but now that i look back, i can see it like yesterday. he didn't even try to make sure everything was fine for me to have my baby naturally. 
perhaps more concerned with making money, as a c-section pays more. 
four years later when i got pregnant with my third i was interested in having a v-bac. especially when 
my first was natural, and i "know" that i didn't need a c-section 
for my second. 
but "of course" they do not do v-bacs at mercy.
so i went to jackson memorial. 
my doctor there requested my records from mercy and after some review, she wondered why i even had a c-section. 
exactly what i already knew! 
i had a very successful v-bac with a 9 pound baby girl. 
the c-section at mercy was a 6 pound baby girl.
that may be due to the fact that at mercy, he will even offer you the option to pick a day to induce labor, instead of telling you to wait until you go into labor naturally. or wait until after your actual due date, before thinking about inducing.
i will not say that he is a bad doctor. but "intuitively" i know that he was not as concerned about me as he was about getting me out of there and making money. if you are a mother that is into having a natural pregnancy and not being cut open unless it is absolutely necessary. 
do not choose this doctor...
just a little additional info, i am a fit mom. i had some pain when i would walk during the pregnancy. so i told him during a visit, i believe it was pubic symphysis pain, maybe from working out. 
he told me it "cannot" be that because i wouldn't be able to walk at all, and i would have to deal with it until after having the baby then it would go away. 
i went to a chiropractor who adjusted my pubic bone. i stood up and almost cried. 
the pain was gone. and after that i was gone from mercy.

dr lim did not appear until minutes before the procedure and did not prepare me, ask for consent, or discuss anything about the procedure with me, leaving it all in the hands of an inexperienced fellow. when i brought the lack of consent up with the dr and fellow after the procedure, the dr dismissed it as a "miscommunication" and the fellow outright lied about our earlier conversation about who would perform the procedure.

might i suggest that the president and ceo of brigham and women's hospital create operational processes (that work) at the animal clinic that she presides over, and fix the rancid culture and demeanor of so many, nasty, brigham and women's hospital employees.

very bad experience here time after time. lpns are regularly rude and act as if you're inconveniencing them. doctors lack bedside manner and rush through appointments. be ready to wait on hold for a very long time if you want to talk to a person. you're always directed to just use the portal. i feel like i'm constantly battling and having to advocate for myself. nothing is ever easy or straightforward here. communicating with my doctor should never be an anxiety provoking event but here it is. i always perceived bwh as the best of the best, but my experiences here have me running away.

this is a warning to anyone who is considering to be a patient of dr. jon einarsson from the obgyn department do not go and see this doctor and do not let him touch you unless you want to end up almost dead like i did. dr. einarsson preformed emergency surgery on me almost two years ago and during the surgery he went to another area that i had separate surgeries on to try to fix without my consent in doing so he perforated my bowel which lead me to go into septic shock with my organs shutting down and needing lifesaving emergency surgery. due to his medical negligence from the permeant damage he caused to me it has absolutely ruined my quality of life. i still to this day wonder why this doctor is still able to continue treating patients. do not go to this doctor!

horrible experience at this hospital. doctors refused to do procedure that i confirmed with pa who called hospital to confirm procedure procotols.  day of surgery while underway with iv in arm was informed that they had a change in policy and refused to do procedure as directly and expressed/confirmed two days prior.  they would not honor doing procedure as confirmed and did not provide any advance notice of changes in procedures. stay away from this place, they care more about policies than well being of people. it was a traumatic experience to have to walk away from a surgery after given iv and waiting hours for confirmation on their changes in procedures. patients have right to care, but this hospital has other priorities! please reach out/respond if i have any recourse for my experience as this was beyond traumatizing!

the er doctor is callous and his bedside manner lacks basic manners. he doesn't listen to patients convey their complete medical problems and he is too quick to jump to conclusions. rural hospitals struggle to obtain qualified medical staff. however, the other members of the staff appear to be highly qualified and caring.  most er doctors work in high-stress situations. they are under pressure to save lives and often have to break the bad news to loved ones. their patients are usually scared and in some of the most traumatic situations of their lives. this means that er doctors have to remain calm under stress, as well as have a warm personality when talking with patients and their families. this doctor lacks warmth, patience, empathy, and other essential interpersonal skills required for an er doctor position.

i wish i could give negative stars. i am 33 weeks pregnant with covid-19 symptoms and they won't have me tested because they claim i don't have symptoms and that my symptoms are pregnancy symptoms (coughing ??) so if i'm positive for this and my baby suffers they are to blame. worst experience ever

not how i planned to spend a saturday night in bethany beach, but here we are.  

my husband knocked his head on a beam in the attic while opening up a client's beach house.  he ended up with a bit of goose-egg knot on his head.   he did not think much of it at the time but the next day, he came down with an excruciating headache, unlike anything he has ever experienced.   worried it was related to the head injury the day before, we decided not to take a chance and took off for what siri told me the closest er to our location.

from now on, i think i will make him wear a bike helmet when he is in a low clearance attic.

the rating for this hospital is a negative. i never spend time on writing reviews but this experience was awful. the physicians and nurses are completely incompetent. my fiancé had a bad case of food poisoning and was vomiting from noon to 10pm. i finally was able to convince him to go to the er. he wasn't able to hold any fluid down since he began vomiting at noon. as soon as we got there they said he didn't need iv hydration that they would do a po challenge after giving him sublingual zofran to see if he tolerates the fluids. based on his vital signs he was stable meaning he was asymptomatic from signs of dehydration..but why wait to be symptomatic when you are told a person has been vomiting all day unable to keep fluids down! obviously he tolerated little sips after the zofran it's antiemetic and makes you sleepy. they discharged us with a prescription and said to come back if he continues to vomit. during the night of course he began to vomit. i called the ed and explained what happened and the apparent hospital supervisor "betty" said well bring him back in but there is no guarantee  what the doctor will order him maybe more zofran maybe iv fluids. does this make any sense? completely incompetent providers. if you want to live do not go there because they don't care!
this place is fantastic! everyone from check in nurse to the room nurse to whole staff so nice and quick! so appreciative of what they do and highly recommend!

gwinnett medical can change their name to gwinnett northside all they want but unless they change procedure they will continue to fail in patient and patient family service. it's even worse with covid19. i now know from first hand experience why my mother choose eastside in snellville now.

they let you sit in the parking lot for 10 hours with no word until ya finally lose it and demand service !!!! if you want service, go elsewhere.

absolutely the worst, charging my insurance $50,000 for inconclusive tests.

not sure if it's the change to northside medical or if it is the new climate of gwinnett medical center. so many lapses in service with little to no recovery.

i wanted to give a shout out to leigh ann and elaine on the mri team. i have a pacemaker, and scheduling is never easy to get one done (despite having an mri compatible device). they both went above and beyond to make sure i could get my scan promptly done.

overall, a good experience and when i need another mri, i know who i trust to get it done.

i was not allowed for an ultrasound with my wife, due to the covid-19 situation. bummer, but i understand. i was told we could facetime instead. when the sonographer arrived, she wouldn't let us facetime. she said it was hospital policy and insisted that my wife turn off the phone. 

pretty inconsiderate for a new father to miss the ultrasound because someone was on a power trip and lacks compassion or empathy.

i recently spent one night in the hospital following surgery.  the nurses and staff were all first rate.  people answered the call button within a short period of time.

the building and everything in it is very new.  

the food was quite good for hospital food.  there was a menu with 10-15 choices in each category such as entree, salad, etc..  i picked up the phone and my order was there 30-40 minutes later.

my dad spent two months in this hospital last year and was hospitalized again last month. he passed away in the hands and "care" of the hospital staff, if i could even call it that. what was an already traumatizing experience from his first hospitalization down to his last dying breath was only intensified by the lack of care, communication, consideration, and ethics shown by this hospital.

background: my dad struggled with congenital heart disease as well as a number of other health issues. in april 2019, he ended up in van ness cpmc to get the lvad. there were multiple complications with the surgery, was in the icu, and survived. it was a miracle that he survived that. two months of his recovery was spent here, and went to another hospital after. fast forward to a few weeks ago. he was hospitalized again and was brought to the icu once more. he passed away and due to the pandemic, we were unable to be with him.

our experience:
me, my three sisters, and mom spent every day at icu during my dad's first visit. my mom has been an rn for the last 30 years at a nearby hospital (and a damn good one at that)  and was deeply concerned for the quality of care he was receiving. most of the staff was quite friendly, but wouldn't follow through on their promises. so, we found ourselves assisting our dad to make up for a majority of the nurses' lack of help (will list reasons why later). second time, it was strictly phone communication with both my dad and staff. we were faced with similar issues again.  

concerns:
(first hospitalization)
- staff, both nurses and doctors, would set up meetings for updates and would hardly ever be on time, nonetheless show up  
- would promise phone call updates without delivery
- lack of patient care: wouldn't turn him regularly, my mom had to do it
- during intubation, found that his trach site had puss and was smelly, indicating they weren't cleaning him properly. we addressed this, and found it was infected
- during his approx. 1 month of intubation, they kept him on restraints constantly which put even more stress on my dad.  even when there weren't any ivs to pull out, no trach, they still restrained him, adding onto my dad's restlessness
- nurse practitioner was trying to send my dad home without rehab, even though he was clearly imbalanced and was in no condition to leave 

(second hospitalization) 
- dad was put on npo in preparation for multiple tests, but staff would regularly reschedule his tests. he literally wasn't eating ever because of this 
- ****we had a half hour discussion with the nurse practitioner via phone call to discuss our concerns including that my dad was lactose intolerant and shouldn't be given ensure, and that my dad did not want to be intubated anymore. she said "oh, wow, i will have a meeting tomorrow with the staff about this" on a friday then found out my dad was intubated on sunday night. we did not receive that information until monday at 3pm by the doctor. when we told him about our discussion with the nurse practitioner, he said he didn't know that.****** 
- ...and my dad was still given ensure after we mentioned lactose intolerance. 
- my dad passed away the next day and we were told by the nurse we would "receive a phone call" regarding 1) autopsy, 2) what to do with his lvad, 3) results to his bone marrow biopsy immediately because he might have had tuberculosis. we didn't hear anything. my dad's physician who is not apart of van ness cpmc was the one to tell us he had tb and for me and my mom to get tested since we were exposed. 
- on his death certificate, they put the wrong date of hospitalization and apparently, there was no autopsy at all, despite my mom's request??

  
this hospital has some serious work to do on their organization, communication, and ethics. although the runt of our interactions were with the nurses, this is an issue that the hospital must tackle as a whole. it was a deeply saddening experience to witness my dad's condition from beginning to end, especially being unable to advocate for him by his side during the pandemic. i can only imagine how much more stressful this would be for a family that had no medical background. please, please fix this, so other families don't have to go through what we had to go through.

my wife and i live in marin and we are having our first child. the obgyn that she used forever was based in sf. she convinced us to use cpmc as our hospital. as she was diagnosed with gbs we were somewhat anxious about having to drive all the way to the city if anything happened...  needless to say we had a situation where her mucus plug broke and we needed to understand if it required us to head to the hospital.  we called 5-7 different times only to get a hold of triage nurses - who all said different things. we decided better safe than sorry and drove all the way to the hospital.  took 10 min for the security guard to check her credentials...  only to say "sir sir - yeah you can't go in at all. you can't even wait outside. you need to be on the sidewalk. that's as close as your allowed in unless she gets admitted...". awesome..  thanks cpmc. i'll freeze outside while my wife waits for hours to have a dr. talk to her bc your phone system apparently doesn't work. def will be trying to switch our delivery to marin general.  this place is laughable...

we labored, delivered, spent post partum and then our son spent some time in the nicu at cpmc. we cannot rave enough about the quality of care we received from beginning to end. even though nurses have different shifts, we were treated with the best care. they were so kind, sympathetic and knowledgeable every step of the way. the 5th floor (l&d, nicu) is run like a very well oiled machine. when our son was in the nicu, we had rounds of doctors/specialists looking into his case, we had lactation consultants, social workers, childcare specialists and even a spiritual specialist come by. we were so relieved at how well our son was taken care of and they made especially sure the parents were doing well.  i'm sure the bill is going to be massive but the quality of care our son (and us) received was worth it.

i give downtown brooklyn nursing and rehabilitation center zero stars, but i have to give it at least one star here unfortunately. nicole the social worker had scheduled three care planning meetings before she finally did the care planning meeting. the staff is really lazy. my mom's news social worker ms. williams has been promising that she will schedule meetings with the doctor and her with me or with the administrator and the social work director for the past two weeks. those meetings have never been scheduled. the medical student michael abramov has also said twice that he will call me together with the social worker. that has not happened. i am surprised cms even gave downtown  brooklyn center for rehabilitation and nursing two stars overall. no one should go to any nursing home especially this one. there are so many options for you to stay at home. ms. williams is also very rude. if anyone knows the administrator extension i would like to have it.
best hospital with the best staff ! the nurses are the sweetest i can't say enough about them ! thank y'all for helping me !!!!!

i wouldn't recommend this practice to a single person, not even my worst enemy. i am from out of town, but i purposely scheduled my anatomy scan a month in advance at this location in order for my husband to be able to accompany me to this special appointment (covid restrictions were occurring at my regular doctor, so my husband couldn't come which is why i was scheduling here because 1 guest was allowed). so a month after scheduling, some office worker called me 55 minutes before my appointment to cancel it. she said someone had called in sick. apparently there is no contingency plan here if someone calls in sick?! i asked if she could at least re-schedule me, and she couldn't even offer me an appointment within a week of my scheduled appointment!  i explained to her the multiple hoops that i had to jump through to schedule this appointment in the first place, being an out of town patient. she was unapologetic, careless, and clearly had no ability to understand the magnitude of this appointment to a first time, expectant mother.

they canceled my appointment 2 days before i was to find out the gender of my child , when i told them how upset i was they acted like i didnt care about the health of my child, i told them when i asked about being work and pregnant and how concerned i was they told me i was fine to be at work then call me and tell me its better for me not to have my appointment because i shouldn't be around  people who could have corona virus. so which is iy im ok to be at work or not ok to come to my appointment.  then when i ask when my appointment is in the next 2 week they tell me i dont have one and they dont know when it will be . i understand we have a very serious health issue right now but treat people in such a way is horrible.

they treat patients like shit. as a former employee i was privy to information during the time i worked there where entire limbs went missing, body parts were sent to patholgy and then lost...how do i know?  i worked in both or and lab!!!! idc if no one believes me because i know what the fuck has gone on while i was there.  i know better.

i've rewritten this many times, because i always go over my character amount. 
the only way i know how to describe my stay is miserable. i was treated like a piece of trash thrown in a room for 4 days. all the nurses i saw acted terrified of me. like they all just wanted to run out of my room as soon as they got in. i'm 100% certain they weren't sure what to do with me since i was a pregnant covid patient. i was in the hospital for 2 days until i saw someone from respiratory, and an ob nurse finally came by to check on my unborn baby on day 2 of my stay at around 10pm. i'm still in disbelief of how my stay went. i went to bayfront instead of sarasota, like my husband wanted me to, because bayfront is in our backyard. i should be able to trust them. but i can't and i won't make that mistake again.

while all of my family have a doctor at primacare, we will never return to this hospital again and will go to charlton instead. too bad primacare is affiliated with them.

my father was brought in by ambulance to the emergency room to receive steroids infusions. while in the emergency room the doctor took a chest x-ray and blood work . the x-ray showed bilateral pneumonia and the doctor saw the x-ray and gave my father antibiotics and also gave his 1gm of solomedrol daily . instead of putting solumedrol on hold per request of family the doctor refuse . my father ended up getting worst . i went to visit my dad , on that day he was upset the pt and doctor refuse to let his walk making him bed bound. that evening dr. singh from st anne called saying she was going to put my dad on a breathing machine with a tube down his throat. i said no and told dr singh to transfer my dad to charlton memorial hospital to get the right care he needed . they should have never gave the steroids on top of his pneumonia. dr. singh refuse to sent my dad to charlton memorial hospital saying they had no bed aviators in icu. i told her that was a lie and told her that she was going to held responsible if anything should happen to my dad . she was going against the health proxy request of a transfer. i work in the health field for 15+ years . i told her on the phone there no way there not one bed open when patients come in all the time in serious conditions due to accidents and have to go to icu. dr singh hung up the phone with me. after 10 minutes dr. singh called me saying she called charlton memorial hospital and pulled some string and got my dad a bed at icu. my dad passed away 2 days later due to receiving the solumedrol steroids while having the bilateral pneumonia. st annes failed in the care of my dad and the request of the health proxy went out the door at st annes. definitely do not recommend this hospital to anyone. if you want your family members to live please send to another hospital for care. st annes also refuse to give my mother the next of kin to my dad the medical records of my dad from this visit.

then the bill arrived !! 
er visit: $13,801.20 yes thirteen thousand dollars !! billing had coded it wrong. 
the corrected bill is now $7290.94 
seven thousand two hundred + dollars to be tested for the flu !!! 
then the kicker, the doctor's bill was an additional $974.00. thousand dollars to read flu test, order a iv and o2,
i still owe them close to $3000.00 after insurance. after insurance this 30 minute er visit cost more than my entire trip !! 
this is crazy 
please try to find a urgent care before you go here. if it is late at night, rough it out until the morning then find a urgent care or dr office.

edit: a personal reply would be nice not the meaningless automated reply.

do. not. go. here.

update: just got another bill for $147 from them, at this point it's a joke. i would love for them to contact me and explain what a joke they are.

review based on blood donation. 

during this crazy pandemic i heard that there was a shortage of blood donations due to companies being closed down, and the source for mass blood drives. 

i saw something online about children's reaching out, so i called and they returned my call with a near immediate time/day slot that became available. 

it was easy to find, wasn't busy, and the staff was available to direct me where i had to go which was not too far from the front entrance.
