my grandfather had terminal lung and brain cancer and was transferred to calvary on may 20th from new york presbyterian hospital. my family and i were sold a beautiful story of how everything would be including being able to have virtual visits and an open line of communication. we were also told once my grandfather was in critical status or imminently dying  my mother would get a call to go see him. none of the above happened, it was all the opposite. communication was horrible, staff does not care about the patients nor do they have any compassion for the family. my grandfather was moved three times from floors, during one of my calls i noticed there was something strange with the way my grandpa looked. i asked what medication was being administered and discovered he was being given haldol. this was without our authorization or consent so i asked to speak to the doctor. when i asked dr. devmani the reason  she couldn't give me a straight answer. i told her that moving forward no one should administer any medication without our knowledge and consent. after i raised that concern amongst others i noticed we were being treated even worst. almost felt like they were retaliating. yesterday at 12:18pm i called to ask how my grandfather was doing and demanded a virtual visit. i saw him in really bad shape so i begged for an exception so that my mother could go see him and i was told no. at 9:15pm yesterday we got a call that my grandfather "expired" . this totally broke my heart. calvary has no compassion for family members or for the patients and they do retaliate if you raise any concerns.  if you really care for your family member do not place them here. rip grandpa, i'm so sorry you had to spend your last days surrounded by people who truly don't care. they wouldn't even allow my mother to go see his dead body and they also refused to send us pictures. the staff at calvary has no regard for human life.

about the person who complained about the length of time it took for their  er visit.  if you were making an er visit in portland or you'd still be waiting in the waiting room.  appreciate kootenai health...sounds like a great community place to me.  :)

avoid kootenai health at all costs. unfortunately i had a er visit recently. after receiving care ( lidocaine injection,x-ray of hand and a small cauterization of a finger wound ) it took approximately a hour and a half of which maybe 20 minutes of i was actually receiving care from a person ( the rest of the time i was twiddling my thumbs). on my discharge paperwork there was a total of two words skin defect.  they called it a skin defect when in reality it was a laceration to a finger. i left the hospital with dried blood still covering my hand. they took no time to make sure my hand was clean before exiting the building. after receiving a itemized bill (took over a month after calling and requesting one on three separate occasions) i was charged $800 for a injection to a peripheral nerve. really $800 to inject a needle into my finger is absolutely absurd. on top of that they billed me for a level 3 er visit at $900. when asking the billing department why they categorized it as a level 3 visit they couldn't give me answer as to why. i was told they would contact me in 2-3 days with an explanation and the rates they charge are fair based on the area. since they are the only er in the entire cda area it is a monopoly and they can charge whatever they want. how is $800 to give someone a just a injection fair. besides the er bill i was also billed by the physician for another $1000 ( 650 for their time and another 350 for administering the injection). this place is price gouging and unwilling to negotiate on their bills. i will be filing a complaint to kh as well as the idaho state medical board. please do yourself a favor and avoid this place at all costs.

my elderly aunt passed away from covid last night and they said they would call if it turned that way and she passed and no one got to say goodbye, but of course they called multiple times  about the dnr. when my cousin got the call and she said i thought you were going to call me so we could say goodbye the nurse said well you can say goodbye now. she was already dead! there should be mandatory communication between families and loved ones via cell phones every 30 minutes for people who are not doing well.

denied medical care by the fat bald guy sitting at the desk. had very recently been in contact with someone who tested positive with covid at the same location. i was clearly sweating from fever and had a sore throat with a cough (symptoms of covid) and was denied covid testing because i "didn't meet criteria". no screening was ever done. was told to come back when i showed possible symptoms to be considered for testing. staff was very unprofessional and completely disregarded my concern for my health.

i went to centennial medical plaza on memorial day for abdominal pain that had left me unable to eat or drink anything for the previous three days.  i was vomiting and having terrible spasms. i was even crying from the pain.

we went to centennial medical plaza, where the nurses were great, especially lois.  very helpful and caring. but the doctor  seemed uncaring and unhelpful.

i am allergic to chemicals and antibiotics.  i wouldn't allow the contrast dye to be injected prior to the cat scan because it's very toxic.  i also wouldn't allow the antibiotics because i am allergic to so many of them.
i didn't want to die seeking help for my issues!

the dr.  seemed annoyed with me and wouldn't give me anything for pain, nausea or anything else.  i did receive two bags of iv fluids.  i was sent home with a script.  all of this took 3 hours.

the radiologist wrote on my permanent medical records form that "stranding in anterior abdominal wall, possibly related to subcutaneous injections".  the radiologist must think i'm a drug addict whose been injecting myself in my abdominal area.  this is all without ever examining my abdominal  skin which shows no sign of injections.  i had the md"s at uc health er verify that by actually examining me.  what a concept! 
what an insult!  i don't use illicit drugs.  i just wanted something for pain so i could stop crying, stop vomiting, maybe eat or drink something and to be more comfortable.  the pain wears me out and keeps me from having a life.

please don't ever, ever, ever go to this place.  haven't received a bill from there yet, so i can't address that.  

the next day i went to the er at uc medical center at anschutz center in aurora (the old fitzsimmons area).

excellent care received at their very busy er department.  they took care of the pain, nausea and even gave me prescriptions for follow up. they found a gastric ulcer by x-ray and gave me a script for a liquid medication that is actually helping.   i would recommend going there anytime a decent and competent er is needed.  i will never go back to centennial medical plaza for anything.

im extremely disgusted that today around noon  the security guard  that worked at the hospital jefferson in washington twp nj is not wearing gloves or a mask . he also took bag  up to my fathers room to give him and went into his room with no gloves and mask . my father is high risk and getting ready to have surgery . this is unacceptable and also against nj law not to be wearing mask . this is unacceptable . as a daughter i cant see my father with glove and mask but a security guard thats around people all day can walk around with no mask and gloves and interact with high risk patients! jefferson of washington twp south jersey get on this !

i went out to the back yard with my dog so she could relieve herself - it was approximately 6:00 am. i then got the urge to use the bathroom, then rushed upstairs. i was sitting on the toilet and instantly began sweating out of every pore of my body. i was weak, scared, nauseated - so i did what many of us do and called 911. got in the ambulance to go to the emergency room. i was only there for help.
i don't currently have insurance so i don't go to the e.r. unless i'm really worried that i need professional support. i was discharged with no covid-19 test,i was still vomiting i was given no iv support. i had to ask for anti nausea drugs - they did give me one round but i was still vomiting and the rudeness from the nurse was off the charts. and most the rest were not to much better. the overall compassion and level of care was obsolete. i am hopeful that they will wake up and do their job or better yet find a new one. shame on you for treating the members of your community so poorly when they are there for your help. yes, i totally understand that a pandemic is underway. however, this is the third time in a row i have endured the same treatment from the staff of the er. they said the only reason they didn't give a covid-19 test was my current lack of fever. after i got home, my temp was 100.1 and climbing. nope, not going there again.

look i adore the doctors i've had at this hospital. the nurses and staff are wonderful too. but yesterday when leaving the hospital everyone had to interact with one parking attendant. they weren't wearing gloves or a mask. 

i guess our lives were worth a couple bucks. this is an unacceptable risk

this is one of the best emergency rooms i have ever had to visit. they were extremely professional, very quick, friendly, and efficient. the hospital is also very clean. i went in for some stitches on my knee and was out within 20 minutes. 
thank you to all of the staff, doctors, and nurses for your constant hard work and dedication. special thanks to dr. michael ward for the beautiful stitches he did on my knee! i'm on day 3 of healing and my knee looks great! if i ever find myself or a friend in the position of needing an er while in az, i will be coming back to this specific one.

i had coronavirus symptoms 8 days ago (started on thursday 3/12), i've been to the emergency on friday 3/13 at 8:30am to get tested, so i can let know my employer, co-workers and family.
i've been waiting for 3.30 hours, and for some time outside, on a rainy day, with high fever and flu symptoms.
they told me i should wait 4 to 5 days to get my results, so i called 5 days later, then they told me one more day, so i just called them and now i should wait for them to call me back and that, if i gave them accurate information, they "should" call me back... and actually, they looked pretty confused and non organized when i get the test and they collected my information.
so it's been a week, and i still don't know. i behaved as a responsible person and quarantine myself, just in case, but they also told me , this is up to me... so if i have the virus, i'm free to go out and contamine others...
this hospital is just the closest from home, but i'll do my best not to have to go back there again!
i love being here , not only do i always get awesome service but the nurses go above and beyond. when i had my twins they made me cry in that floor because of how well they treated me

one of the worst hospital i ever been in. 
it is a money making machines. i have full coverage insurance. i had abdominal pain, needed to have my gull bladder removed, after all test have been done. big day at 12 noon. 1130was at the front desk,sorry your surgery is postponed to 3pm, thanks i reply no one can call and tell me so i can stay at home i tell then ,no she said like if i was in fault. long story short at 2pm in to be prepared 2 nice nurse trying to do their job with what they have on hand with broken tools. i laid on the bed til 330pm,one dr walk up to me explain the situation tel me to hung up it goin to be a wild,before i have a chance to ask any questions he left. 4pm the nurse come up i said can i ask a question?she replied i have no answer for you,i am sorry i need answer what time is my opperation? she call the dr after i insisted and the answer was. there is an urgent matter if we don't operat on you tonight  we might operat tomorrow afternoon. 
oh thanks lady can i have my clothes, i will try my luck at metrohealth tomorrow. ok thas your right she replied. gave me my stuff showed me the way out without singing any paperwork and i left. 
the next day went to metrohealth did my tests at the er and my gull bladder was in perfect helth . the dr found my pain is that i caught some stomach cold.

i could have died waiting 2 1/2 hours to be seen while i struggled to breathe.  they knew i was gasping for air, but they didn't show any concern.  horrific experience!!!!   they tried to get me to do all kinds of expensive tests, which after seeing a doctor, he said they were unnecessary.  i have good insurance, so they were obviously hoping to get some income.  

in the meantime, why was i made to wait so long while struggling to breathe?  because o'connor filed for bankrupcy in 2018 and the county rescued them.  so now, they offer a free walk-in clinic to anyone who doesn't have insurance and even doesn't have an emergency.  outrageous!!!!  they did not even show any ability to triage for what is urgent and what is not.  lots of people in front of me did not have emergencies.  i could hardly believe what was happening.

on top of this extremely severe situation, none of the staff are kind or friendly.  this is now a 1-star place where you go if you have no money, no insurance and nowhere else to go.  i plan to never return.

oh, last thing, the place is filthy, dirty and unsanitized.  my god!

i suffered the same terrible billing experience as some of the other reviewers here. i went in for a routine physical, which was covered 100% as preventative, and my doctor removed a piece of earwax during the exam. they coded this as "ent surgery", and i was charged $200. i called them, and they admitted that the coding was wrong, and told me not to worry about the bill. 

then, a year later, they randomly re-billed me. i called them and emailed several times trying to explain my situation; they didn't budge. i finally paid them just to stop receiving endless bills.

even though i liked my doctor and nurses, i won't step foot in a sutter office again. due to their coding practices, anything a doctor decides to do or say could cost you hundreds of dollars, even if you have great insurance.

as others have reported sutter health charged us three times and more for an ultrasound. the worst part is that they are not transparent and upfront about the costs. i got an ultrasound done from another medical center and they told me how much it will cost me and if i was okay with the cost before the ultrasound.
i went in at 10:17 pm on a sunday night during the covid-19 pandemic. i was in and out in less than 40 minutes. they were prompt and caring. great er staff.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: billing department forgot to turn off my scheduled auto payments after paying for my thyroid cancer surgery in full. it has been 2 months since they drafted form my account and have yet to issue my refund. have called multiple times and they state it is waiting for approval...
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: i went to their er and was seen quickly and was thoroughly evaluated. they were so efficient and organized. thank you baylor scott & white mckinney! i would highly recommend them.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review:
in may 2019 a nurse in the er struck a nerve in my arm attempting to insert an iv and i'm still suffering after a year of treatments that i have had to pay for myself. it's a shame such damage can happen in the hospital and no one will take responsibility. this is not the first issue i've had with baylor. in 2016 i had major surgery at another facility and there were major complications, bmy surgeon left the state and no one knew who was supposed to tend to me. thank god the doctor my surgeon he had to call to help repair the damage he did during surgery was there to save my life. he even has to take me back to surgery. i didn't think i would leave alive. it's such a shame. it's not just one location, it seems their whole system is flawed. my surgery in 2016 has been so hard to relive, but now with the injury to the nerve in my arm it's my duty to let potential patients know what could happen if they have to visit a baylor scott and white hospital.



it's so funny that they responded to my post 6 hours after i posted, but it's been 6 days since i submitted my contact information and i have not heard from anyone representing baylor scott and white. as i said their doctors and nurses do great damage and this hospital doesn't care. by the way, the radial nerve was damaged in my arm.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: wife and i had a terrible labor & delivery experience at this facility.  i was personally mocked and chastised by several nursing staff members from the labor & delivery unit.  this is completely uncalled for and beyond unprofessional.  extremely disappointed in how we were treated here.  i would like representatives from bs&w to follow-up with me for further details.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: i never write reviews but this place is awful. the staff is always so rude, i dread coming here over getting sick because of how terrible of a staff is there. get a different job if you're not there because you don't care about the people coming in. worst place ever.

we teamed up w/ heaven's kitchen to donate meals to staff working in the lab.  we often think front line workers are doctors and nurses but it's actually everyone working w/in those 4 walls.  

thanks to valley medical foundation for coordinating w/ us.  due to the strict guidelines meals need to come hot (fresh), individually packaged, and prepared from commercial kitchens.  like now if you wanted to bake cookies for them they wouldn't be able to accept, is what i'm saying. 

i took a long lunch for this - definitely made my heart smile.

i wouldn't bring a hang nail case to this hospital much less anyone i truly cared about.  the worst experience ever was at this hospital.  to begin with, i couldn't understand anything the assigned physician - khoi duc nguyen was saying about my wife (the patient).  when it was finally determined that this hospital couldn't provide the care she needed, they still refused to transfer her to good sam where she could get the care she needed.  they wouldn't release her to me either.  things got so bad that i finally walked her out of there against all their protests and within an hour at good sam she was getting the care she needed. this hospital should have closed when it was on the brink of failure recently but regardless - do yourself a favor - drive a few miles north and go to a real hospital.  pass this failure of a healthcare facility and continue up the road to good sam!

once again, huron valley saved my life....literally.
after my pcp dismissed my intense arm pain, stomach pain. sweating and nausea and sent me home, the pain became unbearable and i went to huron valley. in less than 30 mins i was in surgery to clear two arteries...i was having a heart attack.
last year i had severe pneumonia and the care was superb. the nurses are efficient and compassionate.
i switched all my care to dmc because of my experiences- pulmonary, cardiac, and primary care.
i love this hospital.

are all ers notoriously bad, or just this one. should it really take 2.5 hours to see a doctor, get a diagnose a uti and give you antibiotics?  brought my child here at 11:00 pm and didn't leave until nearly after 1:30 am. i had this diagnosed within seconds through the mayo clinic website list of symptoms. saw the doctor for less than a minute at 12:10. at 1:10 he popped back in long enough to say its a uti and here's a pill until you can get more at the pharmacy later in the morning.

i had an injury where a large portion of my finger was removed by a power tool. dmc was the closest er. i sat in the waiting room for over an hour before even being registered. then i waited another hour after to get called into the er. i was actively bleeding. i got into a room, met the rn and md, got a tetanus shot and then didn't see either for 2 hours. no pain medication, no wound care, nothing. i finally asked another rn if they were too busy to see me. she said i'd only been waiting an hour and 8 minutes. i corrected her that this was only reflective of my time in the exam room. i asked her if i was getting anything for the pain. they said they gave me tylenol. i said for losing the tip of my finger that's it? she then went to find the dr. 20 minutes later the dr- who was a resident- not a physician- a student- and who should have been practicing under an attending physician told me i didn't need anything and to call their plastic surgeon in the morning. she didn't clean the wound that required a surgeon, stop the bleeding or even clean the blood which ran down my arm. as i departed the rn said "here's the pain medication you wanted" and gave me a pill. i then went to st. joseph's who took appropriate care of me, cleaned my wound, taped it with a splint, gave me medication, and coordinated a surgeon. i would avoid dmc at all costs.

i had to go to the er this past weekend for a non covid-19 related issue.
the care itself was very good, nurses and doctors compassionate.
i was however, surprised that one nurse used no gloves or mask. i was sick in the restroom and it was not cleaned up in the several hours that i was there...which was most concerning, even though i alerted them immediately.  so the sanitary conditions were the concern.
had a great experience with my surgery with dr. ching. awesome staff as well. everyone was very caring and attentive to anything i needed.
don't ever come to this pharmacy. nurses fucking suck, no communication, and takes fucking forever. i'll take my talents to legacy health
excellent hospital.  i was treated very well in the emergency department and would recommend providence to anyone.

worst hospital ever! my daughter has been in there 8 days! (she has crohn's disease) they are slow, it takes days to get x-ray, cat scan, or any lab work back, she has a abscess in her pelvis and they let her lay there for 7 days before they took her in to clean it out. drs don't start work till after 12:00. if you ask me they are more concerned about sucking as much money out of you then giving you the proper medical treatment. when the ambulance came to get her my gut told me not to take her to this hospital ( i read reviews before ) but she was in so much pain she just wanted to go. ( we live out of town too) they wouldn't take her to loma linda. my advice is do not go to this hospital it will be worth it to drive yourself or your loved one to loma linda. 
worst experience ever! 
there were some pretty awesome nurses but the care system needs some serious work!

i wouldn't even give one star but i have to. i only went because i needed immediate help. i had to have my appendix removed and i was in desperate need of help. first night was ok. the next day everything changed. nurse would ignore me for hours no one would answer the call button. they put my iv into my tissue and my arm swelled up huge, when they finally took it out so much fluid leaked for the site that i needed a towel. blew out my veins in both arms. forgot a machine was running and let it for over 5hrs causing my legs to swell up. the list goes on. i am young and healthy enough to stand up for myself and demanded to be discharged the day after surgery. i feel horrible for anyone who is timid or can't speak up. they probably are treated very poorly.

this establishment treats patients like cattle. they do not care about service or well being. the outpatient clinics might have good dr. care but front staff violate hippa and make policies to get big corporation money and little sensitive care.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple

review: hey i had a stroke a couple weeks ago in the midwest and came to palo verde hospital for a follow up the nurses were very pleasant and efficient my favorite part was interacting with all the prisoners .... cloudy and psycho had such fascinating stories thumbs up to them

while the doctors who work in leased offices at this location are amazing - my review is based solely on ordered imaging i had done here. do not do it!  
they max bill your insurance, even my insurance company was completely dumbfounded with how much they billed. it was $500 for 2 hip extras, total time 2 minutes, i waited 2 hours to have these 2 images taken. 

after the fact, the employees in payments are beyond rude. i have not had one good call with them. 
even today paying my bill off the representative started with attitude. 
i've asked for a note to be made - never let me be a patient in this facility again. in an emergency transfer me somewhere else as soon as possible.
fac_name: CHI St. Luke's Health-Sugar Land Hospital

review:
no wonder this place has bad reviews this hospital is by far the worst in every single thing starting from customer service from their phone operators to their nurses and front staff !! everyone gives you a round around no one can give you any answers and on top they all seem bitter and mad to work their as they keep giving you attitude no compassion at all like aren't you health care workers didn't you go to school i thought they teach you how to be compassionate to patients family members!!
not sure why people working here are rude as the 911 operators !! 
even the negligence of not taking care of a patient correctly and releasing him/her without proper care !! it's non sense !!

i came into st. vincent's clay county emergency room on 04/02/2020 around 830pm. i was greeted by the screeners and by a very nice young lady at the registration desk. i then had my vitals taken and was led to a room by nurse kaitlyn. she walked ahead me because i was moving slower than usual because i was in pain and i was never offered a wheelchair. once in the room she needed me to get onto the gurney. since my back was hurting, i asked for a pillow and i was told by kaitlyn that "i don't have one right now so". she raised the head of the gurney to accommodate me but seemed to be very frustrated. she placed the leads for the ekg on me as if she was frustrated and had a frustrated tone in her voice. she was not clear with her ekg instructions and seemed pissed when i moved because she started snatching the cords off of me and pushing buttons on the machine angrily. she then attempted to start an iv and by this time i was angry and asked her for her name. she was unsuccessful with starting the iv. she said that she would attempt to start the iv again and left the room to get the kit. after about 15 minutes another nurse, rose and the doctor came in. rose started my iv on the first try. patty, who wheeled me to radiology, was very nice caring and professional and the radiology tech was nice too.
 kaitlyn needs some sensitivity training and be reminded that she works in the medical field and that compassion, kindness, and professionalism is part of the job description. i am a health professional also and do not allow how i'm feeling, a person's race, religious, or political views dictate treatment. if i am running behind, i do my best to make sure that my patients do not feel rushed. i felt rushed, like i was ruining her night. the doctor who "treated" me did not thoroughly address my concerns. i am having the same pain on today april 20th, 2020 and will have to spend more money to seek further treatment for my issue with another health facility.
i did not want to go to the ed, but my primary doctor told me to go after i explained my symptoms. kaitlyn's behavior is unacceptable, and i felt like she couldn't have cared less about me nor my health. i left the hospital more frustrated than i did when i walked in.
fac_name: Saint Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review: oh my god i can't stop coughing, coughing!!!!!!i don't know if i'm gonna die of corona, however i decide to stop at this hospital tonight and i got the best service from dr. tim!!!!this guy puts my other three doctors from denton, little elm, and bonham to shame!!!!i so high five to bonham hospital, i'll be seeing you guys again!!!!!!thank you dr. tim,you nailed it

i had a colonoscopy and the staff was very nice and polite and helpful and also the receptionist cleaned everything up debbie and angela had taken care of me during the procedure and i was being discharged successfully and also the nurses go over the results of the procedures

great hospital that gave my wife and i great care during separate stays. my wife had surgery for an intestinal issue and i had heart valve replacement, both in 2014. we're alive and kicking and i credit the doctors, nurses and other staff we had at gateway. we live in sc now but i still miss having that hospital nearby.

had a collection show up april 2020 on my credit report. called and they stated it was from 2013 at bartow regional!! 2013. i never got a letter or a call. shame on you for waiting 7 years when i never knew that i owed a balance. for all that i know it was probably an error on your billing departments **update: as you can see below someone commented on my review, i followed through and no one has contacted me still.

we just had our first baby here at northside one month ago. i cannot say enough good things about our experience at northside during this corona virus situation. very pleased with how they protected us.

amazing labor and delivery. i was in labor for 48 hours and i can't say enough good things about the nursing staff. i was pleasantly surprised by how amazing each and everyone of them were. after l&d we were in mother baby for another 48 hours. they did a great job checking in when needed and making us feel comfortable. each nurse and tech in mother baby did an amazing job. highly recommend.

i was just released today from northside after a 6 day stay for a lung operation. this review is about the food and food service. i have had hospital food while visiting friends over the last 20 years in different hospitals around georgia so i expected cold, cheap, poorly cooked meals.
from the first meal i was served that night, i was surprised at how good it was.
every single meal from then on was well balanced and and tasty. i was quite shocked at how good they were flavor wise. i never in a million years expected any thing like what i ate while i was there this past week. it was all good quality, well cooked, healthy food.
ok, food is one thing and service is another. the food server on the floor i was on was unbelievable, nina knew what foods i liked after the first day, always got all the little things i like to go along with my meals and took special care of me the whole time. today when i told her i was leaving and did not want lunch, she brought me the most amazing chef's salad anyway and asked me if i wanted it.  heck yea nina! she was great and it was so good.
shoot, i can't get service like that at most of the higher end restaurants i go to.
my name is bryant baker and i using my wife's yelp to post this.

i went on a friday evening and am shocked how quickly i got seen . they literally had a bed for me after they saw my heart rate was up . the tech , x-ray tech and nurses well all so kind. even the doctors! eventually i got admitted into the hospital and the care i received was amazing. the nurses and techs were so patient with me and understanding . i am not used to that, i am used to people getting mad etc.  really enjoyed my nurses the first two days i was there. my tech was also amazing and brought me anything i needed . they work on unit 72 and if i ever have to come back i am going to ask to go back to unit 72. thank you guys for everything , out of all my years of living i never received great service from a hospital.

well they could not locate my baby for three hours but assured me he was somewhere upstairs. that's a good feeling after you give birth. 

while i was in labor the charge nurse was discussing a hispanic patient and said, "it's probably her tenth baby. you know how mexicans are." i won't deliver here again.

the qualifications to work for northside's customer service department: 

1. have a piss-poor attitude
2. be stereotypically rude
3. be as incompetent as the trump administration

northside's customer service workers are a disgrace to the actual health care workers. disgusting how they treat patients  trying to resolve billing issues, especially when its an error on northside's end. who the hell hires these people? they might as well just outsource their customer service to some third-party company in india, at least they get shit done without giving you some urban attitude along the way.

the billing office has guaranteed that i will never use or recommend any northside facility. i work in healthcare and had a marginal experience with the care provided here but it was made worse by the treatment received after discharge. the billing dept was rude, aggressive and lied to me. a manager called a week later to apologize for the employee but i would not recommend coming to northside for any treatment.

my mom has always bragged on northside hospital for all there wonderful staff . she was fortunate enough to have a great deliver with my little sister in 2013 at north-side women's center atlanta by her obgyn doctor.

please read my previous review. after the birth of my son (who is now 3 weeks old) i took some time to reflect on my birth experience. i want to say first that there are some spectacular nurses in the mother baby unit. i will not forget how kind and caring they were. dr pham is absolutely amazing. she really made me feel like i could trust myself and how i was feeling. she truly cares about mothers care.

we had a nurse (his nurse) come in several times and make comments that were completely unnecessary about how often he needed to be fed and how we needed to keep him in the bassinet, etc. she didn't even make eye contact with us. just came in, said her peace, and left.

her reply was "well we just have to give you this information and in the past we even had to call cps if you declined it". why on earth would you tell me you had to call cps in the past?! it was very alarming. i did everything i could to just appease her and get her to leave, i almost cried thinking why didn't i just go along with what they wanted. she returned the day we left and was very rude about us needing an appointment made for him with his pediatrician prior to us being able to be discharged. i literally stopped talking to her to make this appointment. these doctors think we are ignorant. they know better i guess in their minds. or perhaps they are so overwhelmed/worn out/ have seen it all, that they just don

there's still so much that this hospital can learn. truly the only shining star they have is a handful of diligent and loving nurses.

it has been 37 days since i last was able to see my son who is only 62 days old and still in the nicu - all because of a covid visitation policy at texas children's that is excessive, insensitive to parent's/ patient's well-being and out of line with nearly all surrounding hospitals.  37 days i have been prevented from holding him, watching him grow, and having critical moments of bonding.

tch's visitor policy is one parent per stay.  nearly all hospitals for children in medical center have a humane policy of one parent per day (hospitals offering that are children's memorial hermann nicu, harris health ben taub nicu, houston methodist hospital children, shriners hospitals for children) and woman's hospital of texas even allows both parents to visit.   

how is tch so out of line with their competitors? why are they so unsympathetic to the needs of their patient and their families?  

not to mention that the policy itself is illogical - my wife and i live and breathe  in the same household - we represent the same risk factor & germ pool.   i understand limiting the number of visitors in the hospital at any given time, but allowing parents living in the same household to switch daily would not increase the level of statistical risk for the hospital. your intent here was well placed, but the excessive (& out of line) policy that you have drawn is causing harm to parents and preemie babies and without any real benefit.  

so in conclusion tch has a visitation policy that is dramatically more harsh than their peers, that is causing real harm to patients/ their families and doesnt make their patients any more safe.   

i have worked with child advocacy multiple times and spoken to hopsital administrators, they all recognize the policy does not make logical sense but they are either unwilling or incapable to make humane, logical, reasonable accommodations.
the entire staff takes such great care of our egg donors, surrogates & intended parents. we enjoy creating families with this team, it is a privilege to create families with you!

in mid-march, just as the covid-19 virus was ramping up, my husband required emergency surgery, not related to covid, for which time was of the essence.  he had initially been taken to st. mary's where it was determined that they didn't have the resources to perform the necessary procedure and he would have to be moved to long beach memorial.  there was no guarantee that he would survive the short trip to receive the procedure. 

he did survive the trip under patrick's care and from the time he arrived at long beach memorial, my mr. received the best care that i could have hoped for.  from the surgical team to the ccu and icu nursing staff, from the nurse practitioners to the physician specialists, the care and professionalism were awesome.  it was apparent that each of the individuals caring for mr. had a personal investment in his recovery.  i was treated with great empathy, was included in the bedside change shift huddles so that i was informed as to what was going on, and any questions i had were answered fully.

because of the virus lock down, i was only able to stay with mr. for a couple of days of his two week stay before i was locked out but was encouraged to call the ccu and icu nursing stations from home for updates.  staff recognized how difficult the separation would be so they also encouraged me to bring his phone to the hospital so that, after mr. awoke, we would be able to communicate, making it a little bit less isolating for him.

i will say that there were a few hiccups at discharge time.  i chalked this up to the fact that mr.'s discharge took place just as non-essential employees were being furloughed and consequently a couple of non-medical things fell through the cracks.  i was pleasantly surprised (and relieved) when i received follow up phone calls from the nurse practitioners for several days following discharge.

i would not wish mr.'s medical situation on anyone but feel confident in saying that if it happens, the patient will be in the best of hands.

this is one of the worst hospitals we've ever used. we will never go back. my wife has been neglected for hours at a time. using call button does nothing. a few of her nurses have been nice but still don't help her when she needs it. it reminds me of those nursing home horror stories.

just called to check on having blood work done the guy i talked was rude and really ignorant!!!! get some decent people to work there would not recommend this place to anyone period. not the first time this has happened.
worst hospital i've ever been to. their staff don't give a shit and don't care about the patients here. there's barely anyone here! why?? because they know not to come here or they might die.

my son was in the nicu for over a week. no updates, no information, and no help from any of the nurses. i had to actually call a separate hospital before i was able to find out why this hospital was treating him the way they were. the only thing i was told here was "it's hospital policy." we were also told different things about hospital policy based off the staff that day. i was told they would be able to give my wife a discharge class one day, then the next day they said they didn't want to give it her, their reasoning was they just didn't want to.
to top this all off, i have spoken to several people who share my opinion about the hospital (specifically the nicu). horrible. babysitters at best.

my family loves having a hospital close to us.  we have utilized the hospital multiple times for my husband and myself.  there is one thing that we would like them to change.  the tv channels are very limited and actually doesn't have very good programs for families.  the news channels is cnn which is not preferred in this area.  fox news is what most like here.  please consider adding more family programs & the fox news channel.
fac_name: St. Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review: i used to live in florida, and this was the closest, a couple of times i had to go there, in the er they rarely checked on me. one time i was admitted for a night because they thought i had a mini stroke, they did not even check on me. they even put on an intermittent pneumatic compression (ipc)  and it was never turned on. yep, good ol' times! my then boyfriend now my husband had to go there several times, and i went to accompany him, the treatment for him was 5 stars!!!! i had several opportunities to make sure it was not a "well maybe they were having a bad day" excuse. now, this is the kicker we are both hispanics both college educated, he is white blue eyed with an english last name and good health insurance. and me well i look different and at that time for a few months had medicaid. things have changed now, my insurance is amazing and so is my job and he is under my insurance. i often wonder if moved back to florida and i went there what would happen. again i had plenty of chances to compare! and oh by the way no neurologist ever saw me ‍
fac_name: St. Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review: i was a patient here for 3 days and two nights last july.  during that time i continued to wear the clothes i came in wearing.  i was not offered a gown or any personal care items.  the nurses were very mean.  i was hooked up to an iv and asked for assistance to use the restroom.  the nurse came in and yanked the machine's plug out of the wall and told me to go into the restroom.  i am not a medical professional; how was i to know the machine could be unplugged?  hire some nurses that are not afraid to smile for fear of cracking their faces.  get rid of the hospitalist archibald.  she basically does not have time for patients either.
fac_name: St. Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review: have had 2 spots in the derm clinic now and they have both been virtual, on time and thorough. our new normal is different but they has so far exceeded my expectations in every way.
fac_name: University of Minnesota Medical Center, Fairview - University

review: the er wait times are long but that's considering that some covanant hospitals in the area have closed increasing the number of patients they have to see in a given day & considering the sickest are seen first like they should be. the doctors were great and kind and the nurses were fast but amazing at their job and respectful. only hospital i'll go to.

my friend (transgender woman with bipolar disorder) stayed at cedar hills hospital. they are terrible. their staff has clearly had zero training on how to treat transgender patients. my friend was denied medical care because she spoke up when a doctor misgendered her. the following day, a patient called her the f-slur and still the staff suggested she needed to "use her coping skills." thankfully she spoke up, refused to stay another day, and we got her out before they could do any more damage.

staff has a high turnover and are not paid enough. the food is made with exploitative prison labor. their coronavirus safety procedures are almost nonexistent. every therapist is a contractor from somewhere else. just a complete shitshow all around.

my friend would likely be dead from her time at cedar hills if it weren't for her pre-existing coping mechanisms and her wide support network. fuck this place. if your friend is having a mental health emergency, please do not send them here.

every worker at this hospital needs to go on #generalstrike, and the bosses who run this place should be tried in criminal court.

i wish i could put zero stars. dr neha gauri held me against my will agter i came in voluntary and was told i could leave at any time if i decided their facility wasn't right for me. against my will and against the entire staff of rns, she placed me on a medical hold without ever examining or talking to me because i asked to leave! upon arrival we were told many things and they were all false. the nursing staff was very nice and helpful, and they were just following orders, but "dr" gauri went out of her way to be spiteful and make my life hell. threatened me and hung up on my wife. absolutely ridiculous. i came in looking for help and was dismissed and essentially kidnapped for 17 hrs. when a real dr showed up the next day, it was determined in less than 5 minutes that it was the wrong fit for me and i was released shortly thereafter. she should have her medical license revoked and should not be allowed around patients. this was a horrible and traumatic experience for me, and soured me on the entire mental health system. pretty sad when i needed help and was treated so poorly. very disappointed doesn't even scratch the surface.

worst hospital experience.  left in more pain than i came. nurse straight up lied to me.  "you will get something for the pain before you leave.  as i'm leaving "no we would never allow that for that procedure"..... then don't tell me... on top of being told i would be conscious for the procedure . . they put me to sleep!

.... get this when they brought me into the exam room.  they forgot i was there till after shift change

is there no chain of command? 

is there no notes? 

does everyone get to say whatever they want?

5/19/2020: i went up there for my medications, and what an awesome l.a. day, and everything went so smoothly. i even found someone who hadn't heard one of my corny jokes. :-)

5/19/2020: although they said they'd remove the paranoia note, they didn't. if they think i'm delusional about a danger here with a prowler going through my mail and all the rest back to when i moved in (the ransacking 'plumber' the lady next door gave me the number for, the guy across the way w/ intimidation after the flood, my brother yelling and breaking stuff, him jumping my locked gate, the handsome undercover felon/cop from al-anon, the beautiful al-anon thief, cops with my dad setting me up for an abusive psych. hold + "cracker" at my birth hospital,... ), why do they choose to believe that i'm not honest about the obvious lack of safety? my feeling of lack of safety is up to an unsafe hospital?

this is far and away the best care i've had. they figured out some stuff that has been vexing my doctors for a very long time, and they figured out what works to make it better, and i will continue that as an outpatient. 

i met some truly amazing employees and assistants that made the long stay less difficult, and of course nothing's perfect. 

these are the issues i ran into:

the worst were that they took me off of an important antibiotic before my course here was done and the bad infection came back, and i told them how many i had left, but they said i tested 'negative' for c. diff, so they didn't know what was causing symptoms, so in preparation for a colonoscopy/biopsy to find out, i had to go through the empty, super-sweet 'calories' only to find out it was hiding all along (as they do if not fully treated), and because of admit and delay, i had to have two covid tests, and the second one was pushed harder than the first and i bled like the dickens, and it was totally unnecessary since the procedure was cancelled due to the c. diff misdiagnosed/'hiding' as 'negative'; they immediately took me off of my heart pill because they thought i was bleeding (?), but when they realized i wasn't it wasn't restarted, so i needlessly went into afib for the third time at three hospitals;

strike that, my mistake, starting at a hospital very near where i live almost exactly one year ago, it's been four needless atrial fibrillations (plus a hypovolemic shock) at three hospitals. i still wonder if my healthcare killed partner is in there keeping my ticker going with love. four plus the shock in one year - jeez! 

[cont.] the menu doesn't match my super healthy diet causing some digestion issues; the night crew made it needlessly impossible to sleep (ignoring alarms...), it was not possible to heal like that, but the good people's work is not in vain: we know mostly what is wrong and what works, and i hope to get infusions whenever needed (i don't mind driving, & i'll bite the bullet on parking), w/ appropriate follow up w/ teams.

lastly, and this is minor, in my online portal for results, programs, ... there is a mindfulness research project with an upcoming webinar series that is advertised as open to the public, but when i go through all the pages to get to the registration page, the page fails with just blank, no error, so i looked under and it says an internal server error, but if i clear the cache while there and refresh, bam! the page loads for about one second and is of course unusable - the 'errored' server can serve, just too reluctantly.

what is with healthcare anymore? some incredible wonderful lights surrounded by the worst most abusive 'humanity' has to offer. i thought i missed a call from the main coordinator, dr. napolitano, but to just leave a message was difficult with multiple calls and numbers, and bad phone people, and again a woman giving me a hard time about my last name. i'll start faxing my birth certificate in advance.

best surgeons in the world!! yet, recovery on 2nd floor was like being in a 3rd world country, frightening.

nursing staff is negligent and indifferent.  it was a surreal experience.  

we had been warned that ucla ronald reagan hospital is as bad as the reviews, but didn't believe it,  given that ucla santa monica surgical center is a+

i believe my husband's recovery was set back by the poor care he received on 2nd floor overnight stay. 

by the way ucla admin, care partners were caring and kind.  care partners were working very hard to do the job of cnas and cover duties which are beyond their training.  

while nurses are laughing loudly and literally on fb huddled up making in appropriate jokes about covid-19, care partners are checking ivs,  monitors, vitals, responding to alarms, and answering nurse call buttons??? 

this is a management problem, it comes from the top.  hospital administrators are weak and incompetent.  

the best surgeons have no support.  shame on hospital administrators at ronald reagan ucla hospital.  how many bad reviews do you need to see before believing the patients?

the worst place to be. literally feeling suicidal and they just letting me go. they literally have a floor for mental patients and instead they rather have that patient go home. they could at least that person stay in the er over night then send them up in the morning . they don't care about other people only their wallet. how can this place say they care for other people. literally the worst hospital ever. they make ucla look bad. they don't take mental illness serious.

huge shout out to dr. kuo for masterfully orchestrating a tee and an electrical cardioversion with incomparable bedside manner. he devoted a great deal of time, effort, and care to ensure that everything was executed flawlessly and he succeeded. thank you from the bottom of my heart, pun intended.

i was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis and itp at 19 in 2014. was in and out of the hospital for 5 years, recurved my liver transplant there in 2018. that next year i had a splenic infection and typhoid cancer removed. i was treated with more care than i could have ever hoped for. the nurses felt more like friends. doctors went above and beyond for me. still they follow up with me with care and concern. i will forever be biased that this is the best hospital in the world and saved my life numerous of times. yes, the er can be slow to get into sometimes (which hospital doesn't have a long er wait) but once you're in, it's the best care.

we had a horrible experience in the er a few weeks ago.  the manager of the er, claudina torres, spoke pejoratively about patients in spanish as she walked down the hall.  she was very rude and abrupt as she spoke to the filipino patients.  she obviously does not like filipinos.  after waiting in the er for nearly 24 hours, she offered me a bed in the 10 bed unit.  when i refused, she became hostile and aggressive.  there is a blatant racial problem within ucla.  her last name had tape over it, but an employee told me her name was claudina torres.  claudina torres is a racist and she is being supported by the people she works for who allow her racist behavior to continue.  all minorities should stop getting healthcare at ucla.  the er needs a new manager !!

i feel very conflicted about my experience as a patient at ucla in the epilepsy monitoring unit nearly twenty years ago. because i had just had a brain injury i don't remember much and i tried to get a copy of my veeg because i noticed that the doctor's written report didn't look right. they only had the tracing, but no video portion. those records need to be kept longer for situations like mine because it looks like the doctor lied because his verbal statements to my parents at the time and the eeg don't match his written report or the eeg during the pet scan or my symptoms at the time or for the past twenty years.

i had my liver transplant there 17 years ago and had no complaints - except i thought the food was terrible. i spent 6 months there - several weeks here and there, but mostly there. a few years later i had part of intestines and appendix removed and had a good stay. still bad food. haha.

i gave birth to my son at this hospital in february and would 100% give birth here again. every nurse that i had made this experience as comfortable as possible for me and listened to my needs. dr. mccullough delivered my baby and did such an amazing job. she made the entire birth experience enjoyable and thrilling by being upbeat and positive the entire time.

the other thing i enjoyed was the blueberry pancakes from room service! the chef made really good food which is rare for a hospital! 

littleton adventist was great and i will definitely consider delivering at this hospital again with my future children.

was not impressed with the level of service at lah. sent to er for a cat scan when i had a ski accident at keystone & was determined i had a fracture. sent to lah er as keystone can't do cat scan. was determined multiple fractures, er doctor who i saw for maybe a minute and was not very forthcoming with info (and found out when i got the bill was out-of-network). needed overnight hospital stay turning into 2. arrived in er at 6pm finally in bed at 10pm; was offered a snack so i could take pills. next morning was never offered a menu; after not eating all day the day before because of tests i was fairly hungry, at 9:30am i asked do they offer something to eat here? shouldn't that be part of the nurses duty to make sure you are fed? was told that the assigned doctor would come and see me the next morning (i never saw him but in notes it indicated he evaluated my case and spent time with me, i wanted to see him but he never stopped in). instead a team of a few came in and in front of me were discussing my injuries and were disagreeing amongst each other in front of the patient, does not give you a warm fuzzy. the occupational therapist who assisted me with a shower gave me wrong instructions for my injury of a position i was not supposed to do. i had to stay an additional day since i was not able to complete my pt successfully. i asked the next day again to see the doctor, instead his pa came in and was very thorough but still did not understand that i had 4 fractures, not 3 (why am i explaining this to the pa)? the doctor that discharged me (wound up being out-of-network, extra cost to me) after i had just saw a pa in-network?? why do i have to pay out-of-network costs, it was during the week and i just saw a pa that was in network? i was shocked at the costs, the bills keep pouring in. kind of strange the total amount and of that how much is over the customary acceptable charges (don't get that). the positive experience was i had a great physical therapist; most of the nurses provided good care and a couple not sure why they are in nursing.

i had the absolute best experience at this hospital giving birth to my 2nd baby on april 1, 2020. with all this craziness going about the pandemic, i was super nervous to (1) give birth in general (2) not be able to have a support person due to visitor restrictions (3) be in the hospital amongst all the sickness and whatnot. 

i got there at about 10:15am, got screened right at the entrance, got wheeled up to the 3rd floor and brought straight to my room where i was monitored and checked to see how far dilated i was. regina (i don't really remember if this was her name but i hope it is - it for sure started with a r) was my labor & delivery nurse and she was there with me through my entire labor & delivery and she was amazing. she was very attentive and caring and made me feel very comfortable in a very uncomfortable situation. i could go on and on about how great it was to have her as my nurse because she really was just the sweetest person. 

i gave birth around 2pm and got transferred to the recovery wing around 4pm. i had amazing nurses over there as well. melissa, fe, jordan, shawna are the names that i could remember and they were all extremely nice and took very good care of me. they made sure i always had anything that i needed and also took care of my fiancé's needs as well. 

i'm honestly so happy that i chose scripps mercy as my hospital to give birth. i had a better experience here than i did when i gave birth to my 1st child.
i just delivered my baby at this hospital and it was amazing.the all nurses and doctors in labor and delivery and postpartum were so nice and professional.

while i've found an incredible doctor at scripps mercy, (sup, dr p?!), it hasn't always been my favorite when it comes to physicians. i've had some decent ones in the past and i had one in particular that really got under my skin - moving on...

all in all, great hospital that has always been very quick to accommodate and get me in as fast as they can. whether that's to see a doctor, a np, or to get an x-ray, it's never been a long process. 

parking is free when validated if you park below the facility and there are several pharmacies that surround the hospital making meds easy to receive in one quick trip.

on wednesday may 13 my mother went in for knee replacement surgery. as you can imagine it was crazy especially since no one can go in with patients all we could do was pretty much just drop off at entrance.  we were kinda worried for my mom....but with nursing staff apparently we had nothing to worry about!!! my mom was very very very comfortable and even ended up staying an extra day. much to my surprise.  i called her and she told me she was told she could probably leave on thursday but asked to stay another day. made me feel great!!! the following nurses helped with my mom.

cervantes family

jon keith ludwig in er is the most uncaring, unprofessional and most egotistical person i have experienced, ever. 
with multiple weekly visits to scripps for well over 3 years with one parent having contracted wne 3 years ago, mother with stage 4, etc i know the facility and employees well, would highly recommend all, until my personal experience 2 days ago.  
in a matter of 1 minute of him bursting into my world, after being in the er 12+ hrs with no food or water, my condition is not normal and obviously beyond his capabilities, he sucked all hope and made my conditions immediately, and dangerously, worse. 
the way he conducts himself to overcompensate for his inability to care for others, his obvious personal stress or other issues, and his lack of education necessary, is a serious concern to patients and the hospital as a whole. 
i would be embarrassed to be associated with this less than able so called m.d. in any capacity and am shocked i have not found any prior negative medical actions taken against him, and his license (yet). 
he quickly erased all hope from my mind of a positive outcome and he showed me for the first time what the "god complex" i have heard about with some self centered humans is really all about. scary to say the least, this man is insane and needs to be evaluated for his own personal health before causing more harm to others as he did me. 
he, scripps (that i have a very good relationship at all levels of the facility), his insurance and attorneys will be hearing from us soon.
you can't treat people with such disrespect and disregard, regardless of your own personal issues at hand and regardless of what is going on in our lives with covid-19, etc.

shame on you ludwig, we will be speaking again.
cut funding to this place; its psychiatric department is useless. i'm done dealing with absolute nut cases that think they get to harass individuals with no justification.

the er was so great to me in the early hours of this morning. i apparently have a kidney stone and they were so kind and efficient. my doctor dr. remington explained what was going on and was so compassionate. nurse iday was tireless i'm getting me everything i needed to feel comfortable. everyone else was great too - from admitting nurse mary and her team of chris and jacob at the front desk to the helper lorraine and the registration rep janet everyone was terrific. i was very impressed and grateful. thank u team so much!
i also wanted to give a thank u for another dr. who came into specifically explain what a kidney stone was and it's likely process. he was so clear and easy to understand i felt i could have written a paper on it after he was done. i don't remember his name but he deserves to be given a shout out as well.

quite a dirty place, actually, filthy! having been to various other hospitals, i can make a comparison on how dedicated each is to providing a safe environment for patients. scripps mercy comes short. bathrooms: gross; floors: looks like they don't mop. floor was so sticky in areas, my shoe stuck. this is important because we are in the middle of a world wide pandemic where sanitation is key to containing the spread of covid 19. if target, costco & supermarkets can see the necessity to continuously disinfect during these days, then why can't this hospital? after all, isn't  this the place where people go when they are sick and contagious? a close look will reveal that the grime isn't new, but rather built up over time, clearly indicating neglect. they need better housekeepers!

in spite of the above, the medical & nursing care was actually good and am pleased with the outcome. recovering well.

i just gave birth via c section 2 months ago. all the nurses were great expect for the ultrasound tech that told me that my baby was breech. she was rude. splashed all the gel and did the ultrasound like she was mad then said "yup she's breeched i have to tell someone" she said it in a bothered way. and when she lifted my gown it hit and covered my face and never did she apologized or moved it. wish i knew her name. the other nurses were awesome! jordan, monica, rese i believe it was their names.

be careful with your possessions at this hospital. my father was admitted due to a dangerous drug interaction. thankfully, medical treatment was good, but the costco gift card that was in his wallet was missing. his driver's license was not returned to him before leaving the hospital, so we were told it would be mailed to us, but never received it. disappointing to know, when you're in a debilitated state, in a hospital, your possessions can just disappear.

so my mom was in the er earlier this week while simultaneously my dad was having serious symptoms of covid 19. i called several times to warn to them that my mom may need to be tested and to take proper precautions. the operator had a serious attitude with me. as my dads symptoms progressed the next day to shortness of breath he called to see how he can safely arrive to the er without possibly infecting anyone else. they gave him another number to call the next day and very rudely asked if i was a health care professional. they deterred my dad from getting treatment and then called him to pick my mother up. he let them know he was sick and they insisted he come get her. guess what he was admitted to another hospital with pneumonia and tested positive for covid the next day. they never tested my mother. this is very poor decision making on their part. very disappointed in the attitude we received and lack of information or help.

worst hospital i have ever encountered and believe me when i tell you i've dealt with most . there actions today towards a client who was transported by ambulance was grossly mistreated and discharged . complete negligence on there part yet they never take responsibility . you call trying to talk to someone in charge, someone emphatic but all you get is people completely desensitized to human suffering . and when you call them out they make it clear they dont care.  they shift blame on to the medics or the doctor and in the meantime you have a 66 year old patient in terrible condition fall between the cracks.  that person is an alcoholic who is now facing the physical consequences of that drinking . but in no way does that make her less worthy of the proper care . even when you send detailed msg to relay to the doctor or nurse it gets shoved off to the side . they consider that person a frequent flyer and dismiss them. what they did today to this person is uncinsiouable and negligent yet they not only refuse to take responsibility , they get an attitude as if your bothering them yet someone that needs assistance gets none . i'm so disgusted with this hospital and it's not the first time or even the third time .... it's an ongoing issue with scripps mercy and the lack of empathy and medical attention and details they care nothing for.  i'm horrified by this hospital and there staff. one bad experience after another and there actions today were pure negligence . please if you have a loved one that needs care, avoid that hospital if you can. ucsd is around the corner and the difference is day and night. i have expressed gratitude towards those on the front lines but i have no respect for this hospital, the majority of the staff and the complete lack of professionalism of there staff . i keep filing complaints on behave of my friend but nothing changes . worst hospital ever

truly the worst experience of my life at this hospital. i had a vitamin lodged in my throat. emts who originally picked me up we're extremely rude and gave me major attitude. all they did was check my vitals and scold me for coughing on one of them. told me i didn't have a pill lodged in my throat, just the sensation of one. that it had probably dissolved and that it was just a scar from when it was there. they told me my heavy breathing and coughing was making it worse. when i finally was admitted to the hospital, they told the nurses this. instead of listening to me (ya know the patient in pain) they took their word. i could tell they weren't taking me seriously and laughing at me. until, they tried to give me medicine with water and i couldn't swallow it. must have been there for at least an hour before they realized this. then suddenly, they realized maybe i wasn't exaggerating. after a cat scan, they did see that i had a pill lodged in my throat still. they performed an emergency surgery to have removed. i went into the emergency room at 2am, didn't see the doctor until 7am and i didn't have the surgery to remove it until 8am. woke up at 8:45am and they had finally removed it. they told me the doctor wanted to see me and she would discharge me. she never even showed up to talk to me. finally at 1:30pm my girlfriend and i made the nurse discharge me. now i have an outrageous bill that i have to figure out how to pay and i actually have decent insurance. can't imagine what this would be like for someone with terrible or no insurance. it could bankrupt you. anyways all this is to say the fact that i didn't have the emergency surgery i needed earlier is true disgrace. i'm lucky i could hold on and breathe (though it was like death) the entire time. i could have died and it was sad, i should have felt properly cared for and not like everything was taking so long. i hope i never have to go back to this hospital.
