review:
my 95 year old father needed antibiotics. he cannot hear so his wife (93) took the call while i listened. the nurse said she would call in a prescription as ordered by a doctor. my parents do not drive and so my mother requested it mailed.  the nurse said it would take a week by mail. so to get it right away
i had to drive to the kaiser  pharmacy but being 70 i did not want to go inside.( corona virus seclusion) i drove up curbside and saw personnel standing around an awning. after 5 minutes one told me to park. i did. ( there were maybe 5 cars there) i stuck my arm out of the window with a kaiser card showing. after 5 minutes no one moved toward me. i got out of the car and started over. then one came over and took the card and placed it in a bag and went inside. at 2:21 i got a text the prescription was ready. i stayed in the car 10 minutes and no one brought it out. again note -they were not busy. i got out of the car and approached one of the people standing around- she said when its ready we will bring it out. 
i had to tell her it's been ready. she brings it out and i ask what it is. she tells me. i tell her my father is allergic to penicllian and she says well does he go into anaphallactic shock or just get a rash? i said i have no idea. she says it'll probably be ok. i tell her it needs to be something else. she sends me into the pharmacy and it takes 40 minutes to correct this. again i am told it probably would have been ok to give him the other drug. are these people nuts or lazy or both? my father has been a kaiser patient for 65 years and so they never give him penicillan. kaiser spends millions on "thrive" ads but won't fed 
ex or overnight drugs to people during this epidemic. i had on fresh gloves which they made me remove before entering the facility and they made no offer of another pair-though afterwards i saw that they had new gloves.  my health was jeopardized by a bunch of employees. i took an hour to pick up a prescription that should have been delivered. it i had not corrected their mistake then and there my father could have died from the incompetence of these kaiser employees. watch out!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Orange County - Irvine Medical Center

review:
i would give them a negative score if i could.  
if you are going there without good insurance, don't go there. they don't inform or explain the total cost of my surgery before i pay. i went there for a surgery knowing that my insurance wouldn't cover me and inquired about the full price of the surgery multiple times before i went there. the day i went to have the surgery i asked the check-in assistant three times (during check-in, before i pay, and after i pay) about the total expenses giving that i don't have insurance coverage, she told me i only need to pay $850 upfront. six months later, i received another billing from the hospital asking for $900+ more. i called them and filed a dispute. however, the administrative staff of this hospital were not very helpful in explaining and getting back to me during the dispute. firstly,  they asked me to call (not transfer) three different places/departments to find people to talk with. secondly, they consistently asked me to call my insurance company after i told them that i knew my insurance doesn't cover the surgery, and even after i explained to them via the phone. thirdly, they never apologized to me for not providing the whole picture of the billing before my surgery. instead, they held a very condescending attitude and said to me there was no point arguing about whether they told me the whole price or not, i still owe them money and have to pay. i had no choice but paid them the other $900+.  
in summary, this hospital tends to persuade their patients to do a surgery without telling them how much they should expect to pay. i am very disappointed about my experience there and i will never go back there again. please consider my experience if you are thinking about going to this hospital.

my father in law was admitted this weekend- i cannot say enough about the nursing staff there - from director, susie sorge, to marianna on one of the covid floors.  we are blessed our father has these angels in his life.  thank you!  we are eternally grateful!!

my dad went in to the hospital on june 8, 20 because of uti, he doesn't speak the language,  my family was grant 1 day visit last saturday for 1/2 hour, we been on the phone every day check on his condition, we felt the hospital whoever's making the decision should look at case individually,  my dad is 99 years young in his mind he believed family are abandoned him, and no one care about him but that is absolutely not the case,  my dad living with us and we care for him 24 hours 7 days a week, i just need someone reading this  post can permitting us to spend 1/2 hour with  him, reassuring him that he is getting better and will be home with us soon, his is in room 458a, his name is yet-hai chen, my contact information is 973-886-4106

my husband at 56 years old has a major heart attack. his heart stopped 12 miles from the hospital. the paramedics were amazing. dr. robert wang, the interventional cardiologist was amazing. the er staff was amazing, the local ambulance, green pond, the paramedics, the nurses the cardiac icu....were all providing top notch care for which i remain grateful. my husband is fine thanks to their speed, sense of urgency and professionalism. i have never experienced anything less there and i will be grateful forever. never underestimate this hospital because morristown is close. i felt i had the same physicians, closer to home, and the skill and talent level was without comparison. thank you st. clare's, thank you dr. wang, thank you to his assistants, the paramedics and the local ambulance. you are amazing

yesterday at the request of my mother's doctor my mother and i donned our masks, got her wheelchair, and went to the east doors to take her for her infusion. we were met by a nurse and security guard both without any mask or gloves, the nurse leaned over my very ill and aged mother breathing on her, while the unprotected security guard insisted only he could take her upstairs. i can understand my not being allowed in right now due to covid-19. however, when her appointment had run 5 hours instead of 2-3 i went back to the doors to inquire as no one on at the cancer center was answering their phone, and they had a message setup that they aren't taking voicemail messages to call anyone back. two different people without protective equipment are present. not only that, but when i got upset that no one can find out anything for me, he throws me out and calls for more security. i had already explained that my mother's memory is shot and she can't remember my cell number to call me in the parking lot when her appointment is over. i had also explained that her cell phone had been left in the car, but was dead and she wouldn't be able to call it either, and there is no one else she can call. the staff couldn't care less. the extra security rolled up in an suv, as i am walking to my car to do whatever they thought they would do. that security person was able to do what the guy inside insisted is not possible...find out why my mother's appointment had run so long and find out was she hospitalized now. however when my mother was returned about an hour later, the person bringing her wore no protective gear. this placed both me and my mother at risk and i am very disappointed. i called the security desk this morning to file a formal complaint and i will take video of all future interactions. a very poor experience indeed!

my husband rushed me here last night during an allergic reaction to accidental ingestion of mushrooms ( i am deadly allergic). as i was continuing to struggle to breath i arrived at the hospital looking for assistance only to be told to sit and take a seat as they inputted my name into a computer and watched other staff hang out in the lobby. the supposed doctor on duty was completely aware that i was having an emergency, but only walked past me to talk to someone standing outside. my husband who was waiting in the car with my 3 year old daughter saw what was happening and told me to get back into the car where he then drove me to our nearby fire station so that they could administer an epipen.
had i waited any longer my daughter would be without a mother. dont waste tour time here! horrible service! if your in an emergency call 911 or go to your local fire station where real emt's can help. 
it's a shame, i had my daughter at this hospital 3 years ago and it was one of the most wonderful experiences of my life.

i have been coming to this hospital since october 2019.they always treat me very well,professional and fast.i love all staff and doctors.i feel like at home.i can t really ask for more.thank you for all your help.god bless you all.

only some doctors and nurses wear masks, zero eye protection, valet is still open, and they don't check temps of any workers (incl. non-medical workers) coming and going.  how do they know staff isn't bringing covid in?  yet they won't let spouses in with patients even when they are dying so patients have no advocates or loving support.  why is st. john's making people suffer if it can't be rigorous itself?

i'm shocked at how horrible the er nurses treated me during a very severe allergic reaction!! i was rushed into the er at 11:22pm 6/13/20 due to a severe allergic reaction, when i walked in my mouth and tongue was so swollen i could barely talk or breath. the front desk at er took their time asking me what i had ate? instead of rushing me to the er bed while i'm breaking out in hives all over. i had taken benadryl 10 mins before arriving to the er, so once it started to take effect my eyes started getting really heavy. i had 5 nurses ask me multiple times "did you smoke any weed? did you drink any alcohol? did you do any drugs tonight?"   i kept saying no because i don't do any of those things. they kept asking me again and again, "did you do any drugs tonight?"  finally i said "no!! i took benadryl, my eyes are heavy and i can barely breath!!" i asked for iv fluids because that's helped me in the past with severe reactions, they refused. all they gave me was pepcid/prednisone. the doctor came and said "okay you're all set to go home". i said "what? i just got here? i can still barely breath? i still have hives all over my arms?"  i started to get dressed. the other nurse came in and said "why are you getting ready to leave?"  i was so confused. they made me wait around while they figured out what to do with me. it seemed like the nurses had no idea what was happening. i was told to pay $150 for a 40 mins visit in the er. walked out of there just as bad as i walked in. it seems like i'm not the only one who has something to complain about this hospital! it's a shame

my dear father was recently there and after too many hours in pain,ignored at the er he was admit  to the hospital room...the doctors were good but most of the nurses treated him very bad and just forgot him alone at his room,without any water or care...also rooms and bathrooms were dirty and they never washed him...when his sons called for help they were getting very mad! and nurses were coming to the room without getting appropriate masks during corona virus times...(watch the news!) this place used to be so much better,what a shame! something has to be done asap!!! i hope they read this review...and make changes!

the nurses and doctor were very attentive and thorough. they answered any and all questions i had and were very detailed each step of the way. they explained each procedure and also referred me to an ent. very thankful i came here today.

i have cancer and due to cdc and american cancer society guidelines, i qualify as being immunocompromised.  given i have severe cough and shortness of breath i went to the er.  prior to going into the er, i consulted with an md at urgent care, 211 information line and a private practice md to make sure it was safe for myself and others in the community.

after multiple phone screenings confirming my need to go to hospital, i took an ambulance to the er (due to inability to drive or take ride shares as recommended by the cdc).  

i presented to the er with compromised breathing and severe cough. my discharge paperwork showed a photo of a lung and prescribed an inhaler due to my cough after x-ray was given.  

upon leaving the hospital, the nurse, tim, stated that i was 'faking my coughs' as was witnesses by a staff member named graham.  this comment caused me extreme distress due to lack of empathy and blatant lack of common courtesy for cancer patient already scared and in pain (hence er visit).

as proof,  have discharge paperwork stating i have a cough and upper respiratory infection, so understandably it was veunprofessional for an er nurse to state that i was 'faking a cough.'

i attempted to address this concern with the hospital directly prior to writing a public review yet this attempt was unsuccessful.

please train staff to deal with immunocompromised patients as this caused me severe distress on top of the current pandemic we are experiencing.

i hope this helps both other patients and the hospital improve care for very sick patients.

my father was here after suffering from a heart stroke. the doctor and nurses were very informative and they always made sure my father was comfortable. that was a weight off of my shoulders!

recently had a heart procedure here.  staff was great from start to finish.  on time, every person was professional every second.   and all alone with the virus keeping family out.  the folks were great!  could not ask for a better situation.   thanks to dr. singh and the team who did such good work.

love my physiatrist here  although kaiser is notorious for pushing group therapy aggressively to cut costs, i only get it occasionally by the people i see.

i went in a few months ago to get my burns treated on my hand. but it took them forever to see me and the doctor didn't even try to wash or clean my hand. he was more worried about my burnt hair. i left there with huge disappointment.

i went in yesterday with terrible stomach pain suspecting it was appendix.
i was seen immediately and well taken care of. they are affiliated with arrowhead hospital so was even able to schedule immediate surgery for me! i went into abrazo emergency room at 10:00.
they did bloodwork and a cat scan and x-rays which were all needed prior to my surgery.
surgery was at 3 pm and i was home by 6:00 p.m!
excellent facility and i highly recommend.

overall, i'm struggling and disappointed. the midwife i saw was fabulous, hence the one star.

the doctors at this hospital know that no food is getting past my daughter's damaged esophagus and into her stomach. they also know that she needs iv medications. they have denied her an iv. having to give a star to be able to comment is disgusting. she is 5'6" and down to 86 pounds. she's being given bouillon instead of broth and sugary drinks with little nutrition that all gets drained off into a container for fluids in her lung.

on a weekend, is there no regulator who can force caregivers to do the right thing? 

they swore an oath to do no harm and they are starving her to death!

it's hard to write a review about a hospital because it's truly never a fun time. my newborn was having breathing issues so i rushed him here at 9pm at night. i'm so thankful they didn't make us wait in the waiting room since he was a newborn, we waited in a private breastfeeding room for only about 10 minutes before someone whisked us right back to triage.

i'm thankful to report that all the doctors and nurses were very nice during our overnight stay. we waited in triage a long time to wait for a  room for the overnight, but the nurses kept coming in to check on me and him and keep us in the loop. once we got to our room they settled us in and were in and out checking on us all night and morning. we waited longer than normal to see the ear, nose and throat doctor because apparently on weekends it's a smaller staff. i'm glad they set that appointment up for us though. 

i'm happy to report the issue ended up not being a big deal at all... such a rookie move too after already having a 3 year old! he was crazy congested since birth and had dried snot, but we had no clue. anyway, glad it was something so simple. 

the one thing i wish is that they'd make the couch/bed more comfortable. it is the worst night sleep you'll get being in a hospital to begin with, it would be nice if they would make them a little more comfortable. food is not great, but not terrible either, and so glad they offer a pretty extensive gluten free option. 

happy we have this amazing resource in our city.

this place is sweet. i went there last november and this february, and it's pretty coool! it's clean and people are nice. you guys should go here too one day! thank u doctors and nurses and everyone here! i love pittsburgh:)

i delivered my baby boy at this hospital and my experience was wonderful!

now, the attending nurse i had after sarah left for the day was sandra. she was there for the majority of my stay and was there for all the eventful stuff such as the breaking of my water and the birth of my son. sandra was amazing and extrememly attentive to both my husband and i! honestly, i want to go ahead and say the entire staff that came to assist me at the labor & delivery ward and post-partum ward were all amazing including the anesthesiologist, dalton, who set up my epidural. i also want to specifically mention the nurse who helped me through the setup of my epidural. unfortunately, i forgot her name but she was the one with dark hair and glasses. she was incredibly sweet throughout the epidural setup process. 

salina and marissa at post-partum helped me breastfeed my son when i was struggling for him to latch on and feed. i was starting to feel i was doing something wrong but they reassured me that it was okay and normal for him to not immediately latch on. their techniques and advice helped me successfully nurse my son.

i'm new to henderson moved from calif and the er lines were very long u woukd wait any were to 2 hours to 5 just to get seen so i was dreading going to the er but boy was i wrong 
they take u pretty much right in was there 2 days in a row both times there took me fast and the nurses were very compassionate and very knowledgeable this hospital was very clean on top of being fast i'll use this er room again

this hospital was one of the best i have ever been to. i went to the er for what i thought was the stomach flu & ended up needing emergency surgery for my appendix. it was a stressful time as it is the stress of the virus on top of it all going on. they acted fast & did an amazing job from the surgeon to the nurses & the rest of the staff.
best place to work and best hospital in henderson!! all staffs are very professional they put patients first.

i delivered my daughter at this hospital on april 30th under the advise of my ob who said this hospital was great. i went in for a scheduled induction at 8am on the 30th and my first attending nurse was amazing. super supportive, nice, upbeat and reassuring. unfortunately i can't remember her name but i know she was from hawaii because we made small talk during the induction process. 

well i got to the point where my contractions were coming too rapidly and lengthy (coming every 30 secs for at least 45secs to 1 min each) for the only 4 cm i was dilated. so i elected to get an epidural being that the contractions were strong and i was dilating super slow; i went in already dilated to 3cm. fast forward and things started to move faster after the epidural and dialing the pitocin up quite a bit. the attending nurse was so sweet that she hung out slightly after her shift because she was determined to see my baby girl. unfortunately she couldn't hang out to that point since she was born at 9pm and her shift ended at 5pm i believe. 

fast forward again to postpartum. everything started out good.  but the reason i gave 1 star starts now. the room was freezing cold, i informed the nurse that it was super cold and the thermostat was not working. i was told that they would contact engineering and have them check it out. 2 hours later and freezing, nothing was done. i called again and finally a different person contacted someone who fixed it... temporarily.  of course after delivery things can be "less than tidy" and i consider myself a pretty clean person. well the cleaning crew did absolutely nothing but empty the trash in the bathroom. no one checked the bed/changed the linen, swept or mopped the floor or actually cleaned the bathroom. and unfortunately i had to be there for 2 days since my discharge time would have been too late in the night because of the required 24hour stay after delivery. 

the following day the lactation specialist, nicholette, came in to go over breast feeding with me. not once did she ask me about my personal situation e.g.) personal life and whether i have a partner to assist,  medical history, potential work schedule, nothing i think would be important to establish my personal feeding plan. i had a pacifier for my daughter because i couldn't stop her from crying. the first thing she did was tell me her name and write it on the board. the second was to take the pacifier out of my daughter's bed and throw it in the drawer and tell me "she doesn't need this, these are terrible" i was in disbelief and speechless. she never asked why i had it out but just shut down the use of it. she asked me to try to breast feed her so that she could see how things are going. i obliged and picked her up and attempted to latch. i explained to her that i was having some issues getting her to latch because of the shape of my nipple so i was going to try using a nipple shield that my doula suggested may help.  she asked if i tried different positions, which i had and told her.  i said i was going to try using a nipple shield to help with latching and again shut me down saying those are terrible and she will latch i just have to make her. keep in mind, i've just had a baby, i'm exhausted, i've been trying to breast feed, and my baby was crying quite a bit. now she's come in and told me that everything i've been doing is wrong. so finally my daughter latches, she asked me if she could help out. i said "sure." so she starts aggressively massaging my breast while my daughter is latched and i'm just sitting there because i can't get a word in because she's over talking me. a nurse comes in to ask me a question and suddenly she storms out of the room. she goes and tells the attending nurse, wendy, that i was "non compliant." wait... what?!?! she starts immediately asking me why i didn't want to work with her without asking me how i felt, if there was an issue, if i felt comfortable... none of that. just basically that i was wrong. luckily the pediatrician on call came in to take a look at my daughter and he asked about breast feeding and how it was going. i explained to him that she hadn't urinated and she was crying a lot. he suggested supplementing her with formula because she was likely hungry. well he was right! she sucked down 3 ounces of formula in no time which was what i was trying to explain to the nurse and lactation specialist.  

overall, the lack of room maintenance, communication, and bedside manner were definitely subpar. i definitely would not choose this hospital if i have another baby, and wouldn't suggest it to anyone either.

review:
this office was a huge disappointment and a reminder why i haven't had a primary care doctor for the last 20 years! but you hit a certain age and feel like you should have someone (other than pas and nurses at walk ins) checking on your physical health on a semi regular basis. well, don't make the same mistake i did - stay away from this office!!

i researched for months before booking an appointment. i posted on local facebook pages. all evidence (besides yelp) seemed to suggest this was going to be the best spot in the area. oh, how wrong that was!

immediately upon walking in, i was turned off by the sheer number of signs telling me that if i'm more than 10 minutes late, i'll lose my appointment time. well, that didn't stop them from keeping me waiting for 25 minutes past my time! it's pretty hypocritical to hold me to a standard they aren't willing to maintain themselves.

i finally get called in. i'm irate. my blood pressure is elevated. first stop: they make me take off my shoes and put my bare feet on the dirty floor in the hallway to measure my height. first of all, ewwww. second of all, i'm an adult. i know my height. i promise i'm not lying about it. this is a truly unnecessary step. i try to brush the scum off my feet and out my shoes back on as i'm rushed to the next spot.

i go into a room. change into a gown. then sit and wait and wait and wait some more. when will the nightmare end??? before the nurse takes my blood pressure, i explain that it tends to be high on initial arrival especially when i'm aggravated and that my gyn usually takes it at the end once i've had a chance to relax. ok, she doesn't care and does it anyway. of course it's high, i've just told you it would be! 

doctor (linda weiss) bursts in shortly thereafter and literally starts yelling at me about my high blood pressure and how i need to be on medication. i take a deep breath and again explain my situation and how my other doctor does it and how he finds it to be normal once i've had a chance to relax. she doesn't care. she is literally badgering me that i need medication. i'm arguing back. this is so not what i need in a doctor's office! she does a physical exam that i would call cursory at best and then says she wants to do blood tests in case i have diabetes. ok, i wanted to do blood tests too, but why hone in on diabetes? i had recently lost 50 pounds, which i told her, and no longer fit into even the overweight category based on my bmi, just normal. so why assume i'll have diabetes? and again she's yelling at me for no reason. this is literally the worst doctor i've ever met in any setting in my entire life.

she tells me to get dressed and leaves and then comes back to take my blood pressure again. wtf! she's been screaming at me and badgering me the entire time she's in the room, then gets me up and moving around to get dressed, and now somehow thinks i'll be relaxed? so i call her out on it all. the waiting, the attitude, her terrible demeanor- and she tells me the wait was due to a medical emergency and if she didn't keep me waiting, someone else could have died. funny, i didn't see an ambulance arrive and carry anyone out, so let's not misrepresent ourselves here!!

even on check out, there is a huge sign that says something like check out here. the woman was on the phone and just waved me past. what now? where to go? the main check in spot had a line of 6 people - i'm sure not going to do that twice! so i just left.

i didn't bother getting the blood tests, since i never want to go back there or talk to anyone from that office. but i wasted my once a year physical benefit and now can't get those blood tests until i find a new doctor...next year. i continue to monitor my blood pressure at home regularly, it is totally normal when i'm not enraged and engaged in a screaming match with someone. i will most definitely not ever step foot in this office again.

i've had aud (alcohol use disorder) for about 40 years. i've tried everything: hypnosis, acupuncture, years on antabuse, 6 months and then 7 years sober in aa in 2000s. each relapse turned into a several weeks long binge, forcing me to seek help again. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe limits and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak - until covid struck. 

i live alone, the lockdown made me seriously depressed. all my routines and nearly all social contacts were broken and it felt like a solitary confinement. at some point in april, i stopped taking my medication as prescribed by the sinclair method. from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge. by may 13 i had to go to er and then to a 10 days detox in holister; spent the first night in icu nearly having a heart attack. after i got back home on sunday may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds left from my last refill); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

in the meantime, my gf discovered the intensive outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i got a double diagnosis and could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not feeling up to getting back to work immediately. on thursday, may 28 i was there and talked to marcella (admissions) dr khan (sp? md), nurse diane and some other people. i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it.

thursday and friday sessions were pretty nice, with meditation, some cbt and open discussions on topics suggested by patients themselves. and then, on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i keep up the  controlled drinking, i have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could easily refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- i researched it, and it has about the same success rate as aa - which is in single digits - whereas sinclair method has success rate near 80%". "- i don't care. this program requires full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

there are several things that really upset and anger me. 
1) why did dr bradley prescribe my medicine all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 
2) how does a doctor refer a patient to some program the name of which he can't even remember? does he know anything about it? or he just doesn't care?
3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions, knowing dr bradley's views and giving me false hopes? 
4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rate and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (5 years probation). he also was known to be sending referrals to and working at a couple of shady rehabs ran by an uncertified drug addict.

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director at well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of staff seems to be ok, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

review:
let me begin by saying that i did not want to be there.  i was facing that regular screening test/procedure that is gifted to you as you pass the milestone of turning 50.  yeah - that one.  i will not go into the prep and how unreasonable and stupid it is - having accomplished this same goal with other methods of roto-rooting the pipes which we were much more palatable and equally effective.

i also won't b**ch and moan about having to get a covid test and quarantine prior to the procedure - only to be surrounded by staff who had not been covid tested or quarantined so i was clearly the one at risk.

instead, i'll start with the fact that i was pleasantly greeted, promptly processed and flew through the bureaucracy and hoops to jump through.  my nurse assigned to me was super sweet which made the process so comfortable.  to back up, i was grouchy getting there, but the first person i spoke with re: patients rights and billing was so funny and nice - it immediately turned my mood around.  how could i possibly spew the venom that had built up when every person i came in contact with was nicer than the last.

i was the first person on the line up so i could not get ready fast enough.  fine by me!  the staff was not nit-picky and didn't make me take off my wyze band - the only piece of jewelry i still wore - to see the time (and get my steps in).  i had a nice warm blanket to cuddle under, the nurse did a fantastic job of getting the iv in, everything was great.

in the procedure room the entire staff was female!  yay us!  the doctor was young'ish and clearly competent and all the personnel worked well together and clearly liked each other.  they hit me with the meds - but i never feel asleep.  instead i watched my innards in high def.  i didn't feel any discomfort or pain - the really important part.

soon enough, the procedure was over, they unhooked me, reviewed my results and sent me on my way.  i was home within 2 hours of my initial appointment time (wow!) and felt absolutely fine so logged into work and shortened my 1/2 off to just a couple hours.  amazing!

i highly recommend you go here for your medical care.  also - get that first appointment and be early to it.  be nice to your staff as they sure are nice to you.  while i won't be back soon (knock on wood, fingers crossed), i'd gladly return here in 10 years when i'll get this done again!

i've been here 4x with hyperemesis in my first pregnancy. my favorite er person was a resident dr, dr. khavarian because each time i went he talked to me calmly and not rushing, asked me questions, checked on me often and explained everything he did or did not do. brandon the lead nurse was also very kind, knowledgeable and caring each time i saw him too. a host of lady nurses were also very caring and treated me with such respect even though i often looked like death in there! i had a bad experience with resident dr. gomez who prescribed a med i was allergic to (noted in my chart) for an infection that i didn't even have. scary to take that unnecessary risk with a baby in my belly but luckily i got a second opinion from my primary and didn't end up taking the med. anyway, i was admitted the fourth time i went in and put on the oncology floor to protect me and baby from covid exposure. the entire oncology nursing staff was superb for the five days i was there. they were so personable & kind. my condition didn't improve at first & eventually required me to be on a medicine that has a small risk to the baby which the nurse and i had spoken about prior to dr prescribing it. (several obgyn drs also spoke to me about this in depth) so when it was time for my first dose, the nurse came in and said she had just read up on it and wanted to triple check if i was comfortable taking it before giving it to me. she took time to read up on it and ask me in private so i didn't feel pressured into it! because of the no visitations due to covid, i felt alone but each nurse would chat with me, share stories & generally make me feel comfortable and help pass the time. the level of respect, professionalism and care (physical & emotional) they gave me was unmatched. because of these wonderful folks i am now considering delivering my baby at this hospital. i really appreciate each of them and hope this praise gets back to them somehow. s/o to dr. wong, dr. hodges, & oncology nurses saba, angela, dennis, pamela, & i forgot the last two names  but thank you for saving me all with kindness & grace!

mountainview hospital has adequate supplies of ppe. the problem is that the hospital is not giving those supplies to the nurses who are currently on the front lines working with covid-19+ patients on a daily basis. worse even, they are not allowing nurses to protect themselves when they have the ability to do so. this is not in alignment with what you say is the hospital's top priority of "protecting your patients, clinicians, nurses and colleagues so you can best serve our communities..." in fact, it seems quite the opposite, it would almost appear as though your policies are directly intended to put our patients, clinicians, nurses and colleagues at a greater risk.

here are the facts about what mountainview hospital is doing at this moment:

* a nurse is only given an n95 rated respirator if they are working directly with a covid-19+ patient that is undergoing aerosol treatments while the nurse providing care to this patient.
* a nurses is only allowed to wear a surgical mask around covid-19+ patients who are not undergoing aerosol treatments as well as all others that are presumed to have covid-19 but are waiting the 3-5 days it takes for test results to come back. 
* nurses who bring in their own n95 or kn95 rated respirators are required to remove them and replace them with the hospital supplied surgical mask.
* doctors seem to have a different set of rules that apply to them as doctors have been observed wearing n95 respirator brought in from home under their surgical masks without recourse. however, your nurses have been told if they attempt to wear an n95 or kn95 respirator, even under their surgical masks, they will be required to leave the hospital and not be allowed to return until they submit to the hospital's ludicrous policies. 

remember, our nurses and doctors live at home with their families and loved ones. if they catch this nasty virus, they bring it home to us as well. your hospital's policies are a possible death sentence to not only your own staff but to our entire community!

what i would like to understand is what is the harm in allowing a nurse to wear an n95 or kn95 mask which they bring in themselves and is very likely to provide much more protection than the hospital supplied surgical mask which has been cited even by the cdc to be inadequate protection against covid-19? our nurses and doctors are the most at-risk people in our community. we already have communities around the world where 20-30 percent of health-care professionals in a region have become infected with the virus. what is the hospital's thinking here in requiring better protection to be removed?

the hospital doesn't compare well to other hospitals in vegas. lack of attention to detail and the staff aren't always the most patient. cleanliness is another issue, compare them to other hospitals and you may be surprised.

review: memorial hermann is the most difficult organization i've ever had to work with. let me start out by saying that the doctors, nurses, and other staff receive 5 stars, even the food was pretty good. however, their billing department is the most backwards, confusing, difficult department i've ever encountered. you would think a large, million dollar organization like memorial hermann would be more put together in this area. needing a payment plan for any bills? you can sign up online only to realize their "online system doesn't *always* sync with their regular system" (???). your payment will come out every month, but you'll still receive statements and calls about a past due balance (???). need to update the card on file? make sure you call at least twice because they definitely won't be able to get it done on the first try (or second try at this point). want to have email statements instead of paper statements? ive asked several customer service reps to take care of this yet i still receive them via mail (and sure this isn't that big of a deal but when you receive eight different statements / payment plan reminders / past due (but not really past due) items in the mail in a single week it can get pretty overwhelming). i've called their billing department roughly 20+ times in the last 6 months to discuss bills. on numerous occasions i've mentioned that i wish i could view all my bills in one place because each bill having a separate account number is really confusing. it wasn't until today that someone said "oh you can view them on the everyday well app". don't even get me started on the fact that we were told that our physical therapy would be covered at 100% only to receive $330 and $470 bills later on (just tell people you don't know! don't lie!) it shouldn't be this difficult to get care for my family and then pay for it??

early this morning, my sister woke up with intense abdominal pains, trouble breathing, fainting spells, and clammy skin. without hesitation and very concerned for her wellbeing, as any family would be, we called 911, explained her symptoms, and the 911 dispatch sent an ambulance over. she was quickly rushed to the hospital. given the current times and covid-19, we were unable to join her, only able to communicate with her via text message when she was passingly lucid. she began receiving treatment and testing to find the source of the problem but during that time, her nurse, a man named david, became increasingly critical of her and our usage of 911 to get her to the hospital. why anyone would feel the need to criticize someone for this is beyond frustrating. my sister, laid out in a hospital bed, fighting the previously mentioned symptoms, was forced to defend herself and told david that he was being rude. again, why should someone in her position be forced to defend herself? my sister then overheard david talking poorly about her to another employee out in the hall, continuing to criticize her for using an ambulance to get to the hospital. there isn't any logic in his stance and if anything, it's just absolutely heartless. my family and i have been going to doctors hospital for decades and have never experienced anything like this. we hope something is done about nurse david so that people seeking help and treatment don't have to suffer criticism for doing so.

my mother was here for 2 weeks following a mild stroke. the staff were never too busy to stop and help or answer questions. my mother felt safe and she absolutely adored the nurses! 5 star compassion and care!

sadly had to use facility for an emergency with my mom- thankful they are allowing 1 person to be with patient- not one person at a time but the same person for that particular day. staff were professional and attentive. followed safe guidelines- they are testing all patients for covid unless patient states otherwise. clean facility- was quiet- room was a double room but most of time there my mom was in the room alone. free parking, mom said food was ok.

during these stressful times amid covid 19 the staff was amazingly professional, proactive and sensitive to the patients and their visitors.

review:

button for help. as my family watched him deteriorate at your hospital we voiced our concerns and tried more than once to get him transferred. we were met with complete disregard for our concerns and told the only way to get him out would be an emergency transfer. that happened shortly after as my stepdad was in cardiac and septic shock because his sepsis was not properly addressed. my mom and sister walked into his room to see him flailing and struggling for his life. doctors and nurses standing around his bed watching. a nurse told my mom "this has been going on all day, we're not sure what's going on". no one had called to inform my mom of this and it was into the afternoon. my sister snapped and asked if this was enough of an emergency to transfer him to ohsu now???  reluctantly than we do to go through the court system.

excellent experience. my surgeon dr. frank valone is outstanding. other doctors on call, like dr. but were wonderful. all the nurses was kind and attentive. shonda was especially nice during the night shift.

review:
i went here for my first labor of my baby girl. while in labor i asked them to take a biopsy since i had my epidural and i needed to know what was wrong with my skin.  after weeks of never hearing results i finally called them just to have them tell me they lost my biopsy. no one bothered to call me and they didn't offer any compensation what so ever just said to get a new one at my six week appointment. so now after i'm just healing from literally pushing a human being out of me i have to get numbed again, have them take the biopsy and more stitches.  this is the last thing i need to be worrying about after i just had my first baby that is stressful enough. not to mention i needed the results because breast feeding has been abnormally painful due to my skin problem and having those answers could have saved me a lot of tears and money spent on lactation specialists just to be told it's a skin condition and i need a steroid to make it manageable. 

secondi will never be returning here again! 

update, they have confirmed that they are doing absolutely in compensation for me for losing my biopsy. even though i owe them $5,000 after my insurance!  this absolutely insane and i cannot believe they are getting away with such negligence. if lawyers weren't so expensive i would be suing!  i'm beyond disappointed. 

i'm severely disappointed in your lack of a resolution. i've exhausted all the time i have, which i'm sure was your goal in the plethora of pointless emails back and forth. i hope this never happens to another girl again and you've learned from your mistakes. i will not give up in telling people my experience and how awful you all were  i'm going to make sure all the people i know don't come to you so they don't have to go through anything even close to what i had.  i'm beyond disappointed, exhausted and frustrated by how everything was handled.  i'm glad my baby is alive and has no birth defects, for that is the only reason i'm not pursuing legal action at this time.  thank you for wasting so much of my time that i could've spent with my new baby.

do yourself a favor and make the drive to jupiter medical center if you can. the emergency room nurses are indifferent and incompetent. i can't give specifics, because of pending legal action. but if you have any other options do not go here. i would have given 0 stars if i could.

review: sorry must give a review here.  my dad went in low some chest pain over easter weekend and they kept him there for 5 days pending angiogram.  five days later he had a stent placed in his artery.  the next morning he dropped dead. why were his leads not on him the next day? was he even being watched over?  i could not be there myself to advocate for him during the times of covid and visitation restrictions.  he called for help and who knows how long it took someone to come help him. when the leads were put back on him (again, why were they off?) he was in v tach. i'm hearing more and more that this "heart hospital" isn't as great as it used to be.  maybe the cardiac docs  are world class... i am not so sure about support staff.  my last conversation with my father was him telling me that drs and nurses were having a party as he lie in the recovery area post angiogram/pci.  my dad was my gold and unfortunately they robbed me of many years with him.  when i asked the dr what went wrong he told me it could be like 8 things... in my heart i feel like he should have been monitored more closely in the end.  if your loved ones is getting a pci/stent make sure they are highly monitored throughout! the report was that he did excellent, better than ever.  and then poof! gone!

when i was 17 i had a breast reduction done here because i was constantly having pain in my shoulders and back.  my breast came out uneven, the scars heales nicely but my nipples were not placed correctly.

i also had my 3 children at hcmc and i had all c-sections and the scar caused my stomach to look uneven and like there is a dent in my belly.

i have been completely self conscious about my body since my divorce almost 10 years ago.

i switched to children's and allina for my children and myself. i haven't trusted hcmc since.

so far i am very impressed. i've only had video visits and went in once for tests but everyone i have dealt with has been super friendly and helpful.  even with slight bumps i was never made to feel like something was my fault which is great.  i deal with a lot of doctors offices for all my ailments so to finally have one where all of the office staff is professional is a wonderful change from what i usually have to deal with.  i'm with dr. jon bigler and his assistant celeste (she's beyond fantastic always takes care of things quickly and efficiently), dr. bigler has also been great, hasn't recommended anything i thought was weird, is aware of how his office works and what to do, listens to what i say, explains why we're doing one thing and not another, what next steps will be so it's really been great to have a clear plan and feel like my health actually matters.

im never going to this hospital. my mom got sick of the stomach flu and my dad took her to this hospital because we live in town. my mom told me that it was the worst experience ever. she had to go back there for almost a week until they told my dad that my mom needed to go to another hosptial. when my dad called to know how my mom was doing, the nurse said that the information isnt to be given to him and hung up. so i called and the nurse and the doctor were rude to me. huge difference in merced. dont waste your time here.

continued.......

the staff mike , robert, tabitha, the pregnant room attendant with her beautiful smile and positive outlook, dr lachina, sheila, macy,  adriana   all the staff victor came in touch with but can't remember their names.  i am eternally grateful for and for you teaching victor tenacity and that he can do it.  if there were ten star rating you would get it from me and victor.  you know what it is about and you are there to make it happen if the patient wants it to happen

coming in, the temperature nurse was really sweet and brought me a chair to sit in while filling out the paperwork. they brought me in after a few mins to get my history, vitals and blood draw to check my troponin.

triage nurse and ecg tech were very friendly. nurse told me they're probably going to monitor me to make sure everything's okay. 
i head back out to the hallway and finish the paperwork..

1.5 hours pass and i'm nodding off in the hard plastic chair. butt is numb and i feel cold. 
i ask the registration if they could inquire if i was going to be monitored like i was told (and what usually happens when i go to er).

the nurse comes out and says they're gonna do a 2nd blood draw after 2 hours. i ask about the monitoring, and she says they're just gonna take my ecg again with the 2nd blood draw... this was news to me. 
we vibed well but it didn't help with the miscommunication.. the reason i wasn't getting taken in was cause they were full, but just a little communication goes a long way.

after waiting 2 hours, i asked registration if i could just know what my initial vitals and labs were. 
every time i spoke with the older lady, she made me feel like i was such a bother, when all i wanted was some communication. she literally told me nothing other than they don't see that info and the charge nurse never got back to her (only after i stood near the registration window for 5 mins, sat back down and asked about my results the second time 15 mins later!)
this was what really discredited my experience at bhh. 
at my hospital, they require us to maintain communication with our patients regarding any delays and reason for delays so they stay in the loop instead of sitting out there wondering and getting frustrated; to acknowledge patients without attitude. 

man, this made me wish i just stayed home. 

after i was taken to draw labs for the second test, i asked the rn if they could just call me if anything was up. i was cold, tired, and very uncomfortable. 

the er doctor, who was very cutthroat and straight to the point (i dig that), came to meet me after i mentioned i wished to leave. he ended up seeing me twice and said "i'm happy to share good news..."  

i believe that i'm a very patient person. i understand that extended wait times happen. miscommunication happens as well, but complete lack of it and attitude was not something i came there for. i come in respectful and optimistic about the care and experience i will have, but that really turned me off. 

so, all in all, mixed feelings about bhh, but i would not come back.

i've been coming to methodist for my obgyn needs for a few years now.  in, fact i delivered my son here!  this review is a bit bittersweet as my current health insurance carrier is terminating their relationship with methodist, so looks like i'm going to have to seek out a new practice and that makes me grumpy!

anyway, as with most doctor's offices - wait times can be rather atrocious so i would advise trying to take the earliest appointment in the morning or the first available after lunch.  they do tend to run further and further behind as the day progresses (this is common with most medical practices), so just bear that in mind and bring along a book or your ipad (there's free wifi).  i've been a patient of two doctors in the obstetrics and gynecology department and i've been pleased with the interactions and quality of care i received.  even the front desk staff, techs, and nurses have been understanding and patient, even when i've been disheveled and bewildered (as a first time pregnant lady can sometimes be).

i was especially pleased with my stay in the childbirth center.  it's a smaller labor and delivery area compared to some other hospitals in the medical center, which i feel facilitated a quieter and calmer stay, and it enabled the nurses and staff to provide more individualized attention to me and other patients.  granted, i only have this one experience to draw my opinion from, but the nurses were just so extraordinarily kind and helpful during my stay here.  almost two years later, my husband still brings up how lovely everyone was to us during our brief three day stay here.  i had a traumatic (but not life-threatening) postpartum complication that was rather unpleasant to deal with and the nurses really busted their butts to make me comfortable as possible and continuously tried to seek a resolution to my issue.

anyway, highly recommend methodist - especially for the obstetrics and gynecology department and the childbirth center.  hopefully i'll be able to return to the hospital in the future, should my insurance get their crap together.

given the specifics of this person's medical history and the changes he has recently faced, as verified by other medical professionals in my family who work in successful emergency departments, this is an acuity 2 altered mental status, which can be caused by delirium triggered by an underlying infection or other serious medical problem. this warranted workup. period. 

this is nothing below the level of gross negligence. we do have a plan to seek competent medical care, but we should have already received it. i look forward to a personal phone call from the er director to discuss this further.

review:
well, i guess spring break will become a do not leave the house practice in future years.
last year it was the hubster who after a gentle nudge from one of our 100 pound retrievers fell forward down the steps and broke his ankle on the second day of our camping excursion. (unfortunately misdiagnosed by an urgent care facility near walker, tx.)
this year it was my turn. i was backing down the steps to be more able to open the door wider to accommodate me and several items i had in my hands. well dang if i didn't miss a couple steps and felt myself falling backwards onto the concrete slab shared with our rv. i had time to say "oh no" before  a hard landing -not sure if i stuck my head first or my tailbone first but i had the wind knocked out of me (and since i haven't ever experienced that) i panicked thinking i was not going to start breathing again. i was unable to get up and thankfully some camping neighbors came over and after a few minutes were able to help me stand. by that time my son and daughter-in-law and hubby had arrived. my head was not bleeding but had quite a nice goose egg with colorful abrasions and  along with my tailbone (which i had fractured years ago),
and then a cut and abrasion on my elbow. i was convinced that it would be best to go get examined so agreed to go to an urgent care. sadly, the urgent care didn't have the capability to do skull  x-rays or a ct scan which the physician assistant felt was necessary to determine that i did not have any internal bleeding or swelling in my brain .
she called the emergency room at this local hospital and informed them i would be headed that way. the urgent care was really awesome, i could feel the compassion by the pa and she knew i did not want to go to the er but strongly encouraged me, so off we went.
of course this is when the coronavirus had started to manifest itself in texas so there were many precautions once we entered the emergency room waiting area.  upon our arrival we presented at the registration area-explained the situation and advised that the urgent care pa had called ahead. he advised that he just come on shift and didn't know anything about it. that was certainly understandable but he didn't offer to go and ask anyone either. took all my insurance and payment info and sent us out to sit in the waiting room.
don't get me wrong, i fully believe that people should be triaged and treated accordingly but i was surprised that we waited an hour to even go back to be examined in a pre-entrance room. the two nurses that assessed me decided they needed to apply a cervical collar-ugh. they did ask my head pain level which was a 10 at that time. they put me in a w/c and they brought me to my er room. we saw a nurse almost immediately who hooked me up to all the devices they like to apply to monitor you, asked me to rate my pain (still 10). she said i would be going for a ct scan shortly and then would see the doctor. it was evident they were quite busy-which they said had become routine there over the last couple of years. 3 hours later a very nice physician arrived and was dismayed that i had not had a ct scan yet. she advised that the collar could not be removed until after i had had the scan. she asked about my pain level which had subsided to about a 7 on its own. although i reported my other injuries they were so focused on my brain they never assessed them. obviously, the potential for brain injury was the most urgent but the injury to my tailbone was preventing me from walking without quite a bit of discomfort and my elbow wound turned into a burning pain whenever i accidentally touched it on anything-and the pain was not at the site of the abrasion. the md went out to the desk and put in a stat order for the ct.
an hour and 15 minutes later someone from the ct department came to get me. they took me for the ct and then back to my er room in 10 minutes time. 90 minutes later my doctor returned (after i had put my call light on and requested they find out if the c-collar could be removed yet) she removed the c-collar (yay!) and reported there was no evidence of any brain bleeding or swelling and that she would be discharging me.(double yay!)
the nurse came in to discuss discharge instructions by which time i was up dressed and ready to go. so back to the campgrounds we went.
i felt very bad that my son had sat with me all those hours, and was exposed to heaven knows what...with other er patients going up and down the hall to get to the bathroom with their gowns and masks on and coughing and hacking the whole way.  ok-i do realize that being a nurse makes me very annoyed when i feel like there are inappropriate delays in care of any kind. god knows if i had had a brain bleed what kind of condition i would've been in after 4+ hours of waiting for a scan. if you follow me at all you also know that i am a stickler about excellent customer service. in all honesty, i would not return here.

on june 26th, 2020 i brought my father to chomp because he was suffering from terrible chest pain after a fall. his face was extremely swollen and he also had a terrible black eye. 
the check in process went very well and he was immediately given an ekg to check his heart. 
afterwards he and i were taken to the emergency room nr 32.
registration came after an hour of he and i waiting without being seen by a nurse or anyone. 
after 2 hours of waiting the doctor came in with a nurse. i explained my father has severe alzheimer's and doesn't understand what's going on. the doctor ordered several tests. 
well the lab came immediately and drew some blood. however during all this waiting my father was becoming agitated and upset. 
he was pulling of the wires etc for the monitor.
i immediately called for help and the nurse came with the doctor. 
my poor father was confused upset and extremely aggressive. well the hospital says they can't help people in this type of situation and sent us home. this is the 2nd time chomp has refused to help my father and i.
the last time was in january and my father ended up in a veterans hospital. 
i am very disappointed that community hospital isn't trained better to help people with alzheimer's or dementia. 
twice i was left dealing with an upset old man having a tantrum and melt down. 
my drive home was horrible and dangerous. 
i don't blame the doctor but blame the hospital for not giving a damn about mental illness and the elderly.

review: if you need open-heart surgery, you've come to the right place. chomp has their tyler heart institute.  had the surgery a few years ago.  before the surgery there's a pre-op meeting, where you meet most of the team who will be working on you, and a few checks are run on you.  when you come in for the surgery, the people working there get you all shaved and ready to go.  went in around 6 a.m. on a monday.  woke up in the icu around 5 p.m. the next day.  the surgeon, dr. gaudiani, ended up doing more than expected, so i had a leg bandaged as well as all sorts of tubes in me.  remember two of the icu nurses, jim and veronica.  great nurses.  remember veronica taking out the breathing tube.  felt like i couldn't breathe.  "i can't breathe!" veronica - "sure, you can!"  and i breathed.  got out of the icu into a "regular" room.  started doing some walking around the floor.  will never forget a mrs. dutt, apparently a nurse's aide, who helped me get to the shower and kept an eye on me as i got cleaned up.  very nice lady, very helpful.  food was very good.  on thursday asked dr. spowart, dr. gaudiani's partner, if i could go home.  "yes".  went home the next day, so overall about four days total.   chomp does great work, but it isn't cheap, at least on the face of it.  bill for the four-day stay was about $230,000.  but my insurance had a contract with the hospital - they actually paid just over $58,000.  my copayment was $11/day, or $44.  when i got the bill, which was a good third of an inch thick, i sent chomp a check for $44, and everyone was happy.  my wife had a knee replaced at chomp.  great care.  other family members have been cared for at chomp, too.

review:
this is for the physical therapy department only.  

i've had the unfortunate luck of having multiple joint replacements and other orthopedic surgeries (before becoming kaiser member) at a young age. the reasons why were never clear though many doctors have tried to figure it out.  the most common theory is that because i have hypermobility but was very active from a young age, this has deteriorated my muscle skeletal structure and started a domino effect. 

i had good physical therapy following my surgeries and the replaced joints are not a problem.  however, i continue to experience profound pain and discomfort on my right hip which is my one remaining major natural joint.  x-rays show no reason for this. i went to kaiser pt multiple times but found that the treatments actually worsened the pain.  when i eventually said this to the pt (actually a very nice guy) he basically threw up his hands.  

this issue has affected me greatly and i am in constant pain regardless of trying things like meditation, turmeric, foam rolling, etc. etc.  i've even had to resort to strong opioids left over from my surgeries even though i had weaned off long ago. i finally decided to bite the bullet and pay out of pocket for a place recommended by a neighbor.  i had immediate relief after the first session.  here's what they do that kaiser pt does not:

- you do the exercises with the therapist monitoring as opposed to going home with an exercise sheet. this allows you to report areas of pain or discomfort as you do the exercises and it also allows them to try other things while making note of your comments.

- hyper-mobile people have distinct needs, and therapy modes that work for most may well not work for them or have to be adjusted. i'm now working with someone who specialists in hypermobile patients.

- the new place truly deep dives into diagnosis.  muscle skeletal issues are complex and there are a diverse set of reasons why x may hurt.  you may have weak hips, but your issue may go beyond that and there may be a reason as to why your hips are perpetually weak.  kaiser pt is great for people who neatly fall into the bucket of widely known issues and common prescriptions, but for people who need a more individualized care it is a black hole. 

- i barely did any exercises in person with kaiser, so needless to say they did not help with any stretching whatsoever. in my case, though i'm double jointed there are a couple of tight areas that i simply cannot stretch on my own.  the new pt recognizes how crucial this is, and i can attest to the importance of this.

i really like kaiser in many ways, but in terms of pt the experience has been literally painful.  i've asked permission for an outside pt referral but if you're familiar with kaiser you understand how almost impossible that is.  this is a shame because i've probably cost them more money in terms of constant doctor appointments, mris, x-rays, etc. than what they could have paid for an outside pt for a few months. i could only afford to pay out of pocket for just a few sessions so i now spend hours each day doing self pt at home.  the personal cost of being in pain is enormous  - financially, emotionally, and socially.  i truly wish that an excellent organization like kaiser, which seems to genuinely care about public health, would take another approach to their treatment of physical therapy and pain management.

it has been 37 days since i last was able to see my son who is only 62 days old and still in the nicu - all because of a covid visitation policy at texas children's that is excessive, insensitive to parent's/ patient's well-being and out of line with nearly all surrounding hospitals.  37 days i have been prevented from holding him, watching him grow, and having critical moments of bonding.

see the attached list of medical center hospitals and several near my home in cypress.   none of them have adopted the excessive policy of one visitor per stay.   i personally called each of these hospitals and was furious to find how out of line tch's policy is, especially since when i argued my case to the nursing director for the texas children's newborn center she told me that tch's visitor policy was enacted as part of a unified visitation policy with all other medical center hospitals -  which was either a baseless assumption or gross misrepresentation.  it should also be noted that when we were originally told about the policy, the nurse manager told us that the policy was being mandated from the state and that tch had no choice but to comply - which was a total fabrication.   texas health and human service commission has stated "our most recent guidance to hospitals allows them to permit patient family members, one at a time, to visit their loved ones in the hospital."     

how is tch so out of line with their competitors? why are they so unsympathetic to the needs of their patient and their families?  
not to mention that the policy itself is illogical - my wife and i live and breathe in the same household - we represent the same risk factor & germ pool.   i understand limiting the number of visitors in the hospital at any given time, but allowing parents living in the same household to switch daily would not increase the level of statistical risk for the hospital. your intent here was well placed, but the excessive (& out of line) policy that you have drawn is causing harm to parents and preemie babies and without any real benefit.  

so in conclusion tch has a visitation policy that is dramatically more harsh than their peers, that is causing real harm to patients/ their families and doesn't make their patients any more safe.   

i have worked with child advocacy multiple times and spoken to hospital administrators, they all recognize the policy does not make logical sense, but they are either unwilling or incapable to make humane, logical, reasonable accommodations.

brought 74 year old wife, with mild dementia, who had taken a fall at house, to emergency entrance,  was accompanied by 46 year old son.  found out later  through x-rays, she had dislocated shoulder and was in great pain.  was bared from entering door from lot entrance when she was being wheeled in.  the ultra hype concerning covid-19 had transformed all personel encountered at entrance to robots with zero empathy and concern.  my wife was scared, in pain and wanted me by her side, but i was told "no visitors".  the "rent a cop" at the door threatened to have me removed from the parking lot if i kept loudly complaining.  what a power trip he was on!

bottom line:  worst experience ever in an emergency department.   all our regular doctors work out of the methodist system and i have had many interactions with their emergency departments.  night and day difference in all respects.  i know this covid-19 is very serious, but the hype it has created seems to be removing all humanity and sanity from the treatment patients are getting, especially if you come in for anything else but covid-19

i was transferred to john muir inpatient from contra costa regional medical center's psychiatric emergency services (ccrmc, pes) located in martinez. john muir was definitely an upgrade, but i suppose anything would be better than pes.

i had 2 inpatient stays, both in february 2020. the first was from february 6 to february 10. the second was from february 18 to february 26. the first discharge was premature, but the second one was helpful in my recovery.

i was admitted on the second day of my 5150 (72 hour hold) as i had attempted suicide. the remainder of the stay was on a voluntary basis as i was willing to comply with treatment. the oak adult unit has friendly staff. most of them aren't licensed therapists, but they are still knowledgeable in various therapy concepts. i really enjoyed the groups, especially expressive arts. the registered nurses are professional and check in with you frequently to make sure you are safe. 

the psychiatrist i worked with, dr. mundi, is a jerk. when i shared what had pushed me to hurt myself, he was very dismissive. i made sure to let the staff know, and was assigned to a nurse practitioner during my second inpatient stay.

the food is really good. they really care about their patients health, both physical and mental. we had patio breaks throughout the day which was our only time to get fresh air. the nurses giving medication were very nice and helped me understand the specifics such as side effects and a time frame to notice improved mood.

naturally, i was home sick, but we were allowed to have visitors and access to a phone to call our family. the rooms had 2 beds, and a bathroom with a shower. 

the reason i was admitted again was because the first discharge was premature. the post discharge care plan did not work, and no one followed up with me despite me leaving several voicemails. fortunately, the second time around the post discharge care plan worked great and i was able to get a referral for further care at a crisis residental, hope house in martinez.

i give john muir behavioral health 4 stars. the facilty was clean, the staff was nice, the rooms were safe, and the food was good. there were rounds conducted every 15 minutes to make sure everyone was accounted for. it may affect your sleep, but the staff tries to be very quiet. safety is very important, so it didn't bother me.

on a side note, my very first inpatient stay was at fremont hospital in 2018. though the facilty was bigger and had a pool and court, i felt the staff was very impersonal. john muir behavioral health may not have all the extra features fremont hospital has, but quality is better than quantity. you are seen as a person, not as your diagnosis. 

we occasionally had students from samuel merritt take our vitals, all of whom were very nice. overall, this was a good experience and helped me grow. i doubt i will ever return because i now know how to cope in times of emotional distress. but i feel reassured knowing a place like john muir behavioral health exists. 

if i were to give any advice, it would be to speak with your social worker regarding care post discharge. this is very important. if you are troubled, you can talk with the staff. every shift each patient is assigned a registered nurse, mental health counselor, and social worker. they will listen.

thank you john muir staff.
fac_name: John Muir Health Behavioral Health Center, Inpatient Services

(there's always going to be one or more that wasn't stellar in any setting ....). the best worker was the lowest ranking one.  after i could finally make my way to the bathroom after i had my surgery, after i finished, she said, "do you want me to wipe your butt?"  music to my ears as none of the higher level nursing staff would have offered. fortunately i didn't need that help.

after finally getting him stabilized, it was time to get him moved to an acute care facility nearby and for days, they kept telling us that they would prepare him for the move and have him transferred on a monday. by the end of the day monday, when no one showed up to give direction on his move, come to find out the administrative staff never sent the paperwork over to the acute care facility!!!! more days went by as they finally sent the paperwork in (in order to clear his insurance and move the case over), then after 3 days of no answers...come to find out, they sent the paperwork to the wrong department!! so again, we go back into the loop of administrative stuff with no answers as to when he will be moved. he continues to sit in icu just twiddling his thumbs waiting to move to the new facility while the team at st. mary's piddles around, racking up his hospital bill (thank goodness for insurance). 

my biggest complaint is how poor the communication is within this facility. there is poor communication between the doctor and the patient, between the doctors themselves, nursing staff, administrative staff.....in general, the communication level has been so poor that 1-star seems too high of a rating. if you just talk to someone and keep them updated, you'll have more informed and happy patients...period, even if you aren't 100% sure with what is wrong you just need to keep everyone informed. it's not hard or complicated. my guess is if they would have communicated better, we would have had a more decent experience.....oh, and work on your administrative staff...what a shame. and leaving a patient in soiled linens for over an hour???? that is completely unacceptable!!!
