pulled off 2 more- nothing. i guess no one is paying attention to the telemetry? i completely understand that a doctor can only do so much based on what they can see. and my tests weren't screaming anything alarming. but i told my attending over and over i felt like i could not breathe and i really didn't care for the nonchalant responses. i asked to go home. here we are today and i'm still having difficulty breathing, but now have a pleural effusion and decreasing 02 stats. i would really love to ask that doctor how many times anxiety has caused those symptoms. and still covid negative! y'all need to retrain on that floor.

he is a great doctor! i would never trade him in for a new one. he actively listens and has great follow through. he also has good bedside manners.
thanks brett hinton~

bureaucracy and poor care.   i had a hard time getting through to my mom - took half an hour for them to simply go to her room and put the phone near her - had to talk to several different people, e.g., a secretary, the wrong nurse, etc.   then they released her - at night - with a broken shoulder, with no care, no treatment plan.   my mother has dementia, and was found the next morning on the floor, apparently had tried to get to the bathroom on her own and never made it.    i complained but they never responded.   go elsewhere if you can.

horrible horrible experience. from the moment my son and i went in the medical assistant failed to take the height and body weight... went to check his blood pressure and grabbed the blood pressure cuff away hard. they refused to give us a work note. and the second time we went they charged us $60 for another doc note due to the doc not being there. not my problem i work in dental office and i know that office has records of the patient along with doc notes in hand for when patients request these matters. worst urgent care ever. its not worth your time for a check up when they only last 3 minutes.

this review is for the psych unit only.
i couldn't have been treated any better. the nurses
and the rest of the staff are very kind and 
professional. this is important to me when i'm 
in a delicate state.

no one reads reviews of hospitals, but i'm so angry i had to leave something, somewhere.

i've been seen here during a fairly normal pregnancy, with a c-section delivery (unavoidable - complications made it necessary and i believe my doctor made the right call!)  i loved my ob and my care team, and all the nurses were kind and capable.  i chose to be seen here, since a small community hospital tends to provide more personal care than in a metropolitan one, where i felt like a number.

this review is for their billing & record keeping, which is an actual nightmare.  i've encountered multiple issues, including but not limited to:

- having to review the same printouts at every single visit because for some reason, no doctor ever noted that i've seen them.  not a big deal but there's more - 

- they ask for prepayment, so when i transferred there around 25 weeks or so, they asked me for monthly payments of $600.  l o l that's ridiculous.  i spoke to a manager who thankfully, agreed that was preposterous and let me pay afterward

- during my hospital stay someone from billing came in and asked for payment!  i paid it because i thought i was doing the right thing, except....

- i didn't owe that amount.  they hadn't even checked with insurance to see if i owed it.  i was so exhausted from giving birth i didn't realize it.

- so i paid them my entire out of pocket maximum and they're still billing me for other things!  shouldn't happen, and they should have taken it out of what i've already paid them.

- called me within two weeks of my daughter being born antagonizing me for not having added her to my insurance.  chill.  i'm working on it.  i have a month per the insurance company to add her.

- they set it to self-pay when they didn't get payment immediately.  guys!

- they call me months later to say i owe this amount....i ask my insurance to look for it and they can't find the claims.  turns out, they used my name but my daughter's dob.

are you kidding?  i'm waiting on my refund, by the way, of that out of pocket maximum i paid to them.  meanwhile other collectors are calling me asking for their payment, which i could have used that money for.  this is a total nightmare, and they are completely inept.  i'm working it all out with them, but it never should have happened in the first place.  beware.  if you have any other choices, go there.

i wish i could give a better rating, but i cannot. because of the current covid pandemic, there has been an access line set up for patient's family members to call and receive information on their care with an access pin. the message recording states the access line nurse will call back within the hour. it has been over 48 hours and i've left four messages with no return call. i am trying to gather information on a family member's condition and health information. it is upsetting enough that i cannot physically be with my family member during these rough times, but now the only other option as an access line is severed because nobody is picking up or returning my calls in response to my many voicemails. my family member has received a lot of miscommunication from staff and is not only sick, but confused. i have tried for days to make sense of these things by trying to get in contact with this patient access line. this place has lost all trust from me that they're capable of helping my family member heal.

my dad is positive for covid and in high risk group by age and preexisting conditions. he has been sick since march 12 and today march 30th he starting to get new symptoms and his cough got worth again. department of health indicated that he need to go to get tests done to make sure that there are no secondary infection.  dr martinez from woodland clinic called  indicating that er would expect my dad visit and they have all his health records and will take care of him. when dad  came to er they didn't want to do any blood work and told him  that he is "classic" covid case and needs to go back home.  after some push  they agreed to do the x-ray.  the issue is that with covid one cannot go to regular doctor for blood work or any concern and er doesn't want to see them until the is in total crisis and it might be too late to save a person. my dad is cancer surveyor and has weak immune system. getting new symptoms after being sick for over 2 weeks and feeling better is more than alarming and need to be evaluated with blood work and not by someone visual assessment.
this is, by far, the worst emergency room experience i've ever had. do not go to this hospital for an emergency. get yourself somewhere else. unorganized, unprofessional and unhygienic.

never go to st. anthony's er.  on june 19, 2020 i injured my left leg and could not put any weight on it.  i drove myself to the er.  there were several nearby parking spaces but i had to pull up to the double doors at the entrance.  there was a lady sitting there taking temperatures.  i got her attention and she came with a wheel chair and helped my get inside.  there were 2 security guards standing there.  i asked one of them if he would park my car in a spot right by the entrance.  first, he said no and said valet would have to park it and it would probably be on the other side of the hospital.  a valet came and gave me ticket to get my car upon release. then the guard changed his mind and told me he would park it in that first spot.  

after triage i was taken to an exam room in the er.  they came and took several x-rays of my leg.  i waited and waited to see a doctor but no one came.  finally a man arrived and told me he was going to put an immobilizer on my leg.  i asked what the x-rays showed and he said i don't know sis they just told me to put this on you.  so he brought a long brace and put it on my leg.  it was new in a package.  then he brought in some dirty looking crutches that were not  in any packaging and gave me a 2 minute lesson on how to walk on crutches.  

a pa came in and told me i was being discharged.  i asked what the x-rays showed.  he said he didn't know.  i asked to see a doctor.  he said no one was available and he was there to discharge me.  i said i wasn't going to leave until i saw a doctor.  he told me they needed the room.  nothing had happened to make my leg bear weight and these people just pointed which way to go to get to the er entrance and sent me wobbling off on those crutches.  they didn't even have the courtesy to wheel me back out.  it took me 15 minutes to get from the room to the front entrance and my leg was killing me. i have never walked on crutches and this is not the way you want to learn.

when i got to the front the guard who was supposed to park my car wasn't there.  the other guard handed me my keys and said your car is out there somewhere. by this time tears were streaming down my face and i saw a blue car and started trying to make my way to it.  i realized it wasn't mine.  i tried using the emergency button on the key and no car alarm went off.  the lady who had initially helped me in saw what was happening and she started walking around helping me look.  then the valet drove by in a van and saw me out there on crutches trying to find my car.  he stopped the shuttle and came and told me my car was across the street at the top of a hill in the valet lot.  he literally ran over there and got my car. then he went and got wet wipes and cleaned it well.  he was the only person who seemed to understand i was in pain.

they had handed me a bunch of paperwork when i was discharged and when i got home i hoped it would have some results of the x-rays but it was all generic photocopies and there was nothing specific about what was wrong with my leg.  i still have no idea.  i am sure they are going to charge my insurance a fortune and i left there exactly the same as i went in except my leg was killing me from looking for my car and trying to get myself out of there with no assistance.  i called the so called patient advocate monday and tuesday with no reply.

this place is a joke. if i should ever need help again i will go to lutheran.  shame on you.

i spent about 2 hours in the emergency room because i broke my wrist. one xray, about 10 minutes with the doctor, one temporary cast. the bill was $7622 for the hospital plus $974 for the doctor. the xray was billed as $760! i had xrays at panorama and they were $76. ok, i expect to pay more in an emergency room. but a 1000% mark-up? i asked for a detailed cost break-down of the hospital charge and all they did was to break out the cost for the cast - $695. what a rip-off. the care is good there but you pay thru the nose for it.

i was harassed and felt threatened with bodily harm when i had to go to er where my sister had been taken by paramedics.  i had no weapons on me or in my possession.  even with that, the security officer picked thru, touched, handled, and examined every small item in my purse after he had dumped the entire contents on his table.  he demanded i remove my jewelry, diamond wedding rings, copper bracelets, and two small chain long necklaces, which i refused to do.  i told him he could use the metal wand detector.  i then went thru the metal detector and he stated that there was something in my shoes.  i told him i wear "lifts", i don't.  he did not make me remove my shoes or even check them out.  he used the wand on my body and getting directly into my face.  i thought and feared at that point that he was going to tell me to remove my clothes.  i also felt afraid that he was going to knock me down to the floor.  i am a 72 year old woman and i was "manhandled."   i called his supervisor with my complaint about his "tough guy and cop wannabe"  of which he referred to as an "incident." 
while he was making me go thru his intimidating process, i was left (forced) standing to wait while he passed thru two other individuals just going thru the metal detector.  his supervisor did not ever have a conversation with me, left voice mail messages.  apparently waiting  for his goon to harm someone as he is a serious risk to public safety.

i have had a few experiences here with radiology and was very happy a couple years ago. but i wish i had found out they were centura now, then i would have gone to lutheran for my er visit. 
i had an allergic reaction to some medication and i came in since it was 2 am. the er doctor gave me the same medication in a stronger dose and told me to take benadryl... went to my pharmacy in the morning and he recommended i didn't fill it instead call my pc. i did and she found it interesting that i was indeed having an allergic reaction to the medication and yet he prescribed something stronger that was just mixed with something else. my pc sent over a different antibiotic and no reactions. just out $1,000.00. i will only go to lutheran from now on!

serious lack of communication from er docs, they weren't busy.  they don't wanna get involved in anything other than the current pandemic, not saying covid19 isn't serious,  however if you need other services,  you're sol. theyre good at over charging for really lackluster service. their billing dept-no matter how many ways you explain it-  doesn't get it, so they just keep billing and over charging for seriously limited service. wasted 6 hrs waiting, in pain.

if i could give this place 1 star, i would. it took me about a week to process this experience i had with st. anthony. not to mention, my father was in the hospital all last week, so i have not had time to document. if i could give you any advice, it would be to never patron this hospital. my mother called me in the middle of the night to tell me that my father had trouble swallowing and breathing. he checked into urgent care in golden (part of the centura healthcare network or there lack of healthcare. because i was not present at that experience, i will not be reviewing urgent care on warner ave -but they basically gave my father a sleeping pill and sent him home. i went to their house to check on my father and at 3am in the morning, he told me it was worse. we headed to st. anthonys and checked into er. we were checked in by a barely trained (looked 15) young man who took his dear time to get my father into the nurse office to take vitals and get my father a room in the er. they only had one nurse to process patients in er and we were one of two patients. not well staffed. my father had a hard time breathing. the young man escorted us to the er rooms which felt like a mile of walking with no offering of a wheel chair. we checked into our room (#34) and that is where everything went downhill. whomever manages the nurse crew on staff at 3am in the morning on the 19th- i beg you to fire this crew. they were loud and laughing- basically having a party outside of my fathers room. i asked for blankets and this took about 20 minutes. i told the nurse that my fathers ekg machine was sounding off an alarm- she slowly waddled to our room and said" oh, he needs oxygen." i was under so much stress and worried about my fathers health that i am so upset i didn't catch this women's name. she was wearing some type of ribbon on top of her head. i could identify her in person. she was sarcastic, not a care in the world, and should not be in this profession. i asked her where the dr. was and she replied" i told you, he will see you when he is able. " it was 4:30am! the dr. finally came in and i said my father is in so much pain, can he have something " he replied- " i am the only dr here, i will get to it when i can sit down." are you serious? this is an er??? he finally came back at about 5am and scheduled a scan, of which, we never got the results. at 6am i once again, asked the nurse what the plan was-  no guidance as to what was happening. i then decided to google this hospital on my phone and was so upset we were here. the reviews were awful; just like mine. the experiences were all similar. at 6:30am, i asked the the rude nurse what the plan was as i didn't feel there was one. i also commented "i am glad you are all having a party out here while my father is in so much pain." it was so loud for 3 hours- the constant cackling and talking about weekend plans. i said, i feel like we should leave as we are not being tended to- she replied" you can go." i cannot believe a nurse would tell you, 'you can leave." are you serious? we have been sitting here for 3 hours and 30 minutes, you don't have a care in the world.  i asked the 15 year old looking intern or whatever he was, to disconnect my father and thank god we ended up at rose/swedish. if they send us a bill, we will fight it. we had no care  at this er facility. please do your research and go elsewhere.

the worst hospital in florida - no the country. the head nurse carlos was a horrible unfeeling macho jerk with a little man complex. stay away if you want to live. ive never written a review ever about anything, but this hospital is so bad i felt its my civic duty. during the corona virus they blocked anyone from coming in. i totally understand why. my husband was in there with a life threatening illness. when i called to find out how he was doing they made it clear i was an imposition. i ask you, if your loved one was in icu for 3 days and they never even told you, would you not be concerned.? horrible place. run as far away from there as you can.  i would give them no stars but its not an option.

i had morton neuroma surgery in february,
dr. sellenriek and  the whole crew were so nice and caring.   my nurse that took care of me to the lady that strolled me to my car and everyone in between.  my foot is doing great, and so thankful for having a kind group of people making it an easier surgery. 
thank you dr. sellenriek.
i'm so disappointed that united healthcare has dropped methodist. i had an amazing experience having my son at methodist willowbrook last year.

i grew up here in houston and i have always known methodist hospital to have a stellar reputation, so i was very surprised at the extremely poor level of care that my stepfather received while he was there. when you come out of the hospital, you should be feeling better than you did when you went in.my stepfather was unbelievably worse after six days at methodist willowbrook. he went in with a uti and kidney issues. he was 89 years old, and before the uti, he was able to ride his stationary bike for 30 minutes a day and hold conversation with me although he suffered from dementia. after his time at methodist, he was unable to get out of bed, swallow his food or speak for himself. during that six days, our calls regarding his condition were never answered. because of covid-19, we were unable to go in ourselves to see how he was doing and with no communication from the hospital or the doctor, we were frantic. because of his dementia, he needed someone who could monitor his care and speak for him, but he was not allowed to even have a family member visit. we couldn't even find out who the doctor was that was supposedly caring for him!  finally, we were able to get through and speak with one of his nurses. she said that she would have to call back, but never did. when he was released, we received no paperwork or anything that detailed what happened while he was there for the six days. he was released to a rehab hospital, and then we finally were contacted about his condition, not by methodist hospital, but by concerned doctors at the rehab. only then were we able to get some details about his hospital visit, including his doctor's name. when we called this doctor, he was in absolutely no hurry to speak with us. we waited hours for a return call. long story short, every single thing about this experience was a huge disappointment. my stepfather passed away on friday and i am convinced it was because of the poor care he received at methodist hospital. i would give them zero stars because there was nothing about our experience with them that was good. i don't know how someone can go in for a uti, stay for six days and pass away a week later. shaking my head.......

my primary care instructed me to go to the er for the covid-19 (coronavirus) test. 

at northridge hospital (er department) i asked for the test because i've been sick for the past 5 days and my doctor asked me to do so. i didn't travel the past 14 days, i don't know anyone who is / are positive (but i told them i have friends who just came back from oversees). i have the symptoms (cough, runny nose, chest pain / hard to breath, diarrhea, and other things). walking from the parking lot to the er entrance was like running a marathon! i was having trouble talking to the staff at the door because i had difficulty breathing and talking the same time. because i didn't travel, none of the friends are/ were positive, and my fever didn't reach over 104 degrees, they denied the test. instead they offered me the flu test (-_-")

the us should learn from singapore, taiwan, or even china. they focus on the health of the citizens. doesn't matter if you have traveled or know somebody who is positive. they will test you no matter what. making sure  each person doesn't carry the virus because the symptoms can be asymptomatic.

i'm home. staying home for another 9 days without knowing anything. i don't know if staying at home for 2 weeks would be enough if they won't do the testing to verify. i don't know if i should let the people that i met / interacted the past few days since i don't know even know. i called my primary doctor and told her that er denied the test.

megan m.  & julie r. of dignity health - northridge hospital medical center -- please don't bother to reply to this review with your general comments about having high quality care and good customer service are your priority and telling me to feel free to speak with your quality department.

after having my dad go to the er with signs of a stroke i have to admit the doctors and nurses here done a fantastic job helping him. the majority of the staff, with the exception of a charge nurse in the er was very pleasant and helpful; it's all about how you speak to people and when the people are already stressed out because of uncertainty, don't come at them with attitude, no matter your position. 

my father was well taken care of and even yesterday after having been discharged we were called to ensure my dad was doing ok. that means a lot. 

keep up the great work but train the charge nurse..

if zero stars or negative stars were an option, that is definitely what i would choose! one star is definitely too generous! my son has a very rare condition and is on multiple immunosuppressants to keep his body from killing him. per mayo clinic, if he has a temp over 101, he is to immediately be seen in the er. i brought him into the blessing hospital 3 hours ago with a temp of 103!!! the triage nurse is a young snot-nosed girl fresh out of her 2 year degree. she has zero concept of how serious this is for my son. she thinks it is just a temp a normal person would have! unfortunately, unless we want to travel 3hrs to st. louis, we have no other option.

well, here we again! my son had a seizure at work. he fell, hit his head on the curb and stopped breathing. fortunately, a passerbyer gave him cpr until the paramedics got there. an additional piece of info i need to add is that my son is autistic. he is 23 yo but is not able to make good decisions for himself. i told them and he told them that if i wasn't able to go back with him that he would leave without treatment. they didn't care. they would not allow me to go back wit him, so he left without treatment.

05/20/20 here we are again. after the last visit, i spoke with the nurse manager and with administration. they told me that if/when we had to return to the er to tell them of his disabilities and that i would be allowed to go back with him. however, this evening we are here with an injury to his leg. yet again, even after i explained his disabilities, they refused to let me go back with him. he attempted 3x to facetime me but the wifi is so bad at this facility that it was unsuccessful each time. i told the nurse but they refused to provide him with a phone. he is in there alone and scared but they could care less. i was voicing my frustration to the nurse. i was not using foul language and was standing a good 2-4 ft away from her. she felt the need to call security. the security guard attempted to make me leave the premises but his supervisor said it was unnecessary as i was not a threat. now it's inappropriate or illegal to voice concerns or frustrations??? this is ridiculous! i have absolutely nothing good to say about this hospital. it boils down to them simply not caring about what is best for the patient. if i could go somewhere else, i would but the next closest hospital is 40 minutes away. i guess blessing, as a whole, feels that they can do and say whatever they want b/c they have a monopoly on this area. also, once again, i was forced to sit outside in the rain while i waited!!!!!

this facility is absolutely top notch. 

the cleanliness, the care of staff, the empathy and bedside manner, the gentle loving empathetic approach to each patient and the whole design of the facility is incredible- calming loving environment. phlebotomist is extraordinary- its difficult to get my veins and the got it in one try.

they also have many precautions in place to protect against covid including providing gloves, social
distancing tapes, taking body temps and cleaning rooms and machines between patients. 

the warm blankets, pillows, spa music, meditation room during the tests, the technicians kind voice made the pet scan a relaxing experience of all things!

i have been in and out of hospitals since i broke my neck in 2011 and i have seen and experienced all kinds- the good and the bad and i am deeply thankful a place like thus exists where excellence is evident in the details, staffing, attitude and the machines are clean and new. 

they hire the right staff, they designed the place wonderfully and i want to make sure my friends  and family know this diagnostic center exists. 

and importantly the radiologists take their time to really study the images. they compare reports.
fac_name: The Margaret W. Niedland Breast Center

review: i went for my annual mammogram here and initially found the center to be beautiful and seemingly top flight. my experience proved otherwise. three weeks post mammo, i received a typed letter stating i had to make an appt for a second mammo due to irregularities in the initial one. i never received a phone call from a doctor at any time explaining the "irregularities." appt was made and i was put into a waiting room with a number of other women. after 1 1/2 hrs of waiting and no communication with anyone, i happened to ask several of the other waiting ladies how long they had been there. some said two hours, others said well over an hour. i stepped out of the waiting area to ask if anyone were going to come and check on us, take us to our appt or anything. an offended tech said yes, but did nothing. without dragging this review on, they had me down for a biopsy for which i never consented. i refused treatment after a doctor telling me she could not tell me what she saw on the original mammo to justify a biopsy. i then made a second opinion appt with a board certified breast oncologist who confirmed my suspicions that there was nothing remarkable to warrant not only a second mammo, never mind a biopsy. i have never given a negative review to any medical office, but i finally decided to leave this one. be very careful of consenting to procedures unless you look at your own mammograms. i have never been back to this center and could not recommend it. for the record this all happened in 2018. please always consider a second opinion if you have a negative outcome on your first mammogram from here.
fac_name: The Margaret W. Niedland Breast Center

review: just an update from my 5/2019 review. my right breast is still a saggy, empty sack from the mammogram i received last year. the muscle was clearly pulled away from my sternum as my right breast now falls way over to the outside of my body when i lay down, i have to pull it back from my armpit and support it with my arm when i am on my side. there is still a large gap in the top of my bra on the right. i still have pain and aches in the nipple area, deep in my breast over a year later. i am still embarrassed to be seen undressed. i have never received anything other than the blowoff from the coordinator at mn, except a letter in april of 2020 asking me to call to schedule another yearly mammogram. i will never have another mammogram. i am going to schedule a breast mri. they tell me it is $2000, but i am hoping because of dense breasts and my age 64 that they may cover it, or at least part of it.
fac_name: The Margaret W. Niedland Breast Center

review: this is a free clinic for low income no insurance patients. the meds are free. the care is free. the nurse practitioner seems to have some knowledge of things. basic care.

i came into the er for low blood sugar via an ambulance. my nurse was okay and my doctor was awesome and friendly. the reason they are getting one star is when i was rushed to the er it was morning and i didn't have my contacts in. i asked when i was discharged how to get the the er exit, the lady laughed and said follow the signs. i said i don't have contacts in should i go left or right at the end. she said it's not that hard follow the doors and you'll find yourself outside  good luck. the rudest thing someone who is cleaning out trash bins in patients rooms could say. as well as this a patient next door to me was fighting (physically) with a nurse and i'm not sure who was at fault but after it settled down. all the nurses were gathered being extremely loud outside the room talking about the patient and expected her to not react when 8 ppl are standing there talking down on her. long story short dont go here unless your desperate. because this place is empty and
dead, there must be a reason.

i visited the er extension in harrison, ohio. i was seen fairly promptly but that was the only good thing i have to say. 
the visit required that blood work be done. results of the renal function indicated that my creatinine level was high and the doctor was admitting me to the hospital. he later advised me that mercy west had no beds available so they would check at mercy fairfield for admission availability but that i would have to pay for the ambulance service from harrison to fairfield. after deliberation and finding that it wasn't the level was not unreasonably high and that i would have to pay for the ambulance service, it was decided to go home and drink lots of fluids and follow up with my pcp on monday. while preparing me to be released the nurse removed the iv from my arm and the tape used actually tore my skin off in 2 places revealing raw flesh when i removed it. i had to treat it with antibiotic ointment and covered it with gauze and non adhesive wrap.
my pcp agreed to fit me into her loaded schedule. she repeated the blood work and treated my arm from the iv tape.  the following day i received a call from her office indicating that blood work looked ok but to continue drinking lots of fluids.
i went to my chart to view my test results.  i found the test results from the work done by my pcp and the results of all the blood work done at the harrison er except for the renal function results. i called
i called my chart who advised that i needed to call the er doctor to get the results posted.  i called the er, waited on hold for 12 minutes and hung up..  they told me to call central records.
i understand not able to be admitted because there were no beds (flu season was at its peak), but for me to have to pay out of pocket to be taken to the fairfield mercy hospital was ridiculous. my chart could be a useful tool but only if has correct information and is kept up to date.
i will do everything in my power to avoid anything to do with the mercy hospital system.

my daughter was born at lucile packard where she also died 3 days later, no fault of theirs at all as she was very sick. however in her 3 days of life, her birth was never recorded, leading to nightmare of phone calls in the weeks i should have been grieving. i just learned today almost 8 months later that autopsy was performed in october and never shared with us. according to lucile packard, my sweet hanna never existed.

review: dad was either in hunterdon medical center or hunterdon care center from 2/25/20 - 4/1/20.  in that span of time both of his hearing aids were lost as well as his glasses.

absolutely horrible attention to patients. came in at 4 pm with a broken ankle. 4 hours later, still no room. every test done quickly, but the wait between them was close to an hour. requested pain killers for my ankle three times. only got lip service. assistants go out of their way to avoid you. finally got a bed at 2:30 am. ten and a half hours after coming in. of course, you are trapped waiting as nobody can give you any information. i can't think of any acceptable reason for this delay. if you can go someplace else, do it.

i am a health worker at another hospital in miami dade county and i have to say the treatment and care that my fiance received today is appalling. she is a cancer patient presenting with  a painful mass near her groin the had her in tears for 36 hours at home. she waited  3 hours  just to get an i.v line put in, but no medications until she was finally put in a bed (in the hallway) at the 4 hour mark. she waited a total of 6 hours to finally get a ct scan just to be told by dr cordova that "i have given you meds for your pain, but you need to follow up with your oncologist, this is your problem and i did my job".  not to mention the worst bedside manner did not even touch her to examine her just simply asked her where it hurt and issue allergic to anything. unbeknownst to him i was on the phone the whole time and heard his disgusting deplorable lack of empathy bedside manner. i will be bringing this to the attention of the administration of jackson south medical center. not only because my fiance is a stage 4 terminal cancer patient but because no person no human being in pain deserves to get this type of treatment. again the name is cordova  of the attending. at least his aprn was gentle, warm and attentive.

my husband was recently a guest of this rehab facility. let's just say, my husband is not a fan of listening to medical advice and he prefers to do what he wants. he went to this rehab and i waited by the phone daily for the inevitable call asking me to come get him because he was done. not here. he raved about the personnel. the therapy staff was understanding, compassionate and pushed enough for motivation. the nursing staff was amazing, explained all transitions and stayed on top of any issues. the nursing assistant staff was a god-sent. especially isabela, she is the reason that my husband succeeded and came home from rehab. so attentive, always had a smile and just enough sassiness to keep my stubborn husband in line. the administration kept communication with me throughout the process. and i am so grateful. thank you all for all you do.

i got to spend two nights here recently. luckily i wasn't the patient -- but i kept my man company after his surgery. i actually slept on two chairs bedside while he was there. 

i've been here before myself, but they seem to have upped their game. in addition to taking all the extra precautions for covid, every person we came in contact with was very professional and enjoyable to deal with -- from the cleaners on up to the doctors and nurses. there really was a great team effort. and it shows. 

each shift change, they came in and introduced the new people. they went over the necessary info and posted it each time on a board by the bed. each patient has a phone with the number to call to reach the attending nurse, the assistant and floor personnel. it's a very efficient system. and they are very informative to prepare the patient for what's going to happen and how to manage your pain. 

the food here was surprisingly way better than average for hospital food. every morning starting at 6:30 am you can call in your breakfast order from their menu. it takes about an hour or less to get your hot breakfast. you use your phone to call the kitchen extension. (hint: they're busy. don't hang up. just hold til they answer.) choices included various omelets, eggs, turkey sausage, potatoes, breads/cakes, fresh and canned fruits, juices, cereals, etc. the only thing they didn't have was toast! you also call in for your other meals at least an hour or so in advance. lunches, too, were good as well as dinners. there's a lot of variety and they try to accommodate all requests if possible. two standouts were their fresh sliced hot turkey with mashed potatoes and gravy and their mac n cheese.

the hospital offers free valet parking which is helpful as the lot fills up. 

the only downside was the day we came their computers were acting up so it  took longer to register and to be processed during pre-op. and a longer time than expected waiting for a room to be available. 

no one really wants to be in a hospital, but if you do need to be, this is one of the better options in town.

the miscommunication, misinformation, incompetence, stolen items and more from hcsfl and their staff is absolutely inexcusable and is a sorry excuse for a hospital!

dr. cappezzuitti is the best ! i have been seeing her for years and couldn't be happier .. her bedside manors are amazing and she always takes the time to listen to you .. if you are in need of a new doctor i highly recommend her :)

great efforts made by the medical staff despite the chaos outside with covid-19.

review:

review:
be aware that kp prefers that you use their pharmacy, and will go so far as to not send your prescriptions at outside pharmacies.  i needed a scrip faxed to my local pharmacy but their policies prevent that from happening, but they wont tell you that, you just won't get the meds. keep that in mind if you are considering using kp. i have never heard of a doctor/hospital that could not fax in a prescription to a local pharmacy and then get dumb about it when called about why it did not happen. and never call in early, you will get passed around with no help, leave them to have their coffee and donuts, call in later in the day. kp is ok for checkups but if you have a serious issue, they will fail you.

review: i went to the er here for tooth pain one night. i knew i had to see a dentist asap not knowing what it was, however i was just hoping to get prescribed strong pain medication in the meantime as none of the over the counter medication worked, i was in tremendous agony, and all my local urgent cares were closed at that time of the night. i waited for about 3 hours just to be seen (which sucks but was expected). when i got inside the emergency room, i waited another few minutes before the doctor finally came to see me. the doctor literally just asked me to rank the pain, didn't even bother to look into my mouth to see if its something she can identify. she prescribed me pain medication and was with me for less than 3 minutes. the payment process took longer than her seeing me. i paid $150 on my credit to get a prescription that night, which sucks but i know the er can't be free. where kaiser has gone too far is when i recieve a bill for $800 7 months later. they're essentially asking me to pay $950 (+ $150 i already paid) to prescribe me pain medicine with absolutely no professional diagnosis. to add salt on the the wound, i tried to dispute it but they said i needed to start a claim within 90 days or so after my visit, even though they sent me the bill 7 months later..i had to fight for them to let me dispute it. once they agreed, they "reviewed it" within 2 days and denied my dispute. absolutely horrible experience in this er. would rather go through the agony again then to deal with this er service. in what world is it ok to charge almost  $1000 just to prescribe medication???

now the big deal, unapproved scans against medicare and insurance rules- i got my bill and it was for more than $20,000 and then i got a letter from my medicare insurance company stating " caromont billed nearly $6,000 for tests not medically required nor appropriate. plus they performed 1 test 3 seperate times for blood work. this sounds like fraud to me, but my insurance company stated to "not pay for the excessive and unapproved testing.

i'm finding it difficult to review this. three stars just because of staff. oh my goodness. they are truly truly top of the line! i have had plenty of nurses in my life. i don't say this lightly. 
as far as the doctors, and this includes today's (erika robb). have any of you physicians had migraines the last 15 years of your life? have you tried to keep a job throwing up and with pain so bad you have to go on disability? have you felt the worthlessness of that? my seizures are not a fluke. however, it seems that i've gotten labeled a drug risk. erika, i do not have narcotics at home. when my migraines started in the beginning and i went to the er i was treated with narcotics and given an rx. when my migraines got severe enough, the er did the same. when i was made aware of the rebound affect, i weaned myself down slowly. i have been telling them if i have to go in, no narcotics. but with this new (small dry brain bleed) i needed something.  so, i'm sure when you dig in my chart you'll find something about "drug seeker"
i would now be interested to hear dr.  boudrueaux's thoughts on my seizures.

first time visiting this hospital for my nephew. he's not doing too well. he probably won't make it. that being said the nurses i've interacted with have been kind, friendly, and have great bedside manner.
two specific nurses anne and fredrick on the fifth floor have gone out of their way to make sure he's comfortable, clean, and has his meds . they seem to be overly concerned for him and his family. something i have not experienced at other hospitals. other hospitals seem to have overworked, overwhelmed, and impatient nurses, but no here. the two nurses(anne,ana, and fredrick) and the ones(alexis and julia) on the phone have taken time to keep us informed and up to date. 
our family wants to say thank you, because we drove a long way and would be so disappointed to have terrible care. we feel hopeful and continue to pray.
fac_name: Jacobs Medical Center at UC San Diego Health

review:
i had my baby here in late december 2020. i have some issues. 

1) billing / insurance. 
i called ahead to both ucsd and my insurance (united) in advance and verified coverage. very little of my services (labor, tests, ultrasounds, blood work) were covered. my max out of pocket was $7,900 and i am now paying over $15,000. this is criminal. neither side will do anything about it. for this reason i would recommend avoiding services. 
2) the midwives are essentially a joke. a few of them were lovely but some were quite pushy about inductions, vaccines, testing. i was heavily pressured into getting induced after my water broke by one of the midwives. i was also talked to at every appointment about the tdap and flu shot. i was also told that a birth plan was basically pointless. 
3) the recovery area was pretty horrible. my baby had a mild level of jaundice and they put her under light therapy for almost 5 days. it made it hard to feed and bond with her. once we did our first ped appointment he was really surprised that they did that based on her actual levels. 
she was under lights and snuggling with my and started sweating a good amount so i got worried. they checked her blood sugar and said it was too high (literally one point over) so ordered tests. which meant she had to get a heal prick before every single feeding for 6 feedings. so i had a hungry newborn that i had to wait for a nurse to stab her before i could feed her. the ped said that the level being one off was literally insane to be worried about. 

so between the jaundice tests (they cut the heal multiple times over the course of the treatment) and the heal pricks she was basically getting tortured for 3 days for literally no reason. 
also, their lactation consultants were not helpful at all. that's one thing that i really wanted help with but they appeared to have never actually breast fed themselves. 

overall i am super disappointed and have been annoyed about this for some months. i am happy to finally note this down. 
i will say that pam (one of the midwives) was lovely and i really liked her. i also love their classes (carlyle's class in particular) and thought those services were great. the birthing sweats in the birthing center area were also quite nice.
fac_name: Jacobs Medical Center at UC San Diego Health

review:
my husband had back surgery here recently and post op/ discharge were the most horrible experience i've ever had at a surgery center/ hospital.  the rn who was there to help my husband in recovery/ post anesthesia was annoyed with my husband's questions and was extremely condescending and disrespectful. my husband had surgery at 3 pm. i was updated via text once, recovery rn called me at approximately 5:15 to let me know he will be able to see me in approximately 30 min. i was picking our daughter up from soccer and was back at the hospital at 5:30 ish. went to the doors and they were locked. walked completely around the building and finally went into the er for assistance who weren't remotely helpful and kept vaguely telling me how to get there. after several attempts to get to surgery waiting a very kind janitor (wish i had gotten his name as he was the only good thing at this facility) was able to get me there. 

post op/ discharge was slightly horrific. rn we had was abrasive and didn't really even know what procedure my husband had and was unable to answer any of our medical or mobility questions. considering he had back surgery, you would think the discharge rn would be educated on the procedures her patients have had. she wasn't able to tell me where exactly the incision was (there was a large bandage over most of his back). she didn't know how to put on the back brace so another rn came into our room and gave her an in room class on how to do this. during this impromptu in room back brace class my husband had a question and was completely ignored. little knowledge regarding pain management meds and had to check twice to articulate what the proper dosage and timing. there were literally too many disturbing to post in one review. 

note: i'm a super positive person who rarely writes bad reviews. typically i'd give feedback on a bad experience (there haven't been many) in hopes that establishment is able to use the information to improve and prosper. i generally give people the benefit of the doubt (i don't know what they are going through etc) but this was just an unacceptable experience. i've never written a review this long or negative but our experience was just so horrible i'd like to save anyone willing to read this whole review the experience we had.

had a terrible experience here. went to l&d due to alot of pain and my baby not moving as much. ive been here many times during my pregnancy as im high risk and its my first. iwas taken care of first by a nurse named lacy, she was so sweet and nice to me and made me feel really comfortable. but 2 times now that ive been to l&d to be monitored the male doctors are very rude. i was told multiple times to go to my hospital to be seen and not come to their er! i live in caldwell and my hospital is in boise so going to their er is easier and faster for me in an emergency and thats where my ob tells me to go when i need to be monitored quickly. not only was i told that but also treated poorly by 2 male nurses and they did not listen to my concerns at all. not returning here again and im so happy im delivering at st lukes now!!!!

last night i fell and hit my head which required stitches. my husband took me to the emergency department at st. luke's, and we couldn't have picked a better place. i was brought in almost immediately, ct scans were taken, and the doctor examined me and meticulously put 10 stitches in my head. he, my nurse, the registration and the triage people were super nice, and i was out of there within an hour and 15 minutes. 

i only have good things to say about the rest of the hospital, since that's where my babies were born many years ago.

took my infant to the er here after calling my pediatrician and describing her symptoms. she's had a fever for four days, lethargic, inconsolable crying, weak, distressed and in pain. she was having a hard time breathing normally and that's what i was most worried about. 

the receptionist was very friendly, took our information and we waited. the waiting room was nearly empty. due to covid 19 they only allowed one parent in w my daughter so my husband waited outside, even though there was a mom and a dad with their baby in the waiting room. 

they took us back to triage and left us waiting. finally a nurse practitioner came in, not friendly at all, almost annoyed that we were there, looked in my baby's ears and down her throat and said as she's walking out that they'll do a swab test her for flu, rsv and strep. she left and i hear her talking happily w another nurse right outside our door. would it kill her to be kind or friendly to us? oh well, i figured, not a big deal, i just want to take care of my baby. 

they take us to a room. 

shortly after that a nurse walks in and listens to my baby's heart. she said she needs to go see what tests need to be done and she leaves the room. 

we weren't waiting long when someone shows up to do a chest x ray. a chest x ray? the nurse practitioner had said nothing about that. i didn't even know they were going to get x rays. i wondered if they had heard something when they checked her a few minutes ago. of course my baby is freaking out the whole time. the guy is kind and we get it done. 

one hour goes by. two hours go by. my poor baby is restless and fussy. no one checked on us or told us what was going on. i walked out into the hall and asked the first person i saw what was taking so long. she said they were waiting for results from the swab test. i told her they hadn't done the swab test yet. she said oh they're probably waiting for the x ray results. 

another hour goes by and i called the nurse to the room and come to find out she thought another nurse had already swabbed my baby. after being there for three hours and hardly anyone else there we hadn't even taken the sample yet. 

another hour goes by and i walk out to the desk where the nurse is sitting there eating cookies. i told them we're leaving. my baby and i are both exhausted at this point and the whole thing has been a joke. another nurse snaps at me and tells me they have a skeleton staff and they don't even have a technician on staff.

i finally get the results of the swab test back and the nurse practitioner comes in and apologizes for everything taking so long and said there was a mix up with one nurse getting distracted and thinking someone else had already done the test. 

still heard nothing about the x rays, why they took them or what they showed. 

frustrating experience.

i called the billing people at bsw, and they told me to send a letter to the director of compliance. here is the letter i sent to the director of compliance today. i don't know if this will do any good or not, but i thougth i could at least give it a shot:

director of compliance, 
 on or about 1 april 2020, i visited the bsw emergency hospital in grand prairie for a severely burned hand. i had burned the entire palm of my left hand on the motor casing on a gas powered rototiller. anybody who has taken a basic first aid class could see this was a deep second degree burn. i went to the hospital, and the doctor there completely blew me off. he said it was a first degree burn, and told me to just go home and put ice on it. the nurse asked me if i was current on my tetanus shot, and i told her i was not, but nothing else was said about that. i did not receive a tetanus shot. the doctors or nurses did not clean it, disinfect it, wrap it, or bandage it in any way. they didn't even give me an ice pack. they told me to go home and put ice on it. 
 the first two nights after it happened, the pain was so intense i could not sleep. i know with the opioid epidemic raging right now, doctors are hesitant to prescribe narcotic pain medication, but he could have prescribed some motrin or another non-narcotic to help with the pain, but i received no painq medication. i was also given no antibiotics. on the palm of your hand, it is hard to keep a blister intact (there were two large blisters, covering almost the entirety of the palm of my hand), and of course those blisters broke. they began to get infected and there was a yellow discharge. the pain was intense. i treated it with over the counter antibiotic ointment, and the infection lessened over time, however once the skin under the blister began to dry, the skin cracked and bled, and the infection set in again. i was able to maintain my primary job as a teacher, however i had to take two weeks off from my other job as a laborer, costing me about 1600 dollars in lost wages.

 this is absolutely unacceptable, and i won't stand for this. i received no medical treatment at the hospital, was charged 500 dollars, and now i am being forced to pay additional funds. this is absolutely exploitative. it is clear to me that bsw and their facilities have no concern for the wellbeing of their patients, and are only concerned with getting as much money out of their patients as they can. 
 i think the only remedy here is a complete refund of the 500 dollars i paid to receive no medical treatment, plus the cancellation of the additional bill i recently received. the doctor who treated me was negligent in misdiagnosing the severity of my burn, and careless in his instructions to just deal with it myself, despite the fact that it proceeded to get infected. a simple round of antibiotics would have prevented that infection and reduced my recovery time.
 i demand to hear back from somebody soon. my phone number is 4053148613. if i don't hear back from somebody immediately, i may be forced to contact an attorney. i strongly suggest that you get in touch with me and resolve this matter. 

sincerely, 
jeff

after places started opening up due to covid, hubby decided it was time to get out and enjoy a ride in the country on his harley motorcycle.  a dog came out of nowhere and decided he wanted to play a game with the motorcycle.  so, the dog won, and hubby went down on his bike at 40 mph.  brought him to the emergency room and they were shocked that he walked in on his own.  one broken arm, 4 staples on other arm, one fractured rib, and about 50% really bad road rash.  the er staff was phenomenal.  courteous, efficient, and very professional.  thank goodness i am educated in wound care, but they took the time to answer all of our questions.  thank you integris er staff.  we are home and doing wound care which is for those w a very strong stomach.  btw, i told hubby that as he is 70 years old, maybe it was time to get a trike or just quit riding.  as usual, i will not win that argument.  thank you god and jesus for placing him in your hands as he was taken care of by the fantastically professionals in the integris i-35 emergency room.

let me start by stating that the medical staff, in their entirety, were absolutely great, professional and polite.  my largest grievance falls at the feet of the facility,  it's poor upkeep, and those responsible for the facilities shortcomings.

i went to the er for a post medical infection.  the er took me in quickly and listened to all of my concerns.  the er physician recommended that i stay over night and voiced his concerns.  i agreed and was quickly taken to my room on the 3rd floor.

again the nursing staff were polite and professional  and did everything they could to make me comfortable.  that's were the problem began.  from the moment i got to my room the constant noise of the hvac unit and the incessant, ear piercing hum of the air bed made it impossible to sleep.  it got so bad and so uncomfortable that i had thoughts at 2am to call in a nurse, sign an ama and walk out.  i stuck it out through the night but informed the day shift nurse that i was leaving regardless for the staff dr's recommendation.  in fact by that time i was so aggravated i became less than courteous and demanded  my discharge.  

the medical treatment i received was premier but i would have to give serious consideration before staying at the edmond facility ever again.

my 88-year-old mother presented to the er 5/8/20 for leg pain and weakness. at the time she was at full mental capacity, ambulatory with walker assistance.
she was admitted to the hospital with our concerns expressed to the hospital that we feared for her life and safety since we would not be able to be there with her due to covid 19 as there were several reported incidents of abuse and neglect during her january 2020 stay that occurred in front of family members and the condition that we found her in when we would leave and come back.
on 5/10/20 we found it very difficult to reach her, her phone was not answered in her room and it was difficult to get in touch with nurse's station. we expressed our concerns about this. by 5/11/20 she was totally incoherent and unable to answer her phone. at times an aid would answer and we heard her screaming in the background. when they held the phone to her she was unable to speak and she had no idea where she was. she believed she was home. the dr. (raza) told me on 5/11/20 that she was on hydrocodone for pain and when i expressed my concerns about her wellbeing he informed me that her bloodwork was good and she could be discharged 5/12/20. on 5/12/20 we were informed by nurses that she had not had any pain medication since she had been there other than 1 tramadol and she was diagnosed 5/12/20 with a uti and was beginning treatment. on 5/13/20 we were told it would be yet another day due to possible small area of pneumonia. we insisted on her discharge 5/14/20. upon picking her up she was brought out in light summer pajamas, a blanket no mask and turned over to us and we thought they had made a mistake and brought the wrong patient out. we did not even recognize what was sitting in that wheelchair. the nurse stated that what we were seeing were probably residual effects from the ativan that was given to her to "calm her down" why did she need to be calmed down and why was she given ativan? we were rushed along and given no real discharge instructions. upon getting her home she laid in fetal position for the first 3 days crying for her mother. she was covered in bruises showing all signs of severe abuse, trauma and suspected sexual abuse. at first the home nurses though that she may have been catheterized for the urine sample and that was painful and traumatizing for her but we later found out that they never even did a urinalysis and she never had a uti that they claimed she had and was treating her for. after a few days she began to come around a small amount and she could only cry and ask why they had done those things to her in the hospital and why they hurt her. we also found out that she had a 14mm kidney stone that was never addressed or told to us. my mother went from being of total sound mind and ambulatory (only experiencing some pain and weakness) on 5/8/20 to now being on end stage hospice care.
we have had several incidents with this hospital that have always fallen on deaf ears.  in researching the many websites, we have come across several similar heart wrenching stories from patients and families in this hospital and i am currently corresponding with a woman who saw my post about her father in law who is currently in that hospital suffering abuse and neglect. i have every intention of contacting medicare, state board of medicine, health dept. and any other agency that will shed light on what happened to my mother in that establishment.
i have worked in the medical profession myself for the past 20 years and have never witnessed anything like this hospital. i am contacting the large benefactors for the hospital, the press and anyone that will listen and help me to stop another human being from suffering this type of tragedy and abuse in this facility. i also will fight as hard as i can to get the license of dr. raza taken from him. i want whomever abuse, assaulted, and basically killed my mother held accountable.
**update since this was first written.
on june 9, 2020 exactly 27 days after she has suffered the abuse, assault, medical misdiagnosis and gross negligence my mother has passed away.
also, the man i mentioned that his family had contacted me due to similar complaints of neglect and abuse was scheduled to be released from that establishment 6/8/20 but had passed on 6/5/20.
i will fight until i take my last breath for my mother, this man and all who walk through the doors of olean general hospital that are unable to speak for themselves.  there has to be change, people have to be held accountable.
i have been in contact with the hospital and melody stuckey informed me that an investigation had been done (it took a day) and that they asked everyone on the third floor if anyone had done anything to my mother and they all stated "no". did administration actually expect someone to step up and admit that they abused, neglected, assaulted, drugged, misdiagnosed and wrongfully treated / medicated an 88 year old woman?  this hospital takes nothing seriously

my mother was fed well and treated respectfully although i know she can be difficult to work with. she was clean every time i saw her and all of her needs were met, which didn't always happen with hospital stays at other facilities. nurses were polite and gracious. visiting hours were ample and the facility was easy access with plenty of free parking. the facility was clean, modern and used brand name healthcare products as part of their hygiene regimen. 

i was very pleased with the level of service provided. the hospital administration and their staff deserve full recognition for all that they do for the community. thank you!

i write this not only as a mother that has birthed three babies at mission bernal but also as a doula that has supported countless clients both at mission bernal and other bay area hospitals. the care provided by the mb team is simply unparalleled. every prenatal appoint i was treated like i was the only patient they had to see that day. i was warmly welcomed and my questions were always answered thoroughly, never rushed. i had an uncomplicated beautiful birth my first time around so going there for my second pregnancy with twins was a no-brainer.  during the delivery of my twins, after delivering my fist twin vaginally, there were complications with the second twin and it looked like it might go to a c-section. pemberton and norell were simply amazing. they managed to deliver the second twin vaginally as well. i think the most important take away from my experience is that i felt like an active-participant in both my births.  i felt safe, heard, supported, and empowered. i felt like the midwives genuinely cared about my physical and emotional well being- probably because they did! even at the end, when i felt like i couldn't go any longer, they made me believe that i could- and i did! they trust the birth process and a woman's ability to birth, and they help their patients believe it, too! surly this factors into their low intervention rates! i love the mb team and sing their praises at every opportunity. 
now, putting on my doula hat... i have seen so many beautiful births at mission bernal that would've been a c-section anywhere else. again- they trust the process. in the last 2 years i've had over a half dozen clients leave cpmc van ness to get care at mb. all i say is, "go meet the midwives, check it out" and the rest is history.  cpmc van ness is very high intervention and not big on informed consent. in the birth community they have a reputation for bullying patients into unnecessary interventions and early inductions. mb midwives on the contrary, give our clients a voice. they empower our clients and make them feel safe. i think the reason so many clients switch from cpmc vn to mb is not just bc of the appealing intervention statistics but bc mb staff makes you feel like family- warm, loving and invested.

i had an amazing experience delivering my first baby at cpmc mission bernal campus in july of 2019. in particular, the midwives at the women's center who supported me in my prenatal months, through delivery, and with my postnatal visits, are what made my experience so wonderful. i attended the group prenatal program leading up to my due date. every midwife that i met through that program and through my additional prenatal office visits was amazing and i felt a true connection to all of them. i definitely was wary at first, of working with midwifes and not an ob, but i immediately found their level of professionalism and incredible knowledge, put my worries at ease. i was also a high-risk case. all the while, i found the midwives were confident and knowledgeable, and handled my treatment perfectly. i was admitted to mission bernal at 40+2 weeks, with a diagnosis of preeclampsia. two midwives handled my labor from beginning to end and worked perfectly with the doctor on the floor. their collaboration was impeccable and although i was delivered by the doctor, what stands out to me was the hours of amazing care i received from the midwives. they added a personal level of care that i know would have been missing, had i worked only with an ob. finally, i was excited to go back to to the women's center for my post-natal visits. it felt like a home to me and i was emotional to see my midwives again. there is no way that i can thank them enough for what they have given me. the postnatal time period is extremely difficult and i relied on their support as i recovered. they were only a quick phone call away to answer any question i had and provided medical support, when i needed it. in the future, i hope to have another hospital birth under the care of these outstanding midwives. i don't believe there is any other place in san francisco that would be able to offer this format and standard of care.

i'll try to make this as short as possible.  i had hip replacement surgery in november 2019.  i was so disgusted with the surgeon.  i used to have private insurance and now have medi-cal because of my disability.  i've worked as a unit clerk at oroville hospital, had front office and back office positions before becoming a case manager with butte county social services.  i am very well aware of being treated differently with private insurance and medi-cal.  maybe this is why that surgeon reserves a separate office for private insurance patients and may see his medi-cal patients for five minutes in the "clinic' office.  this is appalling.  i had to have labs done before surgery (probably a cbc and a chem panel).  my platelet count was 765.  i'm sure you know that the normal is between 140-400.  hmm.  after waking up on the surgery table, my lower back felt worse than labor pains. not the hip, yet.  i tried to tell him this and he kept walking out of the room and didn't even respond to me.  by the time i got to the floor to a room i was experiencing pain as i had never had before.  my blood pressure began to drop and i couldn't stop shaking.  one of the nurses said he knew where the dr. was and needed an order written for pain. i will commend the nursing staff and physical therapy.  they were all very pleasant.  i did not appreciate a male nurse telling me that pain medications were not the answer and i needed to try to do my part instead of being high on pain killers.  this was at the same time i couldn't couldn't quit shaking all over from no pain medication after a 12 inch cut into my hip and nerves.  what!?  get high?  if i wanted to do that i would stay at home with my drug of choice and company of choice.  it would not be any opioids. the last night i was there the dr writing orders for that floor told me that if my pain was seven or above what i was suppose to have.  even though the nurses were nice and probably over worked, i was not given anything for pain from six that evening until six in the morning. i heard my nurse at the station discussing my case with the charge nurse.  she admitted not giving me anything and was afraid she would lose her job.  the charge asked her if i was a trouble maker or if i could have been drinking.  what?  i told them to come into my room if they wanted to talk about me.  my nurse apologized and i understood.  i did tell the charge what i heard her saying about me, not knowing me at all. i, like many in this town knows what to expect when being at oroville hospital.  people make mistakes, but this whole experience from the pain level i endured, to the surgeon not noticing my platelet level, to the surgeon showing no concern or compassion for his patient, was nothing that anyone should experience.  i did not mention his name.  i have a wonderful general practice physician that did notice my labs.  i'm now with an oncologist.  she has been great also.  and again, the nurses were very pleasant, but should give you the medicine that the dr writing the orders believes you need.  i would tell them my pain level and they did not treat it accordingly.  if there is any dispute with what i am saying, i can provide proof.  i took my phone to record or document just this kind of thing.  if not, thanks for listening.  you do have some wonderful nurses and physical therapists.

overall my experiences at scripps encinitas have been relatively positive for having to stay in the hospital. i've also stayed at scripps encinitas about 6 times over the last 3 years, so i know how the process works, and knowing what to expect is helpful. 

positives:
1. treated quickly (this has to do with the condition i have), unfortunately, if you have a broken arm, just like most hospitals, it will probably take longer to be treated.
2. er is a major improvement from 10 years ago, private rooms with doors.
3. good experience with every doctor i've had.
4. i've only had to share a room 2 out of 7 times, however this also had to do with my condition. 
5. they allowed my boyfriend/fiance/and now husband to stay overnight with me when i was in my own room.
6. 90%+ of nurses i've had here have been helpful and sweet.
7. the billing process has significantly improved through online portal.
8. access to medical records and tests as well as communication online is helpful.
9. pcu and the standard hospital rooms on that floor are very nice. 

possible negatives:
1. possibility of not having a private room. this is huge for me. if you are sick, in pain, and recovering, you want your own space and a space for someone to stay with you. all new hospitals in the san diego area are required to have their own rooms now, i'm sure they will get there and understand it's a big undertaking, but it makes a big difference for experience and patient care. 
2. nurse response time - this can be long (i never experienced longer than 20-30 minutes at any given time), and i understand that there are tons of other patients to care for, however, if you are not allowed to get up to go to the bathroom by yourself or your pain really spikes 20-30 minutes can seem like forever. overall, the response time was adequate. 
3. lack of communication between doctors & nurses. i felt like i had to advocate and/or repeat for myself on several occasions. maybe notes weren't written down, maybe doctors don't always read them, who knows. my surgeon also has privileges at this hospital but is not based out of scripps encinitas, so there may be some gaps due to that.
4. not all of the hospital is updated. some floors and areas are, but some feel pretty old.

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

during my mother's surgery, we sat in a big waiting area with a music loop that played the same three songs over and over for hours. there was no one about - no staff offering to help, no activity. again, the waiting area was disgusting. i cleaned the armchairs we used with clorox wipes and they came up black. never once did i see a janitor with a cart to clean. 

the cafeteria was equally disgusting. tables and chairs not wiped down. the area where trays were supposed to be returned was blocked by old trash bags. 

when my mother got out of surgery, and was transferred to a permanent room, the waiting area on her floor was again filthy and empty of people. no attendants, no amenities, dingy chairs, bathroom facilities lacking. 

we overheard one of the nurses saying half the patient lifts do not work. not surprising.

overall, seton williamson hospital has a run-down understaffed feel. no comparison to st david's or any of the nicer hospitals in houston. and it. is. filthy. omg. please disinfect this place! sweep! equip your bathrooms, staff your waiting areas.

my only complaint is that seton cardiologists and the hospital do not share the same health portal i have a login for each site separately. share the same name, doesn't make sense.

they ended up keeping me overnight without properly transitioning my medication schedule, leaving me on the medical floor in pain because they had to wait to confirm that i hadn't received the meds before leaving the er like i was supposed to.
