review: i love this place. the staff are super friendly and they made sure your child gets the correct treatment that they need. took my daughter here 3 times over the course of 1 week due to her fever and cough. they were very nice and took the time to calm my daughter down.  i decided to come to this location due to the review although i wish they open a little earlier in the day but it's worthed . the nurses and doctors here are amazing .

i went into the emergency room for extreme dizziness, vomiting, weakness and total rehabilitation. i was at patrick's point campground at the time. an ambulance was summoned and took me to the hospital. i was treated abominably by the doctor in charge, a 40 year (i overheard him talking with another patient for up to 10 minutes although he basically ignored me and my case!). in retrospect, i realized his attitude and demeanor towards me reflected his profiling of me as a drug user. i had recently (3 days earlier) been to my doctor in ashland, oregon for hearing loss which apparently was connected to my sinuses and i need to see a specialist for this. this problem played a part in my condition, called vertigo, although the doctor in charge (i have lost the paperwork, sadly or misplaced it), asked only questions which seemed to verify his preconceived notion that i was a drug user. i won't go into the full details here but his lack of professionalism, courtesy and bias made me wonder how he got the job. at one point, he challenged me while i was still suffering from my symptoms and said: "so, how are you going to get back to patrick's point!" ah, like, how about some help on that matter especially since there was a local taxi service which i found. none of the staff would help me to arrange for a taxi. after the doctor cleared me, i confronted him on his behavior and he remained mute. i asked him: "so, you have nothing to say?!!" he just walked away, mute!!! i was a professional educator, publisher, community activist and am a published poet and writer. amazingly, this doctor spent less than two minutes trying to put together the symptoms which fit his preconceptions of me as a drug user. i went to get some medication for nausea and the local pharmacist at walgreens....quickly diagnosed the condition as vertigo, told me all the symptoms and recommended to me the proper treatment. all i got from the doctor at the hospital was a piece of paper with information which did not include the diagnosis of vertigo!!!! this man is doctor!!!!????????? shocking, disturbing and a warning to all.

i had baby girl here, and this hospital is one of the greatest hospital to have a baby!  i really enjoy giving the birth in this hospital.  first of all, nurses are amazing!!!! sheryl, kayla, tessa are all the greatest nurses i've ever seen.  

they are professional and sincere, but in the same time, they are so friendly and fun that might be sometime hard to co-exist.  and they  ask, answer, and comfort me everything before i ask,  since, you know, you never know anything about giving the birth if you have never experienced before, and you can't ask what you don't know.  you can ask whatever you don't know how, but you can't ask if you don't know what.  in that point, they are professional.  

they are so nice all the time in the meaning as a friend.  sheryl and kayla talked a lot of stuff from their experience about baby, and that so helpful even my baby became 2 months old now.  tessa made cute bow on the baby hat.  oh, shawn (crna), thank you so much for waiting my decision to take anesthesia until 2am.  i also really appreciate dr. george and dr.thompson.  dr.thompson knows the best for baby.

and plus, food is good too, here!

the worst hospital in the world.   told ambulance driver 3 times to take me to ou med or saint anthony.   nurses were rude as can be i was told no details about the procedures or recovery.   laid there from 1:20am sat morning til 1:00pm sunday afternoon before they did anything.   didn't plug the bed in so i could call a nurse   ordered a nicotine patch that was never delivered    they just set my tray of food outside my door til the next shift brought it in which was cold.      just awful service i'd have been better off going to pets mart

i was very distressed to find they employ a nurse in springfield, mo recently back from mexico.  she was cleared to go back to work and did not self quarantine.  this woman works with oncology patients whose immune systems are already compromised.  isn't it bad enough they have cancer??? this should be made known to them so they may decide whether to continue treatment there or another facility. she's also, potentially exposing the other nurses and their families.  i realize mexico is not a high risk area at this time but she had to travel through at least 2 airports.....probably 3. if she stayed at a resort, there are other travelers who may have traveled from other countries she's came in contact with.   i'm so shocked the hospital has allowed her to return to work.  i'm so disgusted. the hospital is limiting visitors but allowing workers to do this!!

the absolute worst emergency room visit of all time. my wife was clearly in need of medical attention, throwing up so bad she literally passed out. i had to help her into the bathroom to clean her up, with zero offers of help from the staff.
after an hour waiting, i had to put on on the bench outside,  while we waited to be helped. another hour of her throwing up and passing out before she was seen. and to top it off, the charge nurse threatened to have me escorted out because i was getting visibly frustrated and   told the staff it was ridiculous to have someone so obviously in need of help waiting outside, on a bench, to be helped.
shitty from start to the time she was eventually seen.
not to mention, the fact that she spent 11 days there in april for the same issues. the staff had access to those records and didn't seem to care.

last january 2019, i checked into the er because my financial situation brought me to the brink of suicide.  i recovered after receiving treatment, somewhat.  i moved to henderson, nv in may of 2019 because it was a better opportunity financially.  having paid my $400 co-pay, i assumed i was done.  according to mission viejo medical associates, they sent 2 letters to me on june 5 & 10 of 2019 stating that i owed $1286.  since i had already moved, those letters never got to me, and i did not call, because i had no reason to believe i owed anything.

today, i checked my credit score, only to find out that they sent me to collections.  wtf?? they have ruined my credit score.  i lost my job in october, and had finally found one, only to have the offer taken away because of covid-19.  i am destitute, and i now cannot get a job in my profession because i have taken a huge hit on my credit report, and i need good credit because my industry requires it.  mission viejo medical associates has had my telephone number the entire time and never once attempted to call me about owing anything!!!   now they have ruined my credit, and my prospects for attaining employment.   there is no reason they could not have called my back then when i still had a job.  now my financial situation is worse than it was then.  and now those thoughts are quickly back in my mind.  mission hospital is there to save lives, yet they will probably cost me mine.

hi everyone !!! i came to mission hospital with a bad kidney infection but ended up having a great experience, especially with the ultra sound tech, charles. he made 
me feel very comfortable and was so personable !!! he was definitely cheering me up and putting a smile on my face the whole entire time even in these painful circumstances. thank you charles, you were definitely meant to work with patients, you have the gift! god bless

i'll give 2 stars to mission hospital and its nueroscience surgical suite and i will voice my opinion now i feel with all your medical technology and advancements in medicine you did no good for my lower back your surgical team did nothing for my nerve damage your medical surgical suite should be permanently shut down im disappointed with mission hospital

horrible experience with medical records department. continually disconnected and routed to the automated phone system when i asked for a supervisor to assist with obtaining a medical record that was not included in my er discharge packet, but necessary for follow up care.  after explaining what i needed and why i needed it urgently, i was informed that the information would not be provided to me unless i physically went to pick it up.  i explained i could not go to their office as the medication their doctors prescribed prohibits me from driving. the employee' response was "that's life".   
unresponsive. uncaring.  unprofessional

dealt with a problem with my insurance immediately and promised me i'll never see the bill, fast and extremely courteous when i was really really worried about my wife and took every opportunity to calm me down. doctor was professional and the receptionist was an absolute stud who handled her business like a champ. cannot recommend enough. all at one in the morning.

i have been going through a rough patch the past few months with really bad back pain. i had it under control most of the time but unfortunately it's with pain killers. it's a temporary thing but very much needed. i also have daily abdominal pain and discomfort from my past cancer surgeries that they already had be on the pain killers for. this back pain over shadows it. so they just have me take more for this. i recently moved and my new doctor wanted to try me on the pain meds he likes. unfortunately they didn't seem to take away any of the pain and it by the time i figured this out and told them i was already in very bad pain. then they took some time to respond due to the doctor being out. a little too long. this pain completely changes my life. i can't hardly get out of bed or do anything. i have my laptop in bed with me trying to work and it's rough. so i didn't know what else to do. especially with the covid situation. i wasn't sure. so i called the closest hospital to me, st. john's. they said come right down, they'd be happy to see me. it was a rough ride but at least they are very close to me. i got there and no one was in the waiting room. i thought this is great, get right in! so i got signed in, told them the whole story and went back to the waiting room. i then spent two hours curled up in pain on the floor of the waiting room before my pain doctor came through and they just put me back on the meds i was on before that were working. it was a rough ride but i got the prescription and took them and was back to life again. this was 4 hours after the time i arrived at the hospital.

it was a day or so after this that a friend of mine told me that they probably though i was an addict. this is the reason for this review. i am a clean cut professional, i can't even believe i could throw out that kind of vibe but he said that there are clever addicts that exhibit the same persona. all i can say, this is some of the worse pain i've ever experienced and i've had a lot with the gi issues from my past cancer. i was wondering why two different people came into the er after me and got right in. they just kept telling me all their beds are full. so i guess it's true. i will do all i can to avoid this place if i can. unfortunately it's the only hospital around me from what i'm seeing. but i am new to the area. i'll have to explore more and ask around.

i just hope they can read this review and hopefully help the next person that is in pain. stop thinking the worst of people. i hope everyday that most of us aren't bad. i know it's tough with all we see in the world today, but goodness does exist! it is a complete disappointment how i was treated (or not treated really). i am disguised with all of this! so sad!

the only response now is that they think i meant st jude's. i'm not sure where that is at but i live in camarillo and i went to the hospital right down the road from me, st john's pleasant valley hospital at 2309 antonio ave. this is the only one that came up by me since it shows kaiser permanente camarillo as closed currently. so this is why my review is posted here. what is going on over there? are you all okay? i even mention the name st john's in my review.
ended up walking out after being there for hours with no answers or anyone checking on me. it was a super slow day nurses were just sitting on their phones when i left.

i'm going to star(t) this out by saying i'm not thrilled my 5 star winning streak has been broken. sad face!!!!!

i was in st. johns for a week due to cellulitis from a cat bite. it was sever enough to require surgery. the costs incurred are high enough so that my deductible was met many times over. anyone with a modicum of common sense would realize this. when i initially went to the er, they never asked for a copay immediately.

when i was discharged from my hospital stay, i was told to come back for fever, redness, pain, swelling, discharge etc. unfortunately, i had to go to my gp the next day for many of these symptoms. she then called the hospital, spoke to dr mark russell and sent me back to st johns.

when i was seen by dr russell, he was initially communicative and appeared to have a great bedside manner. he seemed kind. then reality joined me in the er: the lady who admits people came in my room and seemed to want a copay. i explained that if she looked at my records from the past week and my insurance plan(she has easy access to all of this), she would see i was way over my deductible and a copay would not be required. this is where it turns into fun times!!!! dr russell came back into my room one more time. i was told to 'be quiet'(his exact words)when i tried to ask a question. huh? i just gave your hospital how much revenue and you are telling me to not ask questions about my care? what is that? isn't that my rite as a patient? that is confusing and rather irritating. after he left my room, he then ordered a brace for my wrist although the incision is by my knuckles. i asked to speak to him as this didn't make sense and he was charging my insurance for it(you can see the money theme starting, can't you?). i was told that he wouldn't be coming in my room again. i asked for a patient advocate. i got the er manager. that is akin to asking for a democrat and getting mitch mcconnell; farthest thing from the request. the er manager told me that dr russell had already come in my room multiple times to talk to me about my care and that he would not be coming in again. i responded that he had only come in twice. the er manager pretty much told me i was lying without having the guts to just state her claim. own your sh*t, woman. i asked her to bring dr russell in so we could get to the bottom of this(remember: st johns is still getting paid for my visit: $$$). the er manager said no. i told her she could look at the security cameras to see i was telling the truth. i was ignored. why would you not look at the evidence that would point you to the truth? that is moronic. long story short: i was essentially escorted out of the er by the er manager who brought in security guards to help. i'm 5'7", 117 lbs and i have one working hand. i'm not a real threat and i'm getting escorted out for not paying a copay? it was surreal. i was in shock. on the way out, i was able to address dr russell's lies with him. his response? he looked like a fish on dry land gasping for air. i received a bunch of subterfuge and not one indication as to why he lied. yes, i did call him a liar eventually. i spoke the truth. at least one person there had the spine to do so.

my final moments at st johns were in the parking lot, two security guards hovering over me, blood dripping down my arm from my iv wound which was not bandaged properly. as a cherry on top, the blood dripped onto my brand new pair of lululemon white studio pants that i just wore for the first time. those suckers in my size are rare!!!  that makes me bitter. that awesomeness is my final visual of st johns. i had to fight to get a quarter cup of cold water and when it was given to me by the security guard(who called me a liar. huh? yes, he was also called out and he did the 'fish' thing) he said, 'that's all you are getting.' a hospital refuses to give a paying patient more than a quarter cup of water? that's rich. i feel like i'm writing a dark comedy. all due to not paying a copay.

have i tried to file a complaint with st john's? of course i have. i have yet to receive a response from two phone calls and 3 online attempts. i have even sent a message to the president. radio silence. to be expected at this point considering they essentially have their insurance money. unfortunately, i now have to bother with the medical board because i can't have the guilt of this happening to someone else and myself not having done something about it. frustrating.

finally and the reason i am most upset(besides the pants): after the way i was treated there, it is clear i would be an idiot to go back. so the hospital that i have used for any emergency in the past is now a no go. i have met 3 drs in the past 20 years that i trust with any general care. dr davies who is an ed dr. at st johns is/was one of them. i now will be unable to see him and be treated by him again. that makes me fume. thanks on that st johns. great job!!!!! go humankindness!!!!

i have a huge problem with this place, my father went into congestive heart failure and also had kidney disease. they treated him and discharged him and unfortunately he weighed significantly more than when he went in, they were supposed to remove fluid from him, dialysis or diuretics, whatever they could. on multiple occasions he had to wait in upwards of 45 minutes to be helped to the restroom. he ended up urinating on himself because no one came within the ten minutes promised. they ended up releasing him in worse condition than when he went in. after he was released he went home and then went to his doctor whom told him he never should have been released. an ambulance took him to another facility where he ended up dying in dialysis. we are discussing  the process of filing a wrongful death lawsuit against dignity health st johns pleasant valley hospital for releasing him too early. why call it dignity health if you let your patients wait so long to go to the restroom without help that they piss themselves! you are an awful hospital and i hope no one brings their sick family members there.

my son got a rock stuck in his ear recently and we ended up needing to have it surgically removed (yikes!).  i can't say enough good things about the hospital's treatment of us, they were kind and helpful and really kind and reassuring to him (he's 7) - they also came up with a nice alternative to an iv when they saw how frightened he was of the idea.  it was a great experience.

we wanted to give a shout to our wonderful rn dalila in the center for women and newborns at henry mayo hospital. she made our time here absolutely incredible. always attentive and went above and beyond when it came to caring for my wife and newborn son. she always made us feel like we were her only patients, knew what she was talking about when explaining any concerns she was having and she caught things that made a big difference in care for both my wife and son. she really treated us as if we were family. we were blessed to have had you as our nurse and grateful for all that you did throughout our stay.

another couple quick shout out to dr. navid and crew in the surgery room who did an amazing job delivering my son and making my wife feel comfortable and relaxed...rn carolyn in the center for women and newborns, you are an awesome nurse, very comforting, and understanding during our time here.

we are sincerely grateful for you all.l and may god bless you and all your families as you did with ours. thanks again!!

some of the nursing staff are so overworked that they are apathetic to their patients care. the younger staff on rotation once in a while that might have some energy left show some more care but also seem to just participate in looking away just to get their hours done with. most of the time they are not busy, in fact, even watching tv and scrolling instagram on their cell phones, but will make excuses to respond or push patients to ask another nurse and bounce patients around multiple around without doing any worthwhile action. while in their care, i was assaulted with a closed jaw facial punch by another delusional patient and while in their care, i also witnessed the nursing staff repeatedly agitate patients. one patient at one point kicked chairs and tables at another patient and nursing staff. i also witnessed patients being sedated with probably long term damaging drugs with minimal consent and asked question wheeled in for business. there were also patients that would request to leave or ask for basic necessities including toiletries, clothing, or ask for needed medical attention being denied. the staffing is also i consistently versed on their resources and policies. i asked to see a physician for severe rashes over multiple days as well as clothing needs and was denied by a few nurses and then another nurse said the the first few nurses i asked gave me a wrong answer. either way, none of the requests get honored or even considered, rather, they get dismissed or given a fake excuse with a fake promise of "later" or "in a few hours" or "soon" and similar that never come to fruition. one perverted nurse walked into my restroom and watched me bottoms naked without knocking on a closed door or voicing that he was conducting a rounds check. 

the doctor i was assigned to work with did not do a significant amount of meaningful work, having only short sessions without any significant care and then shooing away patients and just rapidly giving medications. in my experience, i was not even given explaination or told i was being given medication until it showed up and i was told as a requirement to leave, i must obey their every word and take medications that i was told what they were or why i was taking them. at most, when i asked, i was just given the name of the drug for the first few doses and nothing more. after a few times, i was given summary sheets after repeated requests. they seemed to also lied to family members about actual happenings and reporting because my experience was inconsistent with what they were told. i was also directly lied to about their discharge plans and reasonings including lied to about timeframe, execution, billing, and reporting. i wonder if what do is potentially fraudulent. i know for sure at least that it is not beneficial to patient care. 

if you are looking for a place that cares, this is not it. patient rights do not exist and individuals leave with heavier, not lighter feelings.

i had to visit recently during the c19 epidemic due to an unrelated issue. i came by ambulance at 4:30 in the morning. the nursing staff that helped deserve the star.

after getting blood tests and the covid test i was transferred to the covid watch floor till my results came back and care was good. 

my test came back in a day and i was negative, but still i was experiencing abdominal pain, and a high fever as well as vomiting and other issues. i was transferred to another area of the hospital where i was left mostly on my own, and i had to buzz the nurses to remind them when i need pain meds or when my iv was running out.

then a doctor came in to speak with me. i didn't catch his name, but he was an older indian man. he told me the covid was priority and i should be sent home. i was appalled. i could barely walk on my own, and still didn't know what was wrong. i started to cry and he left. apparently no one told him that i was waiting on being transferred to kaiser. 

i spent three more days at kaiser in panorama city, on antibiotics, fluids and potassium on iv. it took that long for my fever to stop and my body to start working again. when i arrived my kidneys were failing. 

if that doctor had his way and i was not insured, he would have sent me home to die. never going to hm again.

worst experience. if negative stars were available, i would give them that. rude, unprofessional, not understanding nor empathetic to your situation. they don't care. they discharge your loved ones without letting you know even though you have asked multiple times to everyone to let you know. nurses are rude and inconsiderate. social workers extremely rude and offensive, in particular diane, case manager. they don't return calls and do not care about your loved ones. these people should not be working in this area because they are not caring nor empathetic and they are doing it just for the money. extremely unprofessional.

i asked the patient (my mother) if i could post this. she said yes. 

if i could give the emergency room zero stars, i absolutely would. whoever worked there last friday are the most unethical and despicable liars. my mother has some long-term illnesses and was admitted to the hospital last week and had to be in there by herself due to the coronavirus restrictions. they discharged her after treating her for adrenal insufficiency, hypomagnesemya, somnolence, and a bad kidney infection, and lastly while right side body pain. we knew about the body pain but not the infection or adrenal insufficiency, which they never called and told us after i specifically asked very politely to let us know as we were sitting in the parking lot. (this was thursday night. my mom says they were polite thursday which is fine, however they still never called us.) not once did a doctor ever tell my father and i what was going on. friday she went back and was discharged improperly in my opinion. when she was released, she was sobbing uncontrollably and telling us that they accused her of taking too high of a dosage on her medication. back when she had sepsis last year-about maybe a month after, they told us she tested positive for a drug to which we told them that her lupus medication will sometimes test a false positive. this is confirmed by other doctors. my mom was absolutely heartbroken and humiliated as she would never and has never taken any drugs in her entire life. this lady is a saint and has been chronically sick my entire life. i've seen her at death's door more times than i'd like to recall but the point is is i lived with her and she has never in my entire life been anything but severely against drugs and even alcohol. now i have a new issue. they lied and put in her file that they had a conversation with my dad saying that he told them she took three times the medication she was supposed to, not once did they call. they never called thursday either, see my photo below, i called them and asked them to call me since my dad was sleeping in the back of the car. not once did they call me. they're trying to say my mom overdosed and is abusing her medication? i've seen pill abuse and she is the farthest thing from it. i'm absolutely so utterly disappointed, disgusted, disrespected with how much that emergency room sucks. i've had so many unpleasant experiences there myself but this has just tipped the boat completely. i don't know who else to talk to or call other than to let people know of the corruption that they're trying to pull and that the hospital and the doctors are letting it happen. i will never respect anybody who treated my mom except for the select few that has treated her right. i'm so heartbroken by the disgust we've found with this profiling. it's despicable and unethical. the most unethical hospital i've ever dealt with. they lied in her file. if my mom has an emergency we will be sure to take her somewhere else where they won't accuse her wrongly of doing drugs when in fact she's taking prescribed steroids for her disease to keep her alive. my mom has already made complaints, filed a letter after this happened once before and has not gotten pretty much any help at all. if my parents are able to sue, i'm going to push them to sue.

in dec 2019 i fell and fractured my pelvis in three places and my husband was not working at the time but we did have insurance then covid 19 hit we were not thinking we would ever be sent to collections at this horrible  time thank god my husband started working and making payments on my bill we were sent to collections less then six months after my stay in the hospital  i am shocked! we are insured and would never intentionally not pay our bill i on top of this had a horrible experience in the waiting room got a generic response from that complaint why bother if you don't listen to these complaints and do nothing! or have compassion!

i can't even believe i'm writing this. i've been treated like a junkie off the street and that my life is worthless. i've never done drugs and they drug tested me. the nurse acted like she was disappointed when the results were clean. she told me sometimes the machine doesn't work. they left me with 10/10 pain and when i got hives and a rash all over my body with swelling it took them 3 1/2 hours to give me some benadryl or steroids to get it under control. last night i had surgery and was alerting the nurse that i was in pain and she refused to call the doctor for anything. she offered me tylenol. every day while i was there i was balling my eyes out. how can someone who's job it is to make people feel better treat another human being the way i was treated. i ended up signing an ama and leaving. the nurse seemed very happy to get me out of there. i have never felt so worthless in my entire life. i'm bleeding through my sutures but i refuse to go back to any hospital. if there is any advice i can give it's never go to henry mayo! they see everyone as a number not as patients. they can treat you like crap and then still collect their paycheck so they don't have to put any effort into their job.

admitted into the er in 2016 b/c i was experiencing tightness in my chest, irregular heart activity, dizziness and shortness of breath.  staff hooked me up to an ekg machine and iv drip, when the nurse checked my bp my heart stopped and it felt like a grenade went off in my chest.  ekg machine started to beep maniacally at which point the nurse said "oh sh!t" and turned the machine off.  about an hour later my organs started to spasm violently and i went into shock.  eventually my blood work came back unremarkable and i was discharged.  for some reason they prescribed me xanax.  i could barely walk out of the er under my own power.  days later i returned to the er with same symptoms but my condition was far worse.  after more blood work and imaging one of the er doctors told me that i had gerd even though the xrays revealed no evidence of ulcers.  i was released again, this time they prescribed various gerd medications which i threw away after trying one dose.  a week later i was back at the er a third and final time because i was still suffering severe chest pain and tachycardia episodes (and blacking out).  during this visit the doctors and nurses gave me the third degree, pressuring me to admit that i am a drug addict with suicidal tendencies.  i explained to them i never did drugs in my life but for some reason they ignored my feedback and clung to that narrative.  one of the younger doctors actually mocked me when i tried to articulate my symptoms.  my case manager said they would not admit me into the henry mayo hospital but she would try to transfer me to downtown la.  i waited about 4 hours while she "negotiated with my insurance".  at one point i received an unexpected visit from a social worker who probed me about my non-existent drug problem and depression.  after the social worker left i was discharged without explanation.  my condition continued to get worse but i was finally able to consult a cardiologist who determined that i had fluid building up around my heart (pericarditis & heart failure) and he instructed me to go immediately to ucla.  i was hospitalized at ucla for three days and they put me on a protocol to reduce the inflammation around my heart and within a few weeks the issue was resolved.  i find it interesting in retrospect that the nurse did not report my ekg incident as this was not in the doctor's report, this should have been a critical clue to help diagnose the problem.  i am also perplexed as to why they did not perform an ultrasound of my heart which is how another hospital determined that i had pericarditis.  it's a shame hm got to bill my insurance over 100k for basically doing nothing, and i am disgusted by their misguided efforts to profile me as a suicidal tweaker.  fortunately ucla knew what they were doing and identified the problem without gaslighting me and playing games with my health, i guess that is why my providers say ucla is the best and to avoid henry mayo...

i went to progress west for a doctor appointment. they have clear signage in the parking lot so you know which building to enter. they had sanitizing stations set up for use and there was an employee that helped me in and advised me i could go straight to the suite where my appointment was. 

this building is always immaculately clean, including the restrooms and the staff is always courteous and helpful.

we are so disappointed by this hospital. 

we had an labor induction appointment for my pregnant wife at 9am. they literally called us when we pulled into their parking lot and said they have to cancel our appointment because there is no room available. it sounds like no big deal for them but it is such a great deal for us. 

then we asked if we can come tomorrow, the staff asked us to call them before coming. 

i really doubt if this hospital has the capability to handle what they committed. 

i don't recommend this hospital.

having had a severe sore throat, cough and congestion for about a week, i went to my doctor (wearing a mask they gave me) yesterday.  i was told that i likely just had a severe sinus infection (non-contagious) but that i should probably consider being tested for covid 19.  they suggested that i go to the drive through testing at baptist east; so i did.

there was a quick drive through triage with two stops to determine that i "qualified" for testing.  then they instructed me to park my car, where i was called on my phone and told it was my turn for testing.  this all took no more than 10 minutes.  when i arrived at the first of two stops at the testing tent, i was asked for my insurance card and asked how much i wanted to put toward my $1400 deductible.  when i asked what the cost would be for the test, they told me that they did not know but that i would need to pay "something" toward my deductible for the emergency department visit.  emergency department visit!  you have to be kidding me!   those visits cost hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars and i was in a rickety tent in a parking lot trying to do my part to determine if i had exposed anyone to a terrible virus.   i got nowhere when asked why this was considered an emergency department visit instead of a minor medical or minute clinic visit.  i also told the payment staff that they should disclose the approximate cost at the very beginning of the testing process.  nonetheless, i put $50 on my credit card and proceeded to the second section of the tent to be tested for the common good.

two nurses swarmed me as i sat down in the testing section of the tent.  one took vitals while the other gave me a new set of sinus windows with five different swabs.  when i asked why so many, i was informed that they are testing for the flu, strep, covid 19 and one or two other tests.  five tests in all.  i told her that i had no idea they were going to do all those tests but she said that's what they are testing for at the current time.  and i am sure they are profiting for each and every separate test for each and every person being tested.  i went back to my car, a bit stunned from the encounter, and comforted my bleeding nostril with a tissue.

the covid-19 testing at baptist east took less that being in line at chic-fil-a and should definitely not be billed as an emergency department visit.  i feel that the hospital is taking advantage of the pandemic instead of doing its share to help those affected.  they should know better.  and they should be ashamed.

i wasn't comfortable with our communication level with his las encinas physician.  i was skeptical about the precision of the physicians diagnosis, and his recommended pharmaceutical regimen with respect to geriatric dementia care.

my father was placed into a "locked" facility with suicidal, drug abusers, and other mental patients of all ages where he complained of abusive fellow patients. i expected las encinas would exercise due care and responsibility for my fathers well being by placing him in a dedicated ward for geriatric dementia patients.

i retained a geriatric psychiatric specialist at ucla medical school to undertake an independent examination of my father which confirmed an advancing dementia, and, the ucla physician prescribed an alternative drug regimen.

las encinas was eager to discharge my father due to limitations on his medicare coverage. after consultation with county regulators and medicare, we we're provided enough time to find a replacement facility.

although i cannot recommend las encinas for dementia patients based upon my fathers care many years ago, i caution you to examine carefully las encinas or any psychiatric institution claiming to have expertise treating elderly dementia patients. it's my belief that early, specialized geriatric psychiatric care, is pivotal to prolonging the quality of life for these patients.

my father passed away two years later in a hospice, unable to recognize anybody, eat, drink, or swallow.

i wish you good luck with your loved ones in combating this dreadful disease.

i'm writing this review not only as a current employee(who gains absolute nothing by leaving this review), but as a previous family member of a patient as well. 
as an employee i drive by two other hospitals and dozens of therapy clinics where i could work and probably like it there, but i choose to drive 20 miles one way, to work at a hospital i love. as of june 2020 this is the longest i've worked at one place in my life, and i feel like i just started, and can't fathom the idea of not working here. is this place perfect? no. could things be better? absolutely, but what in life is perfect and couldn't benefit from improvement. in healthcare nothing is as ideal as we'd like it to be, and healthcare workers are humans too. we have lives, families, restless nights and stress just like everyone else. at abrazo central i've never worked where everyone is so connected. it's like we all know when our co-workers need a little help and vis versa. i've worked and been on every floor, almost every department and many group functions, but regardless of what your badge says, everyone is willing to stop and help however they can to ensure our patients are taken care of. i've never heard anyone say "that's not my job" or refused to help because the task was "beneath" them. i truly love the moral, environment, and people who work at acc. even our administrators are not afraid to roll up their sleeves and help out during a crisis. not everyone can say that about the people towards the top.
as a previous family member of a patient, i brought my dad here last year because i knew he'd be well taken care of despite me being an employee. to be honest i didn't tell anyone in the ed(one of two areas i'm never in so no one knows who i am) that i worked there. the dr's and nurses made sure he had enough warm blankets and comfortable. ensured he understood what was going on regarding his health and their plan for getting him better. even my dad said this hospital was far better than banner thunderbird where he was the wk before. he loved that the nurses were so attentive and kind. i made it a point to not blast the fact my dad was a patient for alot of reasons, as a result he got great care not because of me but because the people here truly care about the patients. 

there are so many great aspects to this hospital from our acute rehab, to nursing, dr's, surgery, housekeeping, therapy, our administration team and everyone in between. you can't go wrong by seaking care for you or your love ones here.

i got there around 1pm, got one set of vitals, and was told by the nurse that they wouldn't come in, if you needed anything to call.  i talked to a doctor on the phone who said i probably didn't have covid-19 but they needed to wait for the results of the test.  so for several hours i was left alone until the night shift nurse came on (when i finally got a gown and a blanket).  she at least came in several times to check vitals during the night - got woken up in the middle of the night to get a second covid-19 test since they could not find the first one.

granted, i do understand some of this because of the covid-19 virus going around, but even when i was moved to a regular floor, i couldn't get answers and i got discharged with a shortness of breath diagnosis and a diet plan.  i asked for the echo results to give to my regular cardiologist and was told that i couldn't have them because they hadn't been read yet

and the food was not bad (except for the turkey sausage - don't ever get the turkey sausage) but i really hope not to return to this location especially not during the pandemic, but probably not ever

pch  is a great hospital with world class providers. the billing dept, however, is another story. the billing dept at pch represents what is wrong with american healthcare.  my daughter was seen by an ophthamologist in the pch network in 2018. the visit was covered by our insurance minus our usual co-pay.  in 2019, we made another appointment to visit the same ophthamologist and again, paid our usual co-pay at the time of the visit. one year later, we received a bill for the visit from phoenix children's for $418.  it appears that the visit was coded as a routine eye exam which is not covered under the medical benefit of my insurance. i submitted the claim to my eye insurance and received reimbursement of $45. if insurance had covered this appointment, it would have paid a contracted rate that was significantly lower than $418.  i called the number on the bill and the person told me that was the standard charge for the visit and that i could pay it, but otherwise, there was nothing more she could do.  i asked her for options and she did not seem to be very concerned with helping me.  she said that if i didn't want to pay the bill, that after 6 months, the account would be sent to collections and i could just pay them. i was appalled at the lack of concern or the willingness to help. why should i be saddled with a bill of $418 because i am a cash customer when my insurance would have paid a significantly lower rate. i am just looking to be treated fairly and pch should be ashamed for how they treat their patients and their families.

went here because it was a location near me and bc i have heard good things about this place. came with a foot injury, i held off for as long as i could because i did not want to waste space that could be used for covid-19 patients. i checked in and was in a bed within 5 minutes. the nurse was amazing, i wish i would have gotten her name. doctor asked me what was going on, i said i think i might have stress fractures in both of my feet due to jumping head first back into running as opposed to walking. he checks on them, orders an x-ray. i am asked how much pain i am in and i say 4/10. which might not seem like a lot but i have had major surgeries and have gone without any pain medication because i generally just do not feel pain often. so i am given ibuprofen and i patiently wait. doctor comes in a few minutes later and literally just pops his head in and gives me a thumbs up then leaves. the nurse comes in a minute later and said "so the doctor went over this with you" i interrupted her and was like, no he legit said nothing. she said ok, you have to rest for 2 weeks, do low impact things only, and ice 3 times a day for 15 minutes. then proceeds to say that there is nothing wrong with the foot as the x-ray says. at this point i am like ok, weird, not sure how i can barely walk but no injury is seen. i get my paperwork and see a piece added in on opioid abuse. first off i have zero opioids on my medication list, i never asked for pain pills, nor did i actually get anything outside of a single ibuprofen. not every patient who goes in for pain is fishing for pain pills. i also know for a fact that they do not always put that on paperwork bc i compared it to a discharge paper i had for years before and it is def. not there. super offensive in my opinion. anyway its two days later and i see my doctor, bc there is no way i am waiting the 2 weeks the er doctor told me to, who is very upset by the way. because my foot is in fact not fine. i have a fractured foot and i am being sent to see an orthopedic doctor. not an issue nor the reason i am actually mad but then i was told by my doctor that they should have never ordered an x-ray because more often than not those do not actually show fractures. so why on earth would you completely ignore the patient to order something that will in fact not actually tell you what is wrong? you let a very much injured patient walk out of a hospital as if it was nothing to worry about? not because you were busy, not because you were getting off shift. but maybe it is because you don't actually care about every patient who actually comes in for help? either way super disappointed and i hope you don't get my money from insurance and you did literally nothing to help. 

note: the nurse was fabulous and almost seemed shocked that the doctor didn't even care to explain anything to me. that nurse deserves a raise!

we recently had an ultrasound completed on my pregnant wife at an outpatient doctor's office located near saint mary's hospital.  we received a bill from the doctor's office for the services.  we then received a second bill from st. mary's hospital charging us again for an ultrasound.  why would we receive a hospital bill when we were never in the hospital, we were in a doctors office? this bill was for over $5000 and was billed as if my wife was in the hospital as a patient. we went to an outpatient office. we have been to other physicians in this same building (which is not the hospital) and were never charged as if we were using inpatient services. after further research i found that this is over ten times the cost of this service looking at national and local averages.  we also were not admitted in saint mary's hospital.  

after calling to review these charges with bon secours customer service they informed us that we would have to take this issue up with the billing department of the doctor's office.  once we spoke with the doctor's office they said that it was a bill from saint mary's hospital and would have to be handled by them.  after calling bon secours back, they gave me the name of a contact that all billing complaints go through.  they refused to give me her email or phone number.  they said all issues must be through hand written letters.  we contacted her stating our issues and after some time received a letter back.  the contact only offered services which are openly provided through customer service (pay balance right now 15% discount or set up monthly payment plan).  wrote contact back trying to get explanation of charges and cited local health care cost averages for ultrasounds.  stated that these charges were billed unethically (as if we were admitted in the hospital) and that costs of services were not within market value and were not discussed with us ahead of time.  we waited a couple months and heard nothing back.  we called their customer service and they told us our letter was received and under review.  we waited a couple more months and a collection notice came in the mail from bon secours.  we called their customer service back and let them know about this issue and that it had been under review.  they stated the bill was unpaid and therefore sent to collections.  we were never able to speak with anyone with autonomy, were billed extremely unethically and nobody from their organization would directly communicate with us about their bill.  my wife and i have high credit scores and always pay our bills in accordance with our responsibilities.  this company refused to openly communicate with us or explain their absurd billing practices.  buyers beware!!! there are many other companies providing the same services in our area with far better customer service and for far cheaper.

review:
so i'm a teen who's struggled with depression and anxiety in my life. my parents made me attend a program called aspire, which you may or may not heard of. it's a group therapy program meant for people like me who struggle with mental illnesses and uses a thing called dbt. the program is 10 weeks for middle schoolers and 8 for high schoolers, but there's a 2 week period before that, so technically it's even longer. 

during the program, i felt pressured to pretend everything was okay, just to avoid confrontation with the staff and an even longer period of stay. i have trauma, but i feel like it was ignored by staff, simply being told to "use coping skills" despite the fact i feel more comfortable doing them by myself. i have issues discussing things with my family in the room, specifically my parents, but i was forced to do so, despite the fact it's a trigger for both my trauma and anxiety. one of the staff there even triggered an episode for me, too, pressuring me into saying i had an addiction despite the fact that i didn't, and guilted me into saying i had one during our unit on negative addiction. i've had my stuff taken away from me multiple times, which has consistently been a small backpack with a sketchbook, personal sketchbook for coping, pen and pencil, and a book for reading. it was called a "schoolbag" by the staff, which they had to take away because they don't want me doing homework, despite the fact i was mostly in the program during the summer. additionally, the skills we were leaning for coping were things i already knew and was using, and the program taught us, how i like to describe it, how to be a human being. 

the environments there aren't great either. the room you're in for the first two weeks has gray walls and flooring, and is very cold. there's no table either, and you sit in chairs in a circle while the staff member explains things with a whiteboard. there's no windows in this room. after that, there's two other rooms you use. there's a meeting room, which has one wall with windows, and fluctuated between hot and cold. there's also a whiteboard here for the staff to write on. there's a table here and the colors of the room are bright compared to the first one. the next room is meant for creatives, like making art and projects in the program. this is the best room, since it has decorated walls and two walls with windows on them. there's also a whiteboard in here, and the walls are a similar color to the last room. this room is cold, but only a little. the break room is for in between lessons, and has one wall with windows and is colored like the last two rooms. it's small and doesn't fit the amount of people in it well. the temperature changes in here too. 

at the end of the program, they made me fill out a sheet on who i could contact when i needed help, and they had me show it to my parents. by now, i think you can assume i have trauma stemming from negative experiences with my family, so i didn't feel comfortable doing this. however, since they forced me to do so (with the threat of more of this program looming over my head), i did it regardless of how i felt. at the end of it all, they said i didn't qualify for medication for any of my illnesses and disorders, and all i can assume is that because they thought i got better in the program and by the end it wasn't bad enough to assign any, despite the fact it got worse afterwards a few months later i proceeded to engage in self harm. in fact, the program made me feel worse than i had felt going into it, since not only did staff take away my methods of coping and trigger episodes of anxiety, depression, and trauma, everyone else in the program actually had genuine problems, which resulted in me feeling like my problems were insignificant and didn't matter, furthering my problems. 

luckily, they referred me to a new therapist (i had been seeing one before aspire) who i actually felt comfortable with, and i was able to open up to. one of the positives that came out of this, other than possibly more trauma, is that i got officially diagnosed with autism. honestly, i'm happy i was able to get this diagnosis, since i've always had little quirks, but i didn't know why before they told me. 

but other than that, the program was horrible for my mental health, despite how they say they help people get better. i felt like staff didn't care for me, and that they disregarded my reactions to things and situations. with staff triggering episodes for me, and some actually seeing it happen in front of them, i got little to no comfort from them. they didn't care that having to talk about my problems in front of my family was a trigger for me, and that it was a huge issue for my mental state, despite the fact it happened multiple times. 

if you care about your kids wellbeing, send them somewhere else. even the patients i was with hated it there, and were there because family forced them to go, much like mine.

i just under went hernia surgery at bi milton hospital.  the surgery was performed by dr. rahul gupta.  i was very happy with the excellent treatment i received at milton both before, during and after surgery.  dr. gupta is an outstanding physician, kind, caring and very "in tune" with the illness and needs of his patients. both dr. gupta, and his excellent staff of nurses, are to be highly recommended for their work, care and consideration during my stay at the hospital. i highly recommend this hospital, and dr. gupta. i thank you all for the great care. god bless you all in your work.
bad parking. poor service. avoidable.  i didn't think the back dr. was very nice or polite. rude and fast talking was my experience .
admissions is badly managed and abusive to this prospective patient.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Rock Hill

review:
my wife and i are being discharged today from the hospital after giving birth to our 4th child. we are upset because we would prefer to stay. who wants to stay in a hospital ? but because of the staff here , specifically the nursing staff treated us so well we don't want to leave. 

we were both worried about staying in a hospital during the covid pandemic , but the staff here has taking all the precautions needed to protect us and our new baby. 

this is our second tour at the hospital and we came back because we were treated so well. the nurses and drs are so knowledgeable about everything they do , have such attention to detail and have the best bed side manners they made us feel like family. by the time we left we were all on a first name basis. 

we are actually leaving our baby in nicu because of some complications  but we have zero worries. this will be the second child we have left under the care of the fabulous staff in nicu and have all the confidence in the world. i got to watch them on a daily basis perform such care and techniques and let me tell you they all work their butts off on ensuring our children our safe. 

so to all the nurses and dr.'s in labor and delivery, in post op, to the nicu staff
                                      thanks !!!!!!! you all are bad asses.

i have delivered all 5 of my children at methodist hospital over the past 16 years. i have continued to come back for prenatal care there because the nursing staff has always made a huge impression on me and how they have cared and monitored me and my babies. on feb 1, 2020, the most life shaking nightmare happened to me. i was 8 months pregnant with our last child baby #5 my son. i rushed into l&d because i hadn't had any fetal movement and i was concerned. my heart broke into 99 million pieces to learn my son had passed away and that i would still have to deliver him. going into l&d the nurse that came in my room was frantic i could see that they wanted to find a heart beat for me but there just wasn't one. i remember my obgyn saying sorry and the room being full of nurses. i asked for only one nurse to stay and help me and the head nurse assigned emmeline to me. let me tell you she was calm her presence was what i needed to deliver my son that was no longer here with me. she was patient and not frantic. she explained things to me and my partner as best as she could. and i remember asking her would my baby be cold when he was born...she replied kindly this is my first time with something like this so we will figure this all out together. it was the most real response and i knew she felt not only empathy for me but she was doing her best to support me (a complete stranger to her). nurses like emmeline are why methodist labor and delivery are so amazing. in our grief and sadness we kept remembering her. my partner and i wanted to acknowledge her because she's pretty amazing and deserve to be recognized. death is so hard but she helped us in a time of uncertainty and fear. thank you nurse emmeline for choosing l&d and thank you for being our calm in the storm.

if hell was a place on earth, it would be this hospital. please take your loved ones anywhere else but here. 


we donated my cousin's organs after he was left on life support. he barely turned 18. yesterday was the last day that we could see him before the hospital harvested his organs. you would think they would let family and friends see him. even for a few seconds. but the hospital refused. even with proper ppe, we weren't able to say our final goodbyes.thank god that they even let his sis and mom in.

100% the best. ended up being transferred here from kaiser because they did not have the necessary cardiology facilities.

huge shout out to dr. mauer and his team. calm and professional under pressure and very reassuring.

there's a huge list of people that took care of me and i'm sad i can't remember them all but they were all amazing and i felt safe under their care.

big thanks to 

drs: mauer, soldo, chen
nurses: jessica, kristina, jill, alanna, ahn, valerie, rosella, shi

so i called methodist er to ask questions about testing for covid. the nurse i spoke to stated that even if i come in and be placed in the covid tents i may not get tested. the doctor will pick and choose who can get a test. so seeing how i have mild symptoms i may or may not have covid but i'm going to put myself in harms way because i'll be going into the tent with other possible positive covid victims and not get the test when the http://covid19.lacounty.gov website i went to to find sites states i can get a test no matter if i have symptoms or not but i'm subjected to possibly getting infected at methodist hospital and still not get tested by this facility.

the worst hospital ever ! my mother in law recently had a surgery here about two days ago and she was neglected , they are super unprofessional and rude . i have never ever felt so disrespected and my mother in law as well , she was crying on the way home today on how angry she was how she was cared for ! they lack sympathy and professionalism. i will be filing a report and speaking to my lawyer .

my cousin was in the hospital fighting her 4th bout of cancer for 40 days here at arcadia methodist. of course this was right at time the virus for going wild. the nurses were as nice as a person could be that is over worked and over tired. thank you for kindness and care of my best friend in the world.

absolute shit for a hospital. my mom went in for knee forgery a few days ago and has had multiple horrible experiences with different nurses upon her stay. the very first night an unedcated nurse unplugged her ice machine which is needed for pain and swelling, leaving her in even more excruciating pain the following morning. on top of that, she was suppose to stay until tomorrow and we're here picking her up today because she called us wanting to come home due to negligent, rude nurses, refusing to help her as she is unable to get around on her own. truly disgusted by this hospital and staff. people come here to be treated and taken care of, and it is their job to do so. a patient shouldn't feel forced to leave early because they dont feel comfortable!! if you're going to work in health care, please love what you do!!!

my father went to this hospital to have hernia surgery and ended up with aspirated pneumonia. we did everything over the phone because we weren't allowed to visit. we never complained because we wanted to keep the hospital staff safe. now my father is on a vent with ards. we were told today that, although he does not have covid, we could come and have 15 minutes apiece with him while he died. that was it. after that, they would kick us out even if we were wearing protective gear. if we wanted to see the body, we could go to their "viewing room". we would have understood if my father was a covid patient and would have done whatever we needed to keep the staff safe. however, clearly this is not about keeping anyone safe but only lowering liability. we were treated horribly and compassionately during a truly difficult time in our family. they didn't offer us hospice or pastoral care. they insisted that those 15 minutes was being "generous". do yourselves a favor and go somewhere else. make sure you call first so you know what those hospital policies are, but don't go here if your loved one might be at risk for dying. my father actually wanted me to bring him home instead of die there, and now i wish i would have listened.

this is the worst experience ever.
accounting people at michael s agron is rude and ignorant.
tried to make a payment and refuses to help
telling me to keep calling back later time
now the account went into collection
they said they have no record of me calling them
very rude 
hiding behind the phone

my wife and i just had our first born child name atreus with dr. andrew yeh and it was a amazing experience. he made sure we were taking care of ask us important questions and made sure we were in control the whole time. dr. yeh and his staff was amazing they gave us the option to make the right calls and didn't force us to do anything we didn't want to before hand they explained the process and let us know the pros and cons of our decision. i recommend for first time parents if your located in the arcadia area to have your baby with dr. andrew yeh

this place is better than i expected! the er was clean. i came on a not so busy day and was seen quickly. i had met wonderful healthcare professionals but the following stand out: giang (gigi) nguyen, michelle carlos, beatriz landeros, juan villegas, jose from lab, augie from radiology, and jackie from case management. these guys really cared for me and made me feel better when i was sick! all my doctors were professional, explained things in ways i understood, and attentively listened/answered all my questions. the only complaint i have is if some of the staff: one rude er nurse (lily), one unprofessional lab personnel, and the operator kept wiring me to the wrong departments and some of the people answering the phone were very short with me. fortunately that wasn't enough to ruin my whole experience and i assure you the dr expertise & nursing care is what makes your stay. regular meals from the kitchen were also decent (but god save your soul if you got a puree diet), they were able to accommodate and modify my meal as needed. my room was cleaned daily by marilyn and she was very nice. i didn't know what to expect from this place when i first came, but now i am glad i came here and got treated quickly and respectfully.

you're working your nurses to death.... they walk around looking so exhausted. you expect big ratios that work at big hospitals but don't give the nurses the auxiliary staff to even come close to achieving those feats while maintaining customer satisfaction.

as another reviewer said, i'm likewise surprised at the lower ratings given by some reviewers here. i'm pregnant with my fifth child (the fourth to be delivered by dr. rush or dr. meadows), so i've been to this office dozens and dozens of times. dr. meadows ended up delivering one of my babies due to the timing of his arrival, and i have no complaints about her from that experience--she was delightful. dr. rush is my main ob/gyn, though, and i think she's awesome! i have referred many friends and acquaintances here, and to my knowledge they've all liked the doctors.

about the doctor: dr. rush is professional yet friendly and enthusiastic. she sees embryos and fetuses in every stage of development every day, but she always manages to express excitement for the health of your individual baby and whatever stage of development it's in. most importantly, she's a bright doctor. no matter what the outlier condition or unexpected situation, she remains calm, efficient, and expert in her care. she listens to you, never shows judgement, and she responds to needs and concerns with compassion and useful information.

about the office: sure, their reception desk has sliding glass doors on it, which apparently really bothers some people. many things are simply a matter of personal preference. when i arrive, i just give the glass door a little tap, and they get you checked in. i think the doors provide privacy to the staff and patients alike when they're on the phone and checking patients out. it also makes the waiting room a quiet place to check email on your phone before you're called back for your appointment. the office is nice, clean, and sufficiently appointed.

about the staff: i've seen many (if not all) of the nurses there, and they're wonderful. they're warm, efficient, and communicative. i experience extreme nausea during pregnancy (and have experienced a myriad of the other unpleasant symptoms that can come with the process before, during, and after), and i've always been treated with compassion and attentive care. the nurses are promptly responsive to the nurses's voicemail, and they've always worked with me to take care of prescription needs. the ultrasound technician is also great. she's warm yet professional, and she gives perfect explanations as she goes through ultrasounds. as others have mentioned, the front desk staff is busy and efficient, so you won't get a profusion of welcoming or other chitchat. i personally don't need gushing friendliness from the front desk staff, but i appreciate courtesy and efficiency. i've always felt like they're helping keep the office running smoothly and efficiently.
the worst service i ever seen take 1 hour 22 minutes to write a prescription and release
i wish i could give no stars they said i can't see a doctor and they can give no help at all no questions. chose a more professional place to get a doctor.

my daughter was in this facility.  physical rehab, occupational therapy and speech therapy appeared to be very good. after a week it showed not much therapy was happening. 
 
the nurses ( most not all) lack empathy & caring skills.  not all seem to read charts or personal information. every shift has different ways to go about taking care of patients medication schedule.  a schedule is a schedule! 

my daughter was ignored having serious physical symptoms and i had to talk via facetime to the nurse since they were on pandemic lockdown.  i explained her symptoms that were a serious warning that something was seriously wrong!

after my being given a hard time by her nurse and being told "she knows her name and who the president is, "she's just fine"   well, she finally called the doctor on call. my daughter ended up in the hospital needing medical care immediately. 

if they would take the time to talk to the patients and get to know them, they would see something was very wrong!

the nurses lacked in the area comfort for my daughter.  like leaving the nurse call button, drinks,tv remote and bed controller within reach is important to those with physical limitations. most therapists get  it, the nurses do not.  

as for the nursing assistants, my daughter has some very thoughtful caring ones that she adores. they show patience ,brush her hair and tend to her needs, which can be a lot at times. then there are some that just don't want to be there and she feels like a burden when they walk in her room with a snarling face.

when my daughter was slipping out of her wheelchair, she had to have siri on her phone call me. not one person on that floor could hear her yelling for help! i had to call the reception desk! yes, she fell after the nurse arrived. pain meds took a bit after that.

i would not recommend this particular facility for rehab with patients that have memory issues and are unable to move their arms unless they are across from the nurses station!

after being home under my date my daughter made better progress.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of the Mid-Cities

review: wow! community medical center must have pull with "yelp" because every single negative review has been deleted from yelp. what a joke!

it is my honor to work here with a lot of the amazing, hardworking and caring nurses and staff. although the building is not brand new, but it is definitely full of love. it is always very clean and pleasant. we are not perfect but we all tried very hard to get patients better. patients are getting so much opportunity to get better. car stimulation, lite gait, stimulated apartment, virtual reality, all new innovated es, just name a few. i think we are one of the very few facilities that has so many updated and new equipments for our patients. therapists are all passionated, motivated and fun to work with, too. this is a second home to me and to many of my colleagues. will continue to provide care to our patients and residents  every time and every touch.
fac_name: Inova Loudoun Nursing and Rehabilitation Center

review: horrible hospital. has treated me numerous times, every time was disrespectful & despicable. after my car accident, they thought i was just wanting pain medication. i was sent to another hospital & discovered i had fractured vertebrae as well as serious issues with my shoulder. another time i was taken there by ambulance, the nurse treating me told me that if i wasn't acting so dramatic, i would see that it's not a big deal.

i've given birth to both my girls here in 2007 and 2012 and will be giving birth here for the third and last time due in march. the nurses have always been helpful and kind however, after giving birth, i feel like they need to give us moms a break. this review is based on my 2012 experience. they come in just about every single hour for every little thing when you're trying to rest after being in labor and pushing for however many hours. i chose to breastfeed my kids but at one point with my second daughter, i asked for some formula so that my husband could help just so i could sleep a bit because baby didn't want to get off my boobs and cried the whole time if she wasn't on it and the nurse refused and kept telling me i had to keep her on the boob even after seeing how exhausted i was and crying. i find it so damaging mentally and emotionally to basically tell an overly exhausted mom that she pretty much cannot sleep because if baby wants to be on the boob 24/7 (regardless if you already nursed 15-20 mins every 3 hours) then she needs to just be on the boob 24/7, no formula. no pacifier. formula or breastfeeding should be a mother's choice, not something forced upon by the hospital! and if a mom who just went through labor asks for formula just to get 2-3 hours of sleep, then they should be able to grant that. my last hospital stay was overly draining and i plan on packing formula and bottles and a pacifier with this birth because i can't imagine having to endure 2 1/2 days of no sleep again and being told i can't do something


update: i would love to thank all the nurses who helped cared for myself and my son these past few days. i had an amazing experience with em all. can't remember everyone's name i encountered but to list who i can remember - giselle, stacey, brooke, erika, ana (so thankful for your extra kindness on my last day), anna, angie, maria, sally and a handful of others. 

to the awesome rn's i got the pleasure to have encountered in nicu - idonna, lina, kayla and dr. tan. and the two secretaries/receptionist in front; you guys are truly a god send. there aren't enough words and praises in this world to describe how amazingly badass you women are! especially idonna and kayla who i felt really wanted my son to get better quickly and went above and beyond while also having their hands full with other babies. thank you, thank you, thank youu from the bottom of my heart!!!

the only thing i would really want to inform other expecting moms is that memorial is big on breastfeeding. i went in for sure wanting to strictly breastfeed however going through what i did with my son - your baby truly does not get very much from colostrum which is what comes out the first 2 days. i pumped and literally only 2 to 3 veryy tiny little drops came out. this is why babies lose so much weight the first week because they push breastfeeding only. it should be mandatory to supplement with 1-2 oz of formula after breastfeeding!
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review:
i'm only giving this hospital 1 star because they made sure my son was happy. 

my kids and i were in an accident. because i refused treatment for myself, dr. wittenberg and social worker carole said i had an attitude. having panic attacks and them knowing i have anxiety, they did nothing to help ease my mental state. instead they threatened me with dcfs if i didn't admit my younger son (although he was cleared by the doctors in the er) and they kept me from my son who was injured in the accident, they kept me away from him for almost 3 hours! i was in shock, my ptsd was triggered, and i had just experienced a traumatic accident that totaled my car. no one in this ward asked if i was ok. they never tried to calm me down, instead they coerced me and filed a claim with dcfs causing further trauma! 

i do not recommend this hospital at all and if you can, go elsewhere.
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review:
so disappointed. i came a few years ago and my son was seen by dr. jensen. he was amazing. 
now my new baby is sick and i drove over 45 minutes just to come here. i was seen by dr. jennifer lim. she seriously has no compassion or patience. she wouldn't even let me get out all of his symptoms before she cut me off. she said "ok sounds like everyone else in here".... like i don't care about everyone else!!!! she asks if he's been throwing up i said no. 
10 minutes later a nurse comes in with zofran to stop his nausea and vomiting. what?!??? i just told you he wasn't throwing up. 
i have not slept in over a week! i have been pounding my baby with medicine for a month (fever straight for 9 days) going through bottles of tylenol and motrin just this week alone. 
i ask her if it's something in my house because we're remodeling, she disregarded it. 
i told her my older son has asthma if this could be hereditary? she ignored me. 
he hasn't eaten in 36 hours now, asked if he should get an iv. she said no .. he's had diarrhea straight for over a week. 
my primary heard him 5 days ago, took his time, listened, and said he hears some wheezing in his chest. to keep an eye on it. 
the nurse heard wheezing. dr lim listens for 2 seconds and says nope don't hear anything that it's probably a virus. i asked if we could do xrays she said it's not necessary. i said i will not leave until xrays we're done. ).
stop rushing! realize that you may see this all the time. it as a mother seeing her child not sleep, eat, fever for days, at least act you care even though you clearly don't! 
.. they ended up taking xrays and my son had pneumonia in both lungs!!! 
i swear this woman was so inconsiderate and had absolutely no compassion!! i will never take my children here again! it's a children's hospital for gods sakes! we don't go to a regular hospital but we wants understanding people to take care of our babies! this was the worst experience ever. 
i left, went to little company of mary and he was admitted for a week. he is now doing much better no thanks to doctor lim
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review: the charge nurse, karissa, in the emergency room is a horrible human. i was sent around and around from my pcp to urgent care and then the emergency room. no one could help and kept sending me to different departments. i even told her i had my infant with me driving around and around and begged her to help me. she was so unhelpful and slammed the phone down on me mid-sentence. i asked to speak to her supervisor and she wouldn't allow it.
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review: delivered my first baby here at long beach memorial! my experience here with the nurses, doctors, and faculty members was one to remember. i enjoyed every second of my hospital experience and the care that was given to me by each individual at this hospital. with everything going on at this time, the last thing you want is unnecessary tension/anxiety. the nurses were the sweetest most caring people who made me feel at ease throughout my whole labor and after.
