review: my daughter was recently born premature and was placed in the nicu. the doctor (dr. mcnolty) caring for my wife through the very rough pregnancy were phenomenal and extremely attentive. they monitored my wife's situation on a daily basis and when the time came that the womb was no longer a safe environment for my daughter they took the correct steps to begin and execute and flawless c-section. although my daughter was born early she was sent to the nicu dr. fritsell was assigned to her and has been hand down the best doctor i have ever worked with. thank you to all the nicu nurses caring for my daughter around the clock you truly are an amazing force.
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review:
i came in for an er follow up appointment, to have that setup. i called first and was met with some of the rudest behavior i have ever dealt with by the receptionist. i figured this would change by the time i got to the clinic to fill out the paperwork. she laughed at and mocked me the entire time i was there. ignoring all paperwork that i had from providence. at this point, i had to go back to er to get my swimmer's ear looked at, yes that is all i was there for.

the doctor in er informed me that the receptionist actually broke the law when speaking to me. as er follow up have to legally be addressed. which was great news to learn after i was embarrassed by one of the rudest people i have ever met.

i asked the receptionist at this clinic why she was being so rude and she called for back up. like i was some type of thug for inquiring about her incompetency. because of this, i have decided to continue on the path of filing charges against the clinic for the cost of the additional er visit. people should not be treated that way, she does not deserve to work in health care and her behavior is known around town as many people knew "exactly who i was talking about." of course, she wouldn't give me her name when asked.

they need to rid themselves of this woman before someone with more serious issues ends up dying because she can't be bothered to have decent social skills.

i have met many of the doctors that work here, i have always had good experiences with them. this was unacceptable. i of course will not be using them in the future and yes, continue with pressing charges.
fac_name: Chewelah Associated Physicians Rural Health Clinic

review:
i know they mean well, but the employees here are dumb. like really dumb. 

i recently quit and moved across the country for a new job. i needed a signature from my pcp saying i was fit to work. my new employer said my last year's physical would qualify, since my new employer had already met with me and could see i was physically capable of doing the job. my pcp said she would sign the form. then she said she needed to simply lay eyes on my first. then she said she needed to perform another physical. because i don't have insurance for another two weeks, i strongly opted away from the physical, since all she had to do was sign a form, or lay eyes on me. 

staff called me to set up a zoom video meeting and provided me a number that would not work. she gave me online instructions regarding zoom but failed to explain how to log into the meeting, so for 15 minutes i'm rolling around trying to figure it out, calling a phone number that "isn't taking calls right now." 

the appointment took a couple of minutes. no new medications, no change in health condition, etc. 

"expect a bill in the mail." 

they do good work, but would prefer to screw you over for more money.

it's been as almost 10 months and i can honestly say the doctors and nurses have been wonderful. we have had an issue or two, but if you make your concerns known to the staff they do try hard to make things right.

i had been experiencing an issue that began on a thursday afternoon, hadn't resolved by sunday morning, and seemed to be worsening. not wanting to wait another day for medical attention i went to the walk-in clinic at 10:00 a.m. on a  sunday, prepared to wait an hour or more in a crowded waiting area. but that was not the case at all. there was only one other patient checking in as i walked in. there were two receptionists so i did not have to wait. five minutes later i was escorted to an exam room and promptly seen by craig elsner, pa. i was nervous and a bit frightened. he was kind and compassionate and patiently explained to me what the likely cause of my symptoms were and his recommendation for treating them. i was probably there close to 1/2 hour and left with a prescription already submitted to the pharmacy and some notes about my condition and how to manage it. it was an exceptional walk-in clinic experience.
fac_name: Wenatchee Valley Hospital & Clinics - Confluence Health

review: during this time of emergency due to covid-19, i completely understand that the frontline is exhausted, overwhelmed, and frustrated.   i know this because i am on the frontline as a healthcare provider myself.  however, no matter what the situation presented to us, we are to be empathetic, compassionate and respectful to each patient that we treat.  i did not experience this from dr. mendoza or stacy, np (sp) during an e.r. visit with my daughter on march 22, 2020.  stacy was very dismissive, argumentative and continued to minimize my daughter's condition.  no matter what my daughter told her, the bottom line is that stacy was not actively listening.  because this was the second time within two days that my daughter had presented to the emergency room with these symptoms, this was an urgent situation for us.  who would go into an emergency room where there is a greater chance to be exposed to corona if it wasn't an emergency? in my experience, a patient knows their body and how they feel and we as healthcare workers should listen and not dismiss what they are saying.  we are not always right and don't have the right to tell a patient how they feel.  stacy comes in to discharge my daughter after barely assessing her a few hours before.  there was no end result except to go home.  no.  the problem has not been resolved.  the reason why we are back here a second time is because of the dismissive attitude  presented before.  apparently there is something seriously wrong.  i asked to speak to the charge nurse but somehow dr. mendoza, who never treated my daughter at all, found her way into the room.  she, just like stacy, refused to listen to our concerns and basically in a nutshell told us that they would not be doing anything for my daughter and for her to go home and 'stick it out'.  for hippa related issues, i won't go into detail my daughter's condition but it involves constant vomiting, diarrhea and severe stomach pain.  she cannot even keep down water.  severe dehydration is an overwhelming threat at this point.  dehydration leads to other medical conditions like heart problems or kidney failure.  because i have a healthcare background and know that there is a standard that should be met when taking care of people, my mind is completely blown by the behaviors of these two healthcare providers.  again, i understand the stress that we are all under but at the end of it all, when you are present with a patient, be present and actually be of help and not hinder an already stressful situation.  i have had pretty good experiences at south sub before so i am extremely disappointed and will be requesting that if myself or any family member is in the e.r. again, that these two not be in charge of our care.  they need sensitivity and active listening training asap.  if something worsens with my daughter's condition because of their insensitivity and dismissals, there will be legal action taken.

with the scare of covid19, i called the covid hotline and explained my symptoms to the nurse on the phones. she instructed me to go on to the er to be seen and possibly tested. i went to this hospital because they did amazing when my mom was transferred there after having 3 heart attacks. 
when i got there, everyone was confused and a little irritated that they didn't know what all was going on. this didn't bother me at all because i know it's a very scary time to be a nurse or dr right now. this covid19 is new and the rules keep changing. i appreciated everyone's demeanor and positivity. everyone. from the ladies at the screening desk, to the triage nurse, all the way back to the nurses elise and anne (i think were their names). i got taken back to a special area where they were screening for covid19. it was a little scary because they were wearing plastic robes over their clothes...

my mom was told she needed triple bypass heart surgery. we brought her to penn med thinking it was a great hospital. the surgeon they provided was young, his staff, was also young, they acted unprofessional during introductions to my mother and she opted not to have the surgery after meeting the staff.  she demanded to be released from hospital. they tried to scare her to stay and complete the surgery,  telling her should would likely die if she left the hospital.  they refused her any medication and provided no wheel chair to exit her out of hospital.  horrible service and poorly managed hospital. i had a hard time getting my mom out of the hospital and into my car and not one staff member made any attempt to help us leave. this all happened last may 2019. today my mom is still well, seeing drs and taking her meds. her vitals have been great and still she has had no surgeries.  we suspect this hospital saw an opportunity to use my mom as practice for their teaching hospital. i'm glad my mom refused the surgery as i doubt she even needed it!

a family member had to stay at acuity's long term acute care hospital and we had a horrible experience. we had done research online prior to the admission and we learned that ltac hospitals in general provide poor quality of care. we hoped this place would be different but unfortunately, this place proved us wrong. 

some of the individual nurses and staff we managed to talk to were nice but overall, the administration and attitudes of most of the staff were unhelpful and uncaring. due to covid-19, family couldn't visit so it was very difficult to keep in touch with our family member. we were told that staff were stepping up to help keep us in touch but it was like pulling teeth. they acted like we were crazy because we wanted to keep in touch with our family. we would have to leave multiple messages just to get any response.

review:
i will admit before i go to far into this review that i had strong reservations about my mother having a procedure at memorial hospital. given their past history with infection control i was concerned for her well-being. i have to say that this hospital has had a major turn around! not only was it clean and very well maintained.  every staff member i came in contact with was appropriately dressed with ppe.


now i want give a huge shout out to the phenomenal care that my mother received. first i want to start with letitia who checked us in at the women's center. she is someone who takes ownership and does so from a patient centered approach. i was very impressed how things turned out with her. 

next i would like to commend the nurse who took care of my mother, kiri!  i do not think there are enough euphemisms to describe how fantastic she was today!  her bedside manner was asking permission before completing any task and letting my mother know what to expect. she was patient, a true teacher, and centered on my mothers well being.  if you look up the word caregiver kiri is the picture you will see!

the anesthesiologist, dr. bodin demonstrated what true patient centered approach should look like. though  my mother is a retired nurse this doctor took her time explaining the anesthesia the different levels that could potential be used for the procedure and the outcome for each. 

i was more than impressed today  with the bedside manner, approach to customer service and commitment to patient care  my mother received today!  letitia, kiri and dr, bodin truly made a difference and i can't say thank you enough!!


she along with kiri treated my mother like they were the only patients they had that day.

i haven't been here in a while, and not as an in-patient, although i have visited people as in-patients.  i have been here twice in the out-patient surgery and had good experiences there. the staff was really nice and they did a great job both times.  i have used their urgent care center once several years ago for a bug bite and the doctor there took really good care of me and got the treatment right the first time and i healed up very well with no complications.  i had to use the emergency room for a fall and that was a good experience too.  so i recommend memorial hospital.
they are beyond slow and they don't keep you updated. sat in the emergency room for at least 3 hours.

#1 son had swelling on his face and feeling lethargic and urgent care saw something suspicious on his chest x-ray so they sent us here to the ermmediately. 

this is my first experience with this hospital, it is closest to our new retirement town and it takes approximately 20-25 minutes by car to get here unless of course the seasonal traffic is heavy. that's a big change for me since,  in all the 12 states that i have lived in, i have always been pretty close to an er. but it is what it is. 

the covid protocols are very strictly enforced here, there's a person asking questions and taking temperatures outside and they give you a mask if you don't have one. they only allow adult patients to enter however i am my son's medical proxy so i accompanied him for the whole process. 

the wait didn't look bad at all however the urgent care called ahead and we were taken right away. i worked in er's for several years both in the navy and in a civilian trauma center so my critique will be from an insiders prospective.

the receptionists demeanor, efficient and professionalism was very good. we made it through the paperwork and were taken back very quickly. once inside there was a triage nurse who whisked us into an exam bay, two other nurses quickly hooked matt up to a monitor and got his vitals while putting in an iv line. they drew blood from the iv, which proved to later be a problem, and the portable x-ray was done within minutes. 

a phlebotomist arrived in approximately ten minutes to draw five new tubes of blood commenting that the nurses needed to get up to speed on their, apparently new, iv setups as the original draws had hemolized. that's an unfortunate error because blood sticks are sometimes difficult and of course more unnecessary blood draws are not a good practice for time and for the patient. 

moving on, dr. ronnie sims came in within a half hour of our arrival and assured us that the chest x-ray was just fine and after asking some good questions he just wanted to draw another set of enzymes to make sure that there were no cardiac issue. 

the blood draw was taken quickly however the turnaround was an hour, which could have been done in fifteen minutes, but once they got the results we were expeditiously discharged out and we're on our way. 

there's no way for me to know if our experience was typical for this er, since we have nothing to compare it to, but overall they staff did a very nice job. 

bottom line: #1 son is well and this hospital er does a very nice job!

i found this hospital while have hip surgery to fix an infected hip joint which would not clear up.
in all i had 6 surgeries and spent close to a  month confined  in the hospital over  a six month period.
i found  that all of the nurses and support staff went above and beyond in every way possible.
i will always use northside forsyth as my to go to hospital.

one would think that forsyth county would eventually get a real hospital to serve the citizens of north georgia, unfortunately northside forsyth is still a hospital waiting to happen. the er is a joke with their arrogance and non caring doctors that think they are gods. the nurses try hard and deserve a much higher rating than what i'm giving, however the nurses don't make the decisions. the pas are either forced or just right out ignorant to carry out the stupidity of the doctors orders. 
until north georgia gets a real hospital with real doctors the public is forced to travel down to piedmont or the main campus of emory in order to receive genuine and knowledgeable medical care.

beware!!!very poor care at this facility! boy did this service fool us by sitting us down and convincing us that they were just what our loved one needed . they sold us with a pretty good " sales pitch" that was false!!! 100%
this place had nurses that couldn't care less about their patients and we watched their rough treatment several times which is always what caused our loved one to have external bleeding!! not just once but three different times!! which cause surgery each time! and the list goes on and on! this place is a money trap to allow them your loved one to stay in their facility! beware!

the worst clinic ever. i came today and spent here more than one hour waiting in a line. at the moment of signing in i told to receptionist ashley that i will step out and be waiting outside to be outside of crowd at the time of pandemic. ashley acknowledged it. then she failed to tell it to the nurse when the nurse called me. after that, ashley yelled at me and placed me in the end of the line making me waiting for another hour.

review: absolutely impeccable care here. the best nursing staff, physicians and support staff. spotless clean as well. impressed. not one to be easily impressed. if you can choose,  then choose this hospital!

i was here overnight after surgery. i was told my daughter could be there during my pre op until they took me to surgery. they did not allow her back and actually had my family go home. the doctor came out to talk to my family and was not told they were not allowed to stay. everything went well until i was taken to my room. i was ignored. the iv machine beeped for 20 minutes. i could not get anyone to come help. i finally pushed every button till it was turned off. i was told i needed to walk to go home that day. no one came to help me.  i begged the nurses to help me get up to walk but no one came. i had to spend the night when i could have gone home. the nurses only came if i needed meds or to take my vitals. another patient screamed all evening and i was told by my nurses they were looking after her. i was ignored because she was screaming. if my family could have been there i could have gotten something to drink or gone to the bathroom. if you will not let families stay because of covid-19 then nurses need to pay attention to their patients. i owe more money because i had to stay the night when i wanted to go home.

my best friend had a heart attack and spent a week in the ccu, i have unfortunately been to many atlanta icu's and regular units over the last 5 years because of elderly parents, while 99% of nurses were great, cameron at wellstar was truly unbelievably good. i have never seen someone so caring, and in such a way that made myself and family feel so much better in an otherwise terrifying situation! if it we're my choice i would intrust my life and well being with her before anyone else, and knowing her manor with family makes a patient so much more at ease! i truly wish there was more i could say or do to thank this wonderful person! -joey griffin

not sure where to start.  my wife was brought here by emergency vehicle after a bad fall in september 2019.  we received adequate care overall, but had big concerns including a missed broken wrist that they failed to x-ray, pumping her full of opiates instead of the nerve block they did in previous surgeries with anesthesiologists lying about the sequence of events, and now bills for services 7 months ago, after being given a final balance due and setting up a payment plan.  

dr. reddy was the lone bright spot here, as his reconstruction of her face was flawless.  it seems like he will have a lot of work to do to fix this place.  the daily staff on the floors was very caring and helpful.  hospital administrators, some doctors, and some surgeons left a lot to be desired.  

thankfully, after good care at home at osu surgery centers and local pt/ot practices, she has made much progress to overcome the lackadaisical "care" offered at wellstone, and is mostly on the road to recovery.

wow,  i've never had such a fantastic er experience.  my daughter came home from school early with a fever.  i gave her motrin before bed and thought she'd sleep it off. to my surprise,  she woke up at 11pm screaming with a fever of 104.5. i quickly looked for the closest er on yelp and headed out. this er was more than i could've ever hoped for! they got us in right away and took great care of my daughter.  that even dubbed her the "cutest patient of the night". it was great start to finish.  thanks to all who helped our family in our time of need!!

i arrived in the morning because a family member was having surgery. 12 pm rolls around and i need something to eat (diabetic),so i go to the cafeteria and order a spring mix salad with chicken. after i receive about 5 ounces of salad and chicken, i asked if they had dressing or do i get it myself. it was already on the salad and not diabetic friendly. i was offered a salad with lettuce and fruit instead. no thanks,  i don't want the sugar from the fruit.  i don't expect to be catered to, but for a cafeteria in a hospital? it would be easy enough to put dressing on the side for a tiny five dollar salad, i'm sure. they sure have plenty of starchy garbage though. i paid for the salad and threw it away. it's not like they could serve it to anyone else. if you eat there, ask about everything before you buy. i didn't want to hold up the line.
switched over from northside to kennestone for my 2nd child. so far i love the obgyn staff, the hospital, everything has been a much better experience overall.

i was admitted to kennestone after having major surgery. the  day nurse assigned to me was lacking on basic knowledge she did not know how to turn the lights on or off at the bed  she told me it could only be done by the nurse at the wall switch. she did not know how to unhook the compression device on my legs she constantly asked her tech how to do everything  i was very uncomfortable since she was administering all of my pain medicine. that evening the night nurse was awesome she checked on me numerous times and showed a special interest. then the day nurse returned it was not the same individual but this nurse was worse. she never came to check on me unless she had to take stats. after the doctor came by i was ready to go home when my oxygen level reached 90 or above that was around 8:30 my level went passed 90 and i was ready to go. the day nurse told me she would have to get the iv team to take my iv out i waited until noon and no one came. then the nurse told me the doctor had not signed the release and would have to wait on him  after another two hours i inquired about the doctor she said he was a surgeon and probably in surgery she could not bother him   after several hours i was still there she then told me i would have to pass the breathing test again at that point all i could do was cry. i had no cell phone or anyone to help me i felt like a prisoner with no options. it wasn't until my husband contacted the doctor that everything changed suddenly the release papers were signed the nurse took out the iv (the iv team never came) and i was ready to go  that is when i saw the tech for the second time since that morning not once did anyone check on me or try to help me with my problem. the next day i called and placed a complaint. that was over a week ago and i have heard nothing. it was after 5 before i left

went here throwing up blood. i've been waiting to here back from my chest x-ray for 3 hours now. there less than 10 people here. he told me 3 ahead of me and some of the more serious injuries go ahead. ... what ... if i die i die shoulda stayed home to die next time i won't bother leaving the apt if something bad happens. our healthcare system is complete scamily.

my 85 year old mother fell today and ended up with a huge knot on her head and a very bruised eye area.  we took her to tidelands health emergency. she received fantastic care from the staff, nurses, and doctors.  we were very impressed with tidelands and will definitely use them in the future. thank you, tidelands's!!!!

tammy and kristina to save the day for the otter family !!!  they were able to work with the hospital to allow us all to visit in the dining area together for an hour.  a truly special and much needed time together.  thank you.  i have removed my previous review because of their graciousness.

er isn't the best sometimes because the wait time is longer than usual just because it is a small hospital i'd assume they don't have much stuff/room to see so many patients at once. i've had to wait up to 30/45 minutes before. aside from er i will say that this hospital has one of the best labor & delivery departments i've ever seen. coming from someone who has worked in a few hospitals before. the staff is amazing as well. my obgyn delivers here and i was skeptical my whole pregnancy about giving birth here honestly. i was googling and looking into larger hospitals like uchealth hospital in aurora or good samaritan in lafayette and i'm glad i didn't end up going to those hospitals.  i just gave birth recently (march 18,2020) and i have zero regrets choosing this hospital to deliver at. from the moment i went in to be checked if my water really had broken at home to the time i got discharged with my newborn. i had to stay a few extra days due to random blood pressure issues i hadn't had before on my end and every nurse and doctor i met with/came into my room answered every question i had whether it was regarding me or the baby. i highly recommend this labor and delivery department if you're looking around where to give birth and if you're skeptical as i am i hope you'd take my word for it!

i had emergency surgery after a tubal pregnancy ruptured my.fallopian tube and ovary. although the response intially was slow, as soon as things became very emergent, they did not mess around. i was admitted and taken inro surgery one hour after my intial triage amd er admission. the gynecologist on call was amazing. she saved my life. the nurses and doctors were attentive and i recieved immediate pain relief before surgery and pain was manahed beautifully after. i was pushy anout beinf discharged post surgery and they did allow me to go home soonwe than probably normal but staying would not have been an issue. the after care i recieved was exceptional. i see a lotnof bad reviews for this er however, they acted quickly with my emergency and i will assume that those who had to wait forever probably either werent that sick or could have gone to urgent care. drug seekers clog the ers and actual emergencies are delayed because of it.

thursday march 07, 2019

i went on the 3rd floor to radiology to see a specialist for my sciatica. it was a little crowded, but it died down rather quickly. i get in at 10:45am and out the front of the building at 12:15pm. turns out that i have arthritis in my left hip. front desk associates were all pleasant, professional. i felt very comfortable in this atmosphere. shortly after the first meeting, i was under the knife and i did my 2 week follow up, which was a month, in my case for some reason. the three month follow up i didn't show up due to the fact that there's an app they use that you can use to talk to staff.  they'll answer your email on this app within two business days, which never happened to me. they were quick and professional, however, after the operation it was hard to get in contact with the staff and that's my only beef.

i just want to say thank you for taking care or my grandmother while she was in your care in april. thank you for setting up and allowing zoom calls so that we could speak to her and see her. thank you for the kindness and professionalism your staff showed us when she passed. thank you for allowing us closure and a chance to see her and say our goodbyes. thank you for allowing us to grieve during this time.

this is where my sister - despite all odds - did not die from covid19 complications.  this is where she received excellent care from people trying to heal others while learning about the disease as they went along. a nurse called us three times a day to give us updates on her progress and well-being while she was on the ventilator and in a medically-induced coma.

they didn't just take care of my sister at this hospital, they took care of us as well with calls from the people caring for her and the chaplain's office.  everything sucks right now but for those of us who had it worse for month i can tell you that it isn't their job to check in on the family it was appreciated. these people are tired, they're working hard, and too many of y'all are rude, ungrateful, and going out of your way to make their job harder.  they could have been jaded or looked to self-care first but they didn't. i appreciate it and so does my whole family.  

not being able to see my sister would have been so much harder in the dark.  

***my sister gave the appropriate hipa release for them to do all this.

i had the fortunate opportunity to be a patient here at the end of february, 2020. yes, right before all elective surgeries were cancelled due to the corona virus, or covid-19. the staff was absolutely wonderful! check in was easy, as you go up to the 2nd floor, and the check in desk is right there by the elevators, you can't miss it. the waiting room is comfortable, with nice seating, and plenty of it. there are tables there for your use as well. free coffee and tea too.

they have a nice system in place, where there are rooms that you are taken to, once surgery/procedure is done, and your family/friends talk to the doctor/surgeon about how things went. this is done in private. there is also a board where your family/friends can watch the progress of your surgery/procedure as well, all by the number assigned to you when you check in.

the hospital is big, very big. it's clean too. there is a nice cafeteria, and a daz boggs as well. there is a gift shop on the first floor, and a baby joe's gift shop, if i remember correctly, on the 4th floor as well.

parking is easy too. there are several garages with free parking. or, use the valet service, which is right there by the front door. 

the staff is wonderful, as well as all volunteers, and basically, everyone. 

my stay at the hospital was a good one. i was always in good hands. i never needed anything either. the room was comfortable, and i had it to myself, i didn't have to share it with anyone. the food was good too.

if i ever have to have surgery again, i wouldn't hesitate when told that the surgery would be at st. joseph hospital. thanks for the excellent care!

this is specifically about the er. i went in for having covid symptoms that were irritating my asthma. they basically took me back to a room and scolded me for being there. the doc even admitted how shaky the test is. they didn't listen to my breathing or anything. i went home and had an asthma attack but was too scared to go back and face rejection and humiliation again. eventually went back and was hospitalized for covid. hospitalization was better than er but the er needs to rethink their priorities. this is a pandemic with a deadly virus and inaccurate test, treat all your patients with respect and listen to their symptoms, not their false negative. future hospitalization could have been avoided if you cared the first time.

this was supposed to be a psychiatric hospital but yet they send perfect healthy and sane people to this place to go crazy and actually develop mental health issues. the nurses are insane and they treat the patients lile shit. the family of the patients are unable to visit and see their loved ones. only go here if you actually want to go insane.

by far the worst hospital experiences in my life. and i've lived all over the country. i recently went to the er with severe back pain, was told to sit on an stretcher that was in the middle of the hallway, which i complained about due to the pain, but it didn't matter. i was not administered any pain meds for what i was suffering from, was not even seen by a doctor, was taken for x-rays on the stretcher that i was very uncomfortable on and told i couldn't walk there even though it was far more comfortable to walk, which shows they don't care if you're in pain, was given prescriptions and told good luck and never given a diagnosis. then there are the coding issues. every damn time i've had to go to this poor excuse for a hospital, they have incorrectly billed me due to coding "errors", which i believe aren't errors at all, but rather they're trying to con and milk me out of as much money as possible, and have had to contest my bill every single time. i have never seen a more dysfunctional, mismanaged medical facility. the staff is very unprofessional, incompetent, and i recommend that nobody goes here. putting "northwestern medicine" in the name doesn't make it any better. it's still the same ole shitty kishwaukee hospital. if you can, please go to delnor in geneva. you'll thank me.

this review is specifically for the paramedics that came to my grandsons rescue. my daughter had a long labor and delivery at a birthing center in encinitas. the baby was born with low oxygen and blood in his stomach. the paramedics (cynthia, krista & dan) we're so wonderful with the baby. not only were they gentle, knowledgeable & efficient, they also were explaining everything along the way. they made all of us feel at ease. i also have to say the nurses in the nicu (felicia & michelle) have been wonderful with our boy. the doctors are also constantly doing their rounds and keeping us updated on his condition. so far we have received 5 star service. i highly recommend this hospital.

took my son to the er for a fever 102 and to request a covid test. er dr and nurse were wonderful. so kind and helpful. 4 stars for the experience. however they informed me i should get tested asap and provided me the out paiteint lab to go 1st thing the next morning to get tested.

this review is 1 star for the out patient lab. terrible experience. it is so disturbing to me that a hospital can be run so poorly! we arrived 10min after 7am, they hadn't opened yet. we gave our information to the person at check in, she quoted us an hour wait and said someone would call when ready. (pouring rain outside and they don't let you sit inside) after 75 minutes we finally get a phone call informing us that they do not test adults and we would not be seen. i have now waited close to 2 hours in the rain. spoke to a supervisor (who was very nice) but could do nothing. they sent us away. 

1. train your staff. it is pathetic to think a hospital/lab can be run so poorly.

2. educate your staff on who can get tested and where. 

my reccomedations... no idea! i am extremely disappointed and now heading home to a sick child with no peace of mind!

this hospital is so disconnected. the fact that this is a major children's hospital and still standing is astounding. 
my son has a scheduled surgery and the week prior needed a covid screening the weekend before his surgery. my wife and i both received a phone call in different days of the week and confirmed that appointment, and to tell us the requirement of this screening. we both got the date and time for their drive thru covid screening service.

fast forward to that day, after sitting in a long line of cars that have appointments, we got to our turn and find out this staff member that called my wife and i never put the order in. we are now waiting in line for their outpatient lab.

the mere fact that they couldn't coordinate something as simple as this begs to question whether they can handle tougher cases. it it looks like many people feel the same. 2.5 stars for medical service is nothing to boast about!

rady's childrens hospital is abusive, unresponsive and actually risky to bring anybody too. er is unclean, waits for xrays about 9 hours.  no check in from nurses - no breaks for parents for the restroom without leaving your child alone.  the rooms are like prison cells and doctors and nurses are like guards when you can find them. traumatizing for child 5 tries for an iv.  unprofessional bully behavior. with covid 19 it is your word against the providers.  take care - use your voice - ask if procedures are essential.  you are the authority on your child.  like others - disrespect, long waits, intimidation and inconsistent guidance. god forbid your child has pain. only use tylenol.  they openly say other meds for pain cost too much.  so they don't care if your child suffers.   traumatizing for all.
not my place to be.  the staff acts weird and some don't understand english too well.  i have to explain words which is annoying

this review pertains to the care my 36 year old son received at porter adventist hospital after being transferred from mercy regional medical center (durango) almost two years ago.  two years is the length of time that i have spent trying to get justice for brian.  the lies, the condescending sympathy and the refusal to release recorded medical records (until i hired an attorney) have added greatly to the pain of losing my son.  brian had gone to the ed at mercy where he had a ct and egd the next day.   a giant pseudoaneurysm measuring 10.2 cm was found along with gastric and esophageal varices caused by thrombosis and erosive esophagitis most likely caused by multiple episodes of vomiting blood.  the mercy gi doctor shared the findings with a mercy vascular surgeon.  both doctors said they did not have the skill sets to treat brian and recommended that he be transferred to another hospital.  the vascular surgeon had to have known that brian needed urgent surgery because of the high probability of the giant pseudoaneurysm rupturing.  (brian had never been told that he had a giant pseudoaneurysm. he was told he had a blood clot.) to arrange the transfer, a mercy hospitalist had two conversations with a porter hospitalist and one conversation with a porter hepatologist.  the porter hospitalist also talked to a centura connect representative saying he didn't think porter doctors had skills beyond the skills that the mercy doctors had.  the transfer was still approved. the mercy hospitalist read the impressions from the egd that did not mention the size of the pseudoaneurysm.  the size of the pseudoaneurysm was only mentioned in the findings.  neither the porter hepatologist nor the porter hospitalist bothered to pull brian's records during or after the phone conversations.  they just listened to the mercy hospitalist read the impressions for 5 minutes.  the conversations started out talking about the need for surgery and then change to gi being the main reason for the transfer.  the pseudoaneurysm became a secondary concern.  brian left mercy on a flight for life plane in fair condition, but he actually had dangerously high blood pressure, a map reading with alert next to it and 9 out of 10 pain.  he was given an opioid for the pain right before the plane took off.  there was no plan for surgery when brian arrived at porter, instead he was assigned to an inpatient room.  shortly after arriving, brian's medical chart showed bp/high/alert!, map/alert! - nothing was done.  at 4:39am bp/high/alert!, map/alert! - nothing was done.  at 7:30am mottling skin, blue/pale - nothing was done. at 8:00am bp/high/alert!, map/alert! - nothing was done.  at 9:15am - brian was found moaning, doctor performed cpr for 45 minutes.  brian was pronounced dead at 10:03am.  the nurse manager called to say brian died and within the same minute says, what do you want us to do with his body?  my son's autopsy shows that he died from the rupture of a known aneurysm.  brian actually died from the lack of treatment, and an inept medical system.  per john hopkins hospital study - medical errors account for 1/3 of hospital deaths, but you will never see medical error as the cause of death on an autopsy report or on a death certificate.  as of today, there is a reported 60,726 covid-19 deaths in the us.  as of today, the number of deaths in 2020 caused by medical errors is probably much higher than the covid-19 deaths. medical errors are a silent, rampant epidemic and they are hidden from the patients' families.

complaint 2: around day 17, at this point i haven't seen my children since my admission. due to flue season i completely understood. a charge nurse notice how depressed i was and set up a time and date for me to be rolled downstairs to the lobby for a quick visit. i was excited! it was written on my whiteboard. i reminded every nurse i had just so everyone was onboard. the day came, kids were in the lobby waiting and nobody knew what i was talking about. it was not possible they said. after talking to the new charge nurse, many nurses and my attendant physician with tears in my eyes begging them to let me see my kids i got to see them. my kids waited 3 hours for me to come down for a 15 visit. 
complaint 3: my attendant physician dr elias sucked! he only came to see me a few times and every time he came in was to talk about my insurance (medical) and to be transferred to ucsd. i would here him in the hallways yell at other patients about insurance as well. and about their personal stuff. i quote "you hadn't shit in 4 days, you need to shit". 
complaint 4: one day i was out of my room showering. it was around 12 pm. that's was normal for me. when i came back to my room, my cell phone and flushable wipes were stolen straight out of my room! they checked everywhere. i kept calling my phone and a low voiced male answered once and never did again. someone came in my room and still my belongings. the hospital acted like it was my fault. keep in mind at this point i am practicing non mobile, i had to be assisted everywhere. i talked to patients relations and risk management. both admitted it was my fault and that it anyone can go into each others rooms. there's no cameras in the hallways. my upset question was "so anyone can just sneak in my room at night and kill me with no trace of video" and was yes. apparently theft happens all the time, and still nothing is done about it. i am now stuck with an almost $650 bill to replace the phone. 
complaint 5: me scared to leave my room to shower i didn't shower for two days not one nurse asked me if i wanted a bed side sponge bath. which i needed every day because i had a central line on my chest which you need to have a special bath to keep it sterilized. so day two of not showering i got fed up and asked for the nurse if i can shower he said yes and that his assistant will come in and cover up my iv and central line area, seconds later his assistant came in which at that night was a extremely large very deep voice male. he came in charging at me with his hands in the air and said "i'm not gonna shower you it is too early and i have a dead body to put in the morgue" i thought he was joking so i asked him again can i shower. he didn't raise his voice and said "i'm not playing i'm not gonna shower you i got a dead body to put in the morgue" at this point he seemed frustrated and angry. i got very scared and started to panic with tears. so i asked if i can just have some towels in a wheelchair i can do it myself. he then repeated himself again and said no then i just asked him to leave my room. i literally had a panic attack nurses had to come in to call me down offering me medication to call me down i just asked to be alone and cried for hours and hours. the nurse excuse was that he was just a very large male with a deep voice and he didn't mean to startle me. he then just was just asked to not come in my room. i didn't shower that day because i was afraid i was going to run into him in the hallways. 

other than all of these complaints most nurses are very poorly trained. when you call for a nurse they take forever to reply. my room was constantly filthy from bloody gauze dropped on the floor, caps, dirty gloves, just things that never got to the trashcan bin. they were very bad at recording my p intake and dumping my p bucket. my restroom was filthy they hardly took the trash out. house cleaning was just a crappy job. most days i would have my breakfast tray and lunch tray in the room at the same time. these are just a few things. i came home so traumatized. i couldn't sleep i can still hear the hospital in my head i have nightmares about that hospital.

what a sorry excuse for a hospital. this place is dirty and disgusting. i question the medical training and overall literacy of the staff. dont get me started on the nightmare billing dept! its called st victims for a reason people!

although i was hospitalized, i had a good experience at the horsham clinic. majority of the nursing staff were amazing and kind - few of them were overwhelmed from being shortstaffed and unnecessarily strict. 
the psychiatrist that i saw and the social worker i have worked with were empathetic and compassionate. dr. d and mary-ann (social worker) took the time to listen to my story,  my concerns, different ways of coping to deal with my situation, as well as help step up after-care.
the food was so-so. there were days when food was good, days when it was bad. some of the food service staff at the manor house cafeteria were rude.
overall, despite the circumstances, i had a positive experience because of the people i have met. i definitely appreciate the things they do to serve the people and address our mental health issues.

horsham clinic is godsent! trust me, i'm a review guy, if something isn't on the up and up i'll say it, but when it is i'll make sure to praise those who deserve it. my eldest daughter has been getting the best treatment she's ever received and as her parents words cannot express our gratitude for dr kho (he's the best) his team, and the entire staff at horsham! i'm sure you've read some of the negative ratings, i can't speak for any of them but as for me and my family, we couldn't disagree more with anyone who has any negative to say about this facility. thank you all.

dr. kho and his entire team are great assets to horsham. he is extremely knowledgeable, takes the time to explain in detail of treatment and what he feels is best and is very sympathetic. joe as well as the other faculty at horsham has treated my daughter with nothing but respect and have been extremely helpful through this process. i couldn't have asked for a better place to get my daughter the help she so desperately needed!

thank you for everything you did for my grandson who was seen there for the past two and half weeks. your staff and doctors took very great care with him. i like to thank dr m. kho for all his help and care for him. also want to thank ms mary beth social worker for all of her help. the compassion and care and help you gave us helped us through the hardest time in our lives especially  with (cov19 virus ) keeping us all locked in, my grandson was cared for in a very safe and healthy environment.  god bless all the people who work here and your families and friends all our best to you in the future. ms p. dyson.

our young adult son was hospitalized at horsham clinic. the staff were very supportive and communicated updates daily when we visited.  both good and bad news was communicated in a professional manner.  dr. kho worked with our family, reached out to our doctor and really helped get the medication right.  dr. kho counseled us on how to be successful in dealing with our son's illness, and how to best support our son. he provided articles on our son's diagnosis, and counseled us on how to improve family relations.  it was sage advice in our time of crises.  his confidence, advice and interactions with our family was a difference maker in turning things around for our son. we have never had a psychiatrist in a hospital inpatient setting show so much compassion.
           we had a very positive experience and would strongly recommend them as our number 1 option for mental healthcare.  it is reassuring to know that horsham clinic is out there helping people get better!

i will never come to this hospital again the triage nurses are rude ass shit they act like you pissed them off when you haven't done or said nothing to get the reply you get from them i got ready to ask a question and the lady cut me short like i said i wouldn't come back here if my life dependent on it won't be here ever
$1000 for a covid test with insurance. terrible financial aid program that i don't qualify for because of who i live with regardless of how much i make/my financial situation.

i have updated this review several times, but each time i just feel a need to further praise honor health for being so, so excellent. the support staff is great, including brittany and trish, (or is it tricia? apologies if i'm mistaken,) and my pcp, heather holleran, is absolutely superb. perfect. i cannot recommend her highly enough.

she is fast and reliable with refills, she makes the appropriate changes as needed and explains them clearly when necessary without making me listen to explanations when she knows i'm already aware of what's happening- eg, when my thyroid meds are increased after a blood test, she knows i know what's up and it isn't something i need to have a discussion about, so i don't get dragged in for an extra appointment needlessly. she listens to my (informed) opinions on my medications and will make suitable adjustments based on that as well, which anyone who has ongoing health issues can surely appreciate is a vital thing with a pcp.

finally, she recently jumped through a million hoops for me in order to get my humalog (insulin) covered by my insurance. i went through hell with them because it's a medication i need to live, and it was profoundly stressful. even after her pre-auth got denied, she appealed it for me and was able to make it happen- and she had the kind of personal reaction, happiness for me, that shows a real level of genuine care one doesn't always see. the relief to me is tremendous.

thank you to heather and the rest of honor health for their continued excellence- for someone like me who has ongoing health issues it makes a real difference in my everyday life to know i can rely on them.

i'm in tears as i write this. i just got off the phone with lisa at the family birth place. she was extremely rude to me when i was asking her medical advice. i have developed a rash and was told by my obgyn that i needed to be seen by er. i called l&d because i was instructed that when you are over 30 weeks your baby must be monitored by them.
when i explained my symptoms to lisa she replied with, "none of those symptoms are connected. you could probably have bedbugs."
what?????? are you kidding me? this will be my first time delivering at st. vincent's due to insurance issues and honestly i'm terrified of the outcome due to this phone call. i, (just like every laboring mother) am at the mercy of my nurses when it comes to support for delivery. i feel so reluctant to want to deliver there now but unfortunately i have no choice. i know her attitude and lack of empathy doesn't reflect the whole staff but still... this is heartbreaking.

i can't even begin to express my gratitude to the staff in the emergency department, and all of the other nurses, doctors, and technicians who treated me with extraordinary patience and kindness during my stay at mercy general. 

i went to the emergency department in serious condition (both physically and mentally,) and due to the covid-19 crisis, i was skeptical that the hospital would have the energy, means, interest, or (wo)man-power to address my medical and psychiatric needs. that skepticism soon vanished after experiencing the care and thoughtfulness of each and every nurse and doctor who treated me during my 4-night stay.

what's more is that my insurance partially lapsed and would only cover one night of care. the hospital ate the bill for the remaining nights, which saved me much heartache and financial strain down the road. it was an unmerited act of mercy. this hospital lives up to it's name!

in addition, i had no family that was able to pick me up due to the shelter in place ordinance, so i was concerned about traveling back home to santa cruz on amtrak fresh out of the hospital from a severe illness. once again, mercy stepped in to save the day- they arranged a ride all the way home to santa cruz.

i have been hospitalized on two other occasions in my adult life, and this experience far exceeded all of my other visits, and the attention to detail and empathy of the staff here far surpassed my expectations. i am so grateful for all of the providers who helped save my life. thank you all!!!

**a long, but must read review **

this has to be the worst emergency department in sacramento, with methodist coming in a close second. be prepared to wait many, many hours in the waiting room... just to be sat in the hallway for many more hours. it's an extremely small ed and they are limited on beds and space for that matter. 

i wanted to completely avoid hospitals during this pandemic, but unfortunately my daughter was sent here twice by both her primary doctor and urgent care. they have a tent set up just outside the entrance to check for fever and ask covid-19 related questions. reasonable right? nope! it apparently doesn't matter if you have symptoms or not because they lump everyone together in the same small waiting room anyway. 

the first time we went, there was a young man that had a fever, bad cough and difficulty breathing. they just told everyone to go to the opposite side of the waiting room while he and his mom sat a few feet away from us. to makes things even scarier was they sat him near the entrance door on a breezy day and right next to the register line. so, basically everyone had to pass him coming in and when being called to the back for "treatment". there were absolutely no barriers between us or him! 

the second time was just as horrible. apparently there were two patients that were experiencing covid-19 symptoms and were taken in just before we arrived. my daughter and i sat next to the seat that one of those patients was sitting and we were warned by another patient not to sit that close because the staff just covered it with a blanket and hadn't cleaned it yet. the nurse insisted that it was clean and she was highly upset with that man for saying this. when we moved to the other side of the waiting room we were told by a lady who had been waiting a few hours that there was another man who was coughing up blood sitting in the seat right across from us. she said that nurses with full ppe came out to escort him to the back, which scared the heck out of her. i didn't even realize until we were about to be discharged that these freaking people had my daughter and i sit in the hallway just outside his room for about 2 hours while we were waiting for her iv bags to finish up!!! this ed is absolutely dangerously dysfunctional and i promised my daughter that we will never come back again.

oh yeah, i almost forgot to mention that all the communication were through the rn's, a doctor never even spoke to us once during the second visit. patients are almost completely neglected here. it's as though... if you are out of their sight, you are out of their mind. 

thankfully her ppo healthcare plan allows her to have other options.

my sad prostrate experience .
i went to mercy plaza on 12/10/19 for an in and out, outpatient procedure.lt was supposed to improve my quality of life. over the next week i was in and out of the emergency room for what they said was dehydration. finally a specialist in infectious diseases ordered tests. the infection was in my bloodstream. he was afraid it would move to my heart. so for the last 12 weeks i have been in a convalescent facility, getting i.v.s of powerful antibiotics that aren't working.now they want to give me an experimental drug my insurance may not cover .that means thousands of dollars  out of pocket. it turns out the surgical equipment when they proformed the operation was not properly sterilized. but without an affiliate going to court is pointless. the operation was supposed to improve my quality of life, but instead it's changed my life for the worst.

this place is a complete and total rip off. i just found out i am pregnant and went in to get basic labs which were ordered through their women's center which were in-network with my insurance company, they didn't talk to me about what labs they were going to do (i could have told them not to order any sti screening or blood type because i already know all the results for that since i was last pregnant) so i go in, they take 4 small vials, and no one even calls me with the results, it's been weeks, no i get a bill tho that says they are charging $2500 for what i could have gone to lab corp and paid a fraction for? and then i call their financial help line, and the woman was just like "oh, your insurance company is saying you have to pay this because you have a deductible" oh, fuck me right? low income, pregnant, at home and out of work because of covid with a toddler, and they aren't going to do shit for me, very cool! fuck this place, fuck their service, all they give a shit about is getting paid. i am not going back, i refuse to deliver here, canceling all my prenatal appointments i had with them. 

oh, and those labs they took? my thyroid came back abnormal, thank god i manage my own shit directly with my endocrinologist, because tho it could mean very bad things for my pregnancy and adversely effect my baby, no nurse or the doctor who was supposed to be managing my case contacted me to let me know. always be your own advocate, this place is obviously money first, patients last.
these guys are thieves! was charged $1,000 for a twenty minute visit to have my blood drawn. avoid these scam artists at all costs!

review:
best place ever to have a baby! compared to many friends' and acquaintances' reports of their birthing and maternity ward experiences, mine was by far one of the best despite the complications i endured. every nurse, midwife, and physician was professional, compassionate, and accommodating of my birth plan and preferences. the care, attention to detail, and recommendations made by the labor and delivery team as well as the postpartum teams made a huge difference in our learning curve and made taking care of our daughter when we got home much, much easier. 
in addition, the nutrition/cafeteria staff and environmental services staff were also extremely accommodating, and made sure i was well-fed and my preferences were noted. my husband and i were blown away by the level of service and care we received from every single person who we encountered. everyone who cared for us was the utmost professional; thank you, kaiser permanente! we will definitely be back for our next baby, if all goes according to plan! we are especially grateful to dr. erin vance, and the l&d nurses chris, bobbi, and postpartum nurses elouise, tiffany, and kim!!!

review: i previously wrote a negative review based on the labor and diver experience i had with my first son.  2 months ago i delivered my second son via repeat c-section.  this delivery was a very positive experience.  the surgeon and surgical team were friendly and knowledgable.  the anesthesiologist, dr. miyake, and one of the cna's, i believe her name was diane, were particularly kind and attentive.  the main nurse who attended me in recovery was so helpful and also easy to reach.  at no point did anyone even hint at medical condescension, or speak down to myself or my husband.  each medical professional we encountered was professional, confident and kind.  this was such a turn around from the first experience!  as we were being discharged i commented to my husband that i would update my review based on the huge difference we experienced.

review: first let me start by saying the hospital was beautiful and very clean, all the staff was nice and nurses and midwives (mimi) where amazing and i can't thank them enough for being there every second we needed them during the delivery of our baby girl. what concerned me is the severe lack of ppe. my family of 4 has been isolating well over a month to lower our exposure during this current pandemic. we have done everything we can to avoid exposure while wife is pregnant with the lack of data about this disease. we haven't left the house except twice to see dr before birth. the lack of ppe put our family at risk and caused undue stress and anxiety during the delivery. the nurses and staff didn't even have surgical mask, i asked several times if they could wear but they just didn't have. i even offered to give them 3m medical grade sealed n95 but since they weren't hospital supplied they couldn't wear. i still gave them away to hospital workers but non of doctors, nurses and staff wore any ppe, except 1 nurse. i mean there is a pandemic   unseen before going around and they couldn't protect the most important and vulnerable a new born. everything my family has done for the last months was null and void because we had to go to hospital to give birth, we where exposed to at least 30+ people who had no protection. yes they explained they weren't sick and where screening but we all should know how this virus works by now, and there screening was asking if you had fever or cough, or been exposed during time of checkin. all these nurses and doctors see several babies and parents everyday as expected (lots of exposure). but the stress of close contact with so many people was very stressful for wife who is concerned about new born. i'm just hoping we weren't exposed and will remain healthy. i couldn't even begin to explain how upset we will be if we were to catch covid-19 from staff. again the hospital was great, staff was great i just think none of that matters if we can't protect the most innocent. i don't think that is asking to much. so for now we have to wait and isolate and pray we didn't get sick while we should be enjoying these precious moments. we just didn't feel safe while there!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Diego Medical Center

review: first i would like to thank all the doctors and nurses that put their life on jeopardy to take care of the patients, you all deserves a raise! well on tuesday my 3 years old daughter played lego with her brother and she accidentally stuffed a lego up in her nose when i found out it was too late for me to take if out, i rushed her to urgent care but we tried a couple of times and still couldn't take it out of her nose then the doctor called in an otolaryngologist to tried to get the lego out but because my daughter was crying and moving too much the doctor couldn't help us so he scheduled the next day appointment so they can have her sleep for 10 minutes in the operation room so they can take the lego out. of course being a mom i was so nervous and think the worse scenario, when i took her to the pre op the next day i was assured by a wonderful nurse name joe! he is super nice and sweet, he kept checking on us when we waited for all the test to be done before the operation. then i meet the wondering anesthesia and doctor (dr. schaefer)  that would operate on my daughter and let me tell you they assured me numerous time that everything will be okay and that my daughter was in good hands! all nurses and doctors that i got to meet that day was wonderful. you guys are the best and i am so proud to be a member of kaiser! thank you for everything you guys had done.
