review: another great experience on june 1.  i went to the er for fever/chills and another symptom or two.  lacey took great care of me.  i was treated as a potential covid patient but lacey was very compassionate and easy to talk to.  she put in a great iv in a great spot--never felt a thing.

well besides the less than par service you have available here they will also give you a "discounted" option to pay in full then tell you, now if you get any bills any at you come see me and i will take care of them and then you will get another then another then another until ultimately it goes to a 3rd party so don't fall for the pay me now and we will take care of it, they won't and don't.

this hospital sucks. i've never been treated right here but when they treated my little boy bad is when i drew the line! my son was choking on something and i rushed him in. i was promptly told to calm down and my son choking wasn't a big deal. i was told he would be observed for half an hour and he would be given chest x-rays to make sure he didn't swallow anything. he was in there 30 minutes and received no x-ray. he also began spiking a fever while there. apparently having a fever of 101.5 all of the sudden is no reason for concern! i had my husband tell the nurse and she came in checked his temp said shed tell the dr and never did. this is the night shift mind you. my concerns are invalid and i am just a overprotective mom. never even saw a dr. this isn't the first time ever. the only reason we ever go here in a real emergency is because they are three minutes away from our current living place. they also said it was nothing when i had a seizure and my husband took me there in fear of my and my then unborn childs life. and don't get me started on their labor and delivery unit. they aren't great either. i have had one good nurse the two times i've been there. i also found out they made my son and i stay in the hospital for a week because they "didn't think i would properly care for my son" they had no right to judge. it was my first child for one and secondly they don't know me. this place bis pathetic and i'm not sure why they are still open

i honestly wish i could say this is a good hospital after the new owners took over and it is in someways but over all things have gotten far worse. i'v had to deal with this hospital trying to scam my insurance. saying i got tests that i have never had done in my life. i have had nothing but problem with their staff mostly in the er. for example i came in for my gallbladder trouble, was brought in by ambulance. i was in a state where only when i was laying flat i felt okay. the ambulance crew brought me throw the er and where trying to get me a room, a nurse looked at me and told them to take me to the waiting room, when almost all the rooms where free. the er staff made me sit in a chair, feeling as i'm about to pass out from the pain of sitting up. i then asked if i could get a bed and was told with out any question no. so i called 911. another ambulance came to get me and took me to tmc. never again will i ever go to santa cruz valley hospital. they are nothing but a joke.

so my dad spent his 70th birthday here at doctors community. i can honestly say that they took very good care of my dad during his week long stay. i was there daily with him and from the techs, to the nurses, to the doctors they were all sound and showing nothing but dedication to making sure my dad was well taken care of and relieved of any discomfort. 

our plan was to fly in on friday and have a celebration honoring him on that saturday and everything feel through when he started having lots discomfort and we had to get him into the emergency only to find out other medical issues. the doctors told us then that we had no chance of him getting out on saturday. 

i am grateful that we thought to get him in at that time, i'm more so grateful that my dad is here today at 70 and the doctors were able to get things under control for him to be released to come home.  now he is on the road to recovery and i can only say thank you to the staff from the ladies at the front desk to the ladies and gentlemen in the kitchen, the techs, the custodians, the nurses and the doctors and all the other staff members at doctors community hospital.

as a former employee, i was pissed to get a formal letter saying my personnel information may have been hacked by an unauthorized third party hacker.  shame on you doctors community hospital. you should know better and should have had it security safeguards in place a long time ago to prevent this from happening and ruining an employee's credit.  idiots.

this is a truly beautiful children's hospital with friendly, kind, compassion staff. from the receptionist to the parking garage attendants, from the x-ray techs to mri techs, from the nurses to the neurosurgeons and everyone in between --you will not find a building full of people more eager to make the very best experience you and your child(ren) can have when faced with medical needs. 

the aesthetics of the children's pavilion are stunning. lots of windows for natural light by day or a breathtaking view of the city by night. there is artwork on every wall, and the furniture in all waiting rooms is modern and comfortable.

three of my children have been patients here over the years, so i've seen the quality of care under varying situations and it is consistently excellent. 

my little daughter had brain surgery at vcu children's hospital and although it was the most terrifying thing as a parent, i did my research and concluded she would be in the very best hands at vcu. ... dr.tye is the surgeon who performed her surgery and he is everything you'd want in a pediatric surgeon. it all went so smoothly, from check-in to prep, surgery to discharge. i got to room with my daughter in the recovery ward, every person who tended to her was delightful and caring. the room was nice and there was even a rooftop playground she got to visit while there. 

vcu children's is also where i take her for scoliosis treatment. she sees dr.kuster, and nurse patti. vcu has eos, which is a lower radiation for kids getting frequent imaging. it's a breeze compared to traditional x-ray.  the whole scoliosis team treats my daughter with kindness and respect, giving attention not only to her physical progress, but to her emotional well-being, as well. 

last thing to mention, there is a "sibling lounge" open to all kids above age three, where they can free-play or do crafts with the child watch folks during a sibling's appointment. 

oh yeah, and parking is free with validation. 

*** recent visit: brittany at the imaging desk is my hero! she gave me a heads up that my child's mri was a long one and likely to still be in progress when the parking garage closed. i was flustered with her verbal instructions on where to move my car, so brittany literally walked out to the garage with me and led the way to the safe parking area below. she walked me back through the hospital corridors so that we stayed on track time-wiset iam really touched by her willingness to personally guide me and not just leave it to chance. it's an additional level of excellence in vcu customer service.
fac_name: Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU

review: can't understand the low ratings. from my experience, this is the top hospital in the area! ultra clean er. didn't see a sign of another patient when i was wheeled into a private, glass enclosed area. admitted to private room that was spotless and well-appointed. medical & nursing staff was all top notch, and available to family members as well. tests taken quickly and immediately available. definitely on a par with johns hopkins or similar top-rated facilities.

my dog has heart issues and his vet is currently closed. i called here hoping for help as his coughing has increased a lot in the past week. i asked the receptionist if they're accepting new patients, she very rudely said no and before i could even respond she hung up the phone
both doctors and nurses talked shit about me. did not have a care in the world. accused me of drug seeking. the experience only worsened my mental health condition

i am a bit surprised at the reviewers who are shocked to go home and to receive a bill in the thousands. this is an emergency room, not an urgent care facility, and emergency room bills in the thousands is standard. be familiar with your insurance coverage for emergency rooms in and out of state. everyone should do this.

the facility is very clean and sterile and the doctor and nurses were all very nice. i was taken within minutes of arriving. they have everything an emergency room department needs but this is not a hospital, it's a stand alone center, so i'm sure any emergency that would require a specialist they would stabilize you and have you transported to the local hospital for treatment.

it's right off the strip, walking distance in fact.

would not recommend. nurses here are terrible. one nurse who was way more rude than any nurse should ever be told my mom she has covid-19... not even "maybe you have covid-19" but she was sure...and she knew it without testing.

she had tested negative before and we did another test after visit here and it was negative as well.

medical professionalism 101 - don't say things that are not true to your patients.

this facility did a whole bunch of blood work and x-ray and then told us "this is not a real hospital, we just do very minor things here like broken hand."... um really, it says hospital on your documents and why couldn't you say this when we got there, not keep us there for 3 hours, run bunch of random tests, and then tell us to go to "real" hospital where she had to redo all of her tests...  

would not recommend taking anyone here.

i had a freak accident on my vacation and dropped a dish and it sliced my leg. elite medical was recommended, so my husband took me. usually you don't want to seek emergency medical treatment because of the long weight. not at elite. i was called back to exam room before i could complete my paperwork. the customer service was great. they even took my husband up to a lounge with refreshments while he waited on me. the doctor was in the exam room when i entered ...this is unheard of. usually you sit and sit and wait for them. dr. singh was great. he fully explained that i would need 3 staples for my wound. and in blink of eye without pain or discomfort he placed the 2 staples in my leg. the nurses and other staff was just as caring and customer focused as the doctor. it was a bummer that i needed to visit the er clinic on day 1 of my vacation. but good news is? it was at elite medical center.

also, i'm from california and no problem with my insurance and coverage. i paid my co-pay and o was on my way back to the hotel.

go somewhere else!  i read the negative reviews and ignored them.  i wish i hadn't.  unfortunately, this center cares only about money and not the patients!  i specifically chose an emergency room over an urgent care to get a ct scan.  i did not get one, and was only prescribed antibiotics (which i could've got much cheaper at an urgent care facility).  

laura  called me about 30 hours later to find out how i was feeling.   i told her the medication prescribed wasn't strong enough.  she said i'd need to return, as the doctor i originally saw wasn't there.  i explained to laura that i'd come in for a reoccurring condition.  i asked the doctor if the medication he prescribed didn't work in a few days if i could call back and get a prescription for the regular meds i usually take.  he agreed.  i asked laura if the doctor was lying when he told me this.  guess what?!?  the doctor i saw, who wasn't there mere minutes ago, somehow magically appeared! 

the doctor i saw is the owner - dr. nicholas karr.  after 30 hours, i was told i'd need to come back in - for an additional charge - to get the ct scan i should've received originally.  a shameless money grab from me and my insurance for not doing the job that should've done to begin with.  a greedy doctor and lying receptionist.  too bad.  find another place!

this hospital is great! my husband was seen quickly and with amazing care from the staff, especially dr syska, brad, tayler, ken, worku, and maricel. highly recommend this place for future medical emergencies. thank you all!

do not go to this medical center if you feel that you have an emergency, go somewhere else. i googled the nearest medical center because i started having palpitations over 141 bpm out of the blue. dr. traux seemed very agitated and spoke aggressively to me for visiting while the covid19 is present in las vegas. he was more concerned with why i was not at home than my palpitations being so rapid. my heart didn't seem to be of any concern while he was literally giving me a speech about being out at the er which was the only public place id been too today. nothing is opened and i have drastically been socially distant. he said i was just out driving from er to er possibly spreading covid19 because i previously went to a er when i had allergy issues that were painful. his attitude was so awful that i was ready to leave without treatment and go somewhere else until the palpitations became super rapid again going up as high as 175 but dropping back down again. once this happened he was ready to focus on the palpitations and less assuming that i had covid19. he literally made me feel like i was a uncaring nasty rat driving around vegas giving others covid19 from my vehicle. previously when i felt ill from allergies and using too much bleach i seeked medical attention at north vista er because i was in pain and i was also tested for influenza a & b also rsv rapid ag with negative results, i didn't qualify to be recommended for covid19 testing and i did everything they told me to do, not missing one instruction. all i wanted was to get my heart rate under control not become a target of hate because i showed up at the er. if you have a preexisting condition and its becomes an emergency do not go there! 
the remainder of staff was knowledgeable and kind. i appreciated their calmness and skill of care doing this critical time that is scary for us is all. be safe everyone.

dont fall for the fake reviews that gives this joke of an "emergency" room high ratings, they will offer you no help whatsoever, charge you a fortune and accuse you of being a drugseeker just for simply mentioning medications that have helped you in the past, "dr" courtney downes is the most incompetent dr i have ever encountered  by far, she doesn't even know how to write an rx, i had to tell her to put an amount on it and even still she wrote a strength that didnt exist so i was inconvenienced even further when i went to fill it, anybody that sets foot in this place is a stone cold moron cuz you will get zero help with your emergency just a hard time from incompetent personnel, dr downes told me to take benadryl, an antihistamine allergy medication for anxiety, i plan to sue

do not come here! this medical facility does not take most insurances as i learned the hard way. went in for a panic attack and gave them my insurance at the front desk. the lady was super nice and took my insurance saying i was good and everything was accepted. i got treated and was out of there in 20 minutes. a month later i got a whopping $5000 bill from this place saying my insurance was not accepted!! wtf! complete bullshit. i would've never came here in the first place if they told me they couldn't accept my insurance. and the fact the front desk lady was nice and lied to my face shows that this facility is money hungry! regardless if your insurance is accepted or not, they will tell you that it is accepted! be careful!

i was a patient here tonight in the emergency room and the care was beyond 5 stars. jen at the front desk so kind and proficient. jeff, zaim, michelle c and dr singh all took great care of me. they all were quick, caring, and knowledgeable. thank you everyone for an amazing experience!

amazing and incredible staff! on vacation with family and my older son (24) got acutely sick in a strange town.  went to elite medical center and was seen by staff doctor (dr. singh), nurses (michelle, brad, & ivy), radiology & tech (tayler & zaine), and lab (evelyn) were the best team of care givers in my entire life experience in private practice, hospital, or military installations!   the team worked seamlessly together and in harmony giving my son the top class treatment!  due to their expertise and technical medical approach/treatment, my son recovered in less than 24 hours and saved our time together as a family.  just astonishing!  my wife and i look back and want to thank the team for possible saving my son's life, something we will never know but will always cherish we neve had to.  you saved my son, you saved my family vacation, and you saved a family heartache, thank you!  for the readers, this place appears top class on the outside and exceeds all expectations and more in the inside!

i visited this hospital for the 4th time. i had hernia surgery on friday (6/19/2020) as soon as you walk thru the main entrance, depression and anxiety disappear completely. i feel like i'm in a 4 star hotel and the treatment i received is always tops. from the pre-registration, pre- op, pre-surgery and the surgery (2nd floor) itself, i was treated with respect, sincerity and genuine care. i believe that when i pass on and go to heaven, i will be treated the same way there as i was treated at m.c.f.w.  thank you   -   h.m.

this is without a doubt the worst emergency department in the entire state. if you're in recovery, or you are an addict they will push you out as quick as possible without a proper diagnosis. this has happened to many people i cared about. don't waste your time. the lack of compassion is absolutely disgusting. the management here needs to make some changes before lawsuits out this place into the ground where it belong.

i have called my doctor's office everyday this month. in having a severe allergic reaction to food, i have not eaten since. i am being treated like i am on a hunger strike. yet, all my symptoms have stopped upon removal of food. the debilitating nausea, headaches and stiff neck. i thought the stiff neck was from a fall down concrete stairs 12 years ago. no!! it is food!! nine months have passed with my current doctor. i simply wanted a sibo breath test, and a fibrin glue provider. my pcp can provide a sibo kit, but wants to market me a gi. we had agreed to see what's up with the sibo, and take it from there too. this morning, more neat-o developments and no call from the office. oh, wait, someone did call to see if i was still locked out of my echart. um, my echart is just fine. i have been sick for 7 years now, diligently seeking a cure. 40 doctor appointments in 2018; for not one bit of relief from anything. i show signs of elevated eosinophils now, last week. a sign of autoimmune. sibo causes autoimmune too mr. doctor. causes food allergies as well. his careless whim? = "nothing to see here folks" .. i would like to be taken seriously. i would like to get well. it is 2:30pm.. and no call about me, glad my echart made it

read the petaluma argos about all the mold problems that petaluma valley hospital has that have not been repaired. the roof is decades old and during rains, garbage buckets have been used to catch leaks in the halls.    the nurses have not had a raise in many years because the big corporate owners, providence from washington, who have billions of dollars and equity funds, do not want to give their nurses a new contract or fair wages.  many of the experienced nurses have left to work for other hospitals. the ppe for nurses has been inadequate for the covid-19 crisis, and the nurses have been told how they should or should not wear masks that is not in accord with traditional nursing practice and common sense.  the hospital is old, dingy and poorly maintained because, although they make money on it, big bucks providence doesn't want to spend a cent on adequate and proper repairs.  take your chances here with care as everything is going down hill at pvh.

fantastic surgery center! the nurses are amazing and the anesthesiologist, as well. the facility is extremely clean and honestly, everything looked new inside the operating room. i was nervous going in, but my amazing nurse, laurel, gave me aromatherapy and played spa music, which enabled me to relax and not even need a sedative. the iv nurse was also great, i didn't even feel her insert it at all. highly recommend this surgery center!!

horrible hospital. i had a hysterectomy on 12/31/19, i had atelectasis after. it was very scary. i was on oxygen the care was horrible. the nurse i had that nite, brittany, was so bad. she would turn my oxygen machine down so my level would go below 88 and beep waking me. she was the worst nurse ever and i have had a lot of surgeries. i was supposed to go home the next day but bc my oxygen they were keeping me another night. nurse brittany, who thought she was a dr said i have sleep apnea. i do not have sleep apnea. so on jan 1 at 11:00 i called my husband too come get me. i said take my iv out i'm leaving bc i feel like i'm going too die if i stay here. i went gulf coast, they did an artery blood test and my oxygen level was so low they had to keep me. lee never did that. i stayed at gulf coast four nites. they gave me antibiotics. i was off oxygen the next day. i would not take my worst enemy too lee memorial. is a disgraceful uncaring horrible nurses. i'm so glad i took my care in my hands and left. i hope someone sees this in charge of nurses bc nurse brittany that worked that day and nite should not be there. she's an older woman. a dr office but not caring for someone needing oxygen

let me start with the fact that i was screamed at for having an eating disorder with family in the room. it was their job to help me not traumatize me ... the doctor who did my daily checkup was very nice & helpful only good things about this place. it broke my heart to see a patient named candy not be in the right unit.. shame on this place, after a whole year of healing i've come to terms with what was right and wrong & there's so many things wrong with this place starting with the social workers... no social worker in their right mind are holding a patient back for no reason. they had absolutely no reason for my mother and father not to take me home. they were my support system & i wasn't getting any better in there. i had o swallow medicine that often made me feel drunk & out of it... a terrible heartaching traumatizing experience to say the least

people here were very friendly.  from the front door to the rooms everyone was kind and cheerful, and all were wearing masks.  but what freaked me out was the doctor.  i was visiting my mom and the doctor came in.  first he was wearing his mask under his nose. then he removed the mask so he could talk to me!   finally he reached out to shake my hand.  what was he thinking?   he's in a hospital where the likelihood of contracting covid-19 is already elevated.  and if he does contract it he's exposing all his co-workers and all his patients!  he can't plead ignorance, but what else could explain this?!

wen i was in over thanksgiving,  they basically left me to fend for myself for 3 rays; they really didn't help me with alot, like going to the restroom( walking). i could've fallen! they should've been more attentive.

first off i would like to let all ignorant people know that just because you see a person is hispanic , it doesn't mean that is the only language they speak. the member over the billing , walked in our room. and the first thing she asked with an attitude, was if we spoke spanish. 
then she went on to question my insurance and who was covered. which is absolutely unacceptable. my insurance happily takes out of my paycheck, without any doubt or question. and i expect that from anyone else. i understand racism and i am not ignorant to it . but dealing with it in the middle of an emergency is just ridiculous. sadly the person being treated,  served this country and was born in this country . he also spoke english! so it's upsetting to deal with this . then the doctors came in and treated him as if he was uneducated and a homie . if we were of a different ethnicity, we would have been treated and spoken to properly and professionally.

i had my left knee replacement on monday the 15th at 11 am at the melrose wakefield hospital. from the time we started the week before at my pre op appointment to the final push in the wheelchair.  everyone involved made a tough situation not so tough. all the dr's,  nurses, and nurse assistants were fantastic,  not a bad thing to say. my surgeon dr. berenson was professional and seemed like he really cared. i highly recommend mwh since i have been there often the last few years. good luck to all.

dismissive and incompetent! ed discharged me with the most excruciating pain i've ever had. when i told them theyre missing something, something big they suddenly want to do more tests? no thank you, this hospital is 15 min from some if the best hospitals in the country. ill go in town. complete lack of empathy or concern. never send a cardiac patient home until the pain subsides and you find the cause.

i was treated quite well here. i far away and headed straight to the hospital, from the airport.  i'm paralyzed and barely made it onto the plane, as i had an infection due to my condition. i'm sorry this was the hospital recommended to me. i was treated excellent from the moment i arrived. they took me back got some fluids in me and saw i had a uti. the food was the best hospital food i'd ever had. amazing! the staff was friendly and efficient. i was on the top floor with a great view from my private room. it was excellent! i had to go to a short term physical rehab to get some strength and to get social work to help me find more adequate home care. i would have given this place 5 stars because i had something of sentimental value, not to mention monetary value, taken during my sleep. i notified security and nothing was done to resolve that issue. i'm still trying to resolve that he. that's hurt huh huge to me. otherwise, this place is awesome, with excellent nurses, drs, and cnas. i highly recommend this place!

review:
i had a very weird billing experience at this hospital. i came to get my jaw checked out and the receptionist charged me two times my copay for the visit. she assured me she would get me my refund. for several months, i contact their office at least once a month and they assure me they're still working on getting me my refund and that they have this same issue with other patients. another month goes by, and i finally get something in the mail. it's not refund. it was a bill saying i owe the hospital copay. i ignore it since i had already paid it (and paid twice). a couple weeks later, i receive a call from the hospital telling me i owe them copay and that if i don't pay, my information will be sent to the collections agency. they claim that they sent me the full refund by mistake and i have to pay them back the difference. at this point, i'm very upset at the hospital, because i've been very patient with them but they give me less than a month to pay them before i get sent to the collection agency. i had no choice to pay but to pay what i didn't owe. in the end, i paid the hospital three times what i was supposed to. meanwhile i was still waiting on my refund they promised me half a year ago. 

tldr; i visited the hospital once and got charged three times. i did get my refund in the end but half a year later and only after they decided to charged me one for time for the same visit

review:
regenerative orthopaedics & spine institute (rosi) scheduled my spine surgery at piedmont henry, due to insurance related requirements.
dr. zaidi did the surgery, with his surgical team from rosi. they were incredible.
the entire outpatient group at piedmont henry was absolutely awesome and totally committed to making me comfortable, answering questions and getting me through the surgery with a minimum of issues.
i was totally impressed with the hospital and the staff in the outpatient area was incredible! thank you all for doing such a great job in a great way!

sandy shubert an employee of piedmont is a bigot as you can see from her comments. she refers to a funeral as a 3 ring circus from the hood.  after seeing this i shall not give piedmont another dime even if it's from my insurance company!!!

very disappointed in this hospital!! i had a loved one in this hospital. she was on the 2nd floor. this nohospital has  sense of urgency. she waited 2 hours for something to calm her down, if that wasn't enough she wanted to go to sleep also another hour and a half  for that. piedmont has always had a good reputation. i wasn't impressed.

delivering my baby at this hospital back in march was the worst experience in my life. after a failed induction and over 24 hours of non-progressing labor i figure i was going to have a c-section. most likely because of my advance maternal age and underlying health issues. however, the nurse whom was with me the night before my c-section kept telling me that i could still delivery vaginally, basically lying to me just so i wouldn't get angry. i think the "maternity" staff just did want me to deliver vaginally, this is my first and last baby.  
i wished the busted or the doctors would have talked to me the night before about the c-section so i would have been better prepared the next morning. at 8:00am , i was the first one schedule for an "emergency c-section". i was beyond pissed off and hysterical. i literally cried so hard on the operating table, extremely terrified and no one check to see if i was ok. someone  just said "oh she'll be fine"!  after my baby was out, i was taken back to the recovery unit just to find out from my sister they cleaned the delivery room that i was previously in so fast, the cleaning services threw my manual breast pump in the trash.  they corrected this issue by allowing my partner to go retrieve the pump from the trash and a $25 gift card to replace it. therefore, i couldn't pump, the lactation consultant barely helped me latch my baby properly and i had to end up giving my baby formula the entire time.  i am have breastfeeding issues now because of my experience at holy cross.

once i arrived to the recovery room, i was so sleepy and itchy from the morphine that i couldn't enjoy baby's first day of life experience with my family. i could barely hold my baby for pictures but i was so out of it. i vomited multiple times because of the medications from the c-section, more lost time not bonding or breastfeeding my baby the first day. afterwards, i was in extreme pain and they did nothing to manage my pain properly. 
every doctor you could imagined came in just to say a few words with me just so they could bill $500 to my insurance later.  the only physician that seemed caring and genuine was the pediatrician. she really seemed to care.
there is so much more i could add to this review but i want to let this terrible birthing experience at holy cross hospital go! i think about this everyday and it brings me to tearsthis experience what should have been the most happiest days of life was nothing but traumatic. i regret having my baby at this hospital. i am suffering from depression and ptsd because my birthing experience. plus, my son has collapsible hernia for a belly button. please, don't deliver your baby here at this hospital!

i will always have a deep connection to hc! on tuesday september 16, 1986, i was born at this hospital. thank you hc for not botching my arrival, now i'm 33 yo with a wife and 1 yo son (not born at hc) and want to give a review and gratitude (better late than never).

usually when a visit to the emergency room is involved, it tends to be a frightening, confusing, and even distressing at times. one would expect to have medical professionals to show compassion, patience, and helpfulness during such a time. unfortunately, my family's most recent experience with the emergency room staff at holy cross hospital was the polar opposite to each of the traits i just listed above. during this global pandemic, it is completely understandable that no family members can enter the emergency room. this new dynamic requires even more need for there to be open channels of communication between patients, staff, and kin. based off of my recent experience, any attempt to contact our family member (who was admitted to the emergency room) over the phone was greeted with alarmingly unfriendly hospital staff who verbally articulated their frustration, annoyance, and irritation with our phone calls. at one point, the hospital staff who picked up the phone began to openly complain about my family calling too frequently, and to add injury to insult, we could hear other hospital staff join in and express their unbelief and disdain. there seems to be a workplace culture of viewing (and treating) patients' families as obnoxious irritants. is bedside manner dead at holy cross hospital? based on my experience it is a disturbing yes. this is deeply concerning considering holy cross hospital is meant to be a faith-based hospital. not only does the staff reveal a void of professionalism, it gives a terrible representation of what a faith-based hospital should be to people in urgent times of need and care. i know this is worded strongly, but it needs to be said. unless it is a life-and-death matter, i will never choose to seek medical help at holy cross hospital. what a shameful way to represent the hospital, and trinity health.

switched over when my webster pediatricians office closed..... went to one appointment and transferred right back out. absolutely awful experience. doctor jacobs didn't even show up for appt. nurse never introduced herself, receptionist was rude, the building is like a barn. no way.

records took well over a month just to send me my records after calling and calling.
and dr. hawkins is the worst neurologist i've ever seen. late, rushed, sloppy and belligerent.
he's a "here's your pill" kind of guy that didn't ask questions or do a proper examination.
go somewhere else: these people can't be bothered.

review: this place is awesome i came in tonight with a partial thickness avulsion on my finger. i hate doctors and didn't want to go but i couldn't stop the bleeding my doctor  and assisting nurse were friendly and helpful and i was out in less than 20 minutes! wow! i'll definitely be back for any of my emergency needs!

the staff was fantastic and i was seen right away, but the price was astronomical!!! not sure if all emergency rooms charge this much but $2,000 seems excessive for cleaning a wound and putting glue on it (fortunately didn't need stitches or it might have been $4,000).  i know in a medical emergency you don't have time to shop for a better price but if possible, you might want to ask for an estimate before being treated.

i was seen almost immediately. everyone was pleasant - which is important to me! i was in and out in less than 20 minutes armed with references and other information pertinent to my reason for going there. very conveniently located.

i just went to er at the lakes with gout. the doctor gave me 5 pills. that amount of pills will last 2-3 days, not the 7-10 necessary. when i asked the doctor about it, he told me to see a primary care physician. i told him i could not afford to do that, and he did not care. the nurse was even more hostile. the steroid needed is not a narcotic or anything, they simply refused to give me enough pills to actually help me. i have been robbed.
do not go here. super rude, non empathetic, horrible bed side manners.

review:
a social worker who's very familiar with all the nursing homes in this county says, "creekside is about one and a half stars out of five."
  for the four years she was dying of parkinson's, i made weekly visits to a friend, who recently passed at age 95. there were a few members of the nursing staff, though a minority, who were clearly interested in her well-being. unfortunately, all the others took everything i did to help as an implicit criticism, e.g. if i wiped up a puddle, as far as they were concerned i was saying "you lazy slobs! don't you care if one of your doddering old patients slips and fractures their skull?" so they  behaved resentfully to me, to the point of harassment. e.g., they forbade me or anyone else to give her neck rubs, even though her neck and shoulder muscles were so tight; they forbade me to close the door to her room to speak with her, even though she had so little breath i could barely hear her even with it closed. there's a kitchen door near the room she was in that closes with a sound like gunfire; i offered to buy, from my own pocket, a strip of adhesive felt or foam and attach it to the door frame, and they refused. there are no rules for visitors that any visitor can access, and i'm 97% confident that a lot of the rules they were annoyed with me for unknowingly breaking were invented on the fly. a couple of times when i asked one of them where something had gone, she chewed me out for asking and, when i walked away, followed me to continue yammering at me for another minute or so. my sister started her nursing career in hospitals, and if she had behaved that way, the head nurse would have been saying, "ms. ___, please return to the nurses' station now." besides that, every single thing my friend and i brought her was stolen by the nursing staff. how do i know it was staff? everything we brought in was carefully locked up in a cabinet at the nurses' station, and we were given a very official-looking but useless form, signed by a member of the nursing staff, describing the item. example: there were several months, two or three years ago, when she couldn't get anyone to bring her water when she ran out, and she'd have to spend four to six hours thirsty. so i went to a hardware store, got three feet of nylon tubing, sanitized it, carefully wrapped it and brought it to her. i put one end in her water pitcher and attached the other to her pillow so she could have water whenever she wanted. nursing staff stole it, and i say stole because they didn't simply take it away from her and give it back to me--they threw it in the garbage. it doesn't matter what a thief does with an item after stealing it--if they make it impossible for the owner to retrieve, it's theft. the same goes for dvd's, cd's and cd player.

if i could rate this place zero stars i would, the visit was a nightmare from start to finish. i came in to the er on a weekend with agonizing abdominal pain. i'd heard the horror stories about this place but i was very new to the area and was in such intense pain that i just wanted to get the closest care possible. i was triaged and put in a waiting room where i was left to sit in pain for an hour and a half. then finally, i was brought back to what i thought would finally be my room, but i was just placed in another waiting room where i sat for another 30 minutes. i appreciate that there is a lot going on behind the scenes that contributes to long wait times in the er, but this hospital was seemingly empty, with staff just standing around talking. 

finally i get brought back to a room and see the doctor (oluwaseye acabi). nobody asked me for a list of medications i was currently on or for any sort of medical history. i explain to him that i was having severe abdominal pain and that i had an iud and a history of bad ovarian cysts. i told him that i was afraid that either my iud had migrated or i had a cyst that was causing my ovary to twist (which would need to be treated immediately if that were the case). he proceeded to tell me that the iud migrating would be impossible after having it in for a year already. 

he then asked me if i wanted a pelvic exam and/or an ultrasound, which i thought was odd considering he was supposed to be the expert and should know what he needs to do to figure out and solve the problem. i said yes to both. he started the pelvic exam and it was by far the weirdest and most uncomfortable pelvic exam i have ever had. it was clear that he didn't know what he was doing, but i'll leave out the graphic details. 

he then tells me that i am welcome to wait for an ultrasound but that i "wasn't a priority" and would be waiting all night. at this point i was so fed up, tired, and in so much pain that i just wanted to go home and get in bed, there were no beds in the rooms for me to try and get comfortable in while i waited, so i told them to discharge me. 

they came in with the discharge papers and they'd given me bs diagnoses of pelvic inflammatory disease and dehydration. he also prescribed me antibiotics (which i didn't take because i had a feeling i didn't need them, and my obgyn confirmed), and muscle relaxers. mind you, they never took down my medications so they would have never known if i had any medicines that would interact. 

as i'm being discharged, he comes in and tells me "oh by the way, during your pelvic, i couldn't find the strings to your iud. i didn't look any further because i didn't want to inconvenience you." i am still confused as to how he would have "inconvenienced me" by doing his job and investigating the problem that brought me to him in the first place. 

so i went home and stayed in extreme pain until i could get in with my obgyn. within seconds, my ultrasound tech was able to tell me that my iud was embedded in the wall of my uterus and needed to be taken out (something the er doctor told me was impossible, if you remember). when my doctor came in she did a pelvic and was instantly able to see my iud strings clear as day... the ones the er doctor claimed he couldn't find. 

i've been to a lot of bad doctors and hospitals and had a lot of bad experiences but this one takes the cake. i paid $500 to wait around in pain and to be treated with extreme negligence and incompetence. stay far away.
always a great experience at cfvhs.  the team across the board shows that they care. 10/10!

review:
we were visiting california when my son's eye began bothering him.  we went to an urgent care and they confirmed there was something in his eye, but that they couldn't get it out... he needed to see an ophthalmologist.  it was saturday and no offices were opened.  we were referred to choc children's because they have ophthalmologists on call.  

when we got there we told them we had seen a doctor and were referred to choc to see an ophthalmologist.  they made us see a nurse practitioner in order to then see the ophthalmologist.  the nurse practitioner then proceeded to torture my child by doing exactly the same things the urgent care doc did... but she had to give my son a drug to calm him down.  why the drug?  because now they get to charge more for their services.  it was total bs.  i got a bill later from the ear doc, who we never saw for an outrageous amount.  5x more than what the ophthalmologist billed us for.  choc should be ashamed of themselves.  you shouldn't look for ways to milk your patients for as much money as you can with the excuse that... they have insurance.  i have an hsa and i pay for the first $11k.  you screwed me!  not my insurance company.  

i had no choice but to go here.  if you have a choice, stay away!  they are predatory.  i called co complain about my bill and eventually they did give me a small reduction, but i'm left with a bad taste in my mouth because of the doctors bill.

one visit, 4 separate bills.  totaling over $2,000.  and i have insurance.  this is criminal!   i was. it allowed to see who i wanted without paying extra providers for services i didn't want.

i came to deliver a package including a purse with cards and cash and some paperwork to a friend who was staying in room 370. sunday i came by and dropped off her phone and got a little handwritten receipt. i thought it was extra important that i get a little receipt for the purse. someone came by and dropped off some underwear without a receipt which i understand. but we can't go in there because of covid-19 right now. i also understand that. that being the fact that i cannot deliver to this person personally and hand her her purse, i thought it was imperative that i get a receipt for such a valuable item. i don't want to be held responsible for it being lost. four security guards, natalie james mandy and julie, refuse to give me a receipt. even though the head nurse for that room, julie, said they didn't see why it would be a problem. what i ended up doing is sending the person a text on a phone that i knew wasn't working right now just so the four security people would know that i had sent her a message with their names on it. then the main security girl had the audacity to tell me i was being rude. in fact i was not being rude i think they were being rude for not honoring me that small request. i mean like i said if it was some underwear it'd be a whole totally different subject. i was very unhappy with the way i was treated considering the situation.

went here yesterday for severe stomach pain, thought for sure i was getting my appendix removed.  dr. pitt, the nurses, the aide that took me to ct scan, the ct scan tech, registration were all so unbelievably nice and caring.  they made sure i was comfortable, they took great care of me while i was there and discharge was super quick.  i hope i don't have to go there again but if i do i have confidence it will be a good experience.  thank you!

i hadn't been back to this hospital in over 33 years, i was young and didn't have a decent job that offered healthcare at the time. my very first visit to the emergency room was memorable and i definitely would never forget it, while i did get good care it wasn't the best atmosphere. sharing a triage with drug addicts and drunks with only a curtain dividing us wasn't ideal but oh well, what do want for free?! so this visit was a circumstance that i never thought would happen but that's how life is so you have to just roll with the punches, my husband lost his job and so our health care insurance had just ended. i was having unexplained heart issues (fast heartbeat), because of my first experience 33 years ago i did not want to go to the general hospital emergency room. finally i had no other choice but to go, long story short, the hospital has improved tremendously! i signed in, waited 10 mins for a nurse to take my vitals, waited another 10 minutes for a nurse to check me in, then lead me to my own private emergency room where i received immediate treatment from 2 wonderful informative doctors and a couple of amazing nurses. i was fine, hormones was just acting up (menopause), out the door in about 3 hrs (waiting for blood test results). i definitely will not hesitate to pay a visit to this hospital again! i have to say when we were paying for health insurance, i didn't receive this kind of great care, makes me wonder.

review: ok, so this is my update to the florence hospital that reopened in 2019 under new ownership.  new owners, but still a terrible place to go for medical care.  unless you have no choice, i would stay as far away from this place as much as possible.  i had to go to the er and experienced malpractice from a doctor with pathetic medical skills and even worse people skills.  i was there for 5 1/2 hours, in an empty er, the first 4 1/2 alone in the room with no follow up contact by the doctor and no discussion about the tests he was ordering.  in fact, he just disappeared and i never saw him after a very brief and incomplete exam (never even physically examining the area of my concerns).  he hardly said a word to me, and quickly left the room, which in hindsight should have been my signal to get up and leave.  it wasn't until a doctor i had never met before came in 4 1/2 hours later and told me that the first doctor had left and was no longer in charge of my case.  the whole experience was incredibly demeaning and unprofessional.  the radiology/ultrasound technicians seemed nice and competent, but that hardly makes up for me having to demand they scan and ultrasound the right areas, as the doctor had completely misdiagnosed my complaint and wanted them to test parts that were not in my complaint, while completely ignoring the parts that i was complaining about.  to add salt to the wound, they still charged me for unnecessary tests.  while the 2nd doctor was nice and ultimately redid the physical exam and gave me a correct diagnosis in about 2 minutes, he was mostly back peddling and trying to protect his incompetent coworker as i complained about the lack of professional medical care i was receiving.  i will never go back, despite it being such a convenient location to where i live.  i recommend you just drive past the florence hospital and search for a more competent and professional medical staff elsewhere.  i am truly sad that i have to give this review, as we need a hospital in florence and i was hopeful this one would be better than the last.  sadly, my experience didn't even deserve a 1 star review, and if i could give them zero stars, i would.  lastly, i sat on this review update for about 6 months, as i wanted to make sure i was not reacting to my emotions connected to my medical issue.  but now that i've had time to think, i feel even stronger than i did before.  my condition was a simple diagnosis, and they largely failed.  imagine if it had been more complicated or life threatening?  they will get no more attempts at wasting my time, money, or my health, as i will be going elsewhere.

review:
ok so i really want to write this review to personally thank every single nurse, dr, pa, blood girl, ultrasound girl, ct scan girl, registration, check in etc...people my son and i came into contact with on saturday may 16th...my son whom is autistic got very sick 2 hours after eating his dinner friday night from a local wing place... i initially thought it was a kidney stone or something to the like it's so hard for me to tell with him since he can't converse or explain how he's feeling like you and i unfortunately his communication is limited and i have to pay extremely close attention to the signals and what he can tell me he's feeling....in communicating with his dr via messages she said he needed to be seen in the er
omg the thought right now of being in the er causes intense panic in me my thoughts were causing extreme anxiety omg what if we catch the virus...what if i can't take care of him if we get sick  on and on yea the worst feeling ever for me!!  i swallowed my fear and checked in online a registered nurse called within 5 min to evaluate and ask symptoms etc. and determined yes he needed to be seen in the er.  she was awesome.  we arrived large bottle of sanitizer in hand masks on and nerves shot...walked in to the first station amazing guy temp check etc moved on to triage/check in again amazing ladies (my son isn't easy he was feeling aweful and didn't understand what was going on) within a few minutes they had us in a private room, iv line in, blood tests done!!! btw no easy task with my son blood girl and his nurse flawless!!! his dr/pa ordered ct, ultrasound and those experiences same flawless they were not even for a minute challenged by my son they treated him beautifully and with patience...they made sure he and i were always comfortable and informed at all times.  
i cannot say how many times i felt like i was gonna lose it that day i know i looked like i had myself together but inside i was absolutely terrified just the thought of the what if at these times in a hospital almost broke me...it feels good to get that out i know this is long but i really feel i had to write this and just thank these people putting their lives on the line day in and day out right now  to give amazing care no matter what!!! i so appreciate everything and every person that took care of my son that day :)"

what i thought was a routine visit to my cardiologist suddenly turned south when, after some testing, he announced i had to get to the er immediately. that's how i found myself here in the emergency room being told i needed triple bypass heart surgery. 

spoiler alert: i'm still alive

the surgeon (dr. hargrove) was confident and calming. she proved to be exceptionally skilled and performed a successful surgery despite some minor complications along the way. i can't speak highly enough about her.

during several days of recovery, my nurses - there were many - and their support staff were competent, caring and all-around fantastic. actually there was one exception but i believe it was due to inexperience. i was impressed with all the controls they had in place to protect patients while this 2020 pandemic is going on.

as expected, the food was generally lousy although breakfasts were okay. the beds were not the most comfortable. and if you want a good night's sleep a hospital is not the place to be, between getting poked for blood tests all night and patients in other rooms making every type of noise imaginable echo down the hallways. most recovery rooms are double occupancy but i was lucky to have a private room so my stay was probably better than most. 

follow up by cardiac rehab and my surgeon was excellent. 

i certainly hope you won't ever need to come here but if you do, rest assured they will take good care of you. a 4.5 rating from me.

after i parked (special parking lot for er customers) i found mom in the plush waiting room giving info to a lady behind a desk. mom said she was cold and the lady immediately went and fetched a heated blanket for her! we then waited all of about 5-10 minutes and were taken into the back where a nurse filled out more info. then a young man wheeled mom into a semi room. most er's just have curtained areas but mom was in a 3 sided room with a curtain in front. everyone was nice, professional and helpful. i ate at the cafeteria where the cook made me something special becuz of food allergies. everything was very clean, including the bathrooms. we were there from 11am to 2pm. i thought we would be there all day - but was pleasantly surprised. 
the security guard helped us as we left. very exceptional place!

i have had both private and kaiser insurance, so i feel qualified to comment and compare the two systems.  been to private physicians in the bay area (including stanford and ucsf), have had lab and radiology services, and hospitalizations up and down the peninsula over the past 30 years.  i realize people have individual experiences that may not be like mine.

kaiser ssf is designed to handle large volumes of people more efficiently, so it is in some ways less personal medicine.  one can sometimes feel like cattle. however, i don't need a lot of hand holding, and i love kaiser ssf for its relative efficiency.  i've been going to kaiser now as my primary insurance for over 15 years, because i find my coordinated care to be far better than through private insurance.  i like the fact that i can see another doctor in the kaiser system in a timely fashion if my doctor is unavailable.  i like having my meds mailed to me. flu shots are super easy.  your preventive care schedules (immunizations, colonoscopy, mammograms etc) are tracked and you are informed in writing.  

at kaiser ssf, i have never had to wait more than 5-15 minutes for an x-ray or mri or ct or a blood draw.  er was reasonably quick the one time i was there -- i was able to check in and be seen and get a ct, then out the door in about 90 minutes.  the er doctor was kind but also very businesslike and to the point, which was appreciated. the er staff also scheduled an appointment for a specialist for the next morning, so that i wouldn't have to do it myself.  i really appreciated their thoughtfulness. in private practice facilities, i've had to wait over 2 hours for a pre-scheduled simple chest x-ray; over 30 minutes for a lab; and weeks for a doctor's appointment. 

quality of doctors --- i have had some really great doctors over the years at kaiser and outside of kaiser.  (exception: i liked my obgyn and dermatology doctors outside of kaiser better.) my internist, oncologist, and surgeon at kaiser are as knowledgeable and skillful as the ones i had outside of kaiser, but unlike the others, my kaiser doctors talk to each other so the care is coordinated each step of the way.  

my personal feeling is that private practice care is fractured -- the doctors can't talk to each other, and reimbursements with in-network/out-of-network facilities and providers are a real pain. it's sad, and all created because some mbas out there thought they had a better business model.  they broke it, and we will never have american medicine the way it used to be.

i returned to cedars sinai for extensive treatment:  surgery on both feet resulted in complications - an incurable nerve condition in both feet (that potentially can worsen and in some people becomes totally crippling) that has left me with permanent damage, ongoing significant pain, and difficulty walking.  i do not fault the surgeon; this condition can occur after surgery or body trauma.  to stop the spread and treat this, i ended up using the pain center, going for bilateral sympathetic nerve blocks under anesthesia twice a week for more than six months plus some other procedures and another "revision" surgery on both feet a year later that included a short inpatient stay for an intravenous treatment.  that intravenous treatment was to be performed by a doc other than my pain center doctor (who doesn't do in hospital procedures) but needed to be done same day as my surgery to avoid hypoglycemic problems (fasting overnight for surgery and no food for this next procedure).  when this procedure got held up overnight and then was to occur - with no food - hours later the next day, i called a halt to protect myself/my health.  a major "incident" occurred (this "prima donna" doctor tried to kick me out of the hospital without me getting the prescribed treatment, i objected and reached out to cedars' management, head of the department was called to intervene, and finally my inpatient stay to do the intravenous procedure was extended a couple of days and my regular pain center doc enlisted to do the procedure (although i was supposed to have the intravenous procedure twice and was shortchanged with only one).  when i was in the process of scheduling my next pain center outpatient block, i suddenly received a letter from the head of cedars' administration informing me cedars would no longer treat me effective immediately and i should seek medical care elsewhere!  the politics due to one doctor's ego prevailed.  technically that constitutes "patient abandonment" - and it violates state legal/regulatory/medical board rules, particularly given i was in the course of treatment for a serious medical condition.  add to that very few doctors - even in a city as big as los angeles with all its fine hospitals and medical schools specialize in/treat my condition (complex medical pain syndrome) - and it takes months to get an appointment with those specialists, and i got left high and dry.  while i could have initiated action against cedars, i did not:  i was also in the middle of a move, ended up contracting walking pneumonia and had only a month to move out of my residence, and barely had the resources to survive my other challenges at the time.
while i still believe some of the individual physicians at cedars are among the best, there is no excuse for putting petty hospital politics and individual egos above patient welfare.  so know that when you turn to cedars, you take that risk.
(fyi ... i had experienced overblown ego previously at cedars.  i had an outpatient procedure - to drain a huge liver cyst - which required giving me dilaudid (a pain medication) and then putting me into the ct scanner (tube) to allow the surgeon to see/guide him as he cut into my liver.  i began to receive the dilaudid injection - and as soon as the drug began to enter my system, i felt as if i had a metal cord around my neck tightening and choking me.  i immediately grabbed the medical assistant's arm and pleaded "stop," so i apparently received almost no pain killer, and the procedure was allowed to proceed.  
once the (knife? needle? instrument?) got inserted into my side to get to my liver, i experienced the most acute pain of my life:  unbearable.  stuck in the tube and barely able to catch a breath with that much pain, i tried to scream, "stop."  the surgeon replied, "we aren't done yet" and continued.  in agony, i repeated, "stop, please," to which he responded that if he stopped, that would leave the cyst in place (it was about five inches cubed:  very large although not interfering with any function and not posing a threat to me - at least not yet).  the surgeon continued - and it took four rounds protecting, saying stop now, i don't care, stop right now before he did.  i got taken to a recovery room, and called the friend who was scheduled to pick me up later - and hearing me whimper on the phone, she asked if i wanted her to come "now." i said weakly, "yes, please."  
a week later, i contacted cedars to be sure my medical records had been updated to reflect my allergy to dilaudid.  they had not.  i contacted the anesthesiologist - only to hear:  "what makes you think you are allergic?" - and when i explained, he said "no." i even called cedars' medical director.  no one would add my allergy to dilaudid to my records! it would not hurt to add that to my records - but if i ended up at cedars and was given dilaudid, it could endanger (or even kill) me (my docs and pharmacist agree).  sheer stupidity and recklessness.

review:
i had the unfortunate experience of having to visit the er for my teenage son last night.   i was headed straight for dell children's, as all parents of children should, but he was complaining of horrible dizziness and he had a head injury, so i did not feel comfortable driving that far with him.  in hindsight, i wish we had gone to dell.  

screened at front door for covid and masked.  no problem here other than we were not given any introductions.   from screening, through initial triage, i don't have any serious complaints.   my son was identified as a "trauma alert" in triage, due to the mechanism of his injury, and we were quickly wheeled back. i am uncertain of anyone's role up to this point as all staff who came into contact with us failed to tell us their name or role (with the exception of being told we were  "in" triage, no name or role to the person who completed that task.)

once in the room, my son was taken for ct within 5 minutes.  he had been wheeled to the room, placed on a monitor and left lying in a cold, wet swimsuit. upon return from ct, the pa came by to see him.  she was attentive and concerned.  she gave him a thorough exam, but had trouble finding any nursing staff who could assist her to roll him properly to clear c-spine.  throughout the duration of our stay, the nurses were much less than attentive.  there is an informative board on the wall that tells you the date.  ours read yesterday's date and it is unlikely the male nurse attending to us was named paige or esther, as identified by the board.   

the nursing staff was very disappointing.  they were standing at the nursing station conversing about the 6 year delinquency of required trainings for one of the nurse's at work that evening.  never offered a call bell, had to search for a nurse every time, the bathroom floor was covered in urine, my son was never removed from his wet clothes, taken off the wet fitted sheet (despite multiple bed transfers), never offered a warm blanket (standard of care for trauma alert). they did not operate as a team.  if i asked for something, the other nurses relayed the request to our assigned nurse rather than offering to help. when my son left for mri, evs actually assisted mri staff with the bed transfer because the nurses were sitting at the nurses station and did not offer to help.  

the pa was attentive.  if it were not for her, this review would be 1 star.  the pa
took pictures and relayed them to her attending physician, who was apparently involved in care but never came by to see him.  my son was never asked to rate his pain.  no follow up for the tylenol i requested he be given.  the nurses never asked him about his symptoms.   they did not ever assess him.  the only true assessment was completed by the pa and one by a triage nurse.  discharge instructions by the nurse included reading me the titles off the papers and i was told to fill the cephalexin, "which is an antibiotic, i think", the nurse said.  yes- it is.  nurses make all of the difference.   unfortunately, the nurses this evening showed the difference it makes when they don't take pride in their work.

i wish i could leave zero stars. the nursing staff is horrific. they don't dilute their medications. they blew my veins 5x in 6 days time. that has never happened anywhere else. the nurse threatened me with a midline and said if i refused i was not going to get iv meds anymore... when i'm there for an infectious disease that causes dehydration. i had a horrible reaction as i was leaving and the nurses refused to contact the hospitalist. instead the same nurse threw my discharge papers at me.. and tried to refuse to give me my prescriptions as i was leaving. she said they were sent electronically. 
i am someone who is chronically ill. i know that narcotics can not be sent electronically. as soon as i said i was calling the pharmacy, she comes running back in my room with my crumbled up prescription. which the doctor has already left so she was withholding it out of spite. 
i have been hospitalized a good amount of my life due to autoimmune diseases from gallbladder dying to chronic pancreatitis, liver disease, blood clots, internal bleeding and chronic c diff. 
i will never go back to this hospital. truly. don't go here.
the charge nurse on the fourth floor is up to no good, even the other nurses and clinic assistants told me horrible stories about her. only two nurses on the whole floor are genuine and even apologized and said they didn't know why that young girl was a charge nurse. 
my first day admitted, she was laughing with another nurse because she left an elderly woman on the toilet by herself because she was tired of waiting for her. 
you are better off driving to austin another 15 minutes for quality care. 
5 hours without anyone checking on me one day, they skipped time sensitive antibiotics.. then 2 hours of throwing up without any nurse coming in. you're lucky if they check your vitals once a day. 
i am glad i was able to fight for myself. if you have an elder parent or young child.. do not subject them to this type of care. there is a reason for the other negative comments. 
if you are reading this, it's probably because you need medical care and i hope you feel better soon. but this isn't a family hospital. this is an outrage.

so after speaking with the patient care advocate, mcall washer, the billing issues were all resolved. i would give her 5 stars for her compassion. she really worked hard to make things right. it's rare that you find someone that goes the distance for you. thank you again for taking the time to improve the care i received. you a good person and it shows.

i checked into sutter er on march 9th, 2020, because i thought i could be miscarrying my pregnancy and urgent care suggested i go to the er to get an ultrasound. i walked in, the lobby was empty (due to the covid19 scare), sanitized my own seat, and everything went smoothly after checking in. i had no pain, i was offered wheel chairs, but i preferred to walk, the er was also empty, and i even saw nurses sitting and texting on their phones.  i had my blood drawn for standard blood testing and two ultrasounds that showed a baby's heartbeat (i skipped out on the urine test due to lack of cups in the ultrasound room).  on the way out, i asked how much the visit was going to cost me, "$250- do you want to pay now or would you like us to bill you?"- i asked them to send me the bill. i thought this was a pretty successful precautionary visit- until i got the bill.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me. 

i can say whole-heartedly that i feel i have been scammed by sutter. i am in the middle of my pregnancy and have canceled all my appointments. i delivered my first baby with sutter, but not this one, not after this wretched experience. how could i ever trust them again?

after i was taken back, i got in my gown, settled onto the gurney, and then shortly after, dr martinez came in.

she has a great bedside manner, and she talked to me about my symptoms, and explained what she was going to do. she then said the nurse would be in shortly.

i was expecting a long wait, because that's how it goes in hospitals, but then about 10 minutes later, nurse jenny came in.

y'all, she is awesome. very nice and funny, and i did not even feel the needle when she drew blood and started an iv. a+ phlebotomy skills. she sent me off to the bathroom to get a urine sample. i told her i didn't know if i could give her anything because i had just gone before i went to the er. she told me that she actually doesn't need much, and that she laughs whenever people give her a full cup back, because it's just overkill. so after i returned with a fuller cup than i expected, i said "i got more than i expected" and she laughed and said "what did i tell you?! i only need a tiny bit!"

anyway, she took my various fluids to be tested, and i settled in with a podcast, anticipating a long wait.

but about 45 minutes later, dr martinez arrived, said my test results all looked great, and determined that the cause was the cough syrup i had been taking for an allergy-induced cough that i've had since march.

she said to follow up about the cough with my primary care, and said she was ready to "bust you outta here."

i got dressed, jenny came in with a note for work and my discharge notes, and off i went.

all in all, i only spent 2 hours in the er. i think that might be some kind of record.

so, if you have to go to this er, and you get dr martinez and/or nurse jenny, you'll definitely be well cared for. if you get both of them together, you've hit the freakin jackpot.

dr. nelson is not a psychiatrist. in my chart, he wrote in an diagnosis for borderline personality disorder and claimed my behavior (being upset about not being able to have my life saving medication) was due to this disorder. he also claimed that i changed and fabricated my stories while i was there, implying in my chart that it was due to this disorder (one i do not have). i was not visited by a staff psychologist, social worker or other doctor who could have advised him on such a diagnosis. i have since received follow up care and i am feeling better. i don't have bpd. i have never been diagnosed with bpd. i have bipolar 2 disorder and ocd. his uninformed diagnosis reduced the quality of my care by other attending physicians and nurses. the treatment i received at the hands of dr. nelson left me feeling even worse than i had felt when i came in to the emergency room. he stated that i have bpd in these records and to my nurses to invalidate my feelings and reactions to what happened. this is blatant discrimination and disgusting behavior from a doctor.

by now, many of my fellow yelpers have heard about my recent battle with brain cancer.  i had no idea that i had a fist sized tumor in my right temple until i had a massive seizure that caused me to throw myself to the flow, striking my side table next to my bed so hard with my jaw that i broke the legs off!  i don't remember any of that but remember waking in the hospital with a breathing tube in my mouth and feeling somewhat confused.

within a few days my surgery was scheduled and they successfully removed a small high grade tumor as well as the massive low grade tumor.  i spent nearly a week in the hospital and must say that everyone i came into contact with was friendly and caring and encouraging, so i felt the care i received throughout my stay (and my recent follow up visits) has been excellent.

even the food from the cafeteria was pretty good.  not high cuisine, but palatable and with enough diversity that i felt like i had decent choices for each meal.  in fact, my only complaint is that they could boost their wifi since over the course of the week, there wasn't much i could do other than take naps.  streaming on my phone was not very successful.  but honestly, i probably needed the naps to recover from the huge surgery (42 staples needed) more than i needed to watch some episode of a tv show.

i feel like the staff was so upbeat and supportive including helping my wife and i find our way around the hospital.  if anything, they may have given too much information upfront since i am not well versed in medical and medicinal terminology.  fortunately, my wife takes great notes and was able to coordinate all my follow-up appointments for me and to fill my pill box so that i took the right pills at the right frequency.

when i met with the surgeon and oncologist, i felt they explained things in terms i could understand and they prepared me for the upcoming challenge of the multi cycle treatment plan which starts next week.  i understand what each phase is supposed to provide and with so many ways of attacking my disease, i am confident that i will one day be back to my independent self.  it won't be easy, but i felt each doctor and nurse i dealt with cared about me and did their best to make sure i knew they were in this fight with me.

on my follow up visit where i was fitted with a radiation mask, i met a completely different set of staff and each of them was equally helpful whether it was on getting registered, or someone escorting us to the right department for our appointments.  just wonderful people who are doing their best to help the patients in their care.  what more can a patient ask for?  i am thankful for the good folks at methodist who literally saved my life.  and despite having an initial prognosis of only having 15 months if i don't continue with treatments, their support and plan gives me hope that i will one day be back to writing more reviews as i explore our state, one county at a time.

methodist is a great place and benefits with its connection to the greater iu health organization including the goodman hall neuroscience center across the street.

thank you to all the staff who took care of me.

review:
the barranca surgery center is a finely tuned operation.  everything is in its place. everything is efficiently staged. personnel at every level are fully functional, professional, and pleasant.  the nursing staff is abundant and awesome.
